items.title: Direct torque detection of crystal chirality
items.abstract: Chirality governs phenomena ranging from chemical reactions to the topology of quasiparticle charge carriers. However, a direct macroscopic probe for crystal chirality remains a significant challenge, especially in time reversal symmetric systems with weak circular dichroism signal. Here, we propose the ``Chiralometer'', a mechanical detection method that probes chirality by driving angular momentum carriers out of equilibrium. Using first-principles calculations and semiclassical transport theory, we demonstrate that a temperature gradient in insulators or an electric field in metals induces uncompensated angular momentum in phonons and electrons, respectively. This imbalance generates a macroscopic mechanical torque ($τ\sim 10^{-11} N \cdot m$) well within the sensitivity of modern torque magnetometry and cantilever-based sensors. We identify robust signatures in chiral crystals such as Te, SiO$_2$, and the topological semimetal CoSi. Our work establishes mechanical torque as a fundamental order parameter for chirality, offering a transformative tool for orbitronics and chiral quantum materials.

items.title: A Census of Na D–Traced Neutral Interstellar Medium and Outflows at 0.6 < z < 4
items.abstract: Abstract We present a statistical census of the Na D–traced neutral interstellar medium (ISM) and outflows in 309 galaxies at 0.6 10 ), and 12% are in lower-mass systems. At high mass, ISM absorption is seen in both star-forming and quiescent galaxies, whereas in lower-mass systems, it is observed only in star-forming galaxies. In massive quiescent galaxies, Na D detectability appears linked to star formation history: it is preferentially detected in older systems with larger 4000 Å breaks and younger, rapidly quenching galaxies with strong Balmer absorption H δ A . We identify Na D outflows in 25 galaxies, revealing a possible dichotomy in driving mechanisms between star-forming and quiescent galaxies. In star-forming galaxies, outflow properties correlate with star formation properties, consistent with a star-formation-driven origin. In quiescent galaxies, however, outflows are not associated with residual star formation and often require more energy than such star formation can provide. Together with the high AGN fraction among outflow-detected quiescent galaxies, this suggests that AGN dominate Na D–traced neutral outflows in cosmic noon quiescent systems. We further identify four quiescent galaxies with possible AGN fossil outflows, suggesting that AGN-driven outflows can persist beyond the active accretion phase and may help maintain quiescence.

items.title: Ly α Radiation Pressure in Dense Star Clusters: Implications for Star Formation and Winds at Cosmic Dawn
items.abstract: Abstract Observations with the JWST in lensed fields have revealed that galaxies at cosmic dawn may concentrate their star formation in highly dense, compact, star clusters. The high columns and low metallicities encountered in their birth environments suggest that Ly α radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution. In this study, we address this question by postprocessing snapshots from radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of dense star-cluster-forming clouds (Σ * ≳ 10 3 M ⊙ pc −2 ) with a range of dust abundances ( Z d = 0–0.1 Z d,⊙ ) using the colt Monte Carlo code. We infer that Ly α is likely to have mild (∼10%) effects on the gas-to-star conversion efficiencies ( ϵ * ≳ 60%) for Z d ≳ 0.01 Z d,⊙ , and even in dust-free environments, ϵ * ≳ 25%—much higher than the ≲10% values typical of star-forming regions in the local Universe. This is because the densest filaments dominating stellar mass assembly ( n ≳ 10 4 cm −3 ) remain sub-Eddington ( f Edd 1, with noticeable fractions having f Edd ≳ 10, implying that Ly α can launch dynamically significant winds from these systems rapidly (≲4 Myr), with possible implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows. The Ly α force multiplier M F is highly sensitive to Z d , with M F ≲ 3 (≲500) for 0.1 Z d,⊙ (dust-free) environments, respectively. Nevertheless, Ly α dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all values of Z d ≲ 0.1 Z d,⊙ , by factors of ∼3–500. Our results suggest that Ly α radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

items.title: Formation of bound composite vortices of a singly quantized 1 S 0 vortex and half-quantized 3 P 2 vortices in the 1 S 0 - 3 P 2 coexisting phase in neutron stars
items.abstract: Pulsar glitches are believed to originate from the dynamics of quantized vortices in the neutron superfluid interior. The outer core of a neutron star hosts a $^3\text{P}_2$ spin-triplet superfluid, whose half-integer quantum vortices (HQVs) are qualitatively different from the $^1\text{S}_0$ singly quantized vortices (SQVs) in the inner crust. It has recently been proposed that the coupling between these two vortex species gives rise to a large-scale vortex network, providing a candidate mechanism for the diversity of observed pulsar glitch phenomena. Using the Gross--Pitaevskii equations for the $^1\text{S}_0$ and $^3\text{P}_2$ condensates, we perform two-dimensional simulations of one SQV and two HQVs in a coexistence phase near the crust-core boundary, varying the density--density and Josephson coupling constants. We find that the Josephson term, arising from the relative phase between the two condensates, induces a strong attractive interaction between the two HQVs and the SQV, which dominates over the density--density coupling. When pinning potentials are applied to the HQVs and the SQV at spatially separated locations, this attraction is found to be sufficiently strong to drive vortex depinning. These results suggest that two HQVs and one SQV can form a tightly bound composite vortex at the crust-core boundary, with implications for the glitch mechanism in neutron stars.

items.title: The Milky Way’s Missing In-Situ Halo
items.abstract: Abstract The Milky Way’s stellar halo preserves a record of its mass assembly history, encoding accretion events in its structural properties. Among the most prominent of these features is a strong break in the halo density profile at ≈20-30 kpc, long attributed to the apocenter pile-up of stars from the Gaia-Enceladus/Sausage merger. However, whether this interpretation is consistent with state-of-the-art cosmological simulations remains unclear. In this work, we compare the Milky Way’s measured stellar halo density profile between galactocentric radii of 1–100 kpc to those of Milky Way-mass galaxies from the FIRE-2 and Auriga cosmological zoom-in simulation suites, spanning a total of 24 simulated galaxies. We find that simulated halo profiles are significantly steeper than Milky Way measurements within ≈15 kpc, and that profile breaks are rare in simulations and never as strong as the Milky Way’s. Of the three galaxies with statistically significant breaks, only one exhibits a break attributable to apocenter pile-up of an accreted merger remnant. Decomposing the simulated profiles, we find that the accreted halo profiles are broadly consistent with Milky Way measurements, while the in-situ halo dominates within ≈20 kpc and drives the discrepancy. These results raise a compelling question: where is the Milky Way’s in-situ halo? The origin of this tension may reflect systematic biases in current halo measurements, an overproduction of early spheroidal star formation in cosmological simulations, or more fundamental differences in the underlying physics (e.g., dark matter) governing the assembly and structure of the inner Galaxy.

items.title: A Collapsar-disk Origin for GW190814
items.abstract: Abstract GW190814 was a remarkable gravitational-wave (GW) event: a merger between a 23 M ⊙ black hole (BH) and a 2.6 M ⊙ compact object, with an extreme mass ratio that is difficult to reproduce through standard isolated-binary or dynamical formation channels. Recent work has shown that neutrino-cooled collapsar disks can become gravitationally unstable and fragment, producing neutron stars (NSs) or low-mass BHs in orbit around the newly formed central BH. These fragments may subsequently interact, scatter, merge with one another, or inspiral into the central remnant. We explore the possibility that GW190814 originated from such a collapsar-disk fragment merging with the central BH. A key prediction of this scenario is a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova preceding the GW event, and we identify the Type Ib supernova candidate SN 2019npv, which occurred inside the GW190814 credible volume approximately 60 days before coalescence, as a possible electromagnetic precursor. Although this delay is too long for a conventional kilonova counterpart, we show that three-body interactions among disk fragments can excite some compact objects to wide orbits and produce merger delays of weeks to months. While GW190814 itself was not expected to produce detectable tidal-disruption-powered emission, future delayed mergers in this channel could generate luminous transients through either reprocessed kilonova heating or shocks driven as merger ejecta collide with the preceding supernova ejecta. Finally, treating SN 2019npv as the electromagnetic counterpart makes GW190814 a bright standard siren and yields H 0 = 71 . 1 − 7.5 + 9.3 km s − 1 Mpc − 1 .

items.title: Wave optics effects from gravitational wave propagation through dark matter halos
items.abstract: Gravitational wave (GW) propagation is usually studied under the geometric optics approximation. However, when GWs propagate through structures of sizes similar to their wavelength, this approximation breaks down. To study this situation, we present a scheme for numerically evolving linearised plane GWs through stationary, spherical astrophysical structures in both weak and strong gravity regimes. Our simulations evolve the full Einstein equations (with all 10 components) for Gaussian, NFW and Burkert potentials. Our simulations show that the scattering of the GWs depends not only on the mass of the lens but also strongly on the gravitational potential distribution of the lens. Among our most important results, we find that the GWs do not propagate along null geodesics when propagating through the Gaussian density, neither in the strong nor weak gravity setting. Another significant finding is that in the strong gravity case of the Burkert potential, the convexity of the wave is flipped when leaving the structure. We compare our results with the linearized scalar wave predictions and find that the difference between these and the exact GW modes are of order one when the wave is inside the central potential. However, the difference reduces to only a few percent when the wave has passed through the structure. Although these effects are small, future GW detectors and Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) could be sensitive to these signals which could thus potentially help in constraining the structure of dark matter spikes or halos.

items.title: Interpretable human-label-free deep learning for real-bogus classification with uncertainty quantification
items.abstract: Time-domain surveys generate large numbers of transient candidates, making real-bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Obtaining reliable human-labeled training sets is costly, while community-provided labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a real-bogus classification framework for point-like astrophysical transient detections against bogus survey detections, that can be trained without human-labeled data using physically motivated injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, that remains robust under strong class contamination, and that provides well-calibrated and reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) suitable for downstream decision-making. We combine simulated transient injections with a heavily contaminated survey class and train a dual-network model using an asymmetric co-teaching strategy for classes with different label-noise levels. We evaluate performance on a labeled benchmark subset and analyze the learned representation with latent-space visualization tools. For UQ, we compare standard approaches (Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles) and propose a low-cost hybrid strategy that exploits the dual-network setting to improve calibration. We further extend the evaluation to the light-curve domain to assess recovery of light-curve classes. The method achieves strong real-bogus performance on the labeled subset and remains stable under severe class contamination. It recovers transient light-curve classes with high fidelity, while single-source identification is fundamentally limited by intrinsic ambiguity in light-curve-derived labels. Our hybrid UQ approach achieves competitive calibration relative to substantially more expensive ensemble baselines. Latent-space analyses indicate that uncertainty aligns with the decision boundary and reveal that the model can identify subclasses within the bogus population. Our results show that injection-driven, weakly supervised training can enable scalable and consistent real-bogus classification without human-labeled training data while providing calibrated uncertainties. The methodology is well suited for transfer to forthcoming surveys by rerunning the injection-based training pipeline.

items.title: Unveiling the Milky Way with a Gaia DR3 census of OB-type stars within 2 kpc. I. Tracing local Galactic structure, massive star-forming regions and core-collapse supernova progenitors
items.abstract: Abstract O- and B-type stars are young and hot, thereby serving as vital tracers of the star formation and spiral arm structure of the Milky Way. At the dusk of the Gaia DR3 era, a high-confidence and accurate catalogue appears timely. We have characterized 105,971 OB-type stars (Teff > 10,000 K) within 2 kpc from the Sun, using an astro-photometric Bayesian inference tool. Our map unveils a complex view of the young stellar populations across the thin disk, with prominent large-scale features such as the Cepheus Spur, the Giant Oval Cavity, and a segment the Sagittarius-Carina arm all visible. Their inhomogeneous spatial distribution implies that massive star formation has taken place clustered across a few highly concentrated regions. We find a correlation between the overdensities of OB-type stars and young open clusters, and attribute departure from it to extinction effects. We identify 4200 stars as model-dependent core-collapse supernova (ccSN) or direct-collapse black hole (BH) progenitor candidates, including 6 ccSN progenitor candidates within 125 pc – the maximum radius within which a ccSN explosion could be harmful to Earth’s biosphere – but our analysis suggests none of them exploding within the next 5 Myrs. Finally, we anticipate more evolved OB-type stars to collapse to form BHs within the next 1 Myr than ccSN progenitors will explode, despite the former’s much scarcer number. A possible interpretation is a recent star formation burst in the local Milky Way, consistent with overdensities of ccSN progenitor candidates in Cyg OB2 and the Sagittarius-Carina arm.

items.title: Feature–adaptive fusion in hybrid quantum–classical neural networks for robust biomedical image classification
items.abstract: Abstract Hybrid quantum-classical neural networks provide a promising approach for incorporating quantum circuits into machine learning in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum regime. However, existing hybrid models often rely on fixed or globally shared fusion strategies, which may limit their ability to exploit complementary information carried by quantum branches, especially under distribution shifts. In this work, we propose a Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. The model combines a classical deep feature encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) and introduces a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically weight classical and quantum predictions. We evaluate FAF-HQNN on two MedMNIST benchmarks, PathMNIST and BloodMNIST, under clean and corrupted test conditions. FAF-HQNN achieves the strongest overall performance on clean data among the compared methods and shows improved robustness under Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and Poisson corruptions. Further analysis of circuit layout, measurement basis, and depth shows that even shallow variational quantum circuits can provide useful complementary information. These results demonstrate that feature-adaptive fusion is an effective strategy for improving accuracy and robustness in hybrid quantum-classical models for biomedical image classification.

items.title: Mitigating the Timing Impact of Anomalous Pulse Profile Shape Variability in PSR J1713+0747 with Gaussian Component Modeling
items.abstract: Abstract The North American Nanohertz Observatory for Gravitational Waves achieves submicrosecond timing precision for several millisecond pulsars in its pulsar timing array (PTA) with the objective of detecting and characterizing nanohertz gravitational waves. PSR J1713+0747 is one of the most precisely timed pulsars in the array, achieving submicrosecond timing precision. However, in 2021 April, PSR J1713+0747 underwent a sudden and unusual change in pulse shape that disrupted its timing stability. As PSR J1713+0747 is a key contributor to PTA sensitivity, variations in its pulse profile significantly affect the array’s sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves. We apply frequency-dependent Gaussian component models to decompose the pulse profile and track the evolution of individual components through the event. This component-level method maintains phase-connected timing across the shape-change event. At the L band, the recovered times of arrival (TOAs) have a median uncertainty of ∼0.47 μ s compared to ∼0.70 μ s for standard template matching. At 820 MHz, where profile frequency evolution is stronger, the recovered TOAs have a median uncertainty of ∼1.63 μ s compared to ∼0.67 μ s for standard template matching. The recovered TOAs achieve timing uncertainties comparable to conventional template matching while allowing data affected by profile variability to be retained in PTA gravitational-wave analyses. These results represent an initial step toward profile-domain timing methods capable of accounting for pulse profile evolution while reducing the need for additional timing model parameters.

items.title: Nucleon effective mass in neutron stars cooling
items.abstract: The cooling of neutrons stars, which are composed of ultra-high-density nuclear matter, strongly depends on the equation of state because the dominant cooling sources are neutrinos produced in their interiors. Here, we investigate the cooling properties of neutron stars, focusing on effective nucleon masses, whose impacts have been recently examined in supernova explosion and proto-neutron star cooling. The uncertainties of effective masses originate from the difference in the attractive interaction of scalar meson and the definition of the Dirac and Landau masses. At first, we employ so-called Walecka models that allow these two masses to be introduced within a unified framework and evaluate the resulting cooling curves. Based on the Walecka model, we compute the emissivity of the neutrons and the direct Urca process and their cooling curves. We demonstrate that the Dirac and Landau masses affect cooling of massive neutron stars, although most previous cooling simulations do not distinguish them. We also perform cooling simulations with two realistic equation of states based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory, whose differences arise from properties of only effective masses among characteristic parameters. These results are broadly consistent with those obtained from the Walecka models, indicating that the treatment of effective nucleon masses may be an important source of uncertainty in neutron-star cooling.

items.title: Structured coherence: A modern perspective on optical coherence as a resource
items.abstract: Optical coherence is a well-established branch of physical optics in which the statistical properties of fluctuating optical fields are described in terms of correlation functions over continuous spatial and temporal degrees of freedom (DoFs). Nevertheless, in any practical setting, only discrete DoFs are ever accessible. In these scenarios, the modes are fixed, stable, and deterministic, and partial coherence arises from random relative complex amplitudes, a configuration we refer to as 'structured coherence'. Advances in structured coherence have recently unveiled new conceptual ground in optical communications and information processing in which partial coherence may be preferable to full coherence, which we call a 'coherence advantage'. We formulate structured coherence in terms of coherence matrices to investigate these recent theoretical and experimental breakthroughs. We first review optical fields characterized by a binary DoF via 2x2 Hermitian coherence matrices and introduce key concepts that take on new significance for larger-dimensional modal sets. Next, we examine the structured coherence of two binary DoFs, which can be described by 4x4 coherence matrices. We introduce the concept of coherence rank, entropy swapping, and optical cross-purity. In the perspective outlined here, coherence is viewed as a 'resource', which can be exchanged between DoFs, concentrated into a DoF or into particular modes, or spread over the DoFs. We then examine larger-dimensional modal sets, which allow for more versatile applications in optical information processing. The formulation presented here lends itself particularly to the manipulation of partial optical coherence in integrated photonic platforms, thereby opening myriad avenues for novel fundamental investigations of structured coherence and exploiting the coherence advantage in optical communications and information processing.

items.title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley’s comet using deep-space low thrust
items.abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

items.title: Impact of heavy modes on primordial black hole formation
items.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) form from rare fluctuations in the high-density tail of the primordial distribution, making their abundance highly sensitive to primordial non-Gaussianity. Heavy fields during inflation can source such non-Gaussianity, producing characteristic signatures widely explored in cosmological collider physics, yet its impact on PBH formation remains largely unexamined. We investigate this question within quasi-single-field inflation (QSFI), the minimal realization that couples a heavy field to the inflaton. Unlike most PBH studies that consider only the bispectrum, the QSFI can generate a sizable trispectrum alongside the bispectrum, allowing us to investigate their combined effects on PBH formation. In our leading-order calculation, heavy-field non-Gaussianities can amplify the high-density tail and substantially enhance PBH production. Within the parameter scan, the largest enhancement occurs at the smallest heavy-field mass and the largest sound-speed ratio considered. The trispectrum contribution can be comparable to that of the bispectrum and may even dominate the total non-Gaussian correction. Our results establish PBH abundance as a novel observational channel for cosmological collider physics, demonstrating how heavy fields during inflation can significantly shape PBH formation.

items.title: A Decade-scale Ionization Echo of Black Hole Accretion in Galactic Nuclei
items.abstract: Abstract Circumnuclear structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN) respond to accretion variability over different spatial and temporal scales, but whether compact narrow-line gas responds on decade timescales has not been systematically established. We use repeat Sloan Digital Sky Survey and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument spectroscopy of 473 variability-selected galactic nuclei with evidence for recent nuclear brightening. We identify 19 sources whose narrow [O III ] λ 5007 flux increased by more than a factor of 2 over rest-frame baselines of 12.0–20.4 yr, which we term narrow-line ionization echoes (NIEs). In equal-weight stacked spectra, [O III ] increased by 229% ± 22%, while lower-ionization lines remained nearly unchanged or declined, indicating an ionization-dependent response rather than uniform spectral rescaling. The NIE hosts also moved coherently toward higher excitation in optical diagnostic diagrams, with mean increases of 0.46 ± 0.18 dex in log ( [ O III ] / H β ) and 0.58 ± 0.13 dex in log ( [ O III ] / [ O II ] ) . Photoionization models reproduce this evolution with a higher ionization parameter and a harder AGN-like ionizing spectrum at fixed gas abundance. For 13 sources with well-defined mid-infrared (MIR) outbursts, the integrated W1+W2 excess energy correlates strongly with the absolute [O III ] luminosity change ( r = 0.87), linking the dust and narrow-line responses to the same nuclear event. The MIR timescale and spectroscopic baseline constrain the variable [O III ]-emitting gas to characteristic scales of 1.5–5.2 pc. Compact narrow-line gas therefore appears to form an intermediate, decade-scale response layer between the infrared dust echo and the long-lived extended narrow-line region.

items.title: A comparison of particle and fluid approaches for modeling the streaming instability in global patch simulations
items.abstract: Identifying the process relevant to planet formation is still a major task. Mechanisms have been identified that can trap dust and prevent it from migrating inward. A particular hydrodynamic instability, known as the streaming instability, is of high interest because it might cause the formation of dust clumps from which the first planetesimals form. We compared the outcome of nonlinear streaming instability simulations using two fundamental approaches in a more realistic global disk model. The results were not used to identify or disentangle the effect of numerical diffusion in fluid simulations, for instance, or the possibility of crossing particle streams. Instead, they enabled us to determine whether the Lagrangian particle approach is most suitable for numerical studies of the streaming instability. We performed 2D axisymmetric global and isothermal hydrodynamic simulations using the two codes FARGO3D (dust fluid) and PLUTO (fluid and particles) to investigate the temporal evolution of dust scale height, the midplane dust-to-gas ratio, and the maximum dust density, as well as to study velocity distributions and vorticities. For PLUTO particle simulations, we also investigated the influence of the gas Riemann solver and spatial reconstruction orders. Our results from a resolution study of up to 5120 cells per gas scale height indicate convergence between PLUTO fluid and FARGO3D. The two codes yield a Gaussian profile that is dominated by small-scale dust-depleted voids. The particle simulations with PLUTO have not yet converged because a transient midplane dust component persists, indicating the need for an even higher resolution or more particles. A more accurate Riemann solver or a higher-order spatial reconstruction scheme helps to cause the dust density profile to approach the converged structure. At the highest resolution, the maximum dust density in fluid simulations is only 36$%$ of that in particle simulations, which is similar to other code-comparison works. When the streaming instability is studied in a global sense, the choice of the Riemann solver and spatial reconstruction order becomes more important than the approach itself (fluid or particles). When the computational performance of the two dust treatments is included, the fluid approach provides an efficient and suitable tool for streaming instability simulations.

items.title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [O iii ] Emission Filament
items.abstract: Abstract We report [O iii ] narrowband imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the Super Wide-Field [O iii] Narrow-band Survey (SWONS), together with multifiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H α , [N ii ], [S ii ], and [O iii ] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities, and full widths at half-maximum. The [S ii ]/H α ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O iii ] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O iii ] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O iii ] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of ∼160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of ∼28 pc along the north–south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O iii ] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O iii ] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.

items.title: A New Method for Constraining 3D Exoplanet Atmospheres: Application to WASP-94A b’s Panchromatic Spectrum
items.abstract: Abstract A growing number of transiting exoplanets exhibit spectroscopic evidence that their leading and trailing limbs differ. Interpreting these observations is now the limiting step. The standard approach of fitting limb-resolved transit depths results in highly anticorrelated transit depths, and treating them as independent measurements can result in strongly biased (3 σ ) retrieved molecular abundances. We present an inference framework that avoids these correlations by using the temporal signature of limb asymmetry instead. This wavelength-dependent shift in mid-transit time, or “time-shift spectrum,” carries the limb-asymmetry information, is measurable from existing light curves with a spherically symmetric transit model, and is uncorrelated with the spherically averaged transit depth. Simultaneously fitting the resulting transmission and time-shift spectrum with an independent atmospheric column for each limb enables the retrieval of limb-resolved properties from two independent measurements. We demonstrate that this approach reduces the mean squared error on the retrieved molecular abundances by factors of ∼30–50 relative to the next best of the alternative approaches currently adopted in the field, and improves retrieved abundance precision by ∼3–6× . We apply the framework to WASP-94A b and present its panchromatic limb-resolved spectrum, spanning 0.8–5 μ m and combining NIRISS/SOSS and NIRSpec/G395H observations. The planet’s morning limb remains aerosol-obscured across this entire range, while its evening limb constrains the abundances of H 2 O, CO 2 , CO, and H 2 S. We measure a limb-to-limb temperature difference of 415 ± 58 K at 1 mbar. This limb-resolved analysis finds [M/H] = +0.32 − 0.11 + 0.11 and C/O = 0.724 − 0.013 + 0.013 , consistent with the host star.

items.title: νGundam: A unified framework for point-redshift and probability-density-function-aware spatial correlation functions
items.abstract: Photometric-redshift uncertainties redistribute galaxy pairs along the line of sight (LOS) and across projected-separation bins, which dilutes spatial clustering measurements. Modern photo-z methods provide full per-object redshift probability density functions (PDFs), but propagating them directly through standard pair-count estimators remains computationally demanding. We present 1.2 ν Gundam a unified framework for point-redshift and PDF-aware spatial correlation functions. Our aim is to propagate radial PDFs at the pair-count level while retaining a common interface for exact, compressed, and stochastic projected-clustering calculations. The code implements four PDF-aware modes: exact empirical-PDF integration on a shared radial grid, Gaussian-mixture (GMM) compression, Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, and a quantile-compression method, 16quant. All modes accumulate pair counts on a resolved $(r_ ,π)$ grid, from which ξ(r_ ,π) and cumulative w_ (r_ ;Π) are reconstructed. We validated these methods with DESI galaxies and CosmoDC2 mocks using pair-level diagnostics, controlled degradation, convergence tests, and an exact-grid benchmark. p p p p The PDF-aware modes produce nearly indistinguishable LOS redistribution kernels, while point-photo-z estimates discard probabilistic pair information. Controlled Gaussian and empirical-PDF experiments show that radial uncertainty mainly redistributes the existing clustering signal to larger π, and that the LOS depth required to recover the truth-redshift projection scales approximately with the effective pairwise radial dispersion. For practical settings, MC, 16quant, and GMM reproduce the exact-grid result with fractional root-mean-square (RMS) residuals below 5%. Applied to DESI red and blue Bright Galaxy Survey samples, MC sampling recovers their spectroscopic clustering shapes and relative amplitudes for r_ p -1 Mpc -1 Mpc , respectively. Projected clustering with redshift PDFs is best understood as a pair-redistribution problem. When propagated consistently, the projected signal can be recovered accurately and efficiently. The LOS integration depth is nevertheless sample-dependent and should be treated as part of the measurement definition rather than as a fixed technical choice.

items.title: Theoretical pulsation properties of RR Lyrae and Type II Cepheids in the JWST and Roman photometric systems
items.abstract: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars and Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are key standard candles and tracers of old stellar populations. The deep, wide-field capabilities of facilities such as the Space Telescope (JWST) and the Space Telescope will significantly expand their utility as a Population II alternative to classical Cepheids for distance scale calibrations. James Webb Nancy Grace Roman We present theoretical pulsation properties -- including light-curve morphologies, amplitudes, and multi-filter relations -- for RRLs (Z = 0.0001--0.02, M = 0.51--0.80,M_⊙) and T2Cs (Z = 0.0001--0.01, M = 0.495--0.65,M_⊙) to enable detailed studies of Galactic and extragalactic populations. Using already available non-linear convective pulsation models, we converted their predicted bolometric light curves across various chemical compositions and evolutionary stages into the JWST and photometric systems. From these, we derived multi-filter period-amplitude and colour-colour diagrams, alongside period-luminosity and period-Wesenheit relations with explicit metallicity terms. Roman The relations for RRL pulsators display a significantly stronger zero-point metallicity dependence than those of T2Cs, despite having similar slopes. Consequently, T2Cs offer a distance scale indicator that is remarkably robust against metallicity uncertainties. As a preliminary test, we applied our metal-dependent period-Wesenheit relations to a subset of JWST-observed RRLs in the WLM galaxy, deriving a distance modulus of μ = 24.85 ± 0.03 mag (assuming the literature average metallicity). The derived distance to WLM is consistent with most literature values, though slightly shorter than determinations based on classical Cepheids and the tip of the red giant branch. These theoretical relations pave the way for future high-precision distance determinations and asteroseismic diagnostics with JWST and . Roman

items.title: Comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE astrophysical data
items.abstract: A hybrid reconstruction algorithm combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve the reconstruction of photoelectron tracks in the gas pixel detectors (GPDs) on board the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). The method has been validated on laboratory calibration data, but its performance on astrophysical sources with known polarimetric properties has not yet been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE data of astrophysical point sources, with the aim of quantifying the improvement in polarimetric sensitivity as a function of energy. We analyzed two IXPE observations selected to probe complementary regimes: Her X-1, a bright and highly polarized accreting X-ray pulsar used as a quantitative benchmark, and the transient neutron star low-mass X-ray binary XTE J1701-461 in its soft state, a bright source with no detectable polarization used to measure residual systematic effects. For each source, we compared the normalized Stokes parameters, the degree of polarization (PD) and angle (PA), and the detection significance derived from the level 2 event files produced by both pipelines. For Her X-1, the hybrid method yields a consistently higher detection significance at all energies, with a statistically significant improvement above ∼2.83 keV. The significance ratio, R = σ_ /σ_ , deviates from unity by up to 9.3σ in the 2.83-4.00 keV bin, rising to R = 1.18 ± 0.03 at 5.66-8.00 keV at 6.2σ. For XTE J1701-461, both methods yield polarization degrees consistent with zero and significance ratios consistent with unity. Through a Fourier analysis, we identify some modes (m = 3, m = 6, m = 12, and m = 15) with power excesses in the hybrid angle distributions at low energies, which are significant at $>7σ$ relative to the standard method, while at 5-8 keV all modes are consistent with the expected noise level for both methods: these modes are amplified by CNN but do not propagate to the Stokes parameters. hyb std The hybrid method provides a measurable and statistically significant improvement in the polarimetric sensitivity for bright point sources that is fully consistent with the predictions from laboratory calibrations and equivalent to a sim20% increase in effective area without the additional cost of observation time. items.title: A Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of the Birth and Cannibalism of Homologous Coronal Mass Ejections
items.abstract: Abstract Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are sequential eruptions from the same active region. They are of particular space-weather interest because they can interact and coalesce into compound ejecta, potentially amplifying their geomagnetic impact. Yet the full chain from recurrent initiation to magnetic merging has not been captured self-consistently in a single global simulation. We present a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model that generates three homologous CMEs from a bipolar active region by recurrent photospheric shearing. All three eruptions follow the same initiation mechanism by tether-cutting reconnection within a recurrently formed sigmoid, while the later CMEs propagate significantly faster than the first. We demonstrate that this speed hierarchy arises from progressive coronal preconditioning; preceding eruptions evacuate the overlying corona, reducing both mass loading and ambient drag. The faster, later CMEs catch up with their predecessors, and the compression between them forms inter-CME current sheets. Reconnection within these current sheets then progressively merges the interacting flux systems, completing the cannibalistic process. Synthetic coronagraph images reproduce the apparent coalescence of multiple white-light fronts. This simulation provides the first self-consistent global view of the birth, preconditioning, and cannibalistic interaction of homologous CMEs, bridging recurrent eruption initiation and inter-CME magnetic merging in the near-Sun corona.

items.title: ARRAKIHS: The observability of tidally stripped satellites in a Milky Way-like halo
items.abstract: Current and forthcoming deep imaging surveys are revealing an increasing number of low surface brightness stellar streams around Milky Way-like galaxies. These streams encode information about the orbital evolution and internal structure of their disrupted dwarf galaxy progenitors. We investigate the dynamical evolution and observability of tidal features produced by dwarf galaxies consistent with the cosmological constant and cold dark matter ((Λ)CDM) framework and observations of Local Group satellites. We performed high-resolution N-body simulations of dwarf galaxies orbiting within a static Milky Way-like potential comprising a disc, a bulge, and a dark matter halo. Each dwarf comprised two collisionless components: a Plummer stellar distribution embedded in a cuspy or cored generalised Navarro--Frenk--White dark matter halo. Idealised integrated surface brightness maps were constructed from simulation outputs every (0.5, ) over (10, ), and detectability was quantified through the projected area of progenitor stellar light brighter than a range of limiting surface brightnesses, (μ_ =29)--(32, ), chosen to span depths relevant to the Analysis of Resolved Remnants of Accreted galaxies as a Key Instrument for Halo Surveys (ARRAKIHS), the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), and . The detectability of tidal features depends most strongly on progenitor stellar mass, orbital configuration, parameterised by the eccentricity proxy (e_0), and evolutionary stage. Over the surface brightness range explored, extended tidal debris is predominantly recovered for initially more radial configurations, mainly those with (e_0 ≳ 0.75). In the simulated grid, detectable area is dominated by (M_⋆=10^8)--(10^9,M_⊙) progenitors, whereas (M_⋆=10^6)--(10^7,M_⊙) systems can undergo stripping without detectable debris. The detectable area evolves non-monotonically with time, reflecting the competition between stream formation, phase mixing, and the fading of diffuse debris below the adopted surface brightness limits. items.title: Desynchronization between CME Acceleration and Flare Reconnection
items.abstract: Abstract According to the standard coronal mass ejection (CME) model, both the flare and the CME are a result of the common process of magnetic reconnection. This implies that the CME impulsive acceleration and the flare reconnection should correlate in time. However, observations suggest that this correlation may break for CMEs associated with weak flares. In this work, we aim to find experimental evidence of such desynchronization. For this study, we chose a CME that 1) was associated with a weak B7.1 flare; 2) was continuously tracked from the solar surface up to the outer corona with high-cadence observations; 3) for which X-ray images were available. We measured the CME acceleration profile and compared it with the reconnection signatures: the derivative of the soft X-ray (SXR) emission and the motion of flare ribbons. The studied CME had non-trivial kinematics. It first impulsively accelerated to 440 km s-1 over 20 min, then decelerated to 280 km s-1 over 15 min, and then slowly accelerated up to 660 km s-1 over 2 h. We observed reconnection signatures only during the deceleration and second acceleration phases, suggesting that the main impulsive acceleration occurred without flare reconnection. We interpreted the first acceleration phase as a consequence of the kink instability. As the flux rope rose, it stretched the current sheet below it, which slowed down the CME. Eventually, the reconnection started inside the newly formed current sheet, and the CME started to accelerate again. These results show that CMEs can accelerate significantly without magnetic reconnection and exhibit a complex acceleration structure. This means that different mechanisms play a role in CME acceleration at different stages of its evolution.

items.title: Spatially Resolved Cell-Fate Engineering through Nanoneedle-Mediated Optoporation
items.abstract: The development of advanced tissue models demands spatially resolved control over cell fate to provide deeper insights into complex biological processes, yet precise intracellular manipulation remains a critical bottleneck in cellular engineering strategies. Current approaches for gene delivery struggle in achieving the required localized resolution to control individual cell fate, while optogenetic approaches are constrained by the requirement for complex genetic engineering and limited modes of gene regulation. Here, we show that nanoneedle-mediated optoporation enables spatially resolved intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, locally directing cell fate. Through computational modeling and experimental validation, we investigated the dependence of electromagnetic field enhancement on wavelength, nanoneedle geometry, and porosity. We demonstrated the importance of surface chemistry for optoporation efficiency, achieving optimal transfection performance through thermal carbonization. This approach achieves efficient delivery for propidium iodide, 500 kDa dextran, and siRNA, alongside a 72% mRNA transfection efficiency, resulting in sustained protein expression after 24 h. Selective SNAIL1 mRNA transfection demonstrated localized cell-fate engineering, inducing a targeted epithelial to mesenchymal transition. This porous nanoneedle system presents a versatile and flexible approach for precise genetic manipulation through electromagnetic field tunability, offering new possibilities for studying complex biological processes and disease progression through spatially resolved control of cell fate.

items.title: Gravitationally driven fragmentation and classical turbulence: a quantitative assessment of the spectral analogy
items.abstract: The postinflationary inflaton condensate fragments gravitationally, a process well described by the Schrödinger–Poisson (SP) equations. Under the Madelung transformation the SP system is exactly equivalent to a compressible, inviscid, irrotational self-gravitating fluid in which a quantum potential replaces the thermodynamic pressure. That exact correspondence shows that vortex stretching, viscous dissipation and scale-separated forcing are all absent, so Kolmogorov scaling is not predicted. We then analyse the density-fluctuation power spectrum published by Musoke, Hotchkiss and Easther for the snapshot at which the Universe has grown by a factor of 200 since inflation ended, extracted from their figure with an uncertainty budget, bootstrapped confidence intervals, a scan of the fitting interval, and information-criterion model comparison. Over the decade of wavenumbers immediately above the horizon scale the spectrum follows a power law of slope − 3.73 ± 0.18 , which for that choice of interval is consistent with the − 11 / 3 obtained by transcribing the Kolmogorov spectrum into a three-dimensional spectral density and inconsistent with − 5 / 3 . The agreement is interval-dependent and is not a robust feature of the data: the slope varies between − 3.1 and − 7.4 as the fitting interval is changed, a curved spectrum is mildly preferred, and the scatter is dominated by realization noise rather than by figure extraction. The exponential high-wavenumber tail extends past the Nyquist frequency of the source simulation, so we attach no dissipation-range interpretation to it. The correspondence therefore holds over about 1 decade; we set out the measurements that would make the test decisive.

items.title: A two-dimensional numerical simulation of polarization electric field instability in the mid-latitude ionospheric E region at Wuhan, China
items.abstract: Background Ionospheric E-region irregularities modify local electron density and can affect high-frequency radio propagation, satellite communication, and navigation. Existing theories describe plasma density perturbations produced by electron density gradients and electric fields in sporadic E (ES) layers, but do not fully explain the persistence, propagation direction, and spatial structure of quasi-periodic (QP) echoes. Objective This study investigates the generation and evolution of E-region irregularities under geomagnetic conditions representative of the mid-latitude region at Wuhan. Methods A two-dimensional numerical simulation of E-region polarization electric field instability is conducted with initial perturbations and zonal wind shear. The Flux-Corrected Transport (FCT) and Bi-conjugate Gradient Stabilized (BICGSTAB) methods are used to solve the governing equations. The nighttime irregularity evolution at 100 km is simulated under a specified ionospheric background condition. Results The simulated plasma-density structures and polarization electric fields evolve in space and time. Horizontally distributed ES structures extend along the geomagnetic field and develop into stripe-like thin layers. During the 1,500 s simulation, the maximum polarization electric field reaches approximately 2.2 mV/m. The characteristic spacing of the resulting structures is comparable to the 27.0 km horizontal wavelength of the imposed seeding perturbation. Conclusion Under the prescribed background and perturbation conditions, the simulated ES morphology is associated with the imposed perturbation scale, suggesting a possible link between seeding wavelength and the resulting structure.

items.title: Artifact detection and localization in single-channel mobile EEG for sleep research using deep learning and attention mechanisms
items.abstract: Artifacts in the electroencephalogram (EEG) degrade signal quality and impact the analysis of brain activity. Current methods for detecting artifacts in sleep EEG range from threshold-based algorithms to machine learning approaches, yet applications remain limited for single-channel mobile EEG. We propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) model incorporating a convolutional block attention module (CNN-CBAM) to detect and localize artifacts in sleep EEG using attention maps. We benchmarked this model against 6 other machine learning and signal processing approaches. We trained/tuned all models on 72 manually annotated EEG recordings obtained during home-based monitoring from 18 healthy participants with a mean (SD) age of 68.05 y ( ± 5.02). We tested them on 26 separate recordings from 6 healthy participants with a mean (SD) age of 68.33 y ( ± 4.08), which contained artifacts in 4% of epochs. CNN-CBAM achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.88), sensitivity (0.81), and specificity (0.86) among the tested approaches. Under the ideal choice of an attention threshold of 0.66, the attention maps from CNN-CBAM localized artifacts within detected artifact epochs with a sensitivity of 0.61 and specificity of 0.63. This work demonstrates the feasibility of automating artifact detection and localization in wearable sleep EEG.

items.title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
items.abstract: Abstract Water molecules play a critical role in mediating protein-ligand interactions by forming hydrogen-bonding networks and contributing to ligand solvation. However, their behavior—ranging from rapid solvent exchange to persistent occupancy of buried sites—makes accurate binding free-energy estimation with molecular dynamics challenging. Inadequate sampling of water reorganization can bias computed affinities and obscure key interactions by preventing representative hydration states during calculations. To address this, we employ the polarizable AMOEBA force field together with Lambda-ABF-OPES, an integrated enhanced-sampling framework combining lambda-dynamics, multiple-walker adaptive biasing force, and on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling. AMOEBA provides a polarizable description of protein–ligand, ligand–water, and protein–water interactions, while the dynamic alchemical coordinate and adaptive biasing facilitate exploration of coupled ligand-pocket-solvent configurations during ligand decoupling. This construction allows water exchange, binding-site rehydration and solvent reorganization to emerge along the alchemical pathway without explicitly biasing water-based collective variables. Applied to five protein-ligand complexes spanning buried and semi-buried environments, the approach yields binding affinities in good agreement with experiment and captures relevant water-mediated reorganization to provide reproducible absolute binding free energies.

items.title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
items.abstract: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic AI and optimized prompts, may be apt for tackling some of the challenges.

items.title: Integrated computational pipelines using machine learning and deep neural networks for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease classification
items.abstract: Abstract High-speed optical microscopy of Drosophila hearts has become an essential approach for modeling cardiovascular disease and aging. However, manual evaluation of cardiac function is time-consuming, subjective, and error-prone, highlighting the need for reliable computational frameworks. Here, we present an end-to-end dual-modality pipeline that combines segmentation-derived cardiac parameters with ensemble machine learning and raw video-based representations with deep convolutional neural networks. This integrated approach enables automated and quantitative phenotyping of cardiac function across both aging and cardiovascular disease contexts. We evaluated the performance of the pipeline across three biological problems relevant to cardiovascular systems biology: distinguishing between young (1-week) and aged (5-week) hearts, classifying healthy hearts from those carrying the lamin C mutation (LamC G489V ), and identifying phenotypes associated with Ogdh knockdown. Ensemble learning with Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression applied to segmentation-derived features achieved accuracies of 82.3% ± 0.6% for aging classification, 79.0% ± 0.4% for lamin C mutant detection, and 98.5% for Ogdh knockdown identification. In parallel, video-based modelling using a custom convolutional neural network and a residual 3D network (R3D-18) yielded accuracies of 89.1% ± 0.5%, 74.0% ± 1.2%, and 93.9%, respectively. By integrating classical feature-based learning with modern deep architectures, this work provides a scalable computational framework for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease. More broadly, the study demonstrates how multimodal machine learning can enhance quantitative phenotyping, minimize human error in analysis, and expedite the application of invertebrate models in systems-level investigations of cardiovascular health and aging.

items.title: Bearing, heading and the perceptual geometry of collective motion
items.abstract: Traditional models of collective motion commonly assume that animals turn to match their neighbours' directions of travel. In the harmonic theory, decisions follow from a neural representation of direction, and a neighbour enters only as a stimulus at a bearing, the direction in which it lies. Here we show that a neighbour's spatial extent allows its orientation to enter through projection geometry alone, and the theory generates a matrix of coupling coefficients indexed by the neighbour's bearing and aspect. Responses to bearing alone form one edge of this matrix, and classical heading matching is a special case on its diagonal, one ray through a two-parameter family. Independently, an animal that responds only to neighbour position, perceived with a delay, acquires an alignment coefficient set by the slope of its distance-weighted attraction profile, so that it can align, anti-align or reverse sign. Alignment need not be a rule to be measured. In schooling fish and walking pigeons with body orientation measured independently of travel, social responses are recovered, including bearing responses in the fish. Heading excess depends on how turning is measured, appearing in the fish with forward but not centred responses and remaining unresolved in pigeons. Controls show why neither outcome identifies a direct alignment rule. In fish recordings with motion-assigned body polarity, heading-dependent structure departs from Vicsek form and fails the coefficient test for a common angular potential. Whether animals align thereby becomes a measurable question, with geometric, perceptual and behavioural origins that can be distinguished.

items.title: REST: Routing with En-route Seating Thresholds for pedestrian accessibility
items.abstract: Public seating can support walking by providing opportunities to rest at useful positions along complete journeys. We introduce a route-based framework that assesses nearby seating, access to everyday destinations, and whether rests are well spaced along routes. One method finds the shortest route that does not exceed a chosen distance without rest; another allows longer stretches but adds a cost expressed as equivalent walking distance. We apply the framework to Mannheim, Germany. With a 1,000 m travel budget and a 500 m limit on walking without an opportunity to rest, 99.5% of older residents in Feudenheim lived within 500 m of a rest, yet only 33.5% could reach at least one destination in each of five categories (food shops, pharmacies, primary healthcare, public transport, and community services) on ordinary shortest routes meeting this limit. Finding alternative routes with sufficiently spaced rests increased this share to 61.4%; allowing longer stretches with an added cost raised it to 76.2%, compared with 89.7% when resting needs were ignored. Across Mannheim, 20.2% of older residents lost access to a reachable category when routes required a resting opportunity every 500 m, versus 7.1% when longer stretches were allowed at extra cost. Compared with the shortest physical distance, the least burdensome routes incurred extra costs from seating gaps: a median of 7.3 m of equivalent walking distance across city areas (90th percentile: 45.9 m). Better-placed seating could reduce this burden without changing street layouts. These measures help planners identify deficiencies, test improvements and guide route choices.

items.title: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
items.abstract: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of the thermotidal torque on the tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising the star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the role of resonantly excited Lamb waves requires clarification due to its potential impact on Earth's length of day (LOD) during the Precambrian. Building on a previous work, which provided a fully analytical formulation of the atmospheric tidal response of rocky planets, we apply this framework to isentropic and isothermal atmospheres. We perform a comprehensive functional analysis of the resulting torque and compare the analytical predictions with numerical solutions from earlier general circulation model (GCM) studies. The analytical model agrees well with GCM results, accurately capturing the frequency dependence of tidal torque both for paleo-Earth and present-day Earth. More generally, the solutions capture the torque peak near synchronous rotation and the amplification associated with Lamb-wave resonance. Near resonance, the GCM results exhibit a stronger braking torque than accelerating torque. This asymmetry is reproduced by allowing tidal heating to lag behind insolation. The agreement with GCM spectra suggests that thermal tides in the benchmark simulations are driven predominantly by an indirect thermal forcing characterised by a substantial time delay, in contrast to the direct absorption of sunlight that dominates semidiurnal tides on present-day Earth.

items.title: The Composition of M-dwarf Exoplanet Hosts: Atmospheric Parameters and O, Mg, Si, and Fe Abundances from IR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Determining M-dwarf abundances is an important step to discerning the chemical evolution of the Milky Way and characterizing exoplanetary systems, especially since these objects commonly host small exoplanets. However, a dearth of M-dwarf abundance measurements exist compared to Sun-like stars, partially due to their complicated optical spectra dominated by molecular absorption lines and low luminosities. To overcome these issues, we have obtained high resolution H-band spectra of 40 planet-hosting M-dwarf stars and 2 M-dwarfs in wide binaries with FGK primaries with IGRINS on Gemini South and on the McDonald Observatory 2.7m telescope, and NIRSPEC on Keck. Abundances were derived by comparing each observed spectrum to synthetic spectral grids generated with MOOG and MARCS atmospheric models. Effective temperatures were derived using OH and H$_{2}$O lines and [Fe/H] from Fe I and FeH lines. Both Mg and Si abundances were determined using atomic features. Overall, we find that our abundances are broadly consistent with previous literature M-dwarf abundances. We complemented our abundances analysis with UVW velocities and Milky Way stellar population membership probabilities and identified 2 potential thick disk stars from our kinematic and chemical analysis: GJ 1252 and L181-1 which was a previously known thick disk star. Kinematic stellar population probabilities and a low [Fe/H] abundance makes Kepler 42 a likely thick disk star, although uncertain Mg and Si abundances make classification difficult. Lastly, we have determined Si/Mg and Fe/Mg molar ratios for M-dwarf exoplanet hosts and find the abundance distributions leads to exoplanet core-mass fractions between 20 - 40$\%$.

items.title: The JWST Early Release Science Program for Direct Observations of Exoplanetary Systems IX: A Multi-Wavelength Framework for Source Characterization in JWST Coronagraphic Imaging of the HIP 65426 System
items.abstract: We present an updated analysis of the JWST coronagraphic imaging data of the HIP 65426 system. We aim to search for and characterize potential planetary companions as well as provide updated astrometry and photometry for the known exoplanet HIP 65426 b following updates to the JWST and spaceKLIP pipelines. Our measured photometry and astrometry show significant differences to those in Carter et al. (2023) but are consistent to within $2.2σ$ in separation, $1.5σ$ in position angle, and $3.7σ$ in flux. Our results indicate that pipeline updates have changed the photometry and astrometry significantly in some filters, especially in terms of observed flux. We see the greatest changes in separation in F444W and F1550C, position angle in F250M, and flux in F250M, F300M, F410M, F1140C, and F1550C. The SED of HIP 65426 b remains consistent with a young, giant planet best fit by models with a cloudy atmosphere and an effective temperature estimate of ~1436 K. Using both NIRCam and MIRI data, we identified 21 candidate companion sources in addition to the known planet. Of the 21 sources, 13 were attributed to astrophysical sources with eight background stars, four galaxies, one unknown, and zero planets. While one of these sources was detected in Chauvin et al. (2017), the remaining point sources were undetected in previous ground-based observations, which makes this work an initial epoch of astrometry for these objects. One galaxy in particular appears as a point source in MIRI but is highly extended in NIRCam and exposes a potential drawback to single-epoch MIRI imaging in a blind search for companions.

items.title: 3C-guided reflection combined with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among nursing students: a mixed methods study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Humanistic care is essential to nursing practice and directly influences patient outcomes. Since nursing students constitute the future clinical workforce, cultivating humanistic care competencies is an educational responsibility rather than a solely clinical issue. However, current training often faces challenges such as disconnection between theory and practice, highlighting the need for effective teaching models. Based on reflective practice theory, this study evaluates a multicomponent educational intervention integrating 3 C (Context, Content, Course) guided reflection with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among undergraduate nursing students. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was employed. In the first phase, all seven intact classes of first-year nursing students (total n = 350) from a medical university in Guizhou Province were included and randomly assigned using a random number table at the class level to either the intervention group (4 classes, n = 200) or the control group (3 classes, n = 150). The intervention group received a single, integrated 160-minute classroom-based session consisting of 40 min of theoretical instruction, 40 min of scenario simulation, 40 min of 3 C-guided reflection, and 40 min of summary and assessment activities, whereas the control group received traditional theoretical instruction within a 160-minute session that also included assessment activities. Outcomes were assessed using the Caring Ability Inventory, theoretical knowledge tests, and satisfaction questionnaires. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for class-level clustering; CAI models additionally adjusted for the corresponding baseline scores. In the second phase, 40 nursing students were purposively selected from the intervention group for semi-structured in-depth interviews, and data were analyzed thematically. Results The intervention group had a higher immediate post-intervention score on the self-report Caring Ability Inventory (CAI) than the control group (adjusted mean difference = 19.68 points, 95% CI 17.04–22.33; standardized effect size = 1.65; P < 0.001). Higher self-reported CAI scores were also observed for the Understanding, Courage, and Patience subscales. The intervention group also had a higher immediate post-intervention theoretical knowledge score (mean difference = 4.80 points, 95% CI 0.72–8.88, P = 0.021). Learner evaluations of the intervention were generally favorable. Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: empathy awakening, cognitive reconstruction through structured reflection, courage cultivation, and conceptual shift toward professional caring. Conclusion This sequential explanatory mixed methods study (a cluster randomized trial plus qualitative interviews) provides preliminary evidence that the multicomponent 3 C-guided scenario simulation model is associated with higher immediate post-intervention self-reported CAI scores and theoretical knowledge scores among undergraduate nursing students following a single-session intervention. Qualitative findings provided complementary insights into students’ experiences; however, the study design cannot establish long-term causality or sustained competency development. The independent contribution of 3C-guided reflection cannot be determined from this multicomponent intervention. The potential role of the “experience–reflection–abstraction” cycle warrants further investigation through multi-center, longitudinal studies incorporating objective behavioral assessments.

items.title: Role of Personality in Conversational Information Seeking
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for information seeking, where users find, compare, and evaluate information through dialogue. In this role, the assistant does more than retrieve or generate content: it shapes how users articulate constraints, ask follow-up questions, verify claims, and decide when an answer is sufficient for action. Yet little is known about how user personality, assistant personality, and task context jointly influence these interactions. We examine personality as a controllable variable in conversational information seeking and study its effects on user behaviour and interaction quality. We conducted a controlled within-subject study in which assistant personality and task type were experimentally varied, while participant personality was measured using Big Five scores. Twenty-six participants each completed three information-seeking tasks under three assistant personality conditions: extraverted, conscientious, and neutral. Tasks covered exploratory travel planning, comparative smartphone shopping, and verification-sensitive health and diet information seeking. Data included conversation logs, behavioural traces, post-interaction questionnaires, an exit questionnaire, and Big Five measures. The assistant conditions were behaviourally distinct: the extraverted assistant produced longer turns, the conscientious assistant elicited higher user word share and more turns, and the neutral baseline fell between them. The strongest effect was a task-by-assistant interaction on trust and delegation, with preferred styles varying by task. No global winner emerged, but participants strongly preferred style choice or adaptation. These findings position assistant personality as a context-sensitive interactional design variable rather than a globally optimisable system property.

items.title: Outcome-aware Evaluation of Recommendation Rankings in Art Therapy Using Multimodal Physiological Utility
items.abstract: Recommender systems are often evaluated using observable behavioral signals as surrogate relevance measures of user experience.However, in well-being and mental health support applications, user experience is inherently non-observable.To address this limitation, we introduce a multimodal physiology-driven framework for evaluating recommendation rankings in art therapy using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and eye-gaze signals.We define a physiological utility scalar that captures item-level internal response by combining prefrontal hemodynamic responses with attention and engagement dynamics derived from gaze behavior, enabling direct comparison between system-generated rankings and rankings induced by internal user responses.We show that fNIRS-derived utility exhibits moderate alignment with system rankings (Spearman's 𝜌 ≈ 0.40, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.69), with inter-hemispheric functional connectivity showing the strongest alignment among the evaluated neural descriptors.Gaze-derived utility yields stronger observed alignment (𝜌 ≈ 0.55, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.75), particularly for attention continuity and engagementrelated representations.Multimodal integration yielded the highest observed agreement between recommendation rankings and physiology-derived utility (𝜌 ≈ 0.61, pairwise accuracy ≈ 0.77).Our findings provide exploratory evidence that multimodal physiological signals may offer complementary information for evaluating recommendation rankings in outcome-sensitive art therapy.

items.title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory
items.abstract: A safety rule and an episodic log compete for the same tokens in an AI agent's context. When the budget overflows, both are summarized at the same rate; only the rule needs exact wording to remain enforceable. On 20 production agent configurations, Claude Code's /compact prompt on Sonnet 4.6 preserves 53\% of safety rules after one compaction round and 10\% after five. We name this the Compaction Cliff. We address it with Knowledge Triage, a framework that classifies each line of an agent's knowledge base by type and routes each type through its own retention policy. Three deterministic operators implement this triage across the three context-management operations: TypeCompact rewrites items in place under per-type fidelity, TypeDecompose partitions a topic too large to compact safely, replicating in-scope safety rules across partitions, and TypeRetrieve fetches items from external storage with in-scope rules pinned ahead of relevance. On five public corpora, TypeCompact preserves 2--4$\times$ more safety rules than the strongest single-shot LLM compactor at every ratio, with 96\% recall over five rounds. TypeDecompose reaches 0\% locality violations against 93\% under uniform partitioning. TypeRetrieve reaches 100\% recall@50 against 73\% for the best single-shot LLM retriever. On three downstream behavioral benchmarks, we outperform the production Sonnet compactor on medical compliance (paired McNemar $p < 10^{-8}$ on preservation, $N = 200$), the full-policy and hierarchical baselines on retail task pass rate ($p < 0.01$, $N = 115$), and the hierarchical compaction on the airline domain ($p = 0.024$). We release AgentArtifactCorpus (396{,}934 agent configurations from 54{,}628 public GitHub repositories), the classifier, and the reference implementation.

items.title: Do General NLP Embeddings Capture Ontological Reasoning?
items.abstract: General-purpose NLP embedding models perform well on linguistic tasks, but their ability to capture symbolic ontological structure remains unclear. We introduce AVA, a systematic framework for evaluating whether embeddings distinguish logic-sensitive relational semantics in ontologies and knowledge graphs. AVA comprises 171,007 contrastive triplets derived from 163 heterogeneous ontologies using hierarchy inversion, relation substitution, and disjointness injection. Each triplet contains an ontology statement, a semantically equivalent paraphrase, and a logic-sensitive hard negative with contradictory relational meaning. We evaluate more than 25 state-of-the-art embedding models and find substantial limitations: the best model achieves only 0.739 triplet accuracy, while hard negative accuracy falls to 0.135. Fine-tuning improves discrimination by a large margin but transfers poorly to downstream Semantic Web tasks, including taxonomy discovery and ontology alignment. Further analysis suggests that improvements stem partly from perturbation-specific pattern recognition rather than robust ontological understanding. These findings reveal a persistent gap between linguistic representation learning and ontology-level discrimination, challenging the assumption that strong NLP benchmark performance translates to Semantic Web competence.
