items.title: E-MODULE BIOLENDO BERBASIS INKUIRI TERBIMBING BERMUATAN POTENSI LOKAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN BERPIKIR KREATIF DAN KOLABORASI SISWA
items.abstract: This research was motivated by the low creative thinking and collaboration skills of students in science subjects due to the minimal use of digital teaching materials and the lack of integration of local potential in learning. To address this issue, this study aimed to develop the BIOLENDO e-module based on guided inquiry integrated with the local potential of galendo on Ecology and Biodiversity topics. This study employed the Research and Development (R&D) method using the Lee and Owens model with a quasi-experimental Non-equivalent Control Group Design involving seventh-grade students at MTs Darul Ulum, Ciamis Regency. The results revealed that the average N-gain for creative thinking in the experimental class reached 0.514 (moderate category), which was significantly superior to the control class at 0.377 (t=4.005;df=58;p<0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.034). Furthermore, students' collaboration skills showed a marked improvement from an initial baseline of 55.00% to 80.06%, placing it in the high category. Thus, the BIOLENDO e-module is proven to be valid, practical, and effective in enhancing creative thinking skills as well as supporting students' collaborative capabilities. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan berpikir kreatif dan kolaborasi peserta didik pada mata pelajaran IPA akibat minimnya pemanfaatan bahan ajar digital serta belum terintegrasinya potensi lokal dalam pembelajaran. Untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan e-module BIOLENDO berbasis inkuiri terbimbing bermuatan potensi lokal galendo pada materi Ekologi dan Keanekaragaman Hayati yang teruji valid, praktis, dan efektif. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) model Lee dan Owens dengan desain eksperimen semu Non-equivalent Control Group Design pada peserta didik kelas VII MTs Darul Ulum Kabupaten Ciamis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata N-gain berpikir kreatif kelas eksperimen mencapai 0,514 (kategori sedang), lebih unggul dibandingkan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,377 (kategori sedang), dengan perbedaan signifikan secara statistik (t=4,005;df=58;p<0,001) serta effect size Cohen's d sebesar 1,034 (efek besar). Sementara itu, kemampuan kolaborasi peserta didik meningkat nyata dari kondisi awal sebesar 55,00% menjadi 80,06% pada akhir pembelajaran dan berada pada kategori tinggi. Dengan demikian, e-module BIOLENDO terbukti valid, praktis, dan efektif dalam meningkatkan kemampuan berpikir kreatif serta mengoptimalkan kolaborasi peserta didik.

items.title: Large Language Model as Universal Retriever in Industrial-Scale Recommender System
items.abstract: In real-world recommender systems, different retrieval objectives are typically addressed using task-specific datasets with carefully designed model architectures. We demonstrate that Large Language Models (LLMs) can function as universal retrievers, capable of handling multiple objectives within a generative retrieval framework. To address the model expressiveness and inference efficiency issues of generative retrieval, we propose multi-query representation and transferable discriminative mapping layers to model complex user-item relationships, and incorporate probabilistic sampling to reduce computation costs. Finally, our Universal Retrieval Model (URM) can adaptively generate a set from tens of millions of candidates based on an arbitrary given objective while keeping the latency within tens of milliseconds. Applied to industrial-scale data, URM outperforms expert models elaborately designed for different retrieval objectives in offline experiments and achieves a 3.13% revenue increase on our online advertising platform. URM also demonstrates strong performance in impression and GMV for long-tail and cold-start items.

items.title: FinMamba: Market-Aware Graph Enhanced Multi-Level Mamba for Stock Movement Prediction
items.abstract: Recently, combining stock features with inter-stock correlations has become a common and effective approach for stock movement prediction. However, financial data presents significant challenges due to its low signal-to-noise ratio and the dynamic complexity of the market, which give rise to two key limitations in existing methods. First, the relationships between stocks are highly influenced by multifaceted factors including macroeconomic market dynamics, and current models fail to adaptively capture these evolving interactions under specific market conditions. Second, for the accuracy and timeliness required by real-world trading, existing financial data mining methods struggle to extract beneficial pattern-oriented dependencies from long historical data while maintaining high efficiency and low memory consumption. To address the limitations, we propose FinMamba, a Mamba-GNN-based framework for market-aware and multi-level hybrid stock movement prediction. Specifically, we devise a dynamic graph to learn the changing representations of inter-stock relationships by integrating a pruning module that adapts to market trends. Afterward, with a selective mechanism, the multi-level Mamba discards irrelevant information and resets states to skillfully recall historical patterns across multiple time scales with linear time costs, which are then jointly optimized for reliable prediction. Extensive experiments on U.S. and Chinese stock markets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed FinMamba, achieving state-of-the-art prediction accuracy and trading profitability, while maintaining low computational complexity. The code is available at https://github.com/TROUBADOUR000/FinMamba.

items.title: Exploring Model Invariance with Discrete Search for Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization
items.abstract: As language models continue to grow in size due to their success in a wide range of applications such as conversational agents and coding, there is a pressing need to make them more accessible. A popular technique is to reduce their memory footprint by post-training quantization, where we use fewer bits (e.g., 4--8 bits) to represent the model without retraining it. However, quantizing language models remains a challenging task, especially in the ultra-low-bit setup (e.g., 2 bits). In this paper, we propose InvarExplore, a unified framework that systematically explores different kinds of model invariance to maximize quantization performance. Importantly, InvarExplore features a discrete search algorithm that enables us to explore permutation invariance, which is under-studied as it cannot be optimized with gradient-based methods. Such exploration allows us to take advantage of the synergy between each type of invariance. Our results and in-depth analyses show that InvarExplore is compatible with existing state-of-the-art integer quantization methods, achieving an add-on performance improvement over strong competing methods.

items.title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
items.abstract: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user-item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.

items.title: ELBO TDS : Temporal Distribution Shift Generalization for Industry-Scale Recommender Systems
items.abstract: Temporal distribution shift (TDS) erodes the long-term accuracy of recommender systems, yet industrial practice still relies on periodic incremental training, which struggles to capture both stable and transient patterns. Existing approaches such as invariant learning and self-supervised learning offer partial solutions but often suffer from unstable temporal generalization, representation collapse, or inefficient data utilization. To address these limitations, we propose ELBO$_\text{TDS}$, a probabilistic framework that integrates seamlessly into industry-scale incremental learning pipelines. First, we identify key shifting factors through statistical analysis of real-world production data and design a simple yet effective data augmentation strategy that resamples these time-varying factors to extend the training support. Second, to harness the benefits of this extended distribution while preventing representation collapse, we model the temporal recommendation scenario using a causal graph and derive a self-supervised variational objective, ELBO$_\text{TDS}$, grounded in the causal structure. Extensive experiments supported by both theoretical and empirical analysis demonstrate that our method achieves superior temporal generalization, yielding a 2.33\% uplift in GMV per user and has been successfully deployed in Shopee Product Search. Code is available at https://github.com/FuCongResearchSquad/ELBO4TDS.

items.title: Agent-R1: A Unified and Modular Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly evolved from single-turn text generators into the foundation of increasingly capable agents. As these agents take on more complex reasoning, decision making, tool use, and long-horizon tasks, reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming increasingly important for shaping their behavior. This shift is especially visible in agentic RL, where models must interact with tools and environments across multiple rounds rather than produce a single standalone response. In this regime, the usual view of a trajectory as one ever-growing token sequence becomes increasingly inadequate: it makes context evolution rigid and creates representation mismatches between rollout and training. This paper presents Agent-R1, a unified and modular framework for agentic RL built around step-level trajectory representation, flexible context management, and layered interfaces for workflows, environments and optimization. The key idea is to treat each interaction step as the basic reinforcement-learning transition, while keeping the optimization layer flexible: once the interaction is modeled at the step level, the framework can support token-level credit assignment, step-level credit assignment, or other compatible designs. These design choices make the framework compatible with a range of optimization strategies rather than tying it to a single algorithm. Together, these components provide a principled, extensible, and reusable substrate for agentic RL.

items.title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
items.abstract: In real-world documents, the information relevant to a user query may reside anywhere from the beginning to the end. This makes position bias -- a systematic tendency of retrieval models to favor or neglect content based on its location -- a critical concern. Although recent studies have identified such bias, existing analyses focus predominantly on English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for systematic diagnosis. To address these limitations, we introduce PosIR (Position-Aware Information Retrieval), the first standardized benchmark designed to systematically diagnose position bias in diverse retrieval scenarios. PosIR comprises 310 datasets spanning 10 languages and 31 domains, with relevance tied to precise reference spans. At its methodological core, PosIR employs a length-controlled bucketing strategy that groups queries by positive document length and analyzes positional effects within each bucket. This design strictly isolates position bias from length-induced performance degradation. Extensive experiments on 10 state-of-the-art embedding-based retrieval models reveal that: (1) retrieval performance on PosIR with documents exceeding 1536 tokens correlates poorly with the MMTEB benchmark, exposing limitations of current short-text evaluations; (2) position bias is pervasive in embedding models and even increases with document length, with most models exhibiting primacy bias while certain models show unexpected recency bias; (3) as an exploratory investigation, gradient-based saliency analysis further uncovers two distinct internal mechanisms that correlate with these positional preferences. We hope that PosIR can serve as a valuable diagnostic framework to advance the development of position-robust retrieval systems.

items.title: GraFine: Retrieval-Time Refinement for Efficient Graph RAG over Corpus Graphs
items.abstract: Graph RAG on corpus graphs enhances retrieval by leveraging intermediate node content as contextual clues to uncover unretrieved oracle nodes. However, existing methods suffer from two critical blind spots, namely semantically blind graph expansion and topology blind pruning, or else rely on prohibitively slow retrieval and generation interleaving. To address this, we formalize these limitations through an operational taxonomy and propose a retriever design that couples semantics-aware adding with graph-aware pruning under efficiency constraints. We instantiate this design as GraFine, which alternates between two refinement stages: Semantic Proximity eXpansion (SPX) for semantics-aware node addition, and a Graph Smoothing Reranker (GSR) for graph-aware pruning. Experiments on reference networks and text-rich knowledge graphs show that GraFine improves retrieval accuracy and generation quality while maintaining time-efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce Topological Recall (TR), a metric that quantifies the topological proximity between retrieved and oracle nodes. Our analysis using TR confirms that GraFine more effectively steers refinement toward undiscovered oracle nodes by leveraging intermediate contextual clues. Our code is available at this link: https://github.com/asmath472/GraFine.

items.title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Semantic Search Retrieval
items.abstract: Embedding-based retrieval (EBR) for large-scale e-commerce search faces three intertwined challenges: graded (non-binary) relevance where engagement signals are noisy and intent-varying while business relevance guidelines admit acceptable-but-not-exact matches, false negatives in hard sample mining, and unstable similarity score separability across relevance levels, the last of which complicates hybrid search score fusion and downstream ranking. We propose Mine and Refine, a two-stage contrastive training framework that addresses all three. A lightweight LLM, fine-tuned with engagement-driven audit, serves as a guideline-aligned scalable labeler throughout training. Stage 1 establishes a robust global embedding space via label-aware supervised contrastive learning; Stage 2 mines hard samples, re-annotates them with the LLM labeler to mitigate spurious negatives, and refines the model through a multi-level extension of circle loss that enforces margin-controlled separation across relevance levels. Deployed in production e-commerce search across multiple product verticals, the approach delivers statistically significant lifts in user engagement and gross order value, and substantially improves retrieval and end-to-end relevance metrics.

items.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. This expansion has motivated growing research into the ethical and moral foundations underlying LLM behavior, raising critical questions about their reliability in ethical reasoning. However, existing studies and benchmarks rely almost exclusively on Moral Foundation Theory (MFT), largely neglecting other relevant dimensions such as social values, personality traits, and individual characteristics that shape human ethical reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce MOSAIC, the first large-scale benchmark designed to jointly assess the moral, social, and individual characteristics of LLMs. The benchmark comprises nine validated questionnaires drawn from moral philosophy, psychology, and social theory, alongside four platform-based games designed to probe morally ambiguous scenarios. In total, MOSAIC includes over 600 curated questions and scenarios, released as a ready-to-use, extensible resource for evaluating the behavioral foundations of LLMs. We validate the benchmark across three models from different families, demonstrating its utility across all assessed dimensions and providing the first empirical evidence that MFT alone is insufficient to comprehensively evaluate complex AI systems' ethical behavior. We publicly release the dataset and our benchmark Python library.

items.title: DEP: A Decentralized Evaluation Protocol and Toolkit for Large Language Models
items.abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), a large number of benchmarks have been proposed. However, most benchmarks lack unified evaluation standard and require the manual implementation of custom scripts, making results hard to ensure consistency and reproducibility. Furthermore, mainstream evaluation frameworks are centralized, with datasets and answers, which increases the risk of benchmark leakage. To address these issues, we propose a Decentralized Evaluation Protocol (DEP), a decentralized yet unified and standardized evaluation framework through a matching server without constraining benchmarks. The server can be mounted locally or deployed remotely, and once adapted, it can be reused over the long term. By decoupling users, LLMs, and benchmarks, DEP enables modular, plug-and-play evaluation: benchmark files and evaluation logic stay exclusively on the server side. In remote setting, users cannot access the ground truth, thereby achieving data isolation and leak-proof evaluation. To facilitate practical adoption, we develop DEP Toolkit, a protocol-compatible toolkit that supports features such as breakpoint resume, concurrent requests, and congestion control. We also provide detailed documentation for adapting new benchmarks to DEP. Using DEP toolkit, we evaluate multiple LLMs across benchmarks. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of DEP and show that it reduces the cost of deploying benchmark evaluations. As of February 2026, we have adapted over 60 benchmarks and continue to promote community co-construction to support unified evaluation across various tasks and domains.

items.title: Eval4Sim: An Evaluation Framework for Persona Simulation
items.abstract: Large Language Model personas, explicit profiles specifying a user's attributes, preferences, and behavioural tendencies, are increasingly used to simulate human conversations for user modelling, social reasoning, and behavioural analysis. Evaluating whether such simulations faithfully reflect human conversational behaviour is critical, yet current practice often relies on LLM-as-a-judge approaches that provide limited grounding in observable behaviour and produce opaque scalar scores. We present Eval4Sim, an evaluation framework that measures alignment between simulated and human conversations across three dimensions: adherence, whether persona traits are recoverable from dialogue via dense retrieval; consistency, whether a persona maintains a distinguishable stylistic identity via authorship verification; and naturalness, whether conversations exhibit human-like turn-to-turn flow via dialogue NLI. Unlike optimization-oriented metrics, each dimension takes a human corpus as a reference baseline and penalizes deviations in both directions, distinguishing insufficient persona encoding from over-optimized, unnatural behaviour. The framework is corpus-agnostic: any persona-annotated conversational dataset can serve as the reference. Evaluated over ten simulation corpora, Eval4Sim surfaces systematic trade-offs invisible to single-score methods.

items.title: Semantic Caching: From Exact Hits to Close Enough
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) has created demand for faster responses and lower costs. Semantic caching, reusing semantically similar requests via their embeddings, addresses this need but breaks classic cache assumptions and raises new challenges. In this paper, we explore offline policies for semantic caching, proving that implementing an optimal offline policy is NP-hard, and propose several polynomial-time heuristics. We also present online semantic aware cache policies that combine recency, frequency, and locality. Evaluations on diverse datasets show that while frequency based policies are strong baselines, our novel variant improves semantic accuracy. Our findings reveal effective strategies for current systems and highlight substantial headroom for future innovation. All code is open source.

items.title: TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promising potential in E-commerce community recommendation. While LLMs and Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) are widely used to encode notes into implicit embeddings, leveraging their generative capabilities to represent notes with interpretable tags remains unexplored. In the field of tag generation, traditional close-ended methods heavily rely on the design of tag pools, while existing open-ended methods applied directly to note recommendations face two limitations: (1) MLLMs lack guidance during generation, resulting in redundant tags that fail to capture user interests; (2) The generated tags are often coarse and lack fine-grained representation of notes, interfering with downstream recommendations. To address these limitations, we propose TagLLM, a fine-grained tag generation method for note recommendation. TagLLM captures user interests across note categories through a User Interest Handbook and constructs fine-grained tag data using multimodal CoT Extraction. A Tag Knowledge Distillation method is developed to equip small models with competitive generation capabilities, enhancing inference efficiency. In online A/B test, TagLLM increases average view duration per user by 0.31%, average interactions per user by 0.96%, and page view click-through rate in cold-start scenario by 32.37%, demonstrating its effectiveness.

items.title: ContextClaim: A Context-Driven Paradigm for Verifiable Claim Detection
items.abstract: Automated fact-checking pipelines typically begin with a filtering stage that decides which claims are worth verifying, given that the later evidence retrieval and verification components are expensive to apply at scale. A central task in this stage is verifiable claim detection, which asks whether a statement is in principle checkable against external evidence. Prior work on this task, as well as on the closely related notion of check-worthiness, conditions its decisions only on the claim sentence itself. We argue that this is restrictive, because deciding whether a statement is checkable often depends on identifying the entities and events it mentions, and on whether external information about them is actually available in the first place. Motivated by how downstream verification systems rely on retrieved evidence, we move retrieval upstream into the detection stage and introduce ContextClaim. Given an input claim, the approach identifies entity mentions, queries Wikipedia as a structured background source, and uses large language models to compress the retrieved material into short contextual summaries that are then passed to a classifier. Experiments are conducted on two domains and genres, namely the CheckThat! 2022 Twitter collection and the PoliClaim corpus of political debates, and cover both encoder and decoder only models under fine-tuning, zero-shot, and few-shot settings. The added context yields gains on verifiable claim detection in several configurations, although the size of the improvement varies with the dataset, the backbone model, and the training setup. We further find that the same retrieved summaries are useful beyond detection. Feeding them into a downstream verification model on FEVER improves verification F1. Component level analyses, human annotation, and error inspection further clarify the conditions under which retrieved context helps, and where it does not.

items.title: Culture or cognition?
items.abstract: Abstract Gender languages assign nouns to a category, such as masculine, feminine, neuter or common. Gender assignment is complicated and difficult to learn, as languages do not have specific rules for assigning a noun to one or the other gender. This study looks at gender assignment from the perspective of semantics and lexical semantic evolution, exemplified on the Indo-European family. Gender assignment has a semantic core, in which animate nouns are more likely to be masculine, inanimate nouns feminine and neuter, nature nouns masculine, and culture nouns feminine or neuter. To investigate how these patterns emerge, we study the evolutionary dynamics of these semantic properties on a gender-coded lexical data set for Indo-European. We find that masculine is a stable gender that remains in its semantic category and does not change. Feminine is also a stable category which may get lost or transfer to masculine. Neuter and common are unstable categories, which continuously alter or get lost in gender assignment. In sum, our result shows that the semantic core of gender — affected both by cognitive and cultural factors — remains stable and does not vacillate in evolution.

items.title: Understanding Biodiversity in Acer Forests: From Species Diversity to Sustainable Conservation
items.abstract: The genus Acer comprises more than 110 tree and shrub species distributed throughout the Northern Hemisphere and represents an important component of temperate forest ecosystems. This review evaluates biodiversity patterns, ecological functions, environmental pressures, and conservation approaches associated with Acer forests. A systematic literature search conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases on 20 January 2026, without publication-year restrictions. After screening and eligibility assessment, 688 publications were included and analyzed using bibliometric methods and qualitative thematic synthesis. The literature increased substantially over the last four decades, with climate change, biodiversity conservation, forest dynamics, and sustainable management among the principal research themes. The selected studies covered species and genetic diversity, forest composition and dynamics, associated plant, fungal, and animal communities, environmental change, and conservation and management. Native Acer forests were frequently associated with structurally complex habitats, diverse understory communities, nutrient cycling, and multiple ecosystem functions, whereas habitat loss, fragmentation, climate change, atmospheric pollution, and biological invasions were identified as major pressures. Introduced species, particularly Acer negundo, were also frequently examined in relation to impacts on native biodiversity. Important research gaps concerned poorly studied endemic species, long-term monitoring, multitrophic interactions, and the effectiveness of conservation measures under environmental change. Future research should integrate ecological, genetic, physiological, and remote-sensing approaches to support evidence-based conservation and sustainable management of Acer forests. This review provides a systematic and bibliometric synthesis of the indexed English-language literature retrieved using the specified search strategy and identifies major research patterns, evidence gaps, and conservation priorities relevant to Acer forests biodiversity under environmental change.

items.title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
items.abstract: Background Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. Objective To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. Design Cohort study using the target trial framework. Setting Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. Patients Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. Intervention Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. Measurements The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. Results Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m 2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. Limitation Possible residual confounding. Conclusion Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. Primary funding source Research Council of Norway.

items.title: Mapping three decades of consciousness research in neuroscience: a scientometric synthesis of intellectual evolution and emerging frontiers.
items.abstract: Over the past three decades, consciousness research in neuroscience has expanded into a broad and increasingly diverse field. Despite significant progress, a quantitative understanding of how these research areas have collectively evolved has remained limited. In this study, we conducted a large-scale scientometric analysis of consciousness research in neuroscience based on 22,836 publications and 639,975 cited references retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection spanning 1998-2025. We identified three major research paths: neural correlates of conscious contents and states, internal awareness and self-consciousness, and integrative approaches bridging these two paths. Emerging hotspots included neural mechanisms of consciousness, subjective experience, disorders of consciousness (DoC), and interoception. Despite increasing boundary-spanning research across different areas, bibliometric connections between DoC and other major topics, particularly subjective experience and interoception, remain comparatively sparse. These findings provide a field-level synthesis of consciousness research in neuroscience, offering a quantitative framework for understanding its development and emerging research directions.

items.title: Exploring resident doctors' experience, attitudes, perceptions and beliefs about the serious incident investigatory process within mental health settings.
items.abstract: Background Serious incidents, such as patient suicide, profoundly impact clinicians. In mental health settings, these events are uniquely distressing. Despite policy shifts towards learning from serious incidents, many doctors report inadequate support and significant emotional distress. Resident doctors, already vulnerable to burnout and emotional exhaustion, are particularly at risk. Aims This study aimed to understand resident psychiatry doctors' experiences of serious incidents. It sought to gather in-depth insights about how resident psychiatrists navigate the serious incident process, and the effect the process has on their professional and personal lives. Method A qualitative study recruited 10 participants via email in 1 National Health Service (NHS) trust. Semi-structured online interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, employing an iterative, constant comparative approach. Results Descriptive characteristics of the participants are reported. Three overarching themes were identified: (a) when the process becomes the experience, with subthemes focusing on how open and transparent the investigation process was, about communication during the process and how doctors felt the process impacted their clinical role; (b) from theory to practice: when training meets reality. Subthemes here reflected on whether resident doctors felt prepared and knowledgeable about the process. There was also focus on the experience itself being a learning opportunity; (c) the emotional undercurrents: trauma, grief and support. Here the subthemes focused on the emotional toll of an incident and investigation, the grief and wider impact of a patient death and lastly, the need for support to resident doctors including supervisor and peer-to-peer support. Themes are reported accompanied by verbatim quotes from participants. Conclusions Findings confirm prior studies investigating the negative impact of serious incidents on resident doctors' well-being and career confidence, highlighting the need for robust support. The study adds to the literature through emphasising the inadequacy of current support and highlights rectifiable issues such as the need for structured peer support and improved supervisor/resident training for emotional and professional complexities. Future research should compare these findings with experiences under the new Patient Safety Incident Framework (PSIRF) system to assess improvements.

items.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Maternal-Infant (Dyadic) Attachment, Postpartum Depression, and Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Purpose This scoping review explores intersecting relationships among the concepts of postpartum depression, maternal-infant (dyadic) attachment (or bonding), and breastfeeding self-efficacy within postpartum populations and how often these concept relationships are examined among predominantly historically marginalized populations (non-White, low-income, low education level). Background To address the ongoing public health concern of postpartum depression, we must understand its relationship with dyadic attachment and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Discussion Four studies met inclusion criteria, examining the relationships between the concepts of postpartum depression, dyadic attachment, and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Because these 4 studies had heterogeneous study designs, study measures, and study time points, the exact nature of the relationship between these 3 concepts is difficult to parse. Furthermore, only 1 study evaluated these concepts in historically marginalized populations (low-income). Future research using rigorous study design approaches is warranted. Implications for research and practice While studies found a relationship between increased breastfeeding self-efficacy and increased dyadic attachment, mixed results remain regarding the relationships between postpartum depression and dyadic attachment or breastfeeding self-efficacy. Nevertheless, dyad-focused interventions have shown the potential to improve breastfeeding self-efficacy and dyadic attachment while reducing postpartum depression. The scoping review findings suggest that these concepts collectively need more research attention, given their potential effects on improving maternal-child dyadic outcomes.

items.title: Medicating inhibitory control? Treatment with serotonergic antidepressants predicts stop-N200 amplitudes in major depressive disorder.
items.abstract: Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent chronic mental illness often treated by serotonergic pharmacotherapy and complicated by sex differences and comorbid anxiety disorders (COMs). Deficits in inhibitory control are a transdiagnostic feature of MDD and COM, though the presentation of these deficits may be impacted by competing cognitive demands, symptoms severity, sexes, and medication status. Methods This project includes 233 participants from the Tulsa 1000 study who completed concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic functional resonance imaging (MRI) during a stop signal task (SST). We examined how serotonergic antidepressants, biological sex, and comorbidity with an anxiety disorder uniquely relate to neural indices of inhibitory control for healthy controls (HCs), MDD, and COM using linear mixed effect models, type III ANOVAs, and optimal full propensity matching. N200, P300, and correct-related negativity (CRN) components were extracted and analyzed to index conflict monitoring, conflict resolution, and performance monitoring, respectively, in response to stop signals and their absence. Results Our results revealed that HCs exhibited larger stop-P300 amplitudes than MDD and COM ( η 2 = 0.068); females had smaller stop-N200 amplitudes than males ( η 2 = 0.027); MDD/COM participants taking a serotonergic antidepressant exhibited less negative N200 amplitudes than those who were not (LME, B = 1.95; η 2 = 0.044; ATE, B = 2.47). Conclusions Our findings suggest being treated with serotonergic antidepressants are associated with neural differences in the conflict monitoring of inhibitory control in pure and comorbid depression.

items.title: Dietary fibre intake and suicide in Japanese adults: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study.
items.abstract: Dietary fibre intake has been reported to be inversely associated with depression in a meta-analysis. However, most studies were cross-sectional, and none examined the association with suicide, a severe outcome of depression. We investigated the association of dietary fibre intake with suicide risk among Japanese adults. Participants were 40 630 men and 48 178 women aged 44-76 years who responded to the second survey (baseline of the present study) of the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (1995-1998). Dietary fibre intake was assessed using a validated FFQ. Hazard ratios of suicide through December 2018 were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis. During a mean follow-up of 18·7 years, we identified 459 deaths from suicide. Dietary fibre intake was associated with lower suicide risk after adjustment for covariates, including intakes of vitamin B12, vitamin D, Ca, Zn and n-3 PUFA. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for suicide of the highest v. lowest quartile of total dietary fibre intake was 0·65 (95 % CI 0·46-0·93). Similar inverse associations were observed for vegetable and fruit fibre intake but not cereal or bean fibre. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for nutrients highly correlated with dietary fibre intake, including folate, vitamin B6, Mg and Fe; the corresponding value for total dietary fibre intake was 0·85 (95 % CI 0·55-1·31). Our findings suggest that greater consumption of foods rich in dietary fibre and related nutrients, rather than dietary fibre per se, may play a protective role against suicide.

items.title: An analysis of 20 years of retracted articles in psychiatry.
items.abstract: To characterise recent trends in retractions of publications in the psychiatric literature. We examined the Retraction Watch Database for publications with the subject term 'psychiatry' between 2003 and 2023. We then characterised publication type, subject, country of origin, reason for retraction and time between publication and retraction. A total of 315 psychiatry publications were retracted; the annual number and rate (relative to publications) rose steadily across the study period. The median number of days from publication to retraction was 643 (interquartile range 223.0-2966.0). Reasons for retraction were unclear in 20 (6.3%) cases only; most commonly they were attributed to data error (42.5%) or problems relating to peer review (11.4%) - the period between publication and retraction was particularly long for the latter studies (median 3082 days, interquartile range 575-3364). A total of 4.4% were retracted because of falsification, and 6.32% because of plagiarism. Retracted items frequently focused on mood disorders (24.4%), psychosis (14.9%) and neurodevelopmental disorders (13.7%). Clinicians and policy makers rely on academic literature, but should be aware of the ethical, legal, business and professional dilemmas often encountered, yet not reported, in the process of considering retractions of unreliable data. Contested and unreliable findings may persist in the scientific record, with potential negative consequences for evidence based-care and policy, including the erosion of public trust.

items.title: Inflammatory signature of subcutaneous fat after weight loss and regain in women undergoing repeated bariatric surgery.
items.abstract: Repeated metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS, r-BS) represents 10-25% of all MBS and is commonly-performed for weight regain after prior significant weight-loss. It remains unclear how adipose tissue adapts to surgically-induced weight-loss-regain in obesity. We hypothesized that compared to primary bariatric surgery (p-BS), women undergoing r-BS exhibit a distinct adipose tissue signature. Subcutaneous/visceral adipose tissues (SAT/VAT, respectively) from female MBS patients were assessed histologically/molecularly/functionally (activation of human microglia cells by SAT-secretome). Elective MBS in a public university hospital. Women undergoing either p-BS, or r-BS with documented >15% weight-loss after prior MBS. MBS. Inflammation in SAT. Women undergoing r-BS (n=21) trended to be older than those undergoing p-BS (n=35)(47.2 vs. 40.5y, p=0.06), with a lower BMI (42.3 vs. 45.6 kg/m2, respectively, p=0.103), and a trend for improved cardiometabolic risk parameters (fasting insulin, CRP and HDL-c). Adipocyte size, adipose tissue fibrosis, macrophage and crown-like structures abundance were similar, while mast-cells were slightly more prevalent in r-BS. Single-nucleus RNA-seq-based deconvolution algorithm applied unto bulk RNA-seq confirmed the absence of a major shift in adipose tissue cell-type composition. Yet, RNA-seq revealed unique transcriptome of r-BS SAT, with activation of inflammatory pathways. Consistently, SAT explants from r-BS secreted higher protein concentrations of NFκB-regulated cytokines IL6/IL8. Functional impact of the more inflammatory-secretome was suggested by its increased ability to inflammatory-activate human microglia cells. Prior BS-induced weight-loss and subsequent regain in women is associated with inflammatory transcriptome and secretome of SAT that can activate cultured human microglia cells.

items.title: Predictors of Antibiotic Overuse in Febrile Children: A Sub-analysis of the Prospective, Multicenter AutoPilot-Dx Study.
items.abstract: Antibiotic overuse contributes to antimicrobial resistance. Mechanisms that drive overuse, including diagnostic uncertainty, are thought to be complex. We aimed to investigate predictive factors for antibiotic overuse in a large pediatric cohort. This is a subanalysis from the AutoPilot-Dx study, which enrolled febrile children 90 days to 18 years old presenting to the pediatric emergency department with respiratory tract infection or fever without source, including both hospitalized children and those discharged home. We analyzed patient flow from being treated with antibiotics at recruitment to definitive antibiotic treatment after assessment, depending on physician judgment. Variables significantly associated with antibiotic overuse in univariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of antibiotic overuse, defined as receipt of antibiotic treatment following clinical assessment in cases with viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis. Diagnostic uncertainty was assessed by treating physicians. Upon recruitment, 127/1008 (12.6%) were receiving antibiotic treatment. Overall, 186 of 628 cases with a viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis were judged to have antibiotic overuse. Factors with significant association in univariate analysis were diagnostic uncertainty, nonexudative tonsillitis, rales and younger age. Presence of a diagnostic test result upon presentation to the hospital and current antibiotic treatment were found not to be associated with overuse. Among 566 of 1008 cases with complete data on all model covariates, multivariable logistic regression yielded diagnostic uncertainty [odds ratio (OR), 2.09; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-3.93; P = 0.015], nonexudative tonsillitis (OR, 2.78; 95% CI: 1.72-4.59; P < 0.001) and rales (OR, 1.82; 95% CI: 1.15-2.86; P = 0.01) to be positively associated with antibiotic overuse, while age showed a negative association in complete-case analysis (OR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.85-0.99; P = 0.038), which attenuated and was no longer significant in a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis (OR, 0.96; 95% CI: 0.91-1.01; P = 0.150). Diagnostic uncertainty contributes to antibiotic overuse, alongside clinical factors. Future studies should investigate the impact of improved diagnostic algorithms on antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections in whom physicians experience diagnostic uncertainty.

items.title: Prognostic Value and Clinical Outcomes of Spread through Air Spaces in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study in Türkiye.
items.abstract: Spread through air spaces (STAS), first described in lung adenocarcinomas in 2013, has been identified as a prognostic factor in numerous studies. We investigated the prognostic effect of STAS positivity and its potential role in staging and treatment strategies. We retrospectively reviewed prospectively collected data from patients who underwent surgery at our hospital and were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma between 2018 and 2021. Patients were classified into 2 groups, STAS-negative and STAS-positive. Overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) were compared between the groups. Of the 480 patients, 123 (25.6%) were STAS-positive. STAS positivity was associated with significantly worse survival outcomes in early-stage disease, although this association diminished in stage III. Mean DFS was 50.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 47.7-52.4) in the STAS-negative group and 35.1 months (95% CI, 31.2-39.1) in the STAS-positive group (p<0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, STAS positivity was an independent adverse prognostic factor for both OS and DFS, with hazard ratios of 1.574 and 2.345, respectively. Analyses stratified by stage showed that the prognostic impact of STAS positivity was strongest in stage I disease, in which it was associated with worse OS, DFS, and LRFS; formal interaction testing supported this finding. In early-stage disease, STAS is a significant adverse prognostic factor. This finding suggests that early-stage STAS-positive tumors may warrant upstaging in future staging systems and that STAS status may help individualize surgical and follow-up strategies.

items.title: Timing of Long COVID Improvement in Prospectively Followed RECOVER-Adult Participants.
items.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. National Institutes of Health.

items.title: Burden of newly diagnosed hypertension and potential 10-year cardiovascular risk in Burundi: A Bayesian logistic regression and Framingham score-based study
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Arterial hypertension is a major global public health concern. In Burundi, it coexists with other non-communicable and communicable diseases, contributing to a complex and evolving health burden that poses substantial challenges for prevention, diagnosis, and management. We aimed to assess the burden of newly diagnosed hypertension, identify associated risk factors, and assess 10-year cardiovascular risk among hypertensive and non-hypertensive patients. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 714 patients admitted to Kamenge Teaching Hospital between January 2018 and January 2023. Retrospective data were extracted from medical records. Bayesian belief updating was used to estimate the prevalence of newly diagnosed hypertension, while Bayesian logistic regression with bootstrapping was used to identify associated risk factors. Bayesian linear models were used to assess the association between diastolic blood pressure and cardiovascular risk level. Potential 10-year cardiovascular risk was estimated using the Canadian Framingham Risk Score. Results The prevalence of newly diagnosed hypertension was 16.9% (95% CrI: 14.2–19.7%). Higher prevalence was observed among women (18.0%), patients aged 40–59 years (21.3%) and ≥ 60 years (33.9%), those with higher educational attainment (up to 28.9%), and individuals who were overweight or obese or had a family history of hypertension. Predictors of hypertension included age ≥ 40 years, tobacco use, education level, and excess weight. Moderate or severe 10-year cardiovascular risk was present in 24.9% of patients, with more than 60% of patients with hypertension classified as high risk. Diastolic blood pressure was positively associated with cardiovascular risk among both hypertensive and non-hypertensive patients. Conclusion Newly diagnosed hypertension and its association with elevated cardiovascular risk highlight potential missed opportunities for early diagnosis and prevention. Targeted screening and management of modifiable risk factors may help reduce cardiovascular risk in Burundi.

items.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
items.abstract: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.abstract: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. Realizing it calls for a new kind of system, a cognitive symbiont: a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive companion that senses what the person senses through external devices, keeps their context across years, models their situation and their mind, takes part in their thinking at the right moment, carries out everyday tasks with their context, and keeps learning the person as both change. We give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory, and organize its design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing, enclosed by a personal runtime and by trust. Because a symbiont changes what a person can do in front of others, it also raises risks of a new kind, from covert assistance in examinations to pressure on everyone to adopt it, and we treat their governance as part of the paradigm.

items.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
items.abstract: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator. On AlpacaEval 2.0 with GPT-4o as judge, three iterations raise the length-controlled (LC) win rate against GPT-4o from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral, and the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct on every reported win rate. With same-family open-weight annotators, the runs retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of the LC gain achieved with GPT-4o as annotator, so the rating step does not require a proprietary model. In a separate ablation configuration, variants that remove the gold responses, remove the data look-back, or accept only teacher-preferred pairs score 6 to 10 LC points below the full procedure, whereas varying the number of on-policy samples per prompt (1 to 7) moves the LC win rate by at most 2.1 points, and a margin sweep (1 to 5) run in its own pipeline by at most 2.4 points. We also report the cost of the pipeline and where the practical algorithm departs from the theory it approximates. All results are single runs, and GPT-4o is both the teacher and the evaluation judge; we discuss what this implies for the reported gains.

items.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
items.abstract: Undesired model behaviors can emerge or re-emerge at any stage of training. Once observed, how effectively can we suppress them? To study this question, we first construct two model organisms--language models deliberately trained to exhibit a specific misalignment--that differ in what triggers the behavior. The narrow-trigger organism misbehaves only when the prompt contains a specific cue: it cheats on multiple-choice questions by following a planted hint that points to a wrong answer, and behaves normally otherwise. The broad-trigger organism has no such cue: after fine-tuning on insecure code, it gives harmful responses across a wide range of open-ended prompts. We then formalize post-hoc behavioral suppression and evaluate methods along three criteria: immediate suppression of the target behavior, durability under further training, and preservation of general capability. We compare standard methods--SFT, GRPO, and gradient-ascent unlearning--along these dimensions. Building on prior work on alignment shallowness, we hypothesize that more durable suppression requires the ability to recover from a wider range of misalignment states. We introduce Prefix-Expanded Adversarial Reinforcement Learning (PEARL), a GRPO variant that augments rollouts with continuations from intermediate states sampled along cached organism trajectories. Across both organism settings and two model families (Qwen3-4B, GPT-OSS-20B), PEARL achieves strong immediate suppression while preserving task accuracy, and remains durable under further fine-tuning on either the organism's data or unrelated data. It obtains the greatest benefit when the undesirable behavior is broad and cannot be addressed through targeted SFT. Together, our framework and method offer a step toward more durable post-hoc removal of undesired behaviors.

items.title: Whose Guardrail? User Identity Shapes the Effectiveness of Model Disclaimers in Mitigating LLM Political Persuasion
items.abstract: Politically biased AI can shift users' opinions, yet it remains unclear whether model disclaimers protect against such persuasion. We report a preregistered experiment (N=1,586) examining how disclaimer design and user characteristics shape susceptibility to politically biased AI. We varied whether disclaimers identified political bias versus potential inaccuracies and whether they included an explanation. Participants completed two decision-making tasks with an LLM biased against their political views, with outcomes assessed immediately and one week later. Disclaimers identifying political bias and including an explanation reduced persuasion, but effects varied across contexts and did not persist. Individual differences were more consistent predictors: Republicans were more persuaded and reported higher trust than Democrats across tasks. Similarly, participants who used AI more frequently were also more persuaded, whereas those with greater self-reported AI knowledge were less persuaded. These findings suggest that generic disclaimers are not enough: effective safeguards must account for user heterogeneity and context.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.abstract: Speculative decoding has been treated purely as a systems optimization that speeds up large language model decoding without changing the model behavior. Under this view, the growing effort to train better draft models has been focused solely on acceptance rate. We argue that this view does not hold true for long-horizon agent reasoning. Measuring frontier open-weight models on complex agentic tasks with different speculative decoding approaches, we found that numerical noise grows within verification windows, and the draft acceptance results of the thinking process can change the output distribution of the model after 30 steps, thus noticeably influencing the reasoning accuracy of long-horizon agents in random directions. In this work, we improve the reasoning capability of target models by controlling such noise. While we cannot change the overall token distribution verified by the target model, we can encode critical reasoning with highest precision by training the draft model to be rejected. We identify these points in agent traces and train the draft model to favor adversarial preference. At inference the trained draft and the target part ways precisely at these decision points, verification restarts, so that critical thinking tokens are sampled from the target model and encoded under its least noisy conditions. This approach makes critical reasoning better indexed and more durable over a long horizon. On complex agentic coding benchmarks, our approach raises end-to-end success rate with no change to the target model or its output distribution. Our results recast the speculative decoding mechanism from a pure accelerator into an active allocator for context precision that improves the accuracy of long-horizon agents by training 0.06% to 0.28% of hosted parameters.

items.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
items.abstract: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data. Frontier language models have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of small neural networks, an ability called weight-space programming. The purpose of this study was to determine whether such a model, given only a clinical protocol and a network's weights, can audit and repair the network. Networks with 433 to 4,801 parameters were trained to screen head-and-neck planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through the training data: confounds that hid each rule, a 3 Gy shift in the cord threshold, and a hidden trigger. Claude Opus 5.5 audited each network blind, without tools, data or code execution, and every claim and repair was tested on about 420,000 requests. The language model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks (95% CI 67% to 97%), including all 15 with a confound or a threshold shift. It repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters. Fine-tuning on protocol-labeled requests also repaired every network, but changed nearly every parameter. Each confound and shift it found was visible in single units, and a simple statistic chosen for each flaw type found the same flaws. It cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks without being forced and found 1 of 3 triggers. Testing against the protocol detected every flaw, and black-box testing found the confounds and the shift faster. The results indicate that, in small networks, weight-space programming can locate and repair flaws that silence an input or shift a threshold, but cannot yet certify that a network is correct.

items.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
items.abstract: Medical physicists turn a prescription into a delivered dose and check one another's calculations, because one error in a beam calibration or a monitor-unit (MU) calculation can affect every patient treated with it. MedPhysBench has ten seeded generators of calculation items in radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection, up to clinical tasks such as a TG-51 calibration worksheet. Reference answers come from code implementing the governing protocols, and a grader converts units and applies tolerance bands. From the same inputs, separate checking items test error detection, showing a colleague's worksheet or only the colleague's result, half correct and half with one planted error. On a held-out test split of 1,200 items (half for two models), 12 models scored 33.3 to 100.0% on calculation. Of the nine answers graded incorrect for the four best (99.3-100.0%), five contained model errors and four followed NCRP Report 151 on points our items misstate or leave open. Below them, most models did worst on level-3 clinical tasks, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 omitted the inverse-square correction in 19 of 20 isocentric MU items. Five models detected at least 96.7% of mostly large planted errors with at most 4% false alarms; for four of the other seven, checking only the result raised false alarms significantly. In an exploratory targeted test with 20 public cases of an omitted inverse-square correction, the three best models tested caught it in every worksheet, and three weaker models accepted 16 to 18 of 20 planted worksheets, one of them while applying the correction in most of its own calculations. Claude Opus 5.5 accepted 6 of 20 wrong results, although it applied the correction in all 20 of its own. We report the effect of two problems in our shielding items, found after the runs, and release the code, per-item outcomes and targeted-test responses.

items.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
items.abstract: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging ($\text{A}^2$ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on $p$-norm geometry for $p\in[2,\infty]$. The method is line-search-free and employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is simple and unified across $p\in[2,\infty]$, with the case $p>2$ requiring no more elaborate updates than the Euclidean case $p=2$. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, we derive a convergence bound that separates the effects of constant and gap-dependent curvature, with the latter potentially yielding faster-decaying terms. In the special case of local smoothness, this bound recovers a nearly optimal convergence rate.

items.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
items.abstract: Teleoperation remains the default way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs robot and operator time, and every new task starts from scratch. We ask whether a coding agent can take over the teleoperator's job. In our DataFarm, the agent receives a data request and one calibration episode of the robot in the target scene and rebuilds the task in simulation: it writes the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. The simulator supplies exact actions, and a video model conditioned on real images renders each rollout as photographic video, generating all camera views together consistently. The output is real-ready data: synchronized camera views labelled with the robot's actions, on which a policy can be trained directly and deployed on the real robot. Independent judges certify the expert and every rendered episode before admission. On five real-robot tasks, policies trained only on farm data match policies trained on as many teleoperated episodes (93 vs. 84 successes in 100 trials), and under an unseen tablecloth and coloured light they keep 87 successes where the teleoperation-trained policies fall to 46. Adapting a task is fully automatic and costs \$21 of API usage on average, paid once per task, plus \$5 for a render contract; every further episode costs \$0.80 on average for simulation, rendering, and review, with no robot or operator. One hour of three-view data for a task costs \$107 on average, these costs included, slightly below a quote of \$117 for teleoperation in China and below \$290 in labour alone in North America.

items.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.abstract: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the collaborative graph, UNDERSTAND the other side, and SYNC it from the next interaction. This formulation reveals three unresolved communication challenges: the item side never produces a comparable self-description (one-sided BUILD); profile-level signals enter only the bandwidth-limited reranker prompt rather than retrieval, where they would not compete for context tokens (prompt-trapped UNDERSTAND); and the user's description is frozen after warmup with no principled update rule (absent SYNC). We instantiate the missing stages as HARP (Homophily-aware Agentic Recommendation via dual Profiles), a training-free, three-operator addition to a frozen LLM backbone: a rule-extracted symmetric item profile (zero extra LLM calls), a channel-decomposable profile-level homophily H(phi_u, phi_i) consumed at retrieval time rather than inside the reranker prompt, and a single-pass reflective update realising in-context profile evolution without any gradient step. On four public benchmarks (Yelp, Books, MovieTV, Goodreads), HARP lifts Hit@1 over the strongest published baseline by 6.9%-24.0%, with family-wise Holm-corrected p < 1e-9 on every dataset. Ablations and a per-case attribution study show that the operators contribute complementary gains, with the retrieval-side gate as the main source; we also report the trade-off introduced by the reflective pass. We formulate agentic communication and provide a training-free instantiation. Code is available at https://github.com/Jove-Zhen/HARP.

items.title: You don't need long context
items.abstract: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.

items.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
items.abstract: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. We observe that the KV cache of looped models is highly redundant along the loop axis and that the loop steps differ substantially in their sensitivity to quantization. Based on these observations, we propose $\textbf{LoopVQ}$, a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that codes channels of multiple loop steps jointly, and fine-tunes the codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model. At 0.5 bits per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods for standard LLMs on general, long chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval tasks with Ouro and Huginn models. Its design is orthogonal to these methods, and combined with TaSQ, it retains much of the BF16 accuracy even at 0.25 bits per element. We also implement LoopVQ in SGLang, where it nearly halves the decode latency at a 32K-token context and raises the peak serving throughput by up to $4.3\times$ and $6.1\times$ on the 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro models compared to the BF16 baseline.

items.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
items.abstract: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems. Each simulated person is defined by a persona, a written profile of fixed traits, demographics, and attitudes that a language model is instructed to act out. Every such system assumes that a person's identity is a stable attribute that behaves the same way in every situation the simulation presents. We show that this assumption is not a harmless simplification. Three decades of personality research find the opposite. How a given person behaves varies more across contexts than people vary from one another. Drawing on identity economics, which describes how different situations activate different identities and norms within the same person, we separate behavior into three parts, which are stable traits, the identity a context calls up, and the situation itself. We then prove, under two stated assumptions, that any simulation built on fixed personas, no matter how detailed the personas or how large the underlying model, cannot reproduce the part of a population's behavior that is specific to it and its circumstances. We propose a new evaluation criterion based on this result and a person-in-context design that can meet it in principle. We test one version on a naturalistic Reddit personality corpus and on a published clinical-trial recruitment survey of a community with documented distrust of medical institutions. The design does produce context-dependent behavior when tested directly, but in neither setting does it fully match the real population, and we show where it falls short. The consequence for practice is a risk that synthetic-population evaluations misrepresent the groups whose behavior is most shaped by context, a distortion that richer personas cannot correct.

items.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
items.abstract: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) alerts (69 alert cases, 32 no-alert controls, 16 non-U.S. locations) through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline that differ in alert access and prompt design. One rater hand-labeled all 342 alert-case responses under a seven-category scheme written after an initial binary pass, which we disclose. False reassurance was 0.0% for the production pipeline (0/66, 95% CI 0.0-5.5) and for the same alerts under a neutral prompt (0/69), 37.7% for a blind neutral prompt (26/69), and 44.9% when the blind prompt also told the model to disclose its blind spot (31/69). Every case was implicit; no response explicitly denied an alert. Real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001); the disclosure instruction did not (p = 0.40). An automated regex measure suggested the opposite and missed 53 of 57 true cases, so we do not use it. Alert data alone was not enough for safe behavior: with a neutral prompt the model raised some alarm on 87.5% of no-alert controls, against 0% under the production prompt, and a preregistered single-sentence ablation showed that one production instruction explains part of that gap. We also report two failures common to similar systems, NWS test products ingested as real alerts and a token budget that fails on complex cases, and we release the dataset, labels and code.
