items.title: Challenges and possibilities in providing care to women in psychotherapies influenced by Behavior Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Given the growing literature on psychotherapy models adapted for women, integrating these discussions and findings is timely. This study aims to examine the limitations of psychotherapy for women and propose practices to address these challenges through a literature review from the perspective of Behavior Analysis-based psychotherapies. We searched the CAPES Periodicals and PsycNet databases using keywords relevant to the study's objective. The search identified 2,628 items; after screening, 11 were selected for analysis. The results indicate steady growth, with a slight acceleration after 2017. Two broad analytical categories were established: (1) “Challenges in psychotherapeutic care for women” and (2) “Possibilities and suggestions for psychotherapeutic care for women.” The first category comprised the following subcategories: (a) Challenges related to the therapeutic relationship and skills; (b) Challenges in skill acquisition and application; and (c) Contextual and structural barriers to psychotherapy. In the second category, the subcategories analyzed were: (a) Possibilities related to the therapeutic relationship and skills; (b) Incorporation of social, cultural, and biological dimensions; (c) Possibilities for psychotherapeutic interventions; (d) Skill development within the psychotherapeutic context; and (e) Benefits of psychotherapeutic interventions. The findings reinforce the need for a Behavior Analysis-based psychotherapeutic practice sensitive to sociopolitical and cultural contingencies; however, further research is needed to evaluate the efficacy of behavior-analytic interventions adapted for diverse groups of women. Furthermore, it is important to reinforce the idea of integrating a feminist perspective into Behavior Analysis; while challenging, this is essential for building a fairer and more equitable psychology.

items.title: Association between tooth wear severity and oral health-related quality of life in Mexican adults attending university dental clinics.
items.abstract: To evaluate the association between tooth wear severity and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) in Mexican adults attending university dental clinics. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 338 adults aged ≥35 years treated at eight peripheral dental clinics of the Faculty of Higher Studies Iztacala, National Autonomous University of Mexico. OHRQoL was assessed using the OHIP-Mx-49, and tooth wear severity using an adapted approach based on the Smith and Knight Tooth Wear Index (TWI). Caries experience, malocclusion, temporomandibular disorders, periodontal disease, and dentin hypersensitivity were also assessed. Bivariate analysis used nonparametric tests and multivariate analysis used negative binomial regression. Mean age was 50.35 ± 10.8 years; 66.9% were female. Tooth wear was mild in 26.9%, moderate in 55.0%, and severe in 18.1%. Mean OHIP-Mx-49 score was 46.70 ± 32.99. In adjusted analysis, moderate (RR = 0.96; 95% CI: 0.82-1.12) and severe (RR = 0.91; 95% CI: 0.73-1.13) tooth wear were not significantly associated with OHIP-Mx-49 scores. Caries experience, temporomandibular disorders, and dentin hypersensitivity were independently associated with impaired OHRQoL. Tooth wear severity was not statistically significantly associated with OHRQoL after adjustment for clinical and sociodemographic factors. As all participants had tooth wear, findings concern differences in severity within this sample and do not permit comparisons with adults without tooth wear.

items.title: High rates of obesity and excessive catch-up growth in children with perinatal HIV exposure in the United States.
items.abstract: Background Preterm birth (PTB) and small-for-gestational age (SGA) often occur in infants born to women with HIV and may influence growth among children perinatally HIV- exposed but uninfected (CHEU). Setting U.S. cohort at 22 sites. Methods CHEU were enrolled at birth into the SMARTT Dynamic cohort of the Pediatric HIV/AIDS Cohort Study network and followed through age 17 years. We calculated Z scores for singleton CHEU through age 7 years for weight (WAZ), length or height (LAZ/HAZ), and weight-for-length/body mass index (WFL/BMI)]; excessive catch-up growth was defined as WAZ increase >0.67 SD from birth to age 2 years. Birth weight-for-gestational age (GA) was categorized as small- (SGA), appropriate- (AGA), and large-for-GA (LGA). Piecewise linear regression models with slope changes were used to assess growth trajectories by SGA and PTB. Results Among 2,765 CHEU born 2007-2022, 9.2% were SGA, 14.4% preterm, and 47% had excessive catch-up growth. Among term infants, those born SGA had the highest percent (65%) with excessive catch-up growth. Those born SGA had lower mean WAZ and WLZ/BMIZ than AGA through age 7 years. Infants with PTB had higher mean WAZ, LAZ/HAZ, and WLZ/BMIZ at birth than term infants, but were similar by age 7 years. Conclusions A high proportion of CHEU had excessive catch-up growth and obesity at age 5 years. While SGA infants had persistently lower Z-scores than AGA, obesity rates at age 5 years were comparable. These findings represent a paradigm shift from undernutrition to overnutrition, particularly in countries where obesity prevalence is high.

items.title: Timing of antiretroviral treatment initiation and seropositivity to measles virus among children living with HIV in rural Zambia.
items.abstract: Background Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) reduces morbidity among children living with HIV (CHIV) but does not restore vaccine-induced measles immunity. Many CHIV now initiate cART before measles vaccination but the impact on measles seroprevalence is not understood. This study compared measles seropositivty between CHIV initiating cART before and after 9 months in Zambia. Methods This retrospective study was nested within a cohort study of CHIV and community-based studies in Macha, Zambia conducted from 2007-2020. Samples were tested for measles IgG antibodies by enzyme immunoassay from CHIV initiating cART at ages 0-8, 9-23, and 24-59 months and age-matched community-based controls. A cross-sectional analysis compared measles seroprevalence between CHIV groups after 6-12 months of cART and controls. A longitudinal analysis evaluated antibody concentrations from age 9 months through 48 months of cART and during the 2010-11 measles outbreak. Results In the cross-sectional analysis, measles seropositivity did not statistically differ after 6-12 months of cART by age at initiation (0-8: 30.8% [n=12/39]; 9-23: 37.0% [n=51/138]; 24-59 months: 26.6% [n=33/124]). Within CHIV groups, seropositivity was significantly lower than age-matched controls (63.5%, 75.7%, and 80.3%). Among 242 CHIV followed longitudinally, 46-56% had an antibody response, with estimated seroreversion in only 1.8-3.2 years. Among CHIV in 2010-11, 50% seroconverted or boosted with estimated seroreversion in 2.1 years. Conclusions Measles seroprevalence was low among CHIV, even when starting cART before 9 months of age, and the time to seroreversion was short. These findings support recommendations that CHIV, including infants, would benefit from periodic revaccination after immune reconstitution.

items.title: Patient Experiences Questionnaire for Out-of-Hours Care (PEQ-OHC) and EQ-5D-5L: reliability and validity following a national survey.
items.abstract: Background The Patient Experiences Questionnaire for Out-of-Hours Care (PEQ-OHC) is used in local and national surveys of primary care but has not been evaluated for measurement properties since 2010. This study assessed aspects of validity, reliability, and internal consistency alongside the EQ-5D-5L. Methods The PEQ-OHC and EQ-5D-5L were part of an electronic survey of 1,765 OHC patients recruited nationally across Norway 4-8 weeks following care. At 7-12 days, respondents received a retest questionnaire. Testing followed the COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement INstruments (COSMIN) checklist for patient-reported instruments. Results The 509 (29%) respondents had a median (IQR) age of 55 (38-66) years and 54% were female. Confirmatory factor analysis showed evidence for structural validity including PEQ-OHC scales of doctor contact, nurse contact, organisation and telephone contact (Comparative Fit/Tuckey Lewis Index = 0.97, Standardised Root Mean Residuals = 0.05). Together with a new scale of video contact, Cronbach's alpha ranged from 0.79-0.98; only organisation fell below 0.90. Test-retest weighted kappa was generally of a high to excellent level for PEQ-OHC items (0.59-0.86) and EQ-5D dimensions (0.76-0.85). Intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.74-0.83 for PEQ-OHC scale scores; EQ-5D-5L index = 0.91, EQ VAS = 0.81. Over 75% of results followed hypotheses, in comparisons of instrument scores with variables relating to experiences, health and services use. Conclusion Evidence for reliability and validity further supports application of the PEQ-OHC in national and local quality measurement. The EQ-5D-5L also performed well and can be used alongside the PEQ-OHC to assess and adjust for case-mix across OHC centres.

items.title: Type I IFN autoantibodies in three of seven Europeans with life-threatening Usutu virus infection.
items.abstract: We previously reported that two of three patients with severe Usutu virus (USUV) disease carried circulating autoantibodies (auto-Abs) neutralizing type I IFNs (AAN-I-IFN). Here, we studied four additional patients, bringing the total number of European patients with life-threatening USUV infection to seven (Austria, n = 1; France, n = 1; Hungary, n = 4; Italy, n = 1). Three of these patients (all male, aged 43, 77, and 78 years, one French and two Hungarian) had blood auto-Abs neutralizing at least 10 ng/ml IFN-α2 and IFN-ω and at least 1 ng/ml IFN-β. They suffered from meningitis (n = 1), meningoencephalitis (n = 1), or myocarditis (n = 1). The other four patients were similar demographically and clinically but had no detectable AAN-I-IFN. No AAN-I-IFN were found in the 63 individuals with silent USUV infection tested (P = 6.4 × 10-4, Fisher's exact test). These AAN-I-IFN increased the risk of life-threatening USUV disease by 98.8-fold (95% CI: 4.12-2,369; P = 0.0046, Firth's bias-corrected logistic regression) and, thus, account for almost half the cases of life-threatening USUV infection in Europe.

items.title: Structure of MPXV DNA ligase complex reveals a virus-specific pocket for selective inhibition.
items.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), remains a public health concern, yet the structural basis of poxvirus DNA ligase function has been poorly defined despite strong genetic and biochemical evidence supporting its essential role in viral DNA replication and repair. Here, we report the crystal structure of MPXV DNA ligase (MpxvLig) in complex with nicked DNA at 2.04 Å resolution. MpxvLig adopts the canonical three-domain architecture of ATP-dependent DNA ligases, comprising an N-terminal DNA-binding domain (DBD), a nucleotidyltransferase domain, and a C-terminal oligonucleotide-binding fold domain (OBD), which together form a clamp-like configuration that embraces nicked DNA for catalysis. The structure captures MpxvLig in an active catalytic state corresponding to the adenylylation step, in which Lys233 forms a covalent ligase-AMP intermediate. Comparative structural and biochemical analyses with the catalytic core of human DNA ligase III reveal substantial differences in domain arrangement and DNA engagement, consistent with the stronger DNA-binding capacity and higher ligation activity of MpxvLig in vitro . Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) further shows that apo-MpxvLig adopts an extended flashlight-like conformation in solution. Notably, we identify a virus-specific small-molecule-binding pocket within the DNA-binding domain. Mitoxantrone binds directly to this pocket and inhibits MpxvLig activity at micromolar concentrations, while exerting minimal effects on the human ligase. Mutations in pocket-defining residues markedly attenuate this inhibition, supporting an on-target mechanism. Together, these findings establish the structural basis of poxvirus DNA ligation and provide a framework for the rational development of selective antiviral inhibitors targeting MpxvLig.

items.title: Temporal Trends and Associations of Antimicrobial Use and Resistance in Enterococcus Species From Broiler Farms in Canada.
items.abstract: Introduction Antimicrobials are widely used in animal production for the treatment, prevention, and control of infectious diseases. However, antimicrobial use (AMU) is also a key driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In response, the Canadian poultry sector implemented a phased three-step AMU reduction strategy to mitigate the emergence and spread of AMR. Enterococci are ubiquitous inhabitants of the gastrointestinal tract of animals and serve as important sentinel organisms for AMR surveillance because of their capacity to acquire AMR. Methods This study investigated associations between farm management practices, including AMU, and AMR in enterococci isolated from broiler chickens. Farm management data were collected using standardized questionnaires, and faecal samples were obtained during farm visits. Phenotypic AMR profiles were determined by minimum inhibitory concentration testing of 623 isolates from 419 flocks across five Canadian provinces over a 4-year period. Generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate associations between AMR and other factors, including AMU, province, year, breed, stocking density, downtime between flocks, and sanitation practices. Results Avilamycin use was significantly associated with avilamycin resistance in both E. faecalis and E. faecium. Provincial and temporal differences in resistance were observed for certain antimicrobials, with a notable decline in resistant isolates to Veterinary Drugs Directorate's Category II and III antimicrobials following implementation of the three-step AMU reduction strategy. Conclusions These findings suggest that targeted AMU reduction strategies were associated with reducing AMR percentages in enterococci from Canadian broilers.

items.title: The scientific development of Environment and Climate Change Canada's new ventilation index.
items.abstract: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has updated its ventilation forecast guidance through the development of a new ventilation index. This index was created using output from a Lagrangian stochastic model (LSM), with ventilation defined as inversely proportional to modeled ground-level concentrations from a surface-layer point source. The index is calibrated to the LSM output via parameterizations involving 10-m wind speeds, friction velocity, and Richardson number (Ri). The resulting Calibrated Ventilation Index (CVI) ranges from 0 (worst) to 100 (best), where a ±33-unit change corresponds to a doubling or halving of ventilation. Testing and development spanned a wide range of atmospheric stabilities, wind speeds, and land-use classes, guided by LSMs utilizing diverse parameterizations of surface layer turbulence, idealized and NWP-based meteorological fields, as well as output from a Gaussian plume model. The CVI shows a strong dependence on Ri within the -0.1 0.25) conditions. A qualitative evaluation in the Province of Quebec during one winter (December 2020 through March 2021) compared hindcast CVI values on evenings with and without ECCC air quality advisories. The CVI successfully resolved subtle ventilation differences under highly stable conditions (coefficient of variation of CV=1.51), whereas ECCC's legacy index lacked sensitivity-compressing its hindcasts against its lower bound (CV=0.56). The CVI is intended for local surface-layer dispersion guidance, not elevated stacks or open burning with high vertical momentum. ECCC uses the CVI to produce 48-hour forecasts across Canada four times daily at 2.5-km spatial and hourly temporal resolution. Implications : Environment and Climate Change Canada has developed a new Calibrated Ventilation Index (CVI) with the goal of protecting public health through improved guidance around the impacts of open air biomass burning activities. Index development was based on Lagrangian stochastic modeling and offers a scientifically robust and calibrated tool for forecasting surface-level atmospheric ventilation. Its implementation will enable more reliable guidance for open-air burning and other near-surface activities involving atmospheric dispersion. ECCC's CVI forecasts are now operational with guidance provided at high spatial and temporal resolution across much of Canada.

items.title: WLS protein is highly expressed in glioma: A biomarker for grading and prognosis.
items.abstract: We investigated the expression level, clinicopathological significance, and mechanistic function of Wnt ligand secretion mediator (WLS) in glioma. WLS expression in glioma was evaluated using public data from GEPIA (gene expression profiling interactive analysis) and immunohistochemistry. siRNA-mediated knockdown was performed in LN229 and U-87MG ATCC (glioblastoma of unknown origin) cells to assess its functional effects. Survival analysis was conducted based on the Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA) database. Protein-protein interaction networks were constructed using the STRING database and downstream Wnt signaling events were experimentally validated. Both mRNA and protein levels of WLS were significantly elevated in glioma tissues relative to adjacent non-tumor brain tissues. Elevated WLS expression correlated positively with higher World Health Organization (WHO) tumor grade and negatively with IDH1/2 mutations but not with sex, age, or 1p/19q codeletion. Knockdown of WLS suppressed glioma cell proliferation and invasion and promoted apoptosis. Mechanistically, silencing WLS led to the downregulation of canonical Wnt/β-catenin target genes suggesting that WLS contributes to Wnt pathway activation in glioma. Importantly, high WLS expression was significantly associated with poorer overall survival. The association between high WLS expression, advanced WHO grade, and poorer prognosis implies its potential utility as a biomarker in glioma patients.

items.title: Managing equine asthma: Owner adherence, practical constraints and environmental protocol evaluation.
items.abstract: Background Adherence to recommendations for environmental management is central to equine asthma (EA) treatment. Reasons for non-adherence warrant further investigation. Objectives To: (1) evaluate adherence to recommendations for environmental changes, identify reasons for incomplete implementation, assess changes in clinical signs and medication use; (2) evaluate owner acceptability, practicality and perceived usefulness of a structured stable-side protocol. Study design (1) Retrospective online survey and (2) prospective onsite testing with owners of EA-affected horses. Methods (1) Online survey on implementation of standardised recommendations, clinical progression and medication use; and (2) environmental protocol evaluation during stable visits. Results Seventeen of 40 horses still received dry hay and 13/40 were bedded on straw. Reasons for non-implementation included time, financial and infrastructural constraints, boarding stable restrictions, group housing, weather dependence, use of self-produced roughage, perceived ineffectiveness and individual horse preferences. Owners reported that overall clinical impression had improved and the proportion of coughing horses decreased from 88% to 55% (p Main limitations Use of small convenience samples, lack of a control group and potential selection and recall bias. Conclusion Owner non-adherence arose from diverse and often structural constraints. The environmental protocol was well accepted by owners and helped to structure discussions on risk factors.

items.title: Cryptosporidium Infection Is Associated with Gut Microbiome Alterations in Bangladeshi Children and Families.
items.abstract: Background Cryptosporidium spp. are enteric protozoa associated with moderate-to-severe diarrhea and impaired growth in children worldwide. However, the relationship between Cryptosporidium infection and gut microbiome remains poorly understood. Methods We investigated gut microbiota dynamics associated with Cryptosporidium infection in a longitudinal cohort of 84 children and family members in Bangladesh. Fecal samples (n=233) were collected pre-infection, during infection, and post-infection. Microbial profiling was performed using 16S rRNA sequencing, with taxonomic classification and abundance estimation conducted via Cosmos ID-HUB. Associations between infection status, microbial diversity, and taxa abundance were evaluated using multivariable models adjusting for age and sex. Results Most Cryptosporidium infections were subclinical (96.1%), with 3.86% presenting diarrhea. In individuals ≥ 3 years of age, gut microbial α-diversity decreased during infection (p-value range = 0.01-3.68x10-10) and increased following recovery (p-value range = 0.0017- 0.0019). During infection, Roseburia and Megaspheara were reduced relative to both pre- (q-value = 0.011 and 0.02) and post-infection (q-value =2.34 x10-5 and 0.001). In addition, Prevotella (q-value = 0.03) and Leuconostoc (q-value=0.04) were reduced relative to pre-infection. Shigella abundance increased during infection (q-value =3.4x10-5) and persisted post-infection (q-value=9.0x10-6). In children ≤ 3 years of age, α-diversity increased during infection compared to pre-infection (p-value=0.045). α-diversity and β-diversity during the post-infection period were associated with lower weight for age z scores. Conclusions Cryptosporidium infection is associated with dynamic and persistent alterations in the gut microbiome, even in the absence of diarrhea, which may be related to impaired child growth, and deserve deeper analysis as promising potential targets for microbiota-mediated interventions.

items.title: DectiSomes as broad-spectrum antifungal drugs.
items.abstract: SUMMARYFungal pathogens represent a significant threat to public health. Aspergillus fumigatus , Candida albicans , Cryptococcus neoformans , and Rhizopus delemar are the primary causative agents for aspergillosis, candidiasis, cryptococcosis, and mucormycosis. They and their closest relatives are responsible for more than 94% of fungal disease-related deaths. All four fungal diseases may lead to meningitis, with mortality rates approaching 99%. They are among the WHO-designated priority fungal pathogens needing new and more effective treatments. In response to this therapeutic gap, we developed DectiSomes-drug-loaded liposomes targeted to fungal cells by host-pathogen receptors. Host-pathogen receptors have many advantages over antibodies as liposome-targeting proteins, including a lack of immunogenicity. Of the pathogen receptors we tested, Dectin-1 and Dectin-2 are the most effective targeting proteins against the fungal pathogens tested. Liposomes loaded with amphotericin B and coated with one of these pathogen receptors bind specifically and strongly to the four pathogens and kill them, reducing the effective dose of amphotericin B by more than an order of magnitude over the untargeted control. DectiSomes are also more effective in murine models of fungal infection. Furthermore, we developed small, malleable versions of DectiSomes with improved drug delivery to the brain and are more effective against cryptococcal meningitis, holding promise for treating all forms of fungal meningitis. Herein, we review our progress and discuss the potential of DectiSomes as a new and effective targeted delivery system for antifungal drugs. In addition, we discuss the challenges associated with fungal diseases and the roadblocks to antifungal drug development and medical mycology research.

items.title: Atp12 regulates mitochondrial fusion and chronological aging through Fzo1 in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
items.abstract: Atp12 is known as a chaperone for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly, yet its functions and mechanisms in regulating mitochondrial and cellular aging remain elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that Atp12 plays a critical role in regulating mitochondrial dynamics and chronological lifespan (CLS) in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe . We found that Atp12 localizes to mitochondria, and its deletion leads to severe mitochondrial fragmentation, reduced complex II activity, dissipation of mitochondrial membrane potential, and a marked shortening of CLS. Mechanistically, Atp12 acts partially independently of ATP synthase, as the Δ atp12 Δ atp1 double mutant exhibited more severe defects in mitochondrial function and viability than either single mutant, and its mitochondrial morphology resembled that of Δ atp12 rather than Δ atp1 . Transcriptomic and phenotypic analyses identified Fzo1, a mitofusin essential for mitochondrial fusion, as a key downstream target of Atp12 in regulating cellular aging. Further analysis revealed that Atp12 physically interacts with Fzo1 and stabilizes its protein levels. Genetic epistasis experiments demonstrated that Fzo1 insufficiency largely accounts for the mitochondrial fragmentation and functional decline observed in Δ atp12 cells, as Fzo1 overexpression effectively rescues these defects. Collectively, these findings uncover a novel function of Atp12 in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and delaying cellular aging by stabilizing the mitochondrial fusion machinery. Given the evolutionary conservation of Atp12 from yeast to humans, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how the coordination of mitochondrial biogenesis and dynamics drives the aging process.IMPORTANCEMitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of cellular aging, but how mitochondria are regulated at the molecular level to influence cellular longevity remains elusive. Here, we reveal that Atp12, a conserved chaperone for ATP synthase assembly, also serves as a stabilizer of the mitofusin Fzo1 to preserve mitochondrial fusion and chronological lifespan in fission yeast. Through direct physical interaction, Atp12 sustains Fzo1 protein levels, thereby maintaining mitochondrial morphology, respiratory function, and cell survival, a function that is largely independent of its canonical role in ATP synthase. This discovery uncovers an unexpected link between a mitochondrial assembly factor and organellar dynamics, establishing the Atp12-Fzo1 axis as a conserved regulatory node that couples mitochondrial quality control to the aging process.

items.title: Epithelial responses to pneumococcal capsules drive leukocyte activation and functionality in a serotype-specific manner.
items.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) poses a major disease burden to young children and older adults. About 100 different polysaccharide capsule types (serotypes) have been identified. The capsule is a crucial virulence factor that contributes to pneumococcal immune evasion, and the capsule structure differs per serotype. Some pneumococcal serotypes are associated with invasive disease, while other serotypes are predominantly found in carriage. In this study, we evaluated how the pneumococcal capsule of different serotypes affects epithelial cytokine secretion and ensuing epithelial-mediated leukocyte activation, and functionality. To study the possible effects of the pneumococcal capsule, we infected primary nasal epithelial cells with isogenic capsule mutants of TIGR4 (serotype 4) expressing a serotype 1, 6B, 8, or 35B capsule or no capsule (Δ cps ). The serotype-specific epithelial cytokines were thereafter analyzed and used to examine their effect on leukocyte activation, migration, and leukocyte-dependent pneumococcal killing. We showed that epithelial cytokine secretion differed per serotype, with the strongest induction after infection with the unencapsulated mutant. Distinct expression profiles of epithelium-induced leukocyte activation markers were observed for each serotype, involving changes in activation marker expression for all investigated cell types. Furthermore, compared with other serotypes, epithelial chemokines induced by serotype 8 reduced neutrophil migration and leukocyte-mediated killing of pneumococci. These data highlight the serotype-specific effect of epithelial cells on leukocyte activation and pneumococcal clearance. The results provide additional insights into serotype-specific differences in the pneumococcal interactions with the mucosal surfaces of the human respiratory tract.IMPORTANCE Streptococcus pneumoniae , also referred to as pneumococcus, poses a major disease burden in young children and older adults, with differences in virulence between serotypes. Little is known about serotype-specific effects on colonization of the upper respiratory epithelial tract. Using isogenic mutants of a single pneumococcal strain expressing capsules of different serotypes, we were able to solely look at the effect of the capsule on epithelium-leukocyte interaction. We found that the various serotypes induced distinct cytokine responses in epithelial cells, and that these epithelial cytokines affected leukocyte activation and their pneumococcal killing capacities. Together with pneumococcal serotype-specific differences in immune evasion described by others, our findings provide additional insights into serotype-specific differences in virulence and help unravel why some serotypes are prone to cause invasive disease while other serotypes are mostly associated with carriage.

items.title: Phylogenomics of "Candidatus Rickettsia mendelii" reveals a distinct early-diverging lineage with small genomes within the genus Rickettsia.
items.abstract: The genus Rickettsia comprises obligate intracellular bacteria belonging to the class Alphaproteobacteria. Although Rickettsia species have traditionally been classified into several phylogenetic groups, recent genome-based studies have revealed greater diversity within the genus and related Rickettsiaceae lineages than previously recognized. Here, we isolated six rickettsial strains from Ixodes turdus ticks collected at various locations across Japan and performed whole-genome sequencing. A closed-genome sequence was obtained for one of the isolates. The six isolates shared highly similar genomic features and were identified as " Candidatus Rickettsia mendelii" on the basis of conserved rickettsial marker gene sequences. The genomes of " Ca . R. mendelii" were smaller (1.05-1.06 Mb) and had lower GC content (29.2-29.3%) than most analyzed rickettsial genomes and were comparable in these respects to those of Typhus Group rickettsiae. Family-wide phylogenomic analysis using a quality-filtered Rickettsiaceae genome data set placed " Ca . R. mendelii" in a distinct early-diverging lineage within the genus Rickettsia . Chromosome-level comparisons with many other Rickettsia species revealed stretches of conserved synteny distributed across the chromosome of " Ca . R. mendelii." Genes encoding major secretion-related and host interaction-associated components were detected, whereas no hits meeting the detection criteria were obtained for the F-type IV secretion system (F-T4SS) proteins encoded by Rickettsiales-amplified genetic elements (RAGEs). These results provide the first genome sequences from cultured " Ca . R. mendelii" isolates and expand our understanding of genome diversity and evolution within the genus Rickettsia . Importance Genome-based studies have expanded the known diversity of the genus Rickettsia and related Rickettsiaceae lineages, but genome information from cultured isolates remains unavailable for some poorly characterized taxa. Here, we report the first whole-genome sequences from six cultured isolates of " Ca . R. mendelii" and show that this taxon represents a distinct early-diverging lineage within the genus Rickettsia . The genomes of " Ca . R. mendelii" were smaller and had lower GC content than most analyzed rickettsial genomes and were comparable in these respects to those of Typhus Group rickettsiae, despite the distinct phylogenetic placement. This indicates that similar genome characteristics can occur in phylogenetically distant rickettsial lineages. The low genomic diversity among geographically separated " Ca . R. mendelii" isolates suggests broad dispersal of closely related strains, which may be facilitated by infected ticks carried by migratory birds. These findings improve our understanding of the genome characteristics and geographic distribution of " Ca . R. mendelii."

items.title: Tomatidine derivatives suppress Dengue virus infection through entry and post-entry inhibition.
items.abstract: Dengue is a rapidly spreading disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is caused by the Dengue virus (DENV), affecting approximately 390 million individuals globally. Approved vaccines for use have limited efficacy, and there are no approved antivirals. Tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid obtained from Solanum species, has demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral properties, leading to the investigation of its derivatives for their anti-DENV activity. In the current study, the anti-DENV potential of tomatidine and 11 such derivatives was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in silico approaches. Vero cells were used to evaluate the cytotoxicity and antiviral effects of the derivatives in pre-, co-, and post-treatment settings. The results indicated that the derivatives 5d, 5f, and 5c possessed the most potent antiviral effects; 5d achieved a 2.81 log decrease in viral RNA, while both 5f and 5c suppressed viral activity under both pre- and post-treatment conditions (5f has a selectivity index of 43.36), including the entry phase, as indicated by the entry assay. Furthermore, effective inhibition was noted between 0 and 9 h post-infection (hpi) and 15-21 hpi via a time-of-addition assay, indicating dual-phase activity. Additionally, docking and molecular dynamics studies revealed stable interactions of compounds 5c and 5d with the non-structural proteins NS1 and NS5-RdRp of DENV, reinforcing the experimental observations. In conclusion, tomatidine derivatives, especially 5d, 5f, and 5c, showed significant potential as anti-DENV therapeutics, necessitating additional mechanistic and in vivo studies to determine their clinical efficacy.IMPORTANCEDengue is a major global health threat, infecting hundreds of millions of people each year, yet there are no antiviral drugs available for this disease. Identifying safe and effective therapeutics is therefore a global public health priority. In this study, we discovered three promising tomatidine-derived compounds (5d, 5f, and 5c) that markedly reduced Dengue virus replication in laboratory experiments. These compounds acted at multiple stages of the viral life cycle, suggesting that they could both limit the establishment of infection and suppress viral spread after the infection has begun. Computational analyses further indicated that these molecules target key viral proteins while also influencing host pathways that support viral infection, providing insights into how they may exert their antiviral effects. Together, our findings identify tomatidine derivatives as promising lead candidates for dengue antiviral drug development and provide a strong foundation for future preclinical and clinical investigations.

items.title: Relationship Between Parental Vaccine Hesitancy and Health Locus of Control: A Structural Equation Modeling Study.
items.abstract: Parental vaccine hesitancy (pVH) remains a major public health concern. While sociodemographic and trust-related factors are well studied, the role of parental health locus of control (PHLOC) is less known. This study examined the association between PHLOC dimensions and pVH in Italian parents. This secondary analysis of a cross-sectional online survey (Italy, October 2024-February 2025) included 308 parents of children aged 0-18 years, recruited via social media using snowball sampling. Participants were mostly female (79.6%), with a mean age of 43.6 years (SD = 8.5). pVH was assessed with the PACV-5 and PHLOC across six dimensions (Parent, Child, Professionals, Media, Fate, Divine). Bayesian structural equation modeling (SEM) estimated associations between PHLOC and pVH, adjusting for age, sex, education, civil status, living context, and healthcare professional status. pVH prevalence was 12.99%. In the fully adjusted model, greater perceived influence of healthcare professionals was associated with lower pVH (β = -0.28, 95% CrI [-0.47, -0.09]). Higher educational attainment was also inversely associated with pVH (β = -0.28, 95% CrI [-0.39, -0.16]). Other PHLOC dimensions were not credibly associated with pVH. The model explained 27% of the variance in pVH. Beliefs regarding the influence of healthcare professionals, along with educational attainment, appear to play a central role in shaping parental vaccine hesitancy. Strengthening trust in healthcare providers and tailoring communication strategies for parents with lower educational levels may represent key targets for interventions aimed at improving vaccine confidence. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework (10.17605/OSF.IO/6SVQX).

items.title: Advances in HIV-associated pulmonary diseases: an official American Thoracic Society workshop report.
items.abstract: People with HIV (PWH) are at increased risk of a broad range of infectious and non-infectious pulmonary diseases. Since the last ATS Workshop on HIV-associated pulmonary disease, large national and international cohorts have demonstrated ongoing gaps in our understanding of lung disease in this vulnerable population that range from underappreciation of disease incidence and prevalence to lack of targeted treatments. Translational work on the underlying mechanisms of disease has demonstrated novel, HIV-specific mechanisms that may lend themselves to tailored therapies. Twenty-four experts in HIV-associated lung disease from across the translational spectrum were invited to participate in this ATS-sponsored Workshop utilizing a modified Delphi method that included a series of pre- and post-workshop electronic surveys and a two-day virtual workshop. Lung disease among PWH is driven by complex and interrelated mechanisms including persistent immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, accelerated aging, and microbiome alterations. Despite these advances in our understanding, important gaps persist between mechanistic insights and clinical care that include limited HIV-specific trials, underrepresentation of PWH in studies of lung disease, and the absence of tailored care strategies. These gaps are further accentuated by substantial variation in the availability of data from the most affected populations, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and among children and adolescents. Overcoming these challenges will require coordinated, globally representative research efforts that leverage large cohorts, integrate multi-omics and longitudinal phenotyping, use mechanistic insights to inform clinical trials, and consider implementation science approaches with the ultimate goal of developing tailored prevention and treatment strategies for HIV-associated pulmonary diseases.

items.title: Organizational barriers to addressing climate-sensitive diseases in the Global South: A case study of Peru's dengue response.
items.abstract: To address infectious diseases such as dengue, the World Health organization advocates a 'whole-of-government' approach that promotes coordination across all levels of government within the health sector and across related sectors. Yet not all health systems have the organizational arrangements needed to facilitate such coordination. This paper examines Peru's dengue control program to investigate how the organization of the health system shapes the government's capacity to respond to public health threats. Drawing on the sociology of organizations and qualitative analysis, the study examines how decentralization and performance-based management-legacies of adopting New Public Management (NPM) principles and neoliberal reforms in the 1990s and early 2000s-shape the organizational culture and design of Peru's health system. The findings identify several barriers to coordination across government levels and policy sectors. These include cultural factors such as context-blind universalism and organizational environments that discourage public-sector entrepreneurship, as well as organizational design features such as fragmented data systems, a lack of incentives to pursue a public health career, and rigid performance-based budgeting. Together, these factors limit coordination within the health sector and hinder intersectoral collaboration. The study proposes that improving the government's capacity to respond to health threats requires integrating whole-of-government principles into existing NPM arrangements to strengthen both hierarchical and horizontal coordination.

items.title: As-needed inhaled corticosteroids in asthma: an Official American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline.
items.abstract: Background Inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing reliever therapy has demonstrated efficacy in improving asthma outcomes when compared to short-acting beta2-agonists (SABA) alone but remains underutilized. The purpose of this guideline is to provide recommendations surrounding the use of combination ICS-formoterol or ICS+SABA (in combination or separate inhalers) as reliever therapy across the asthma severity spectrum in adolescents and adults. Methods The American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline panel evaluated six research questions in the PICO format addressing the use of ICS-containing reliever therapy across National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) asthma treatment steps 1-5. The methodology team conducted systematic literature reviews and GRADE assessments, which the panel utilized to inform the recommendations for each specific PICO and overall. Recommendations In patients at NAEPP steps 1 and 2, the panel made strong recommendations for the use of as-needed-only ICS-SABA or ICS-formoterol over SABA-only therapy, and conditional recommendations over scheduled ICS + as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5, the taskforce made a strong recommendation for the use of maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) with ICS-formoterol over scheduled ICS-LABA plus as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5 who are using scheduled maintenance ICS-LABA, the panel made a conditional recommendation for use of ICS+SABA reliever over SABA reliever. In considering these recommendations, the panel valued the importance of preventing severe exacerbations and considered the risk of SABA-only treatment, as well as ICS and systemic corticosteroid (SCS) exposure. Conclusions This clinical practice guideline, informed by systematic reviews and GRADE-based appraisals of PICO-framed evidence, makes these evidence-based recommendations for the safe and effective use of ICS-containing reliever therapy in asthma.

items.title: Translating absolute risk of breast cancer into screening frequency: a framework to guide practice.
items.abstract: Background Current precision mammography screening trials use heterogeneous risk models, risk strata, and screening intervals, with no consensus on how absolute breast cancer risk should translate into screening frequency. A standardized, risk-model-agnostic approach could improve consistency in trial design and facilitate broader clinical implementation. To develop and evaluate a risk-model-agnostic framework that maps guideline-defined absolute breast cancer risk cut points to screening intervals that can guide the design of future personalized screening strategies and translate smoothly to routine clinical practice. Methods Screening interval and frequency derived from the absolute risk of breast cancer in US women is the main outcome. Results The framework yielded a gradient of estimated screening intervals that scaled with absolute risk: annual (2%-3%); annual with supplemental imaging/counseling (≥3%); biennial (1%-2%); and potentially less frequently. When compared with ongoing intervention trials, screening intervals assigned by trials varied widely and were not uniformly aligned with absolute-risk levels, underscoring the lack of standardized mapping between risk and screening intensity. Conclusion A risk-model-agnostic framework based on absolute-risk cut points can provide a transparent and standardized method for specifying screening intervals in personalized mammography screening. This approach may improve consistency in future intervention trials and facilitate equitable implementation of precision screening across population settings.

items.title: Electronic health record embedded frailty index and outcomes among older adults receiving cancer chemotherapy.
items.abstract: Purpose We evaluated whether an automated electronic health record (EHR)-based frailty index (eFI) is associated with hospitalization and overall survival (OS) in older adults receiving chemotherapy. Patients and methods We identified 509 consecutive patients aged ≥65 years with newly diagnosed lung, colorectal, or breast cancer treated with chemotherapy (2017-2020). An automated eFI score was calculated using data from ≥2 visits in the 2 years before chemotherapy, including vital signs, smoking status, diagnoses, selected laboratory values, and functional measures. Frailty was categorized using a cumulative deficit approach as fit (eFI ≤0.10), pre-frail (0.10-0.21), or frail (>0.21). Hospitalizations at 3 and 6 months were compared across groups. Adjusted associations between eFI and hospitalization and mortality were assessed using Cox regression models. OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier methods and compared using log-rank tests. Results Among 509 patients (median age, 72.2 years), 27.7% were fit, 42.4% pre-frail, 14.9% frail, and 14.9% had non-calculable eFI. Six-month hospitalization increased with frailty: 24% (fit), 42% (pre-frail), 62% (frail), and 50% (non-calculable) (P Conclusion EHR-derived frailty was associated with hospitalization and survival, supporting the eFI as a scalable approach to risk stratification in older adults undergoing chemotherapy.

items.title: Assessing policy readiness for climate-informed infectious disease early warning systems in Vietnam: a scoping review and stakeholder consultation.
items.abstract: Background Climate change is reshaping infectious disease patterns, increasing the need for climate-informed early warning systems (EWSs). However, the extent to which Vietnam's governance frameworks support their development and implementation remains unclear. Objectives To assess policies and guidelines governing infectious disease EWSs in Vietnam and identify gaps and opportunities to strengthen system readiness. Methods A policy review using a modified scoping review approach was supplemented by qualitative stakeholder consultations. National regulatory documents issued since 2000 and in effect as of July 2026 were identified through Vietnamese legal databases. Documents were analysed thematically and mapped against the core components of EWSs. Twelve key stakeholders were interviewed to contextualise policy findings and explore implementation challenges. Results Fifteen policy documents met the inclusion criteria. Vietnam has established strong legal and policy foundations for disease reporting, outbreak investigation, emergency response, and intersectoral coordination. Recent policies increasingly recognise climate change adaptation, environmental risks, digital transformation, and cross-sector collaboration, creating an enabling environment for the development of EWSs. However, these policies primarily provide strategic direction and institutional support rather than operational guidance for implementing EWSs. Key gaps include fragmented governance arrangements for data sharing and integration across meteorological, epidemiological, vector, laboratory, and vulnerability datasets; limited guidance on model validation and adoption; weak mechanisms linking forecasts to authorised anticipatory actions; and constraints related to financing and workforce capacity. Conclusions Strengthening policies and operational guidance for forecasting, data integration, and forecast-based action will be critical to enhancing preparedness for and responses to climate-sensitive infectious diseases in Vietnam.

items.title: Comorbidities and Complications: How the Association of Caesarean Delivery With Postpartum Hospital Encounters Varies by Risk Indicator.
items.abstract: Background Objective: Research on potentially avoidable caesarean deliveries frequently centres on births to nulliparous birthing people with a singleton, term delivery with vertex presentation (NTSV). However, caesarean deliveries in this population are heterogeneous, and little is known about how the association with caesarean delivery varies across risk indicators. We aimed to estimate absolute associations between caesarean delivery, categorised by risk indicators, and postpartum hospital encounters within 1 year among NTSV birthing people in Massachusetts. Methods We used data from the Pregnancy and Early Life Longitudinal data system, which captures birth certificate and hospital discharge data for all births in Massachusetts from 2011 to 2019. Risk indicators were categorised into five groups: chronic/acute disease, placental complications, labour complications, fetal concerns and no documented risk. We estimated risk differences for the association of caesarean versus vaginal delivery with hospital encounters within one year postpartum according to risk indication subgroup. Hospital encounters within 30 days, 31 to 180 days and 181 to 365 days were examined. Results Overall, we estimated 23 (95% confidence interval [CI] 19, 27) excess cases of one-year postpartum hospital encounters per 1000 live births for caesarean deliveries compared to vaginal deliveries. Among birthing people with no documented risk, caesarean delivery was not associated with higher postpartum hospital encounter rates within one year compared to vaginal deliveries. Caesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of hospital encounters for all other subgroups. All estimated risk differences were positive for hospital encounters within 30 days; however, across all subgroups, these associations diminished after 180 days postpartum. Conclusions The association of caesarean delivery with postpartum hospital encounters varies by risk indicator and by the timing of the postpartum hospital encounter. These results suggest that caesarean deliveries among those with no documented risk are not associated with an increased risk of postpartum hospital encounter.

items.title: Weight Trajectories Across Antiretroviral Therapy Regimen Switches in Older People With HIV in China: A Nationwide Multicenter Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background As China's HIV epidemic ages rapidly, evaluating metabolic risks in older people with HIV (PWH) is increasingly urgent. Weight gain associated with integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs) has drawn increasing attention, but data on older Chinese PWH remain scarce. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of PWH aged ≥ 50 years across 19 cities in China within the National Free Antiretroviral Therapy Programme. We assessed weight change trajectories across antiretroviral therapy regimen switches among non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), INSTIs, and protease inhibitors (PIs), using piecewise mixed-effects models and restricted cubic splines. We performed subgroup analyses to assess whether associations differed by sex, age, and baseline metabolic risk. Results Among 5618 participants, the adjusted weight-change slope increased from 0.41 kg/year before switching to 0.90 kg/year afterward (p = 0.03). Slope changes were +0.76 kg/year for NNRTI→INSTI (p = 0.03), +4.76 kg/year for PI→INSTI (p Conclusions Switching to INSTI-based regimens was associated with steeper weight-gain trajectories compared to switching to other regimens, while switching from an INSTI to an NNRTI was associated with attenuation. These findings support weight and cardiometabolic monitoring after regimen changes, while decisions regarding ART modification should remain individualized.

items.title: Toward a co-designed dengue early warning system in Vietnam: Stakeholder mapping and expectations in the Mekong Delta Region.
items.abstract: This study aimed to map key stakeholders involved in a prospective dengue EWS and explore their expectations to inform its design and implementation in Vietnam. The study employed an exploratory qualitative design, beginning with a stakeholder inception workshop involving 48 participants to identify key actors across governance levels and sectors. This was followed by 15 in-depth interviews and three focus group discussions with national experts, representatives of local health agencies, and community members in the Mekong Delta Region. Stakeholders were grouped into government health agencies, government non-health agencies, local health agencies, and professional institutions. Expectations consistently emphasised a user-friendly system integrated with existing workflows, reliable forecasts, supportive policy and governance, cross-sectoral data integration, and adequate workforce capacity. Differences in forecast lead time and intended end-users reflected stakeholders' distinct responsibilities rather than conflicting priorities. Power-interest analysis identified national agencies as key strategic actors and local health agencies as central to implementation. These findings provide practical considerations for designing and implementing a dengue EWS aligned with Vietnam's governance structures, routine health system processes, and stakeholder needs, thereby supporting a more sustainable implementation of climate-informed dengue EWS.

items.title: Multistate, travel-associated outbreak of listeriosis linked to a local ice cream producer - Florida, 2021-2022.
items.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) outbreaks linked to ice cream were historically small and included ill people in institutional settings. In 2021-2022, a large Lm outbreak occurred where ill people did not reside in institutional settings. Cases were identified using whole genome sequencing. Investigators reviewed interview data, customer lists, invoices, and molecular subtyping results that linked illnesses to a single Florida ice cream producer. This outbreak included 28 cases from 11 states, which resulted in 27 hospitalizations and one death. Seven illnesses were associated with pregnancy; one resulted in a foetal loss. Of 28 patients with information, 25 (89%) reported living in or travelling to Florida before illness. Of 23 patients with exposure information, all reported ice cream consumption before illness, and 16 (70%) reported Creamery A ice cream. Creamery A recalled all product. This is the first known travel-associated listeriosis outbreak in the United States and the largest reported listeriosis outbreak linked to ice cream. This outbreak included pregnant women and teenagers, which are populations not seen in previous Lm ice cream outbreaks. Recently, more listeriosis outbreaks linked to ice cream have been associated with small, local producers. Continued education and outreach to ice cream producers is critical to prevent Listeria contamination.

items.title: Risk of Distant Metastasis and Oncologic Outcomes of Clinical Near-Complete Responders After Neoadjuvant Therapy in Rectal Cancer: A Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Watch-and-wait has allowed organ preservation in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer who have a clinical complete response to neoadjuvant therapy. The expansion of non-operative management to patients with a near-complete response raises the question of oncological safety in a nonoperative approach in this subset of patients. Objective We aimed to assess the prognostic impact of clinical response after neoadjuvant therapy and to assess the oncologic safety of nonoperative management in patients with near-complete or complete clinical responses. Data sources We systematically reviewed PubMed, Embase and Web of Science in October 2025 to identify studies comparing oncological outcomes of patients with clinical or near-complete response. Study selection Studies comparing clinical response after neoadjuvant therapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer were included. We excluded conference abstracts. Main outcome measures Primary outcome was overall survival. Secondary outcomes included distant metastasis, local regrowth, local regrowth-free survival, and organ preservation rate. Results We included 10 studies and 1,763 patients. Near-complete response after neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer is associated with higher risk of distant metastasis (16.8 vs 7.3%; RR 2.31; 95% CI: 1.63-3.26; p Limitations Heterogeneous definitions of near-complete response and lack of standardized reassessment timing and management. Conclusion In contrast to individual studies, we found that near-complete response after neoadjuvant therapy may have an increased risk of distant metastasis compared to patients with a complete clinical response.

items.title: Unraveling the Early-Life Influences on Healthy Aging: Insights From the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the association between early-life circumstances and healthy aging among community-dwelling older Chinese adults.MethodsData were from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. We used regression methods to identify independent and joint associations of six early-life factors with healthy aging as assessed by the Chinese Healthy Aging Index (CHAI; 0-12), a composite score evaluating six physiological systems.ResultsOf 3,069 participants, 4.82% had the healthiest CHAI score (0-2). After multivariable adjustment, personal education and family economic status were associated with healthier CHAI individually; the cumulative early-life score was associated with the CHAI, both dichotomously and continuously. Each additional score was associated with 37% (95% CI: 23%, 53%) higher odds of being in the healthiest CHAI category.DiscussionFavorable early-life socioeconomic conditions support healthier aging among Chinese older adults, highlighting the need to address early-life inequalities to promote healthy aging.

items.title: Human Rights Violations and Well-Being in the Israeli-Occupied Palestinian West Bank: An Inquiry Into Structural Violence.
items.abstract: Human rights violations (HRVs) occur across multiple layers of daily life, within families, communities, governing institutions, and the broader political context, and together shape people's well-being. This study examines HRVs by different perpetrators and their association with well-being among adults in the Israeli-occupied Palestinian West Bank. A cross-sectional household survey was conducted in 2022 with 1908 adults. Well-being was measured using the WHO-5 index, and HRVs were assessed using a locally developed multilevel scale. Different multiple linear regression models were used to assess the effect of HRV on well-being. Overall, 39% of participants reported poor well-being (WHO-5 ≤ 50). HRV was reported by 60% of participants. Higher HRVs were linked to poorer well-being (β = -2.34, p p p = 0.027), Palestinian Authority (β = -0.85, p = 0.037), and occupation violations (β = -1.47, p p p = 0.044), while men were more affected by community (β = -2.21, p = 0.003) and occupation violations (β = -1.62, p < 0.001). In this study, HRVs emerge as critical social determinants of well-being, requiring integrated approaches that combine legal protection, social support, and contextually grounded health services that recognize the multilevel conditions influencing health and well-being.

items.title: Exploratory Evidence of a Gene-Smoking Interaction Involving MTR rs1805087 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is the most common form of diabetes worldwide. In Brazil, diabetes affects 7.7% of adults and represents a substantial public health and economic burden. Variants in the MTR gene may disrupt one-carbon metabolism, potentially contributing to hyperhomocysteinemia and increased susceptibility to T2DM. A case-control study involving 219 age- and sex-matched individuals was conducted to evaluate the association between the MTR rs1805087 variant and susceptibility to T2DM. Associations under different genetic inheritance models were examined using χ 2 tests and odds ratios (95% confidence interval [CI]). In parallel, machine-learning (ML) algorithms were applied, with predictive performance assessed using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC). The variant was not independently associated with T2DM. However, among individuals with T2DM, genotype distributions differed according to smoking status, with significant associations under the codominant and recessive genetic models. Exploratory ML analyses showed limited discriminative ability in the independent test set, with ROC-AUC values of 0.555 for K-nearest neighbors (KNN), 0.524 for support vector machine (SVM), and 0.503 for random forest (RF). All models exhibited substantial declines in performance compared with cross-validation results obtained in the training set. MTR rs1805087 was not independently associated with T2DM in this studied population. However, differences in genotype distributions according to smoking status among individuals with T2DM may reflect context-dependent genetic effects. Exploratory ML analyses showed limited predictive performance but identified smoking as one of the most influential predictors across all evaluated algorithms.

items.title: Variability in Posterior Vault Distraction Osteogenesis Protocols and Outcome Reporting: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Distraction Protocols.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis meta-analysis characterized variability in the posterior vault distraction osteogenesis (PVDO) distraction protocol and outcome reporting and explored study-level associations between distraction parameters and postoperative complications.MethodsThis PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis included pediatric PVDO studies from PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, and EMBASE (June 12, 2025). Studies underwent quality assessment and data extraction, with pooled proportions calculated using a random-effects model.ResultsEleven studies including 479 patients were analyzed. Median distraction distance and activation phase duration were 26.3 mm and 25.4 days, respectively; median latency and consolidation phase durations were 3.1 and 94.5 days, respectively. The pooled complication rate was 44.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 31%-57%; I 2 = 86%, p p = .027). Weighted linear regression showed that longer activation phases significantly increased skin complications ( p = .025) and device failures ( p = .040). Distraction distance was not significantly associated with postoperative complications in weighted linear regression modeling.ConclusionsThis review revealed substantial variation in the distraction protocol and patient outcome reporting. While MDV and distraction distance showed weak or inconsistent associations with complications, activation phase duration showed the most consistent study-level associations with postoperative outcomes. However, divergent trends between models, substantial heterogeneity, and reliance on cohort-level averages limit the ability to establish definitive relationships between distraction parameters and complications; these findings should not be used to guide clinical practice. Future studies reporting patient-level distraction protocols, subsequent protocol modifications, and postoperative outcomes are needed to support more robust risk modeling.

items.title: Inpatient Patient- and Assignment-Level Nursing Workload Measures: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Aim To review the scope of nursing workload measures that include patient and/or assignment characteristics. Design Scoping review. Data sources In June 2024, articles published between 2004 and 2024 were gathered from Academic Search Complete, Business Source Complete, CINAHL, Medline, and IEEE Xplore. Articles describing formal approaches to assess nurses' patient- and/or assignment-level workload in inpatient settings were included. Results A total of 36 articles were included. Workload measures were categorized according to five attributes: intended care setting, patient-level and assignment-level workload factors assessed, data sources, assessment method, and intended application. Measurement approaches encompassed a range of workload factors, using data from nursing assessments, staffing and patient census data, electronic records, physical measurements, and proprietary systems. Conclusion There are varied approaches to measure nursing workload with consideration for patient and assignment characteristics. Between 2004 and 2024, patient classification tools were the most prominent approach, but there is demonstrated interest in approaches that may provide more objective, automated, and dynamic workload measures. The complexity of workload measures and screening methodology may limit the completeness of this review. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Formal workload measures can support more equitable patient assignments, improve communication and understanding of patient demands, and inform staffing decisions. More work is needed to develop comprehensive workload measures suited for specific care settings. Impact There is a need to synthesize workload measures that consider more than unit-level and task-level factors. Nursing workload is shaped by the characteristics of their patients and assignments, commonly evaluated using patient classification tools. Findings can inform healthcare leaders, frontline staff, and workload researchers. Reporting method This paper was guided and reported using PRISMA-Sc guidelines. Patient or public contribution This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting. Trial registration Open Science Framework (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5WK26).

items.title: Time to untether transitional care from hospital quality: Healthcare utilization following discharge from a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital among community-dwelling older persons.
items.abstract: Background Thirty-day performance measures (e.g., unplanned readmissions), designed to evaluate inpatient care, were neither designed to reflect the experience of patients transitioning from hospital to home, nor the impact of transitional programs to improve postdischarge outcomes. Objective To identify transitional care outcomes by examining a range of postdischarge encounters and mortality. Methods This retrospective observational cohort (October 2022-September 2023) included community-dwelling patients ≥65-years-old, discharged from 120 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals to home after medical or neurological admissions. The outcomes, assessed 30- and 90-days postdischarge were: mortality; planned and unplanned readmissions; observation stays; Emergency Department (ED) visits at VA or non-VA hospitals; and number of days in acute care. Results Among 99,778 patients, 71.1% had no acute care utilization within 30 days postdischarge; 49.9% in 90 days. Unplanned readmissions occurred in 14.4% (N = 14,400) at 30 days; 27.5% (N = 27,386) at 90 days. Mortality occurred in 1.8% (N = 1750) within 30 days; 5.6% (N = 5624) within 90 days. Mortality was highest among patients with unplanned readmissions: 30 days, 6.1% (882/14,400); 90 days, 13.1% (3599/27,386). Planned readmission mortality rates were 30 days, 5.8% (59/1017); 90 days, 9.6% (258/2692). Half of patients who died within 30 days postdischarge did so after an unplanned readmission (50.4% [882/1750]); 35.0% (613/1750) had no acute care utilization. Among N = 94,154 patients who survived 90-day postdischarge, 11.2% spent ≥10 days in acute care settings. Conclusions These findings support using the number of days in acute care within 90 days postdischarge as a transitional outcome. Thirty-day readmissions do not capture the full scope of postdischarge healthcare utilization and mortality among community-dwelling older adults.

items.title: Changes in Social Wellbeing Among Older Adults With Limited Prognosis: Results From a Nationally Representative Cohort.
items.abstract: Background Physicians use clinical prognostic estimates to identify medical tests and treatments likely to benefit patients within their lifetime. Poor social wellbeing is associated with mortality, but it is unclear if prognostic indices can identify older adults at risk for worsening social well-being. We examined associations between a mortality prognostic index and social wellbeing at baseline and over 2 years to inform care priorities in the context of a limited prognosis. Methods Data from the National Social Life, Health and Aging Project (NSHAP) Round 4 (2021-2023) and Round 4.2 (2024) included 1630 older adults. Social measures included loneliness, living alone, and at least monthly volunteering, socializing, and attending community groups and religious services. Scores of 8 or higher on the Lee Index (range: 0-26) indicated high mortality risk. Survey-weighted logistic regressions adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates were used to compare baseline and 2-year changes in social wellbeing in the high versus low mortality risk group. Results Participants had a mean age of 70.3 years, and were 54% female, 62% White, 20% Black, and 14% non-Black Hispanic. At baseline, higher mortality risk participants had poorer social wellbeing on all measures except socializing. Among those not lonely at baseline, 24.2% of higher versus 15.6% of lower risk participants became lonely at follow-up (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.01-2.14). Among those socializing at least monthly at baseline, 19.0% of higher versus 12.3% of lower risk participants transitioned to less-than-monthly socializing (aOR 1.60; 95% CI: 0.97-2.65). Higher risk participants had larger declines in all measures of social wellbeing at follow-up. Conclusions Older adults with higher mortality risk had poorer social wellbeing at baseline and were more likely to become lonely and decrease social participation at follow-up. Prognostic information may help clinicians avoid low-value medical interventions while prioritizing interventions to support meaningful social connection.

items.title: Explanation of the ergonomic components of safety shoes based on the experience of industry workers.
items.abstract: Objectives . Safety shoes are essential for worker protection, yet ergonomic shortcomings may reduce usability and lead to non-compliance. This study aimed to identify ergonomic components of safety shoes based on industrial workers' experiences. Methods . A qualitative content analysis was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 30 industrial employees in Kerman, Iran, with at least 1 year of safety shoe experience. Participants were purposively selected, and interviews continued until data saturation. Data were analyzed using open, axial and selective coding based on Graneheim and Lundman and on Corbin and Strauss, and used investigator triangulation to ensure trustworthiness. Results . Five primary categories and 14 subcategories affecting safety shoe use were identified: musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), negative effects on performance, skin and thermal discomfort, difficulties with shoelaces and donning/doffing, and individual feelings. These factors contributed to reduced usability and effectiveness, as shown in a paradigmatic model. Conclusion . Key usability-enhancing factors include appropriate alignment of upper and sole dimensions with foot anthropometry, reduced steel-component weight, greater material flexibility, softer and more breathable lining, effective adjusters (e.g., laces or zippers) and consideration of user preferences and safety culture. Manufacturers and occupational health professionals should prioritize these user-centered features to improve comfort, compliance and workplace safety.

items.title: Intergenerational Perspectives on AI-Generated Health Misinformation: A Qualitative Exploration of Visual Framing and Cultural Schemas.
items.abstract: In the digital age, artificial intelligence (AI)-generated short videos increasingly package health claims in visually persuasive formats, creating new challenges for public health communication and the dissemination of accurate health information. While institutions strive to improve digital health literacy, research remains limited in explaining intergenerational differences, particularly regarding gerontological vulnerabilities, when health messages employ culturally coded aesthetics. Grounded in visual framing theory and cultural schema theory, this study explores how young and older adults interpret visual and cultural cues when appraising AI-generated health misinformation. During semi-structured interviews, participants evaluated AI-generated health messages presented in two contrasting styles: a Chinese ink-painting style and a computer-generated three-dimensional cartoon style. Findings support a tech-cultural framework integrating technical visual cues and cultural schemas. Among the two sampled cohorts, culturally authoritative visuals were associated with higher perceived legitimacy and lower vigilance, whereas participants differed in the technical visuals they foregrounded when judging credibility. The findings offer intervention advice for improving communication with diverse generational audiences.

items.title: Modeling the cost-effectiveness of NVX-CoV2705 and the public health impact of vaccination for the prevention of seasonal COVID-19 in the US.
items.abstract: Background Older adults and those with comorbidities have increased risk of severe disease and mortality from COVID-19. This analysis estimated the cost-effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination versus no vaccination in the US and potential impact of increased vaccine coverage. Research design and methods A Markov-based model was updated using the latest epidemiology and vaccine reactogenicity data. Cases, costs, and outcomes for individuals aged 18-64 with ≥1 comorbidity and ≥65 years were estimated for NVX-CoV2705 (Nuvaxovid) versus no vaccination from a third-party payer perspective. Scenario analyses considered the societal perspective and analogous comparisons for BNT162b2 (Comirnaty), mRNA-1273 (Spikevax), and mRNA-1283 (mNEXSPIKE). Results were scaled for public health impact analyses. Results Base-case results associated NVX-CoV2705 with fewer cases (0.0447), hospitalizations (0.0037), and deaths (0.0004) per person on average. NVX-CoV2705 yielded an ICER of $9,840/QALY gained, reflecting fewer QALYs lost (0.0039) alongside increased direct costs ($38.09) per person. Differences for mRNA vaccines were driven by price and reactogenicity. Increasing vaccine coverage by 5-15 percentage points resulted in 114-341 hospitalizations and 11-33 deaths averted per 1,000,000 individuals. Conclusions NVX-CoV2705 was predicted to be cost-effective over no vaccination. This analysis included a more granular approach to modeling reactogenicity events, an important consideration in vaccine cost-effectiveness analyses.

items.title: Primary Prevention Needs to Reduce Family Violence and Sexual Violence Among Older Adults: A Culture-Centered Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
items.abstract: Family and sexual violence are significant public health issues in Aotearoa New Zealand, but research examining prevention strategies is limited. Grounded in Dutta's culture-centered approach, this study examines the primary prevention needs of older adults to reduce family violence and sexual violence in Aotearoa New Zealand as part of a broader project that is co-developing a prevention framework among high-risk groups. Through 63 interviews with older adults in Aotearoa New Zealand, participants expressed the central role of whānau (extended family) and community in reducing violence against older people through strengthening relationships, as well as the importance of education in increasing awareness of violence prevention throughout the lifespan. The findings disrupt singular, individualistic approaches to violence prevention by emphasizing responsibility, solidarity, and connection.

items.title: The TOGETHER Model: A Next-Generation Integrated Framework for Communication in Healthcare.
items.abstract: Communication is a core clinical competence that directly impacts treatment adherence and patient outcomes. Although excellent communication, coaching, and educational frameworks have been developed, they often operate in isolation, leaving clinicians to navigate between disparate approaches without a unifying reference. The TOGETHER Model is introduced in this study as a conceptual proposal that integrates and synthesizes established evidence-based communication practices and professional coaching methods into a coherent and operational framework for patient-centered care, further grounded in recognized psychological theories. TOGETHER Model translates theoretical constructs into eight practical domains: "trust building and relationship," "open communication," "goal setting," "explanation," "treatment options and shared decision-making," "humanity," "education and empowerment," and "review and follow-up." Each domain is associated with practical professional actions and essential competencies, providing clinicians with structured yet flexible guidance that can be integrated across diverse care settings and patient journeys. The model is designed to be modular and scalable, supporting its use in medical education and continuing professional development. Operational applications include structured training curricula, simulation-based assessments, AI-enhanced digital platforms, and organizational toolkits for implementation and change management. Beyond education, the model offers a pathway for embedding communication competence into accreditation systems and quality standards, thereby aligning professional development with broader institutional and policy goals.
