items.title: Illusory cold desensitizes touch.
items.abstract: In Jack London's To Build a Fire, the doomed protagonist notes that "the tremendous cold had already driven the life out of his fingers… dead fingers could neither touch nor clutch." Indeed, our hands are numbed when exposed to cold, a desensitization process traditionally attributed to biophysical and physiological effects on mechanoreceptor and afferent responses.1 Yet perception is not based solely on sensory inputs and often reflects prior beliefs and expectations.2 Accordingly, the mere experience of coldness, given its association with tactile desensitization, conceivably modulates touch independent of physical effects. We dissociated the physical and subjective influences of cooling on touch by leveraging the thermal referral illusion,3,4,5,6,7 in which cooling of the index and ring fingers induces an illusory perception of coldness that is referred to the middle finger, which did not experience local cooling. We found that both veridical and illusory cold elevated tactile detection thresholds. Threshold shifts scaled with subjective ratings of cold intensity, which varied with thermal adaptation. Thermal referral induction did not result in changes to skin temperature, ruling out indirect physical effects on the tested finger. To account for cold effects on touch, we implemented a computational model incorporating both physical and subjective factors by simulating changes in tactile afferent spiking activity8 and modulation of decision computations, respectively. The model reproduced empirical cooling effects on afferent responses9 and recapitulated psychophysical detection patterns. Our results reveal that subjective thermal perception contributes to cold-induced attenuation of touch, highlighting how multimodal experiences and expectations shape somatosensation.

items.title: Tubulin autoregulation factors recruit γ-tubulin to non-centrosomal MTOCs for neuronal microtubule nucleation.
items.abstract: Neuronal function and survival depend on stereotyped non-centrosomal microtubule (MT) arrays. How these arrays form remains poorly understood. Here, we found that two factors previously implicated in tubulin mRNA turnover control neuronal MT content through γ-tubulin-dependent nucleation. In C. elegans neurons, loss of scaper, ttc5, or both reduced MT numbers to a similar degree as depletion of γ-tubulin, the main MT nucleator. Using conditional single-cell degradation alleles and endogenous tagging, we find that scaper and ttc5 are required to recruit γ-tubulin to non-centrosomal MT organizing centers (MTOCs). SCAPER is also instructive, as its overexpression raises γ-tubulin levels at nucleation sites and increases MT density. SCAPER, TTC5, and γ-tubulin are dispensable for developmental axon growth but play essential roles during regeneration, where SCAPER recruits γ-tubulin to a growth-cone-localized MTOC to orient MT nucleation. Last, SCAPER is required for activity-dependent MT nucleation in rat hippocampal neurons, suggesting a conserved role. These findings reveal mechanisms governing neuronal cytoskeleton assembly and function and suggest potential crosstalk between tubulin autoregulation and MT nucleation.

items.title: White matter lesions in brain MRI in Meniere's disease; More findings on MRI?
items.abstract: Recently, the role of vascular risk factors in developing Meniere's disease (MD) has been proposed. Brain MRI has been obtained from MD cases to rule out tumor lesions in CPA and Labyrinth. In this study, we investigated the frequency of vascular risk factors and white matter lesions (WMLs) in brain MRIs of MD patients and the control group. In a case-control study, 30 definite unilateral MD cases and 30 individuals as the control group (aged 18-65; none had migraine) were enrolled. Their demographic and clinical information was collected through questionnaires, and brain MRI was performed and interpreted in both groups. The extent of WMLs was assessed using the Fazekas criteria. The patient and control groups showed no significant differences in terms of mean age, sex (p = 0.08 and p = 0.3, respectively), and any vascular risk factors. 60% of MD patients and 23.33% of individuals in the control group had WMLs on MRI (p = 0.004). Indeed, MD was associated with a nearly 5-fold increase in WMLs in MRI. The difference between the two groups in periventricular white matter (PVWM) lesions was more significant (P = 0.032), compared with deep white matter (DWM) lesions (P = 0.052). Despite no association between vascular risk factors and MD in this study, WMLs were nearly 5-fold more prevalent in the brain MRI of MD patients, particularly PVWM-type lesions. It seems that aside from detecting tumoral lesions and structural abnormalities, MRI has more findings in MD subjects.

items.title: Awareness, attitudes toward epilepsy, and first-aid knowledge of seizures among rural primary care doctors in Eastern China.
items.abstract: We aimed to assess the awareness of, and attitudes toward epilepsy among young rural primary care doctors from rural clinics in Zhejiang Province, Eastern China. Ninety-five young rural primary care doctors working at rural clinics participated in this cross-sectional study in 2025. A custom-built electronic questionnaire, which comprised four sections, including 12 items for general condition data, 10 items for awareness (including first aid), a 16-item scale for attitudes, and 6 items for demographic data, was administered to the rural primary care doctors. Descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis H test, and Spearman's rank correlation analysis were used to analyze the data, which exhibited a non-normal distribution. Multivariable linear regression analyzes were conducted to identify independent predictors for each outcome, using the enter method and reporting β, B with 95% CI, p-values, and R2. The young rural primary care doctors obtained a mean score of 18.20 ± 3.48 (aggregate score: 30) on the awareness of epilepsy section, a mean score of 5.40 ± 1.53 (aggregate score: 7) on the first aid knowledge section, and a mean score of 66.05 ± 7.65 (aggregate score: 80) on the epilepsy attitude section. Educational background (rs = 0.293, p = 0.004), training experience (rs = 0.322, p = 0.001), and epilepsy attitude scores (rs = 0.255, p = 0.013) correlated significantly with mean epilepsy awareness scores. Training experience (rs = 0.222, p = 0.031) correlated significantly with attitudes toward epilepsy. Multivariable regression analyzes showed that educational background independently predicted epilepsy awareness (p = 0.016) and first aid knowledge (p < 0.001), while training experience did not (p = 0.492 and p = 0.687, respectively). Epilepsy awareness independently predicted attitudes toward people with epilepsy (PWE) (p = 0.004) and first aid knowledge (p < 0.001). Furthermore, when rural primary care doctors faced newly diagnosed PWE, a referral was usually recommended (95.79%), and a few would initiate antiseizure medications (ASMs) (22.58%). In addition, about 30%-40% of the rural primary care doctors maintained an uncertain attitude toward the marriage, dating and pregnancy. The awareness and attitudes of young rural primary care doctors toward epilepsy in the rural clinics were suboptimal. We recommend targeted training for young rural primary care doctors (covering first aid, novel ASMs, and patient counseling for marriage, dating, and pregnancy), combined with telemedicine integration to establish specialist support networks and optimize rural epilepsy care pathways.

items.title: From the Mailbox to the Microphone: The Neurology Podcast and the Evolution of Medical Education.
items.abstract: When the Neurology® Podcast debuted in September 2007, podcasting occupied the fringes of academic medicine. Smartphones had only just emerged, and streaming audio was uncommon. Nearly 2 decades later, the Neurology Podcast stands among the longest-running physician-hosted podcasts in medicine and has fundamentally expanded how one of the world's leading neurology journals educates its readers. Although the technologies through which neurologists consume information have changed dramatically since 2007, the podcast's enduring success reflects a remarkably constant mission: to deliver practical, clinically relevant education through authentic conversation. This article traces the origins and evolution of the Neurology Podcast through archival documents, contemporaneous publications, and personal recollections from those who created it.

items.title: Improving CommonGround, an Online Peer Support Intervention for People Living With Long-Term Physical Health Conditions and Subthreshold Depression: Theory of Change-Informed Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: People living with long-term physical health conditions who are also experiencing subthreshold depression are at risk of developing major depression. In partnership with lived experience experts, clinicians, and software developers, we co-designed CommonGround, an online peer support and psychoeducation platform. CommonGround's Theory of Change (ToC) was also conceptualized to outline the intermediate outcomes (and associated indicators of whether such outcomes are achieved) needed to improve the mental health of the target population. This qualitative study, informed by the ToC, aimed to examine the acceptability, usability, and intervention mechanisms of CommonGround and ultimately refine the ToC and corresponding intervention design ahead of definitive evaluation. A nested qualitative study was conducted within a remote, 12-week feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing CommonGround (intervention group) to signposting to National Health Service (NHS) web pages (control group). Thirty-nine participants were purposively sampled and interviewed within 6 weeks postintervention about their experiences of CommonGround and trial participation. The interview schedule and thematic framework analysis were rooted in a pretrial ToC while being responsive to emergent themes. Evaluating the assumptions and intermediate outcomes (via their indicators) refined our understanding of how CommonGround may support mental well-being. Overall, participants viewed CommonGround as an appropriate, safe space to access self-management information and support from others with a unique shared understanding of chronic illness. However, many participants felt more time was needed for genuine social relations to form and community culture to evolve. Anonymity helped foster a sense of safety but, for some participants, limited the formation of genuine connections. Other factors contributing to low engagement included personal circumstances (eg, limited time). Key suggestions for future development included creating a mobile app that would be easier and more intuitive to access and navigate. CommonGround was considered an acceptable and appropriate space to access peer support, with the potential to positively impact psychological well-being by fostering shared understanding, support, and knowledge exchange. Beyond informing the future evaluation of CommonGround in a definitive trial, the refined ToC identifies the key preconditions, intermediate outcomes, and associated indicators, and assumptions that may underpin the acceptability and usability of digital peer support interventions in achieving their intended outcomes. We also demonstrate how evaluating and refining components of the ToC after the intervention had been implemented in the trial enabled a more nuanced understanding of how and why the intervention may work, for whom, under what circumstances, and informed changes to improve the co-designed intervention.

items.title: Gα q -coupled receptors activate cAMP signaling through Ca 2+ /calmodulin-stimulated adenylyl cyclases.
items.abstract: Among the various G protein-mediated intracellular signaling pathways activated by G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), Gαs and Gαi stimulate and inhibit adenylyl cyclases (ADCYs), leading to increases and decreases in cAMP abundance, respectively. Here, we investigated the contribution of Gαq-coupled receptors (Gαq-GPCRs), which typically activate phospholipase C (PLC) and stimulate intracellular Ca2+ generation, to the regulation of cAMP signaling. We activated the endogenous Gαq-coupled muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (Gαq-mAChRs) and the group 1 metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR1/5) in ex vivo hippocampal slices from mice. We also used a chemogenetics approach to activate Gαq-DREADDs (designer receptors exclusively activated by designer drugs) through hM3Dq. We found that stimulation of these Gαq-GPCRs not only increased the abundance of cAMP but also activated downstream, cAMP-mediated intracellular signaling pathways. This GPCR-dependent cAMP signaling required both Gαq activity and intracellular Ca2+. Additionally, hippocampal slices from mice lacking the Ca2+/calmodulin-stimulated ADCYs, ADCY1 and ADCY8, did not exhibit Gαq-GPCR-mediated cAMP signaling and showed impaired synaptic long-term depression (LTD) mediated by Gαq-mAChRs. Together, our findings highlight a nonconventional function of Gαq-GPCRs in regulating cAMP signaling through distinct ADCYs.

items.title: An open-source eye-tracking system adaptable to diverse terrestrial vertebrates reveals state-dependent visual acquisition in lizards.
items.abstract: Gaze shifts are fundamental to visual exploration and processing, yet empirical knowledge is largely confined to a small number of model species, limiting our understanding of general principles of visual acquisition across animals. Here, we introduce a versatile, low-cost, and open-source framework design for eye-tracking in small, freely moving animals. Leveraging photogrammetry, 3D modeling, and 3D-printing, we produce headmounts adaptable to diverse head-eye geometries, as we demonstrate for lizards, turtles, and mice. Detailed recordings in Pogona vitticeps, a laterally eyed ectotherm with a high-acuity retina, reveal a rich oculomotor repertoire with kinematics closely resembling the saccadic main sequence in primates. We found both movement-coupled large binocular saccades, which exhibited a strong axial bias as well as small, isotropic, and monocular saccades suggesting a capacity for visual exploration of local details. Visual acquisition strategies were strongly tied to behavioral states with periods of active sampling (3-5 Hz saccades) separated by periods of ocular stillness lasting many seconds and suggesting a visual acquisition strategy distinct from those commonly described in endothermic model species. Furthermore, active states were correlated with pupil constriction in contrast to mammals and similarly to birds. Our results demonstrate the utility of our experimental approach for understanding visual acquisition across terrestrial vertebrates. Such a multi-perspective view on natural visual acquisition across species will be essential for developing a generalized understanding of vision, its ecological functions, and its evolutionary trajectory.

items.title: Temporal dynamics of Spontaneous Blastocyst Re-expansion as A Predictor of Frozen Embryo Transfer Success.
items.abstract: When embryos are frozen and thawed for fertility treatment, they sometimes collapse, but does this mean they are no longer viable? This study followed 438 frozen embryo transfer cycles to understand whether collapsed embryos can recover, and whether giving them more time in the incubator before transfer makes a difference. The key finding is that what matters most is how an embryo looks at the time of transfer, not immediately after thawing. Embryos that re-expanded before being transferred had similar success rates to those that never collapsed. Only embryos that remained collapsed at transfer had significantly poorer outcomes. Importantly, for every additional hour spent in the incubator, a collapsed embryo's odds of recovering improved substantially. This means that rather than discarding a collapsed embryo, clinicians may simply need to wait, giving it time to recover could meaningfully improve the chances of a successful pregnancy. Collapsed embryos that are given longer to recover in the incubator before transfer may have the same chance of achieving a pregnancy as embryos that never collapsed.

items.title: Spyglass is a framework for reproducible and shareable neuroscience research.
items.abstract: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. Current approaches to storing and analyzing neural data involve bespoke formats and software that make replication and reuse of data difficult. To address these challenges, we created Spyglass, an open-source data management and analysis framework written in Python. Spyglass provides reproducible pipelines for common neuroscience analyses and sharing of raw data, intermediate analyses, and final results within and across labs. Spyglass uses the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard and includes pipelines for spectral filtering, spike sorting, pose tracking, and neural decoding. Spyglass can be extended to apply existing and newly developed pipelines to datasets from multiple sources. We demonstrate these features in the context of a cross-laboratory replication by applying advanced state space decoding algorithms to publicly available data. New users can try out Spyglass on a Jupyter Hub hosted by HHMI and 2i2c: https://spyglass.hhmi.2i2c.cloud/.

items.title: Context re-exposure during counterconditioning strengthens episodic memory for aversive and related positive events.
items.abstract: Several clinical interventions rely on narrative reframing, whereby the outcome of an overly emotional memory is replaced with a more favourable one. Recently, concern has arisen that such interventions may not only alter elicited emotions, but also reduce the memory's accuracy or even promote false memories. However, the relative simplicity of memories induced in traditional fear-conditioning paradigms (e.g., a tone-shock association) makes it challenging to experimentally model narrative reframing or test episodic distortions. We therefore developed a paradigm using trial-unique, multimodal, and personally meaningful events to investigate whether episodic counterconditioning can modify the episodic and affective (i.e., psychophysiological and subjective) components of aversive memories through new associations with semantically related positive events. Specifically, we hypothesised that spatial overlap between the aversive and related positive events would strengthen memory for both episodes and alleviate affective responses. Healthy participants (N = 100) encoded 20 memories, each comprising a cue (neutral object image) followed by an aversive or neutral outcome (image-sound combination) presented in a context (background image). The following day, 10 aversive memories were counterconditioned by pairing their cues with a semantically related positive outcome, with half presented in the original context and the other half in a novel context. While counterconditioning successfully induced positive affect, it did not alleviate affective responses the next day. Nonetheless, spatial overlap strengthened episodic memory for both the aversive and positive events. Future research should test whether context re-exposure during psychotherapy can likewise improve the accuracy of autobiographical aversive memories.

items.title: Targeted gene therapy alleviates epilepsy and hyperexcitability in models of SCN2A deficiency.
items.abstract: Pathogenic SCN2A loss-of-function (LoF) variants can cause severe, refractory epilepsy with limited treatment options. Existing Scn2a-LoF mouse models exhibit few spontaneous seizures, limiting the dynamic range needed to assess therapeutic efficacy. We therefore generated gene-trap Scn2a-deficient mice on the seizure-prone DBA/2J background. These mice experienced hundreds of spontaneous absence seizures per day, characterized by concurrent behavioral arrest and EEG spike-wave discharges (SWDs). Partial restoration of Scn2a expression reduced seizure burden. Electrophysiological analysis revealed impaired action potential waveforms yet increased repetitive firing, alongside coordinated downregulation of voltage-gated potassium channel genes, potentially contributing to hyperexcitability. Given the broad potassium channel downregulation and prior efficacy of KCNA1 gene therapy in refractory seizure models, we selected KV1.1 as a potential therapeutic target and used a drug-controllable adeno-associated virus (AAV) to express human KCNA1. We found that this intervention normalized elevated neuronal firing and reduced spontaneous seizure burden in Scn2a-deficient mice. Extending these findings to a human cell-based platform, AAV-mediated KCNA1 expression also reduced neuronal firing in human cortical organoids carrying a SCN2A-truncating variant identified in patients. Together, these findings provide proof of principle for drug-controllable KCNA1 gene therapy as a promising treatment avenue for epilepsy related to SCN2A LoF variants.

items.title: Kratom Use Among U.S. Adults: Clinical Characteristics and Sex Differences in Co-Occurring Drug Use.
items.abstract: The expansion of kratom's availability, popularity, and product diversity in the United States has drawn scientific and national attention. Characterizing the sociodemographic and behavioral correlates of kratom use may help public health efforts. We examined data from the National Survey of Drug Use and Health (2022-2023), to investigate lifetime prevalence and sociodemographic, mental health, and behavioral correlates of self-reported use of kratom as well as the interaction of cannabis and heroin with sex, given co-used patterns with kratom and report sex differences. A pooled prevalence estimate of lifetime kratom use among U.S. adults (18+) was 1.95%, of whom 34.84% reported past-year use and 18.39% reported past-month use. Among those with past-year use, 52.79% reported past-month use. Lifetime use was most common among White, unmarried, younger, working males and those with lower incomes, living in poverty, and participating in government assistance programs. In multivariable analysis, lifetime kratom use was associated with lifetime major depressive episodes, use of pain-relieving medications, and past-year serious psychological distress. Lifetime cannabis and heroin use were associated with elevated odds of kratom use in both sexes. However, kratom's relationship with cannabis use was over three times stronger in males, while its relationship with heroin use was approximately half as strong in males compared to females. Kratom use was correlated with specific demographic, behavioral, and sex- and substance-specific characteristics, suggesting the need for more study to examine whether certain populations may benefit from targeted screening and intervention.

items.title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons.
items.abstract: Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus-pituitary-testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified Synage, a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that Synage expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted Synage_B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of Synage in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically, Synage interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8-KCHIP4 interaction. Synage loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (IA), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent Synage loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8-KCHIP4-Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify Synage as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.

items.title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults.
items.abstract: Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17, P < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08, P < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13, P < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.

items.title: Dissociation of gravity and limb dynamics in motor control.
items.abstract: Human movements remain accurate across substantial variations in mechanical loading, yet how the nervous system anticipates and compensates for intrinsic and extrinsic forces when generating muscle commands remains unresolved. Because the forces acting on the body are complex and nonlinear, dynamical modeling provides a powerful framework for identifying the computations underlying motor control. Here, we exploited parabolic flight to dissociate gravitational loading from intrinsic limb dynamics and directly test how these mechanical components are represented in motor commands. We analyzed kinematics and shoulder muscle activity from nine participants performing visually guided pointing movements in microgravity (0g), normogravity (1g), and hypergravity (2g). Inverse dynamics revealed that the gravity-independent component of muscle torque remained invariant across gravitational conditions. In striking contrast, muscle moments estimated from muscle activation showed systematic scaling of not only static but also phasic components with gravitational load, particularly during movement deceleration. This divergence arises because activation-derived muscle moments capture cocontraction, and thus impedance-related control, that is absent from net torques obtained by inverse dynamics. Gravity-dependent regression analyses further showed that muscle activation could be reconstructed from a compact set of mechanical variables dominated by gravity-dependent torque and movement velocity, revealing a low-dimensional structure of motor control. Together, these findings support a control architecture in which motor commands integrate predictive compensation for limb dynamics with gravity-dependent regulation of muscle cocontraction. This dual strategy provides a mechanism for maintaining stable and accurate movement across changing mechanical environments and offers a unified framework for understanding motor control under variable external loads.

items.title: Late electroencephalographic seizure-risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging as seizure-burden markers associated with neurological deficits after status epilepticus in a remote or chronic cohort.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether time-dependent electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are associated with neurological outcomes after status epilepticus (SE), beyond seizure duration. This two-center observational study included consecutive SE patients from 2017 to 2025. We examined three seizure-related markers: seizure duration ≥ 30 min, a 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on a late EEG (performed the following day or later after SE onset), and SE-related restricted diffusion on MRI (peri-ictal diffusion-weighted imaging hyperintensity with reduced apparent diffusion coefficient values). Outcomes were overall neurological worsening and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits at discharge. Multivariable models included the three markers and age> 65 years, with further adjustment for stupor or coma at admission and third-line therapy. Of 440 patients with suspected SE, 297 had confirmed SE; 221 with an identified seizure focus formed the overall cohort; 127 with remote symptomatic SE or preexisting chronic focal epilepsy formed the remote or chronic cohort. Overall neurological worsening occurred in 96 patients (43.4%) and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits in 68 (30.8%). In univariable analyses, seizure duration ≥ 30 min was associated with both outcomes in the overall cohort. A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, whereas high-risk findings on early EEG were not. In multivariable models including seizure duration, restricted diffusion was independently associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, most strongly with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 28.59, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 7.23-154.99). A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was independently associated with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted OR = 4.26, 95% CI = 1.35-14.24), whereas seizure duration ≥ 30 min was not independently associated with either outcome. High-risk late-EEG findings and restricted diffusion were associated with neurological deficits. These markers may complement seizure duration in estimating cumulative seizure burden and focal brain injury.

items.title: Neural Stem Cell Therapies for Central Nervous System Regeneration: Advances, Challenges, and Integrative Technologies.
items.abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are promising candidates for central nervous system (CNS) regeneration because they self-renew and differentiate into neural lineages. Advances in genome engineering, extracellular vesicles (EVs), biomaterials, organoids, single-cell technologies, and precision medicine have expanded approaches for characterizing, engineering, delivering, and evaluating NSC-based therapies for neurological disorders. CRISPR/Cas9 and related platforms may enable more precise modification of NSC function, while NSC-derived EVs offer potential cell-free strategies. Engineered hydrogels and three-dimensional scaffolds may improve cell survival, engraftment, migration, and integration. Organoids and single-cell omics provide increasingly detailed models of cellular heterogeneity and lineage specification. However, clinical translation remains limited by immune compatibility, tumorigenic risk, manufacturing standardization, graft survival and integration, and regulatory requirements. Rigorous preclinical validation, standardized manufacturing, appropriately designed clinical trials, long-term safety monitoring, and harmonized regulatory frameworks are required before routine clinical application.

items.title: Systematic Microcircuit Reconfigurations Underlie Early Experience-induced Visual Cortical Plasticity.
items.abstract: Experience-dependent reorganization of neuronal connections during the postnatal critical period is essential for the functional maturation of the developing primary visual cortex (V1). However, the systematic reconfigurations across microcircuit synapses underlying experience-dependent plasticity are poorly defined. Using paired whole-cell recordings from excitatory pyramidal cells and three other major classes of interneurons (INs) within layers 2/3 and 4 in the developing mouse V1 monocular region, we found that monocular deprivation (MD) for one day in juvenile mice transiently reconfigures local excitatory synapses onto inhibitory INs that specifically express parvalbumin (PV) or vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP). In contrast, prolonged MD predominantly strengthens inhibitory synaptic transmission from somatostatin (SST)-expressing INs to PV-INs and VIP-INs across both layers. A physiologically based microcircuit model further recapitulated MD-induced activity changes in visual responses across layer 2/3 neurons in vivo. We provide a detailed microcircuit framework that contributes to the experience-dependent regulation of visual function.

items.title: Perimenopause and Menopause: Estrogen-Deficient Skin and Impaired Quality of Life-Dermal Aging a Visible Mirror Reflecting Internal Aging and Health.
items.abstract: Increased awareness in women's health has taken place over the last 5 to 10 years, especially associated with aging, where perimenopause and menopause have been highlighted topics. This review examines how changes with age in women during perimenopause and menopause lead to estrogen-deficient skin and impaired quality of life (QOL). The topics presented include: (1) the reasons why women's health (perimenopause and menopause) is finally taking a prominent position in the public and medical mindset, (2) chronological (intrinsic) and photo (extrinsic) skin aging characteristics and skin changes by each decade of life, (3) the importance of and the changes to estrogen levels in aging women (especially with perimenopause and menopause) that lead to estrogen-deficient skin, (4) in brief, hormonal and selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), including polyphenolic and isoflavonoid treatments, plus influencing lifestyle factors, and (5) using skin changes, as the "observable organ" and a reflective mirror of internal aging in women that may signal the potential decline of various unseen tissue/organ systems. This represents a different paradigm for the functional aspects in the body associated with the shifts in and loss of estrogen. Thus, skin health with aging (and the decline in and loss of estrogen) may provide nutritional and medical professionals, especially dermatologists, with a unique position to lead a discussion with patients to consider healthiness beyond dermal changes. Finally, potential treatments to assist and/or enhance women's healthspan and longevity may be part of this exchange in a collaborative examination.Graphical abstract available for this article.

items.title: The risk of seizure-affected pregnancy in Australian women with epilepsy.
items.abstract: We reported earlier that the occurrence of seizures in the pre-pregnancy year was the main determinant of the following pregnancy being seizure-affected. Additional risk factors were assessed in this study. The pregnancies involved first pregnancies of women with epilepsy. Two categories were compared. One category comprised 711 pregnancies in which seizures had occurred during the pre-pregnancy year and where seizures might reasonably be expected to continue to occur during the 9 months involved in any following pregnancy. The other category contained 634 pregnancies that were seizure-free in the pre-pregnancy year. Multivariate logistic regressions were fitted for 1345 subjects for seizure occurrence during pregnancy for co-variates listed to identify statistically seizure-related co-variates. Seizure-affected pregnancy rates in the 1345 pregnancies studied remained stable over the consecutive 5-year intervals from 1999 onwards, viz. 50.5%, 53.9%, 50.3%, 52.8% and 48.2%. Seizure-affected pregnancy was more likely in WWE, who had: (1) Shorter durations of pre-pregnancy freedom from seizures. (2) Focal epilepsy. (3) Not taken ASMs while pregnant. (4) Not used pre-pregnancy folate supplementation. (5) Longer durations of epilepsy. (6) Earlier age onset of epilepsy. The hazard of a seizure-affected next pregnancy was over threefold higher when the pre-pregnancy year was seizure-affected than when it had been seizure-free. The finding that a year's pre-pregnancy seizure freedom was associated with a reduced risk of seizures in the next pregnancy was expected. The magnitude of the greater than threefold higher seizure risk in the next pregnancy if seizures had occurred in the pre-pregnancy year was not. It identifies a group of women with epilepsy whose medical management during pregnancy warrants particular care.

items.title: Adaptive induction of NFS1 links mTOR suppression to stemness-associated plasticity in glioblastoma.
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits profound therapeutic resistance that is largely attributed to its remarkable cellular plasticity and capacity to adapt to therapeutic and environmental stress. Although suppression of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling has been extensively investigated as a therapeutic strategy, the adaptive mechanisms that limit its efficacy remain incompletely understood. Human GBM cells were subjected to sphere-forming conditions or pharmacological inhibition of mTOR signaling to evaluate stress-induced cellular responses. Proteomic profiling following mTORC2 inhibition was performed to identify adaptive metabolic alterations. Functional analyses were conducted using NFS1 cysteine desulfurase (NFS1) knockdown, orthotopic xenograft models, and publicly available datasets. Sphere-forming conditions and pharmacological inhibition of mTOR signaling induced stemness-associated changes in GBM cells. Unbiased proteomic profiling identified NFS1 as a stress-responsive protein induced by mTOR suppression. NFS1 depletion attenuated selected stemness-associated responses and sensitized GBM cells to mTOR pathway inhibition. Increased NFS1 expression was further confirmed in highly tumorigenic orthotopic xenografts, whereas exploratory analyses suggested a potential modulatory role of iron availability in this adaptive phenotype. Our findings identify NFS1 as a stress-induced metabolic dependency that emerges during adaptation to mTOR suppression in GBM. Targeting adaptive vulnerabilities by therapeutic stress, rather than constitutive oncogenic pathways alone, may represent a promising strategy for overcoming treatment resistance in malignant gliomas.

items.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and tumor microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploratory analysis of CD3 + TILs, PD-L1, and glypican-3.
items.abstract: Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the clinical diagnostic standard in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its association with the tumor microenvironment is not fully characterized. In this study, we investigated correlations between DCE-MRI parameters and immunohistochemistry features of HCC. Forty patients, six women and 34 men aged 61.5 ± 10.1 years (mean ± standard deviation) with histologically confirmed HCC were included. DCE-MRI with Gd-EOB-DTPA was performed before surgery, and quantitative parameters were calculated to reflect arterial wash-in, portal venous wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake. Pathological specimens were analyzed for programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), glypican-3, CD3+ tumor- and stromal-infiltrating lymphocytes, CD68 and CD34. CD3+ stromal lymphocytes infiltration was inversely correlated with the arterial wash-in (r = -0.47; adjusted p-value = 0.025) and several post-arterial parameters. For the other TME components, only exploratory correlations were identified, none of which were statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. CD3+ tumoral infiltration lymphocytes with arterial wash-in (r = -0.35) and transitional phase relative signal intensity (SI) (r = 0.35). Native SI was inversely correlated with PD-L1 (r = -0.32). Difference in SI between the transitional and portal phase correlated with glypican-3 expression (r = 0.32). DCE-MRI shows a moderate association with stromal infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ SIL) in HCC. Associations with other components of the TME, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ TIL), PD-L1 and Glypican-3 expression, were observed at uncorrected thresholds, but did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Question DCE-MRI constitutes the cornerstone of HCC diagnosis. Is quantitative assessment of wash-in, wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake associated with non-invasive characterization of the TME? Findings CD3⁺ SIL were associated with tumor wash-in and wash-out parameters. Exploratory associations involving CD3⁺ TIL, PD-L1, and glypican-3 lost significance after multiple-testing adjustment. Relevance statement Quantitative DCE-MRI parameters may provide additional non-invasive information regarding tumor tissue characteristics and the tumor microenvironment of HCC.

items.title: Singing-based interventions for motor and non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by disabling motor and non-motor symptoms. Although pharmacological and rehabilitation interventions improve many motor and non-motor symptoms, persistent impairments commonly remain in domains, including speech, swallowing, gait, and balance, particularly as the disease progresses. For this reason, over the past few years, alternative rehabilitative approaches, such as singing-based interventions, have been used with the aim of addressing symptoms, such as speech impairment, swallowing difficulties, respiratory dysfunction, and mood. We aim to review the evidences on the efficacy of singing interventions on motor and non-motor symptoms in patients with PD. A comprehensive literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was conducted for interventional studies published until December 2025. Results were summarized into five symptom domains: motor function, voice quality, breathing, swallowing, and quality of life. Twenty-six studies involving 1057 patients with PD were included. Singing-based interventions were associated with improvements in motor symptoms, gait, posture, voice quality, respiratory control, and maximum phonation time. Several studies also reported enhanced psychological well-being, social connectedness, and quality of life, with reductions in stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Evidence regarding swallowing outcomes was limited and inconsistent. Considerable heterogeneity in study design, intervention protocols, and outcome measures precluded meta-analysis. Singing is a promising adjunct therapy for PD rehabilitation, particularly in domains less responsive to pharmacological treatment. Further high-quality research is needed to establish standardized protocols and assess long-term benefits.

items.title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
items.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality. The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses. CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

items.title: Uncovering disability progression in people with multiple sclerosis: a practical guide.
items.abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) often experience disability progression even when receiving disease-modifying therapies that effectively suppress relapses. This phenomenon is commonly referred to as progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA). Currently, it is challenging to characterize pwMS who are experiencing disability progression in clinical practice. Existing definitions of PIRA rely primarily on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), which is biased towards ambulation and does not effectively capture the gradual accumulation of symptoms and signs across other clinical areas associated with disability progression. Here, we propose a step-by-step approach that neurologists can use in clinical practice to identify pwMS experiencing disability progression irrespective of age, EDSS, or disease duration. By using this approach, neurologists can assess the presence or absence of specific variables to help determine if disability is stable or progressing. This could enable appropriate treatments to be implemented in a timely manner, particularly as new disability-targeting therapies become available.

items.title: Seafood loss and waste as nutrient loss: Implications for nutrition security in the United States.
items.abstract: Seafood provides protein, long-chain omega-3 fatty acids, and micronutrients, yet consumption remains low in the United States. During 2014 to 2018, an estimated 22.7% of the United States edible aquatic animal food supply was lost or wasted, excluding processing by-products not sold as food. We reframe seafood loss and waste as nutrient loss and consider implications for nutrition security. This commentary draws on selected studies and official reports on intake, composition, processing, safety, loss and access. We propose nutrient-based measurement, loss prevention through product and market design, and safe, feasible recovery. An illustrative calculation links a specified processing fraction to its nutrient content, distinguishing it from nutrients that are recovered, consumed, or absorbed. Historical estimates and varied study settings limit conclusions about population benefits. Recovery could help use already-harvested seafood more effectively, provided products are safe, affordable, acceptable, and evaluated against alternative uses.

items.title: Elevational patterns in plant breeding systems and pollen limitation in Afrotropical montane grasslands.
items.abstract: Plant reproduction along elevational gradients may be limited by insufficient pollination service, variation in selfing capacity or post-pollination constraints, yet these mechanisms are rarely studied together across multiple co-occurring species. We examined how seed production, pollen limitation and selfing capacity vary along the full elevational gradient of Afromontane grasslands on Mount Cameroon. We combined a hand-pollination experiment with recordings of flower visitors at four elevations above the timberline (2300-3800 m a.s.l.). In seven zoogamous species, we quantified natural seed production, pollen limitation and indices of autonomous and facilitated selfing from controlled pollination treatments, while independently measuring visitation frequency and visitor diversity on unmanipulated plants. Natural seed production peaked at intermediate elevation and declined sharply towards the summit, where the pollen-limitation index was highest. At the highest elevation, some species produced few or no seeds even after supplemental outcrossing. Autonomous and geitonogamous selfing capacities showed no consistent elevational trends despite partial self-compatibility in several species. Visitation frequency and diversity declined towards the summit, and natural seed production increased with visitation frequency, whereas pollen limitation and selfing indices showed no clear relationships with visitation metrics. Together, our results indicate that elevational variation in reproductive success is linked to changes in pollination service, but that pollen limitation and selfing capacity do not track visitation in a simple way. No increase in selfing capacity towards the summit suggests limited potential for increased reproductive assurance through selfing under high-elevation conditions, while additional processes after pollen delivery may also constrain seed production near upper vegetation limits.

items.title: Enhanced forest temperature regulation covaries with greater heat resistance of ecosystem photosynthesis.
items.abstract: Forests regulate the land surface temperature (LST) through biophysical processes and subsequently mitigate climate warming. However, how this ecosystem-scale surface thermal regulation capacity (TRC) has evolved globally remains unknown. Here we use 20 years (2001-2020) of satellite-based LST observations to provide global evidence that TRC has significantly strengthened in global forests, as indicated by widespread declines in both the LST-air temperature slope (-0.0014 ± 0.0003 °C °C-1 yr-1; P < 0.01) and the LST-air temperature difference (-0.0268 ± 0.005 °C yr-1; P < 0.01). The observed enhancement of TRC is primarily associated with increased tree cover and warming trends. Species-rich forests exhibit higher TRC, probably through an enhanced transpiration/evapotranspiration ratio. Moreover, spatial and temporal variations in TRC, which characterize ecosystem-scale surface energy partitioning, covary with the optimal temperature for forest photosynthesis and with photosynthetic resistance to thermal stress. Our findings underscore the critical importance of conserving and restoring diverse forests to regulate surface energy balance and safeguard terrestrial carbon uptake in a hotter world.

items.title: Age and growth of the spiny butterfly ray Gymnura altavela (Elasmobranchii, Gymnuridae) in the Southwest Atlantic (in situ) and under human care in a public aquarium (ex situ): Plasticity and population patterns.
items.abstract: This study provides the first age and growth assessment of the endangered spiny butterfly ray, Gymnura altavela (Linnaeus, 1758), in the Southwest Atlantic, while also updating the growth parameters (asymptotic disc width-DW∞ and growth coefficient-k) estimated in an ex situ a marine aquarium setting. In situ growth was assessed by analyzing the vertebrae of 95 individuals captured off the southeastern coast of Brazil. The Centrum Edge and Marginal Increment analyses indicated an annual annuli formation cycle. After applying a multi-model approach, the Gompertz model was selected as the most appropriate for describing the in situ growth of both females (DW∞ = 201.0 cm and k = 0.100 year-1) and males (DW∞ = 139.4 cm and k = 0.170 year-1). In turn, ex situ growth was assessed by periodically measuring seven individuals kept in a marine aquarium for 8 years (2018-2025). The von Bertalanffy model modified by Fabens was used to estimate ex situ growth parameters for females (DW∞ = 212.1 cm and k = 0.132 year-1) and males (DW∞ = 120.1 cm and k = 0.255 year-1). A well-marked sexual size dimorphism was observed in both in situ and ex situ, with females growing more slowly but reaching larger sizes than males. G. altavela grew faster in the controlled environment (ex situ). However, reaching the maturity size earlier may not necessarily result in anticipated reproduction events and it may also have a negative effect on longevity. Comparing the growth parameters and curves estimated in situ and ex situ provides valuable insight into how this population may respond to future environmental changes and impacts.

items.title: Aquatic Macrophyte Coverage and Organic Matter Enrichment Drive Greenhouse Gas (CO 2 , CH 4 , N 2 O) Emissions in Aquaculture Ponds.
items.abstract: Freshwater aquaculture ponds differ in environmental conditions and nutrient enrichment, resulting in substantial variation in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, including methane (CH4), carbon dioxide (CO2), and nitrous oxide (N2O). However, the mechanisms linking cultured species to GHG emissions remain unclear. Here, ponds culturing fish (Micropterus salmoides), crayfish (Procambarus clarkii), and crab (Eriocheir sinensis) were compared. Fish ponds had the highest suspended particulate matter (SPM) concentration (84.23 ± 43.81 mg L-1), whereas crab ponds had the lowest (18.50 ± 12.38 mg L-1). Fish ponds were also enriched in particulate organic matter (POM) and dissolved organic carbon (DOC), whereas crayfish ponds contained more aromatic and humified dissolved organic matter (DOM). Macrophyte coverage was highest in crab ponds (36.11 ± 26.18%) and lowest in fish ponds (2.08 ± 1.65%). Fish ponds showed the highest CO2 and N2O cumulative emissions (584.06 ± 93.17 and 0.34 ± 0.04 g m-2), whereas Crab ponds had the highest CH4 cumulative emissions (6.70 ± 0.41 g m-2). Random forest analysis (RFA) identified macrophyte coverage and organic matter properties as major predictors of GHG emissions. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) revealed gas-specific pathways linking macrophyte coverage and organic matter to GHG emissions. Macrophytes and organic matter jointly promoted CH4 emissions, whereas macrophytes reduced CO2 emissions despite the positive effect of organic matter. Nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment was the main driver of N2O emissions. Aquatic macrophyte coverage and organic matter were identified as key factors. This study provides a theoretical basis for the regional selection of low-carbon aquaculture species, and the development of technologies for the efficient utilization of organic matter.

items.title: Chemotaxis-Driven Rapid Enrichment and Isolation of Phenanthrene-Degrading Bacteria Overlooked by Conventional Cultivation.
items.abstract: Microbial remediation is a promising countermeasure for organic pollutants that pose significant environmental and health risks. Conventional growth-based enrichment methods have been used for decades and successfully isolated many efficient pollutant-degrading microorganisms. However, their diminishing capacity to access previously uncultured or functionally novel microbes now poses a bottleneck for discovering next-generation bioremediation agents. This study demonstrates that chemotaxis-based enrichment can overcome this limitation and accelerate enrichment rates. After just 1-hour chemotactic enrichment, the proportion of phenanthrene-degrading bacteria and the degradation efficiency of enrichment consortia were 1.4 and 2.3 times higher, respectively, than those obtained from a 4-week enrichment culture. Moreover, because chemotaxis and conventional enrichment rely on different selection principles, they enrich distinct sets of degraders, enabling chemotaxis to access functional strains that conventional methods typically overlook. Through this approach, a unique bacterium, Stenotrophomonas sp. S62, was isolated and found to markedly enhance phenanthrene degradation under microaerobic conditions, supported by nitrate respiration via its membrane-bound nitrate reductase NarG. Contrary to traditional understanding, S62 maintained robust narG expression at dissolved-oxygen concentrations of approximately 1.4 mg/L, indicating that nitrate respiration can proceed under microaerobic stress conditions. These results establish chemotaxis-based enrichment as a rapid, efficient strategy for screening pollutant-degrading microorganisms and highlight S62 as a promising bioremediation candidate for refractory contaminated environments where oxygen is limited.

items.title: Soil lead pollution alters plant chemical profiles and herbivore responses across feeding guilds.
items.abstract: Soil pollution by metal contaminants threatens ecosystems through accumulation in plants and disruption of trophic interactions. However, how metal contaminants alter plant chemistry, including volatile and non-volatile metabolites, and whether these changes affect herbivores from distinct feeding guilds, have received little attention. We investigated how soil contamination with lead (Pb; 180 mg kg-1, the agricultural investigation value under Brazilian regulation), a relevant contaminant in agroecosystems, influences the chemical defenses of kale plants (Brassica oleracea L. var. acephala) and their interactions with the leaf-chewing Ascia monuste orseis (Godart) (Lepidoptera: Pieridae) and the phloem-feeding aphid Myzus persicae (Sulzer) (Hemiptera: Aphididae). Herbivore survival, performance, and host selection were assessed on Pb-contaminated and control plants, together with targeted and untargeted metabolic responses and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. Pb contamination reduced aphid survival and fecundity in the first generation, while lepidopteran performance remained unaffected despite Pb accumulation in adults. Both herbivore species showed reduced preference for Pb-contaminated plants, indicating that Pb-induced changes in plant traits influence host selection. Consistently, Pb contamination altered the VOC blend emitted by kale, decreasing β-myrcene levels and increasing limonene emissions. Metabolic responses were guild-dependent: Pb combined with aphid feeding significantly increased local amino acid accumulation while attenuating the aphid-induced accumulation of JA, JA-Ile, and SA, whereas caterpillar feeding on contaminated plants tended to amplify jasmonate induction, although this effect was not statistically significant. Untargeted metabolite profiling confirmed that herbivory type was the primary driver of metabolic variation, whereas Pb effects were restricted to specific hormonal and amino acid responses to herbivory. Together, these findings show that Pb contamination modulates plant responses to herbivory in a guild-dependent manner, highlighting the ecological significance of pollutant-driven changes in soil-plant-insect systems.

items.title: Bugs on drugs: Trait-specific behavioral responses to fluoxetine and clobazam in damselfly nymphs across temperatures.
items.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly exposed to psychoactive pharmaceuticals while also experiencing rapid warming, two stressors known to influence aquatic organism behavior. Yet, it remains unclear how temperature shapes the behavioral effects of these environmentally persistent compounds-whether occurring individually or as mixtures-particularly in aquatic invertebrates. Therefore, we experimentally tested the effects of a 2-week exposure to fluoxetine (average measured concentration: 0.31 μg/L), clobazam (0.95 μg/L), or their mixture (0.33 and 1.05 μg/L, respectively) on the locomotor and foraging behavior of northern damselfly (Coenagrion hastulatum) nymphs at two environmentally relevant temperatures (10 °C and 16 °C). Temperature strongly influenced locomotion and foraging behavior by reducing activity and feeding after 2 weeks of exposure, accounting for much of the observed variation across treatments. Pharmaceutical effects were comparatively trait-specific. Clobazam reduced active movement speed regardless of temperature, whereas fluoxetine decreased prey-capture success at 10 °C. Combined exposure did not, however, result in stronger detectable behavioral effects than single-compound exposure. Bioconcentration analyses revealed higher accumulation of fluoxetine than clobazam, suggesting that toxicokinetic differences contributed to the observed behavioral responses. Together, these results demonstrate that warming can substantially shape baseline predator behavior and should be considered when interpreting contaminant effects in freshwater ecosystems under ongoing climate change.

items.title: Optimizing light/dark cycle drives microbial synergy and cofactor metabolism in filamentous algae-anammox granules for zero‑aeration nitrogen removal.
items.abstract: Light/dark alternation, which periodically regulates aerobic and anoxic conditions, is a key strategy for improving nitrogen removal in algae-bacteria consortia. In this study, three light/dark cycles (2 h light:1 h dark (2L:1D), 1L:1D, and 1L:2D) were applied to filamentous algae-partial nitrification/anammox (FA-PNA) granular system, improving total nitrogen removal efficiency (NRE) by 10.9%, 28.3%, and 13.7%, respectively. 1L:1D cycle achieved superior nitrogen removal performance, with an NRE of 98.8% under zero aeration, and enriched key functional microorganisms, including Pantanalinema (19.89%), Ca. Brocadia (7.58%), Nitrosomonas (6.64%), and Denitratisoma (13.72%). Mechanistically, these enriched microbial populations exhibited enhanced coordination through increased signalling molecule levels and signalling-related gene abundances. Meanwhile, enhanced cofactor metabolic potential was observed, with higher folate and cobalamin concentrations and 6.15-10.27-fold greater abundances of B vitamins and molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis genes than 2L:1D cycle. This integrated metabolic synergy strengthened key nitrogen transformation processes, as reflected by elevated abundances of amoA/B/C in Nitrosomonas, narG/H/I in Denitratisoma, and hdh/hzs in Ca. Brocadia. Overall, appropriate light/dark alternation promoted nitrogen removal by driving metabolic synergy through signal-mediated microbial coordination and cofactor metabolic support, providing mechanistic insights for developing low-energy algal-bacterial symbiotic nitrogen removal systems.

items.title: Facilitating efficient anammox bacteria enrichment with loofah sponge: coupled roles of physical retention, slow-release carbon supply, and metabolic synergy.
items.abstract: Anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) provides an energy-efficient and sustainable strategy for nitrogen removal. However, the slow growth and challenging enrichment of anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing bacteria (AnAOB) remain key constraints on its engineering application. In this study, the biodegradable biomass material loofah sponge was introduced into the system to enrich AnAOB from nitrification-denitrification sludge and achieve a rapid commencement of the anammox process. During the AnAOB maturation period, the system achieved TIN (Total Inorganic Nitrogen) and NH4+-N removal efficiencies of 66.8% and 99.6%, respectively. Extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) analysis indicated that biofilms formed on the loofah sponge exhibited a high protein-to-polysaccharide (PN/PS) ratio, thereby enhancing microbial aggregation and facilitating AnAOB enrichment. Analysis of the microbial community structure showed that the relative abundance of the key anammox genus Candidatus Brocadia in the loofah sponge significantly increased from 0.03% in the seed sludge to 17.07%. Metagenomic analysis detected genes associated with cellulose and hemicellulose degradation, while the effluent COD profile supported gradual loofah sponge biodegradation and soluble organic matter transformation. The loofah sponge also exhibited higher abundances of genes related to central carbon metabolism, the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, and heme biosynthesis, indicating greater metabolic potential. Overall, AnAOB enrichment on loofah sponge may have resulted from the combined effects of physical biomass retention, gradual biodegradation, and associated microbial interactions. This study offers a feasible pathway for integrating agricultural waste valorization with low-carbon nitrogen removal and steers the anammox process toward greater economic and environmental sustainability.

items.title: Strain-specific temporal dynamics of fecal parasite persistence between fluorescently tagged Ninoa and Y strains of Trypanosoma cruzi during dual infections in Triatoma pallidipennis.
items.abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi, the causative agent of Chagas disease, exhibits substantial genetic diversity across Discrete Typing Units (DTUs), and phenotypic heterogeneity is well documented even among strains within the same DTU. While coinfections with multiple T. cruzi strains are commonly reported in nature, their temporal dynamics within the insect vector remain poorly understood. This study evaluated strain-specific persistence during dual infections in Triatoma pallidipennis using two fluorescently tagged T. cruzi strains, Y-DsRed and Ninoa-eGFP. Fecal parasite loads were quantified per insect at 30 and 50 days post-infection by fluorescence microscopy. At 30 days post-infection, Ninoa strains showed higher fecal parasite loads than Y strains only in single-strain infections (p.adj < 0.01), and no difference was detected between Ninoa-eGFP and Y-DsRed within the coinfection group. By 50 days post-infection, however, Ninoa-eGFP burden significantly surpassed Y-DsRed in both single and dual infections (p.adj < 0.05-0.0001), indicating progressive consolidation of this fecal persistence advantage rather than its immediate establishment. In vitro epimastigote doubling times did not differ between strains (p = 0.446), pointing away from a higher intrinsic replication rate as the basis for this advantage. Both strains remained detectable in dual-infected vectors throughout, indicating partial coexistence rather than complete competitive exclusion. These findings demonstrate time-dependent, strain-specific T. cruzi interactions within the vector, with Ninoa ultimately outperforming Y in fecal persistence. Fluorescent tagging enabled precise quantification of strain-specific dynamics without altering parasite fitness, providing a robust model for studying polyparasitism and T. cruzi transmission ecology.

items.title: Comparative toxicology of Solanaceae alkaloids reveals convergent and divergent physiological responses of generalist herbivores (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae).
items.abstract: Insect generalist herbivores feed on diverse host plants and tolerate a wide range of defensive chemicals. Many detoxification mechanisms have been identified in individual species, but it remains unclear whether different generalist herbivores employ the same resistance strategies when encountering the same host plant chemical toxins. Here, we compared the toxin tolerance, metabolic detoxification, and physiological response to solanaceous alkaloids (nicotine and tomatidine) of three polyphagous noctuid moths: Helicoverpa zea, Spodoptera frugiperda, and Trichoplusia ni. Ecological dose feeding assays revealed that, in S. frugiperda, nicotine increased mortality and both alkaloids reduced larval weight, while H. zea and T. ni were unaffected. H. zea and T. ni primarily metabolized nicotine to nicotine N-glycoside and tomatidine to tomatidine 3-phosphate, whereas no significant toxin metabolism was observed in S. frugiperda. Nicotine injection experiments and feeding assays across a gradient of dietary concentrations demonstrated similar dose-dependent patterns of uptake, glycosylation, and excretion in H. zea and T. ni. However, T. ni consistently excreted a larger fraction of nicotine and its derivatives, while H. zea exhibited higher uptake. Our results suggest that both metabolic detoxification and uptake-excretion dynamics contribute toward nicotine tolerance. Despite their common polyphagous ecology, generalist noctuids have considerable biochemical and physiological variation in their responses to the same host plant toxins suggesting that polyphagy does not imply shared detoxification strategies and that similar ecological niches can be supported by distinct metabolic and physiological processes.

items.title: Food-energy balances measurement in the Lower Danube Basin (1934-1945).
items.abstract: With the intensifying social-ecological challenges, energy accounting has re-emerged as a critical methodological framework for evaluating the material foundations of economic life. By shifting from monetary to physical units, such as joules, calories, or tons of biomass, this approach enables a biophysical assessment of production, consumption, and sustainability. Food-energy accounting offers insight into how energy flows from ecological systems into human societies, illuminating the energetic basis of subsistence, agriculture, and labor. Unlike market-based metrics, which often obscure ecological limits due to distortions in prices and policy, energy-based measures foreground questions of efficiency, equity, and environmental constraints. This article revisits the neglected contributions of Slavtcho Zagorov (1898-1970), a pioneer of energy and ecological economics whose work anticipated many of the field's central concerns. His studies, including analyses of food-energy balances in the Danubian countries before and during World War II, demonstrated how biophysical accounting can reveal the structural constraints of agricultural economies. By quantifying food and energy flows during both the prewar (1934-1938) and wartime (1940-1945) periods, Zagorov highlighted the vulnerability of food systems under shifting geopolitical and ecological conditions. His methodological implications on physical measures aligns closely with contemporary calls for alternatives to monetary indicators in evaluating food security, sustainability, and resource use. By reconstructing and contextualizing Zagorov's contributions, this study contributes to the ongoing recovery of overlooked traditions in ecological economics, reaffirming the enduring relevance of energy-based approaches for addressing today's intertwined crises of ecology, economy, and society.

items.title: Interactions among land use, climate, leaf litter traits, and consumers shape large-scale patterns of decomposition in streams of SW Europe.
items.abstract: Habitat degradation is one of the primary drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem alteration. In streams, leaf litter decomposition plays a key role in energy and nutrient cycling, which is influenced by leaf litter quality, microbial and invertebrate consumers, and environmental conditions. Land use changes alter stream habitats and can modify decomposition rates and dynamics, but large-scale assessments of these anthropogenic impacts remain limited. We explored the consequences of major land use changes (tree plantations, agricultural land, and urban settlements) on stream ecosystems by comparing sites in human-impacted catchments with reference unimpacted sites (i.e., surrounded by native vegetation) across several regions of southwestern Europe encompassing a wide climatic gradient. We quantified decomposition rates of multiple leaf litter types to evaluate the interaction between leaf litter traits and environmental variation, exploring changes in associated invertebrate assemblages. Overall, land use changes reduced total and microbial decomposition rates, with agriculture exerting the strongest effects, and caused marked shifts in invertebrate assemblages including replacement of sensitive by tolerant species and reduced detritivore richness, mainly in urban streams. Climatic variability seemed to modulate these responses, with seasonal climates showing higher vulnerability to impacts. Lastly, leaf litter types differed in their sensitivity to detect degradation, although no consistent trait-based patterns were observed. Our results show that land use changes alter stream ecosystems across climatic gradients, highlighting the urgent need to integrate environmental and biological drivers across spatial scales in watershed management and to provide actionable baselines to optimize riparian restoration and buffer the effects of ongoing climate change.

items.title: Non-land-use forcing significantly drives projected trends of atmospheric black carbon over Africa: Implications for mitigation strategies.
items.abstract: Black carbon (BC) plays a critical role in climate forcing and poses significant health risks, yet its trends and drivers remain poorly constrained across Africa. Here, we quantify the relative contributions of land-use and non-land-use forcing to the projected trends of BC using the Meteorological Research Institute Earth System Model version 2.0 (MRI-ESM2-0) under the Aerosol Chemistry Model Intercomparison Project (AerChemMIP). A variance decomposition framework is applied to SSP370SST and SSP370SST-SSP126Lu simulations to isolate land-use from non-land-use forcing. The MRI-ESM2-0 model reproduces spatial patterns well (r > 0.8, p 0.7 μg m-3) occurs in Central and West Africa, while low (<0.1) concentrations occur in parts of North Africa and the island of Madagascar. Projected trends reveal a statistically significant increase in BC (p < 0.05) over North and West Africa, whereas Central and Southern Africa show decreasing trends in BC until 2100. The projected trends are primarily driven by non-land-use emissions, with the influence of hydroclimatic changes, while land-use forcing is most pronounced in Central and Southern Africa. These findings highlight the need for region-specific mitigation strategies to control future BC concentrations across Africa effectively.

items.title: Elevation-dependent coordination between stomatal and vein densities among leaf habits and growth forms in a subtropical forest.
items.abstract: Stomatal and leaf venation traits are important structural components associated with plant gas exchange and water transport, but their variation along environmental gradients may depend on plant functional strategies. We investigated whether stomatal and vein traits exhibit coordinated yet trait-specific patterns across an elevational gradient, and whether such patterns vary with leaf habit and growth form in a subtropical forest. We examined 12 woody species distributed along a 300-1360 m elevational gradient on Lushan Mountain, China. Stomatal length (SL), stomatal density (SD), and vein density (VD) were quantified from cleared leaves, with species × elevation means used as observational units. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to evaluate associations of traits with elevation, leaf habit (evergreen vs. deciduous), and growth form (shrub vs. tree), and to test elevation-dependent variation in the SD-VD relationship. Stomatal length and stomatal density showed no significant elevational trends, whereas vein density increased with elevation, indicating contrasting responses among leaf anatomical traits. Stomatal density differed among combinations of leaf habit and growth form, with a significant leaf habit × growth form interaction and higher SD in deciduous trees than in other groups. Across species and elevations, SD was positively associated with VD, but the strength of this relationship varied nonlinearly along the gradient, with the strongest association occurring at intermediate elevations (∼800 m) corresponding to the evergreen-deciduous mixed forest zone. Our findings demonstrate that elevation does not generate uniform changes across leaf anatomical traits. Instead, trait variation depends on environmental context and functional strategies, with leaf habit and growth form jointly influencing stomatal density and stomatal-vein coordination. Considering trait relationships in addition to individual traits provides new insights into how plants organize leaf structure across heterogeneous environments.

items.title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills.
items.abstract: Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. In addition, females whose infants throw more tantrums show a greater probability of fetal loss, consistent with observations from other species where living offspring can interfere in parental reproduction. Finally, females who lose a fetus show greater subsequent reproductive success (produce more surviving infants and show shorter inter-birth intervals) than females who give birth but their infants die soon after birth. These findings suggest that fetal loss may represent an adaptive physiological response to the energetic constraints imposed by overlapping gestation and maternal care, potentially limiting the fitness costs associated with short inter-birth intervals and concurrent investment in multiple dependent offspring.
