items.title: On the limits of detection of higher-order epistatic interactions.
items.abstract: The function of microbial communities is often dominated by additive and pairwise interactions, raising the question of whether this reflects intrinsic biological simplicity or fundamental limits of detection. Here, we leverage the theory of fitness landscapes to bridge microbial ecology and genetics, and show that this apparent simplicity is a generic consequence of structural and statistical constraints rather than evidence for intrinsically weak higher-order interactions. We separate the detectability of individual epistatic interactions from their contribution to functional variance, and demonstrate that local k-order interactions suffer from exponential noise amplification while their contributions to total variance are intrinsically suppressed by order-dependent geometric dilution arising from the combinatorial structure of the landscape. Applying this framework to a fully sampled 210 experimental microbial landscape, we find that only first- and second-order interactions are distinguishable from experimental noise. Furthermore, generalized Lotka-Volterra landscapes reveal that experimental noise alone can generate the illusion of higher-order structure in communities where all direct mechanistic interactions are pairwise and indirect interactions are weak. Our findings identify universal, order-dependent limits on the quantification of epistasis that apply to high-dimensional landscapes across ecology and genetics, providing a principled foundation for rational community design.

items.title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra .
items.abstract: The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host-microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. This study investigates the cospeciation and molecular adaptations of Curvibacter to its host Hydra, a well-established model for the study of host-microbe interactions. We provide strong evidence of cospeciation, as demonstrated by phylogenetic congruence between different Hydra species and their corresponding Curvibacter symbionts, along with preferential recolonization of germ-free Hydra by their native Curvibacter strains. Comparative genomic analyses reveal that host-associated Curvibacter strains exhibit distinct metabolic and biosynthetic adaptations compared to their free-living relatives. Specifically, the enrichment of proteins linked to host glycan interactions, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), DNA metabolic processes, ABC transport, sugar metabolism, and bacterial chemotaxis highlights specialized adaptations of Curvibacter symbionts within the Hydra glycocalyx. Importantly, some of these signatures are only detectable within the Hydra vulgaris-associated Curvibacter subgroup, emphasizing the need to examine host-specific adaptations at a finer taxonomic resolution. Functional experiments identify a symbiont-specific EPS operon as a factor for host colonization, thereby establishing its role in facilitating symbiont specificity and stability. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms driving host-microbe coevolution and highlight the evolutionary forces shaping microbial specialization within host-symbiont relationships.

items.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco.
items.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor-odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a 'trunk-branch' network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR-Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

items.title: Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics.
items.abstract: Effective delivery of RNA therapeutics to the brain remains challenging due to the multiple barriers of the central nervous system (CNS). To probe molecular scaffolds that could help overcome these barriers, we analysed the pharmaceutical profiles of over 100 CNS-active drugs and identified hydroxyzine (HX) as a promising scaffold for designing ionizable lipids with improved brain-targeting properties. Specifically, HX1 liquid nanoparticles (LNPs) achieved robust mRNA delivery to the brain through multiple trafficking pathways across CNS barriers. HX1 LNPs also enabled efficient gene editing in mouse brains via co-delivery of CRISPR mRNA and guide RNA and effectively delivered luciferase mRNA to the brain of a non-human primate. Moreover, HX1 LNPs carrying Il10 mRNA mitigated radiation-induced brain injury in mice, highlighting their potential for preventive treatment in the presence of intact CNS barriers. These findings establish HX1 LNPs as a promising translational platform for delivering therapeutic mRNAs and genome-editing components to the brain.

items.title: Temporal cortical gray matter volume relates to symptom improvement during cognitive behavioral therapy for depression.
items.abstract: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a first-line treatment for depression, yet treatment responses vary considerably. Understanding neurobiological factors associated with symptom improvement may help elucidate mechanisms underlying therapeutic change. This study investigated whether baseline cortical gray matter volume (GMV) is associated with reductions in depressive symptom severity during CBT. Therefore, n = 52 patients with unipolar affective disorders and at least mild depressive symptoms (according to BDI-II) and n = 42 healthy controls underwent clinical assessments and structural MRI at baseline; depressive symptom severity was reassessed after six months of outpatient CBT. Multiple regression analyses examined associations between pre-treatment cortical GMV and reductions in depressive symptoms under false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional models included anxiety, perceived stress, and childhood trauma as predictors. Compared to controls, patients exhibited significantly higher depressive symptom severity at baseline and greater symptom reduction over time (all p < 0.001). Within patients, baseline GMV of the right middle temporal gyrus (MTG) was significantly associated with symptom reduction (baseline-follow-up; β = 0.55, pFDR = 0.033). Right MTG volume accounted for additional variance in symptom reduction beyond established clinical variables (ΔR² = 0.15). Group differences in GMV did not remain significant following FDR correction. These findings suggest that temporal gyrus GMV is associated with symptom improvement following CBT in unipolar depression, extending the focus beyond traditionally emphasized limbic regions. Preserved temporal morphology may support cognitive and emotional processes engaged during CBT, underscoring the relevance of temporal cortical structure for understanding the neurobiological correlates of psychotherapy response.

items.title: From attachment insecurity to maladaptive addictive behaviors in trauma-exposed adults: The mediating role of emotion regulation difficulties and traumatic stress.
items.abstract: Attachment insecurity is considered a core vulnerability for maladaptive coping and addictive behaviors, particularly among trauma-exposed individuals. Difficulties in emotion regulation may serve as a key mechanism linking attachment insecurity to addictive behaviors, yet integrative models in trauma-exposed adults remain limited. Using a cross-sectional sample of 203 trauma-exposed adults, this study examined associations among adult attachment insecurity, emotion regulation difficulties, posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS), and maladaptive addictive behaviors, including problematic alcohol use (PAU) and problematic social media use (PSMU). Attachment insecurity was associated with greater emotion regulation difficulties and higher PTSS. Indirect effects on PAU were mediated through both emotion regulation difficulties and PTSS, whereas effects on PSMU occurred only through emotion regulation difficulties. Findings suggest that PAU and PSMU may be driven by partially distinct addictive mechanisms and highlight emotion regulation as a central clinical target in attachment- and trauma-informed interventions for addictive behaviors.

items.title: Exploring Corresponding Cutpoints for Hypoglycaemia Awareness Questionnaire (HypoA-Q) Impaired Awareness Subscale in Relation to the Gold and Clarke Measures: A Post Hoc Analysis From the Hypo-METRICS Study.
items.abstract: The Hypoglycaemia Awareness Questionnaire-Impaired Awareness subscale (HypoA-Q/IA) was developed to enhance impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia (IAH) assessment, addressing methodological deficiencies of the established Gold and Clarke measures. An IAH cutpoint (HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12) was identified from a clamp study in Type 1 diabetes (T1D). We explored cutpoints in relation to Gold and Clarke measures, and their co-occurrence, in the larger, real-world observational Hypo-METRICS study, in people with T1D (pwT1D) and insulin-treated Type 2 diabetes (pwT2D). Hypo-METRICS recruited pwT1D or pwT2D with ≥ 1 hypoglycaemic event in the previous 3 months. IAH was defined as Gold ≥ 4, Clarke ≥ 4 and/or HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. Bidirectional ROC analysis was performed between HypoA-Q/IA and Gold/Clarke cutpoints. Questionnaires were completed by 232 pwT1D and 285 pwT2D (male 47% vs. 62%, p < 0.001; median age 49 vs. 63 years, p < 0.001; HbA1c 7.3% vs. 7.4%, p = 0.03). IAH prevalence was 24% by Gold ≥ 4, 16% by Clarke ≥ 4 and 7% by HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. ROC analysis yielded HypoA-Q/IA cutpoints of ≥ 7 against Gold ≥ 4 (AUC 0.87) and ≥ 9 against Clarke ≥ 4 (AUC 0.89), and cutpoints of Gold ≥ 4 (AUC 0.87) and Clarke ≥ 3 (AUC 0.93) against HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. Of those with IAH by either measure, 24% were identified by both HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12 and Gold ≥ 4, and 32% by both HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12 and Clarke ≥ 4, with lower overlap in T2D than T1D. HypoA-Q/IA cutpoints corresponding to legacy IAH cutpoints (≥ 7-9) were lower than the clamp-derived threshold (≥ 12), suggesting ≥ 12 may identify a subgroup with more severe IAH. These cutpoints enable cross-study comparison; prospective validation against severe hypoglycaemia risk is needed.

items.title: Exercise-induced redox remodeling: A scoping review of hormetic adaptation and translational clinical implications from animal and human studies.
items.abstract: BackgroundExercise-induced reactive oxygen and nitrogen species can be both damaging and adaptive; however, evidence from animal and human studies supporting a unified redox remodeling framework and its clinical impact has not been fully synthesized. This scoping review, to our knowledge, is the first to systematically map preclinical and clinical studies on exercise-induced redox modulation, delineate patterns across exercise modalities, intensities, and populations, and highlight key gaps for future research.MethodologyThis registered scoping review (PROSPERO: CRD420251144680) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidance. Three major databases (PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science; 2000-2025) were systematically searched using a prespecified exercise-redox strategy. Original quantitative human and animal studies involving structured exercise with quantifiable intensity and at least one redox biomarker were included. Two independent reviewers screened the records and charted study design, populations, exercise dose, redox outcomes, and functional or clinical endpoints using a piloted standardized form for thematic synthesis.ResultsA total of 141 studies met the inclusion criteria (37 animal and 104 human studies). In animal models, chronic aerobic, resistance, and combined training reduced oxidative damage (MDA, TBARS, carbonyls, and nitrotyrosine), downregulated pro-oxidant enzymes (Nox2), and upregulated antioxidant and cytoprotective systems (superoxide dismutase, CAT, GPx, Nrf2, PGC-1α, and Prdx2), with improvements in cardiovascular, renal, metabolic, and neurocentric endpoints. In humans, acute high-intensity exercise typically induced transient oxidative "eustress," followed by mobilization of antioxidant defenses, whereas chronic exercise programs (≥6 weeks) shifted basal redox status toward a more reduced, vasculoprotective milieu across healthy, athletic, and clinical populations.ConclusionsEvidence from diverse preclinical models and clinical populations converges on a conserved hormetic redox remodeling paradigm in response to exercise. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the absence of formal quality appraisal, substantial heterogeneity across studies, and the scoping review design. Future trials should use harmonized, multicompartment redox panels, consider individual redox phenotypes, and carefully control nutritional context to optimize mechanistic insight and clinical translation.

items.title: Dimensions of Consciousness in Organisms.
items.abstract: Consciousness research has traditionally focused on neural systems and has often treated consciousness as a late evolutionary innovation associated with complex brains. However, accumulating evidence from unicellular organisms, plants, and diverse animal taxa suggests that cognition and consciousness may be more broadly distributed across life. We propose a multidimensional framework of consciousness grounded in the Cellular Basis of Consciousness (CBC) theory and the concepts of the cellular senome and the multicellular N-space Episenome. Six universal dimensions of consciousness are identified and examined across biological scales: state, awareness, memory, attention, perception, and action. We argue that these dimensions are not independent faculties but interdependent manifestations of a unified informational architecture. The senome, conceived as the totality of a cell's sensory experiences and bioelectrical interactions, continuously integrates internal and external information to maintain self-referential awareness and adaptive competence. In multicellular organisms, overlapping individual cellular senomes form a supracellular N-space episenome, a collective informational space-time matrix that coordinates organism-wide cognition and behavior to effect seamless holobionts. Within this framework, organismal consciousness is localized not only to nervous systems but represents the collective cellular interactions of organism-wide informational systems that sense, remember, attend, perceive, and act in manner allowing survival and evolution. In this senomically-based consciousness framework, evolution is viewed as the progressive elaboration of these fundamental dimensions rather than the origin of entirely novel conscious faculties. This multidimensional perspective provides a unified conceptual framework for investigating consciousness across all living systems and offers new directions for empirical and theoretical research into the origins, mechanisms, and evolutionary trajectory of conscious experience.

items.title: Training Interbrain Synchrony through Dyadic Neurofeedback Modulates Empathy-for-Pain.
items.abstract: Dyadic neurofeedback offers a socially grounded approach for modulating neural processes that unfold between interacting individuals. While recent work demonstrates that dyadic neurofeedback can enhance inter-brain synchrony during interaction, whether its effects extend beyond the trained dyad remains unclear. Here, we examined whether dyadic neurofeedback targeting inter-brain synchrony in the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) is associated with changes in empathy-for-pain toward unfamiliar social targets. One hundred and eighty-six participants, randomly assigned to dyads, completed three neurofeedback training sessions within one week. Feedback was contingent on real-time IFG inter-brain synchrony in the neurofeedback group or on prerecorded signals in the sham-feedback control group. Empathy-for-pain was assessed before and after training. IFG inter-brain synchrony increased significantly across sessions in the neurofeedback group but not in the control group. Empathy-for-pain ratings showed different trajectories across conditions in the primary raw-data analysis, decreasing significantly in the sham-feedback group while remaining relatively stable in the neurofeedback group. A secondary analysis adjusting for a previously observed task-specific test-retest decline showed a significant increase in the neurofeedback group. Individuals with lower baseline trait empathy showed larger training-related increases in IFG inter-brain synchrony. Network analyses suggested broader changes involving IFG-IPL connectivity. Structural equation modeling further identified significant associations among training-related intra-brain synchrony, inter-brain synchrony, and empathy-for-pain change, consistent with the proposed relationship among these processes. Together, the findings indicate that dyadic neurofeedback can modulate IFG inter-brain synchrony across repeated training and may influence the trajectory of empathy-for-pain responding beyond the immediate training partner.

items.title: Racism and Cannabis outcomes among Asian American adults: The role of negative emotions in responses to experiencing racism.
items.abstract: Asian American individuals constitute one of the fastest-growing racial minoritized groups in the U.S., yet there is limited research on cannabis use and misuse among these individuals. Although Asian American persons are less likely to use cannabis than other racial groups, when they do use, they are at higher risk of cannabis use disorder (CUD). Asian American individuals underutilize substance use treatment, which may exacerbate cannabis-related problems. Minority stress-based models posit that stressors such as racism increase negative affect, which may be associated with using substances like cannabis to cope with such distress. Although racism is related to negative affect and cannabis use among Asian American individuals, this is the first study to test whether racism-related negative affect is associated with cannabis-related outcomes among Asian American individuals, and whether the relation of racism to cannabis outcomes occurs via racism-related negative affect. Asian American adults who endorsed cannabis use (N = 116; 62.1% male, Mage = 38) completed an online survey. Experiencing more racism was associated with greater racism-related negative affect, cannabis use quantity, and more cannabis-related problems. Multiple indirect effects analyses indicated that experiences of racism were associated with cannabis-related problems via racism-related negative affect, but not depression or anxiety broadly. This study is the first to show that experiences of racism predict cannabis use quantity and cannabis-related problems among Asian American adults, with racism-related negative affect playing an important role.

items.title: Linking Self-Efficacy to Dropout Intentions in Youth Soccer: The Role of Engagement and Coaching.
items.abstract: Youth dropout represents a challenge for federations. Although research has identified dropout correlates, less is known about how individual and team factors jointly shape players' intentions to persist or withdraw. Building on a social-cognitive perspective, this study tested a moderated mediation model in which sport self-efficacy was associated with lower dropout intentions through sport engagement, with empowering and directive coaching as moderators. Data were collected from 2,195 players (94.9% male; aged 11-14 years) nested within 155 soccer teams, together with reports from coaches and sport psychologists from the Youth and School Sector of the Italian Soccer Federation. Self-efficacy was associated with higher engagement, which in turn was linked to lower dropout intentions, suggesting that confidence in one's abilities may sustain the vigor, dedication, and absorption needed to remain connected to sport. Empowering coaching strengthened both the negative engagement-dropout association and the indirect link between self-efficacy and dropout intentions, indicating that a supportive environment helps players capitalize on their motivational resources. Directive coaching neither strengthened nor weakened these relationships. These findings advance understanding of dropout by showing that personal and team factors play distinct yet complementary roles: personal resources foster engagement, whereas the coach-created environment supports its translation into lower dropout intentions.

items.title: Sleep-stage dynamics in depression: Altered stage distribution and N2 persistence, with incremental information from distribution entropy beyond demographic and subjective clinical measures.
items.abstract: Depression involves sleep complaints not fully captured by polysomnography. We examined whether objective sleep-stage dynamics were associated with documented depressive disorder after accounting for apnea and sedative use, whether associations persisted after anxiety adjustment, and whether distribution entropy added information beyond self-reports. In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study of patients undergoing clinically indicated polysomnography (n = 303; 139 with and 164 without documented depressive disorder; non-depressed clinical comparators, not healthy controls), nine objective features, selected from 678 candidates by exploratory screening, were tested in progressively adjusted logistic models with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control across nine features. Sensitivity analyses addressed anxiety, sleep quality, and medication classes. After adjustment for demographics, night-time sedative use, and apnea-hypopnea index, lower sleep-stage distribution entropy (OR 0.63), longer N2 bout duration (OR 1.52), lower total transition rate (OR 0.66), and lower N2 → N1 transition probability (OR 0.55) remained associated with documented depressive disorder (all q < 0.05). Directions were preserved in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI; n = 195) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) ≥15 exclusion (n = 241) samples; in the latter, none remained FDR-significant (q = 0.054-0.106). In this sleep-clinic sample, adding entropy to a demographic-subjective model increased apparent AUC from 0.78 to 0.81; optimism-corrected ΔAUC 0.034 (point estimate). Conditional on covariates, documented depressive disorder was associated with altered sleep-stage distribution and continuity-related dynamics, including greater N2 persistence. Residual medication and indication confounding cannot be excluded; attenuation after anxiety adjustment limits specificity. These exploratory findings require replication.

items.title: Face-to-face psychotherapy as a straw man in trials of therapist-guided internet interventions: A re-analysis of treatment integrity.
items.abstract: Three meta-analyses have synthesized trials that directly compared 2 modalities of cognitive-behavior therapy: Therapist-guided internet intervention (iCBT) versus face-to-face psychotherapy (fCBT). These meta-analyses have concluded that iCBT has similar effects as fCBT across various disorders. However, it remains unclear whether the included trials have implemented fCBT according to minimum criteria of treatment integrity. This research presents a re-analysis of treatment integrity of trials included in the most recent meta-analysis (Hedmann-Lagerlöf et al., 2023). We included 23 trials out of the original 31 trials. We coded 3 key criteria of treatment integrity: (1) Use of full-length evidence-based treatment manual; (2) use of professional therapists; (3) specific training for therapists. Only 2 trials (8.7%) out of the included 23 trials fulfilled all three treatment integrity criteria. Eleven trials (47.8%) fulfilled 0 or 1 criterion. The results of the 2 trials that fulfilled minimum treatment integrity criteria showed an advantage for fCBT, in the magnitude of a small to moderate effect size (SMD=0.37, 95% CI [0.13, 0.62], p=0.003, I 2=0%). Our re-analysis suggests that fCBT in iCBT trials is typically implemented in a restricted way that does neither meet methodological standards nor evidence-based recommendations for good clinical practice. Thus, currently available trials provide no evidence for the claim that iCBT and fCBT have comparable effects. If anything, the scarce available evidence suggests a superiority of face-to-face psychotherapy.

items.title: Acute Interventions for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Alcohol Misuse in Women Exposed to Sexual Assault: Protocol for a Phased Randomization Trial (Project SARAH).
items.abstract: Sexual assault can have devastating consequences for survivors, including posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol misuse. Interventions provided in the initial months following a sexual assault can prevent the development of chronic problems. Early interventions that are brief, accessible, and focused on shared vulnerabilities may improve efficacy. Project SARAH (Sexual Assault Recovery and Hope) is designed to test fear and reward learning as processes underlying recovery following sexual assault and to elucidate efficacious approaches for brief interventions to address PTSD and alcohol misuse. A phased, doubly randomized, and single-masked clinical trial is being conducted to test the efficacy of acute intervention approaches that target (1) the fear system underlying PTSD with imaginal exposure or (2) the reward system underlying alcohol use with alcohol skills training, comparing these approaches to supportive counseling via telehealth for reducing PTSD and problematic drinking. The interventions are tested in a sample of adult female sexual assault survivors. The phased randomization study design allows for comparisons between imaginal exposure, alcohol skills training, and their combination with the active control, supportive counseling, as well as to test mechanisms of recovery. The study was funded in 2019. After modifications to include remote procedures, necessitated by the COVID-19 pandemic, participant enrollment began in March 2021 and ended in December 2025, and our final follow-up was completed in May 2026. We enrolled 82 participants. Analysis of main outcomes (PTSD severity and alcohol use) and dissemination of main outcomes are expected by the summer of 2027. This design is significant for exploring PTSD and alcohol recovery pathways acutely following sexual assault.

items.title: Assessing Psychosocial and Supportive Care Needs of Families With Children and Adolescents Diagnosed With Cancer Predisposition Syndromes: Protocol for the KiTDS-Care Mixed Methods Study.
items.abstract: Cancer predisposition syndromes (CPSs) are identified in approximately 10% of pediatric patients with cancer, and the number of children known to be affected by CPSs is steadily increasing. Families of children and adolescents with a CPS face substantial psychosocial challenges, including uncertainty regarding genetic risk, communication, long-term surveillance requirements, and concerns about future health outcomes. Despite these challenges, little is known about the psychosocial burden, supportive care needs, and current care situation of affected families in Germany. The KiTDS-Care (Children with Tumor Predisposition Syndrome and their Families-Analysis of the current Care Situation and Support Needs, and Derivation of Care Recommendations) study aims to (1) comprehensively assess the current psychosocial care landscape, psychosocial burden, and supportive care needs of families with children and adolescents diagnosed with a CPS in Germany and (2) develop recommendations for improving psychosocial and family-centered care based on the study findings. KiTDS-Care is a mixed methods study. First, a systematic review will synthesize existing evidence on the psychosocial experiences and support needs of families affected by a CPS. Second, a nationwide cross-sectional survey will be conducted among parents and adolescents or children aged ≥7 years to assess depression, anxiety, quality of life, supportive care needs, and health care use using standardized questionnaires. Finally, qualitative semistructured interviews with families and health care professionals will explore psychosocial experiences, barriers to care, and perceived gaps in existing support services in greater depth. Quantitative data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods, while qualitative data will be analyzed using structured content analysis. On the basis of the integrated findings, recommendations for psychosocial care will be developed and refined with input from families and health care professionals. The study is funded by German Cancer Aid for 36 months from October 2024. Data collection for the systematic review began in January 2025. Recruitment for the cross-sectional survey and qualitative interviews started in May 2025 and will continue until April 2027. A sample of 90 families is planned. As of January 2026, participant recruitment is ongoing, and 52 participants from 24 families have been enrolled. Data analysis is expected to be completed in July 2027, and publication of the primary study results is anticipated in October 2028. The KiTDS-Care study will provide comprehensive insights into the psychosocial situation and supportive care needs of families affected by a CPS in childhood and adolescence. The findings are expected to identify gaps in current care structures and inform the development of targeted, family-centered psychosocial support services for affected families in Germany. items.title: Children's understanding of cancer: the role of age and direct illness experience.
items.abstract: This study examined how age and direct cancer experience influence children's understanding of cancer. Participants were 104 children aged 6-14 years, including 52 pediatric oncology patients and 52 healthy peers. Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted to assess children's understanding across four domains: cancer identification, perceived severity, prognosis, and causal attribution. Data were analyzed using a mixed-methods approach. Qualitative responses were coded using content analysis with inductively derived categories, transformed into categorical variables for quantitative analyses. Logistic and ordinal regression analyses examined associations with age and illness experience, and multiple correspondence analysis explored co-occurring response profiles. Age was the primary predictor of understanding. Older children demonstrated more accurate identification of cancer [odds ratio (OR) = 1.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.02-1.08), p = .002) and endorsed mechanistic explanations involving external (OR = 1.03, 95% CI [1.00-1.06], p = .041) or uncontrollable causes (OR = 1.03, 95% CI [1.00-1.06], p = .053). Younger children relied on intuitive explanations, including anecdotal and contagion-based reasoning, regardless of illness experience. Compared to healthy peers, children with cancer were less likely to perceive the illness as life-threatening (OR = 0.04, 95% CI [0.004-0.312], p = .003) and more likely to consider it curable. However, direct experience did not enhance accuracy, and did not substantially alter explanatory frameworks. Findings highlight the central role of development in shaping children's understanding of cancer. Younger children may be particularly vulnerable to misconceptions, emphasizing the importance of age-appropriate explanations to support adjustment and engagement with care.

items.title: Labor Unions and Better Health.
items.abstract: Social-class inequities in health arise from power imbalances in our political-economic system. However, through labor-union organizing, workers can build power to improve their life chances and health. In our review, we describe the rich historical, theoretical, and mechanistic evidence linking unions and health and critically evaluate the state of quantitative research on the topic. Most individual-level and ecological studies have estimated small beneficial or null union-health associations. However, as we describe, the studies are limited in number, particularly outside the Global North, and face many technical and conceptual challenges, including feedback loops between unions and societies' political-economic contexts. We conclude with recommendations for enhancing the rigor and utility of union-health research, including by richly contextualizing studies' findings and by answering questions raised by workers themselves. As social and economic inequities intensify and workers face heightening attacks on their well-being, unions remain crucial organizations for advancing health justice.

items.title: Effects of music medicine on anxiety among primigravida mothers of preterm neonates: The CalM MOM randomised controlled trial protocol.
items.abstract: Preterm birth and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) admission are significant stressors that heighten maternal anxiety. Although RCTs have reported that music-based interventions used alongside usual care (UC) are effective and low-cost in reducing maternal anxiety, evidence from India remains limited. Primary objective is to assess the impact of listening to recorded classical Indian Instrumental Saraswati Veena music (Ragas Kalyani and Hindolam) (30-minutes/day over 7-days) alongside UC on maternal anxiety (STAI-state anxiety) of primigravida women with preterm neonates in the NICU. Secondary objectives measure changes in anxiety (Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale (PASS)), maternal-infant bonding, breast milk volume, and neonatal body weight. This three-arm parallel-group, superiority RCT among primigravida mothers with anxiety (screened using PASS) of preterm neonates (30-36 weeks of gestation, admitted to NICU) delivered vaginally at Government Lady Goschen Hospital, Mangalore. The intervention arm will receive Music Medicine (MM), the comparator arm Nature Sounds (NS), and the control arm UC. Participant blinding is not feasible (auditory intervention), and they serve as their own outcome-assessors (self-reported questionnaires); investigators and the independent statistician will remain blinded. Personnel interacting with participants are blinded to study objectives; enrolment/allocation staff blinded to the randomization sequence, and assessment staff blinded to group identity. Randomization will employ a STATA-generated, permuted stratified block design stratified by baseline anxiety severity and gestational age (Allocation concealment: Sequentially Numbered, Opaque, Sealed Envelopes; Allocation Ratio: 1:1:1). Sample size (66/arm; total N = 198) was determined through a simulation-based power analysis (5,000 iterations, base-R), assuming an MCID of 4 (MM) and 2 (NS) on the STAI, residual SD of ~8, powered at 80% (α = 0.05). Blinded sample-size re-estimation will be conducted at 50% enrollment completion. Primary powered analysis will employ ANCOVA (baseline-adjusted), and Secondary (exploratory) analyses will utilize a linear mixed-effects model for longitudinal continuous data with time × group interaction. Clinical Trial Registry of India; CTRI/2025/06/088896; URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTM0Mzg0&Enc=&userName= Protocol version: Version 03, July 07, 2026.

items.title: Parent Anxiety and Response to a Telehealth Intervention for Hypoglycemia Fear: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
items.abstract: Parents of young children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) frequently report fear of hypoglycemia (FH), which can impact their diabetes management. REDCHiP (Reducing Emotional Distress for Childhood Hypoglycemia in Parents) is a telehealth-delivered cognitive behavioral intervention shown to reduce FH, but less is known about which parents benefit most. This secondary analysis examined whether pretreatment parent anxiety moderated REDCHiP's effects and explored responder patterns by intervention arm and pretreatment anxiety. This was a secondary analysis of a large, randomized clinical trial comparing REDCHiP to an attention control condition (ATTN). We assessed outcomes before treatment (time 1) and 3 months after treatment (time 3). Our primary outcome was parental FH at time 3, adjusted for time 1 FH. The original trial used validated measures of parent FH and general anxiety. We evaluated parent anxiety at time 1 as both a categorical variable (clinically elevated or not) and a continuous variable (centered). We defined responders as parents achieving a reduction of ≥0.5 SDs in FH from time 1 to time 3. An analysis of covariance tested the treatment arm by anxiety interaction, with sensitivity analyses modeling anxiety continuously. There was no significant treatment arm by anxiety interaction when modeling parent anxiety as either a categorical or continuous variable (P>.05). However, exploratory analyses found that the adjusted mean time 3 FH was numerically lower among REDCHiP parents than ATTN parents with clinically elevated anxiety. Among parents with elevated anxiety, 78.6% (22/28) of REDCHiP parents met our responder criterion compared with 47.4% (9/19) of ATTN parents. Among parents with elevated anxiety, the adjusted odds of meeting the responder criterion were higher for REDCHiP than ATTN parents (odds ratio 6.35, 95% CI 1.47-29.00). While time 1 parent anxiety did not significantly moderate treatment response, exploratory analyses suggested a potentially meaningful pattern among parents with clinically elevated anxiety. As telehealth-delivered behavioral interventions expand in pediatric type 1 diabetes care, secondary analyses of participant characteristics may help guide targeted implementation and enhance treatment benefit.

items.title: The human hippocampus supports auditory coding and multisensory integration.
items.abstract: The hippocampus receives convergent input from multiple sensory systems, yet in humans it has been studied almost exclusively through vision. Here we examine how the hippocampus contributes to sensory processing beyond the visual modality and to the multisensory integration of visual information with these other modalities. Participants were exposed to multiple repetitions of short naturalistic movie clips, each presented in four formats: auditory-only, visual-only, congruent audiovisual, and incongruent audiovisual (audio and video from different movies). Using high-resolution fMRI, we measured univariate activation and multivariate representations across the longitudinal axis and subfields of the human hippocampus. Whereas univariate analyses detected only visual responses across hippocampal subregions, with no activation for auditory stimuli and no benefit of congruent stimuli, multivariate analyses revealed robust representations of both auditory and visual scenes. The posterior hippocampus showed enhanced pattern similarity for congruent stimuli relative to unisensory stimuli, especially in the left hemisphere, demonstrating multisensory facilitation. The anterior hippocampus showed crossmodal decoding between auditory and visual versions of the same clip, driven by the right hemisphere, suggesting a more abstract representation. Finally, whole-brain searchlight analyses revealed parallel effects in cortical regions known to support multisensory integration. These findings advance understanding of auditory and multisensory coding in the human hippocampus, revealing specialization and lateralization along its longitudinal axis.

items.title: "It absolutely enlarged my world": Exploring in-person and virtual performing arts programming for dementia care dyads.
items.abstract: Arts-based programs are increasingly used to support people living with dementia and their care partners; however, there has been a limited focus on multi-modal, participatory performing arts programs offered in both virtual and in-person formats. We completed an evaluation of the Lincoln Center Moments (LCM) program, a free dyadic arts program grounded in four pillars: Validation/Personhood, Social Engagement, Self-Expression, and Artistic Stimulation. An exploratory mixed-methods program evaluation was conducted with 23 dyads (N = 46). Quantitative measures included program satisfaction, social engagement, and arts engagement. Post-session interviews were coded using an evaluative framework aligned with program pillars. Program satisfaction was high across both modalities. Care-partner-reported arts engagement for PLWD increased from pre- to post-season among the in-person subgroup but not the virtual subgroup; modality-specific analyses were exploratory. Social engagement scores were similar across formats, although in-person attendees were more likely to report friendships with others. Qualitative data supported all four LCM pillars. LCM was perceived as engaging and supportive by participants in both virtual and in-person settings. Participants who were initially hesitant to engage described greater comfort and willingness to participate over time. Participant feedback suggests that programs like LCM may provide inclusive, accessible spaces for creative engagement - particularly for those unable to attend mainstream performances. Future researchers should explore hybrid delivery formats and assess longer-term dyadic outcomes.

items.title: Profiles of mental health indicators among Ukrainian people recently bereaved in the context of the full-scale Russian invasion.
items.abstract: Bereavement research has frequently focused on psychopathology, while comparatively less attention has been given to well-being as a component of mental health. This study is the first to examine mental health profiles based on ICD-11 Prolonged Grief (PG) symptoms, posttraumatic stress (PTS) symptoms, and well-being in a sample of Ukrainians bereaved during the full-scale Russian invasion. Participants were 290 adults (Mage = 34.3, SD = 9.1 years), who had lost a loved one on average 5.3 months earlier. Over a third (35%) had lost a partner or child, due to illness (43%) or war (40%). The majority of participants (55%) scored above the threshold of clinically relevant PG symptoms. Latent profile analyses identified three distinct mental health profiles: (1) low PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/high well-being (13%), (2) moderate PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/moderate well-being (57%), (3) high PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/low well-being (30%). People evidencing the third profile were more likely to have experienced the loss of a close person (partner or child) and to have been forcibly displaced compared to people in other profiles. Notably, the distribution of these profiles differs from previous studies, where profiles marked by low symptoms and high well-being were typically most common. Moreover, PG and well-being appeared to lie on opposite ends of a single continuum rather than functioning as distinct dimensions, providing limited support for the dual-continua model. This pattern suggests that Ukrainians may be facing unique challenges due to ongoing war-related stressors. Identifying those most in need of support and highlighting potential intervention targets are particularly important in under-resourced populations where access to care is limited.

items.title: Stimulus-hand proximity shapes conflict processing by task-dependent modulation of distractor activation.
items.abstract: Placing the hands near stimuli modulates interference effects in conflict tasks. Liepelt and Fischer (2016) found that the direction of this near-hand effect depends on task demands: In a complex number-categorization Simon task, conflict was reduced when visual stimuli appeared near the hand, whereas in a simpler color-discrimination Simon task, conflict increased. They attributed this result pattern to a flexible attentional weighting of bottom-up vs. top-down processing. The present study specified and tested this hypothesis by applying the Diffusion Model for Conflict (DMC) to their data. The DMC assumes two parallel evidence accumulation processes: a transient distractor-based and a constant target-based diffusion process, which combine additively to drive response selection. Across two experiments, model fits revealed that stimulus-hand proximity selectively modulated the strength of distractor-based activation, while other parameters remained relatively stable across hand conditions. Crucially, this modulation mirrored the behavioral pattern: greater distractor activation near the hands in the color task producing increased conflict, but reduced activation near the hands in the number task leading to reduced conflict. These findings suggest that conflict is shaped by stimulus-hand proximity through selective adjustment of distractor-based processing, not target-based processing: location signals are typically amplified near the hands but down-regulated under higher cognitive demands. The results further illustrate how embodied manipulations can selectively impact specific processing components as mapped within a formal decision-making model.

items.title: Alteration in functional-structural connectivities of insula is associated with hypoxic ventilation.
items.abstract: Hypoxia elicits ventilatory adaptation, and the anterior insula, a hub for interoceptive and exteroceptive integration, is highly vulnerable to hypoxic stress. We hypothesised that it mediates hypoxia-related ventilatory regulation. Thirty-one college students completed 30 days of high altitude exposure. Respiratory function tests and multimodal MRI were conducted immediately at high altitude. Moreover, follow-up MRI scans were performed 7 days, 2 months, and 3 months after the students returned to sea level. Pulmonary function (peak expiratory flow (PEF), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), FEV1/FVC%, maximal mid-expiratory flow (MMF) and minute ventilation (MV)) significantly declined after high altitude exposure. The ALFF increased in the insular cortex, with enhanced FC with the thalamus, motor cortex and postcentral cortex. FC of the left anterior insula with the thalamus was negatively correlated with FEV1 predicted values, while right lateral prefrontal insula-thalamus connectivity was positively correlated with FEV1 and MMF. FC of the anterior insula with the motor cortex and postcentral cortex was negatively correlated with PEF%, FVC and FEV1, respectively. Moreover, fibre pathways linking the anterior insular cortex with the thalamus, motor cortex and postcentral cortex showed increased fibre numbers between these brain regions. Follow-up MRI studies showed that ALFF in the anterior insular cortex was significantly increased immediately after reoxygenation and then recovered to baseline level. The anterior insula may serve as a potential hub for integrating hypoxic signals from the thalamus and modulating motor cortex activity, which may contribute to hypoxic ventilation.

items.title: Culture, connection, and prolonged grief: a cross-sectional study of social networks and interpersonal emotion regulation after loss.
items.abstract: Background: According to the Emotion Regulation Repertoire of Social Support (ERROSS) model, interpersonal emotion regulation (IER) provided by social network members may play an important role in adaptation to bereavement.Objective: The present study examined social network and IER structures in two cultural groups (i.e. Chinese-speaking and German-speaking) of bereaved adults.Method: A total of 187 bereaved individuals who had lost a first-degree relative participated in an online study completing measures of their social network and access to IER from their network.Results: German-speaking bereaved adults reported larger social networks, access to more grief-specific and general IER strategies and a larger emotion regulation repertoire, compared to Chinese-speaking bereaved adults. Cluster analysis identified three clusters of socioemotional support: resource-scarce cluster (32%), resource-moderate cluster (44%) and resource-abundant cluster (24%). Among Chinese-speaking bereaved individuals, the resource-scarce cluster was predominant (51%), whereas the resource-moderate cluster accounted for the largest proportion among German-speakers (64%). Prolonged grief symptoms were more severe in the resource-scarce cluster than those in the resource-abundant and resource-moderate clusters. Culture did not moderate the relationship between ERROSS variables and grief.Conclusions: This is the first study to examine ERROSS in a cross-cultural context. The findings characterize the interpersonal environments individuals encounter following loss and provide implications for designing culturally sensitive psychosocial interventions that focus on interpersonal support.

items.title: Risk Factors for Posttransplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) is the most frequent malignancy in pediatric patients following transplantation. This systematic review aimed to identify risk factors for PTLD in pediatric recipients of solid organ transplantation (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Following PRISMA guidelines, a literature search was conducted in Medline, Embase, and Cochrane databases for studies published up to August 2025. Study characteristics were extracted, and data on potential risk factors were collected when available. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Meta-analyses were performed when feasible. Of 4917 records identified, 80 studies were included. Among the investigated variables, negative recipient Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) serology before transplantation emerged as the most significant risk factor for PTLD. The pooled relative risk for PTLD in EBV-seronegative SOT recipients was 3.35 (95% confidence intervals, 2.43-4.60), and this association remained consistent across organ-specific subgroups. Additional variables, such as demographic characteristics, EBV viral load, immunosuppressive therapy, and rejection episodes, showed discordant results across studies, likely reflecting limited data and methodological heterogeneity. Negative pretransplant EBV serology is confirmed as a major risk factor for PTLD in pediatric transplant recipients. Moreover, the findings of this review provide a comprehensive synthesis of the available evidence regarding risk factors of PTLD in pediatric recipients of both SOT and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, highlighting the need for further large-scale studies to clarify additional determinants.

items.title: Relationships Between Parental and Offspring Early Maladaptive Schemas: A Meta-Analytic Review of Dyadic Data.
items.abstract: Early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) are pervasive cognitive-emotional patterns formed in childhood that contribute to diverse psychopathologies. While theory and research suggest EMSs may be transmitted across generations, findings are fragmented. This meta-analysis synthesized studies to (1) quantify the overall strength of associations between parental and offspring EMSs and (2) test moderation by parental or offspring age. Systematic searches across five databases identified 12 studies (N = 3,253; 1,473 dyads). Effect sizes for overall EMSs and the disconnection/rejection domain were extracted and analyzed using random-effects models with heterogeneity, influence, and publication bias tests. Moderator analyses examined parental and offspring age. The pooled correlation between overall parental and offspring EMSs was moderate (r = .32, 95% CI [.23, .42], p < .001; k = 11), with significant heterogeneity (I2 = 70%). The pooled correlation for parental and offspring disconnection/rejection schemas was also statistically significant and in the small-to-moderate range (r = .26, 95% CI [.20, .32], p < .001; k = 10). Neither parental nor offspring age moderated associations, and publication bias was non-significant. Findings provide the first quantitative evidence of intergenerational continuity in EMSs, highlighting the need for family-focused interventions to disrupt maladaptive schema cycles.

items.title: Schema therapy for Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID): a repeated case series.
items.abstract: Background: Research on treatment options for patients with Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID) is limited and primarily focuses on phase-based psychodynamic treatment.Objective: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an adapted Schema Therapy (ST) model for patients with DID.Method: A Non-Concurrent Multiple Baseline Case Series Design (N = 10) was employed, in which patients served as their own controls.Results: Mixed regression indicated that ST significantly reduced high-frequently-assessed dissociative symptoms with a medium effect size. Six out of ten participants lost their DID diagnosis and treatment drop-out was 20%. The secondary outcome results (low-frequency assessments from pre-treatment to follow-up one year after the end of treatment) corroborated these findings, indicating large effect sizes for the reduction of dissociative symptoms and dissociation-related dysfunctional beliefs and medium effect sizes for PTSD symptoms and overall disability. Moreover, a decrease in maladaptive modes and an increase in the adaptive modes were seen. Finally, large effect sizes were observed for both therapist- and patient-indicated progress in treatment.Conclusions: The results suggest that the investigated ST protocol may be associated with improvements across multiple symptom domains and warrant further investigation as a treatment approach for DID.

items.title: Biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in Brazilian women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: BackgroundSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), a chronic autoimmune disease that predominantly affects women, can alter both physical appearance and bodily functioning through its manifestations and treatment, posing challenges to body image. Although body image in SLE has been associated with clinical, psychological, and sociodemographic factors, few studies have examined these domains simultaneously in women with SLE within a biopsychosocial framework, which limits understanding of their joint contributions.ObjectiveTo examine biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in a Brazilian sample of women with SLE.MethodsA nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted with 597 women with SLE. Participants provided sociodemographic and clinical information and completed the Body Esteem Scale for Adults and Adolescents (BESAA), Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS), and Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Bivariate associations were examined with nonparametric tests, and independent associations were examined with a hierarchical multiple linear regression including theoretically pre-specified sociodemographic, clinical, and psychological blocks.ResultsIn bivariate analyses, poorer body image was associated with active disease, skin lesions, joint pain, serous membrane inflammation, fever without infection, lower life satisfaction, higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, lower educational attainment, and lower household income. The final model explained 35.4% of the variance in body image, with psychological variables accounting for 17.7% beyond sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Greater life satisfaction and unintentional weight loss were independently associated with more positive body image, whereas higher levels of depression, skin lesions, and joint pain were independently associated with poorer body image.ConclusionsBody image in women with SLE is associated with factors across different biopsychosocial domains, suggesting that it should not be examined solely from a clinical perspective. Rather, psychological and social factors should be considered alongside disease-related characteristics to support more comprehensive approaches to the assessment and care of body image concerns in this population.

items.title: Exposure to second-generation antipsychotics increases circulating small extracellular vesicles that promote insulin resistance in hepatocytes.
items.abstract: Second generation antipsychotics (SGAs) are widely prescribed for the management of psychiatric disorders, yet their use is associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and impaired glucose homeostasis. Small extracellular vesicles (sEV) are mediators of inter-tissue communication in metabolic diseases. Herein, we investigated the impact of the SGAs aripiprazole (ARI) and olanzapine (OLA) on circulating sEV in healthy volunteers and patients with first-episode psychosis, as well as the effects of these sEV on hepatocyte insulin signalling and systemic inflammation. Twenty-four healthy volunteers received OLA or ARI for five days. Seven individuals with first-episode psychosis were treated with SGAs; three were followed longitudinally for 6 months. sEV were isolated from plasma or culture media of SGA-treated human macrophages (h-mac) from donors. Huh7 human hepatocytes were exposed to sEV and insulin signalling was assessed. Inflammatory responses were evaluated by determining IκBα or IL1B expression in h-mac. In healthy volunteers, ARI significantly increased circulating sEV levels, which positively correlated with LDH, GGT, and free T4 plasma levels. sEV from ARI-treated subjects impaired hepatocyte insulin signalling in most cases, whereas sEV from OLA-treated patients produced milder effects. sEV from SGA-treated h-mac induced hepatocyte insulin resistance, accompanied, particularly with ARI, by reduced IκBα and increased IL1B expression in h-mac. Patients showed elevated baseline circulating sEV and increased baseline IL1B expression in PBMCs compared to healthy volunteers, and SGAs further enhanced these alterations. Our results suggest that elevations in circulating sEV associated to disease and SGA treatment may contribute to insulin-desensitization and inflammation, two hallmarks of metabolic dysfunction.

items.title: Women in Integrated Health: Driving Multidisciplinary Collaboration and the Evolution of Comprehensive Obesity Care within International Federation for the Surgery and Other Therapies for Obesity.
items.abstract: Within the International Federation for the Surgery and Other Therapies for Obesity (IFSO), Integrated Health professionals have become essential to the evolution of comprehensive obesity care. As the field transitions from a predominantly surgical discipline toward a truly multidisciplinary specialty, women in integrated health-encompassing nutrition, psychology, nursing, physiotherapy, endocrinology, and allied sciences-are leading efforts in collaboration, innovation, and patient-centered practice. This editorial aims to highlight the contributions of women in Integrated Health leadership within IFSO to multidisciplinary obesity care, examine these contributions across the bariatric care continuum, and propose concrete, measurable actions to advance equity and clinically meaningful outcomes in bariatric practice.

items.title: Role of Family Centered Care on Parental Stress and Anxiety Levels in Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
items.abstract: To evaluate the impact of Family-Centered Care (FCC) practices on parental stress, anxiety, and depression among parents of children admitted to a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). This prospective observational study was conducted over one year (September 2024-August 2025) in a PICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India. Children aged 1 mo to 18 y admitted for more than 24 h were included. Parental psychological assessment was performed within 72 h of admission using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and the Parental Stressor Scale (PSS). FCC components-including information sharing, family participation, presence during procedures and resuscitation, family-centered rounds, dignity and respect, negotiating roles, sharing goals, family conferences, and open visitation-were documented. Illness severity was assessed using PRISM scores. Correlation and comparative analyses were performed to examine associations between FCC practices and psychological outcomes. A total of 326 children were enrolled. Higher PRISM scores correlated strongly with increased parental stress (r = 0.793), anxiety (r = 0.721), and depression (r = 0.719) (p <0.0001). Implementation of key FCC components was significantly associated with lower stress, anxiety, and depression scores (p <0.05). The number of FCC components followed showed a strong inverse correlation with stress (r = -0.836), anxiety (r = -0.709), and depression (r = - 0.754) (p <0.0001). Open visitation alone was not significantly associated with improved psychological outcomes. Structured FCC practices are significantly associated with reduced parental stress, anxiety, and depression in the PICU. Strengthening meaningful family engagement may improve psychological outcomes in resource-limited critical care settings.

items.title: Directional Brain Connectivity Changes Induced by Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback: A Spectral Dynamic Causal Modeling Study.
items.abstract: Heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB) is a non-pharmacological intervention that trains individuals to breathe at their cardiovascular resonance frequency to enhance autonomic regulation. While HRVB improves cardiovascular function across clinical conditions, the directional neural pathways through which it modulates the central autonomic network (CAN) remain poorly understood. Using a publicly available open-access dataset, we conducted a secondary analysis of effective (directional) neural connectivity (EC) data from 32 healthy participants randomized to an 8-week HRVB intervention (n = 15) or a video game Control intervention (n = 17). Pre- and post-intervention resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were analyzed using spectral dynamic causal modeling (DCM) combined with parametric empirical Bayes to examine group differences in EC changes (ΔEC). We also evaluated whether connectivity changes correlated with changes in peripheral autonomic regulation, indexed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (ΔSDNN). Compared with the Control group, HRVB showed strong evidence (posterior-probability = 1) of increased ΔEC from the medial prefrontal cortex to the anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral thalamus post-treatment, along with reduced ΔEC from the right hippocampus to the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (VLPFC). Furthermore, the regression coefficient linking hippocampus-to-VLPFC ΔEC with ΔSDNN was more (posterior-probability = 1) negative in the HRVB group than in Controls, indicating an intervention-dependent association between autonomic changes and effective connectivity. These findings indicate that HRVB may alter directional fronto-limbic communication within the CAN. Given the relatively small sample sizes, these findings need replication, but provide preliminary understanding about the neural circuitry through which resonance breathing may modulate central autonomic control.

items.title: Imposter Syndrome and Cannabis-Related Outcomes Among Black and White Students at a Predominantly White Institution.
items.abstract: Cannabis use among college students has become increasingly prevalent, with coping being one of the primary motives for use. Imposter syndrome, characterized by persistent self-doubt and fear of being exposed as a fraud despite evidence of competence, is particularly common among students. Imposter syndrome was related to coping-motivated cannabis use and related problems in a presumably predominantly White sample at a predominantly White institution (PWI). However, Black students at PWIs may be especially impacted by imposter syndrome, yet no known studies have tested whether these students experience greater imposter syndrome than White students or whether the relations of imposter syndrome with cannabis outcomes generalize to Black students. The current sample included 215 participants (48.4% Black) who endorsed past three-month cannabis use. Contrary to hypotheses, White students reported higher levels of imposter syndrome. Black students reported greater cannabis use to manage negative affect and racism. Among both groups, imposter syndrome was positively associated with coping-motivated cannabis use (coping-negative affect, coping-social anxiety), and racism, but not cannabis use frequency. Among White students, imposter syndrome was related to cannabis-related problems, but among Black students, it was related to cannabis use to cope with social anxiety and racism. Findings from this research could inform culturally responsive prevention and treatment efforts for Black students at PWIs who use cannabis.

items.title: Older adults retain detail-specific associations: Evidence from an indirect memory test.
items.abstract: Research suggests that age-related episodic memory decline is characterized by a reduced ability to form detailed associations. In two experiments, we test this claim using a sensitive, indirect memory test and additionally examine how associative encoding is influenced by encoding duration. In Experiment 1, young and older adult participants studied scene-object pairs for varying durations before completing a speeded congruency judgment task involving intact, recombined, and new pairs. Recombined pairs varied based on detail-specific, perceptual (related pairs), or conceptual (unrelated pairs) features. Participants in both age groups were generally slower to respond to recombined than intact pairs on the congruency judgment task. Critically, both groups formed detail-specific associations, as evidenced by slower response times to related compared to intact pairs - though this effect emerged only at longer encoding durations for older adults. In Experiment 2, using a similar paradigm, we replicated the response time effects in older adults using a single encoding duration and additionally observed poorer memory for recombined pairs relative to young adults on a traditional recognition (direct) memory task. Our findings indicate that older adults can form detailed associations, as demonstrated by faster response times to intact compared to recombined pairs, and can access those associations when retrieval demands are minimized in indirect memory tests.

items.title: Supportive parenting moderates the association between neural synchrony and irritability: Evidence from mother-son dyads.
items.abstract: While research on parent-child neural synchrony using fNIRS hyperscanning has expanded, its association with child psychopathology, especially transdiagnostic symptoms such as irritability, remains poorly understood. Moreover, no prior studies have explored the potential contextual factors that may moderate the link between parent-child neural synchrony and children's irritability. The present study therefore investigated whether and how neural synchrony would interact with maternal supportive parenting to shape irritability. Forty mother-son dyads participated, consisting of school-aged boys with varying levels of irritability (Mage = 7.53 years, SD = 1.25 years) and their mothers (Mage = 39.35 years, SD = 4.53 years). Neural activity was recorded via fNIRS during a frustration-eliciting task. Results indicated that neural synchrony was identified in the prefrontal cortex and the temporoparietal junction. Furthermore, moderation analysis revealed that in dyads with low maternal supportive parenting, higher neural synchrony was associated with higher child irritability, whereas in dyads with high maternal supportive parenting, neural synchrony was not significantly associated with child irritability. This study advances our understanding of irritability by dissecting neuro-parenting interactive mechanisms.

items.title: Giving young patients with ADPKD a voice: preliminary validation of the 'Symptom and impact scale for adolescents with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease' (SAIL-ADPKD).
items.abstract: Unpredictable pain and reduced quality of life are common in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and occur even before gross kidney enlargement or markedly decreased kidney function. Very little is known about pain in adolescents with ADPKD, and there are no patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) in youth. An age-appropriate questionnaire on pain, impact, symptoms, and worries was created by pediatric nephrologists, clinical psychologists, pain specialists, patient representatives, and external reviewers. Self- and proxy-reported versions exist in English and Dutch. Psychometric validation included exploratory factor analysis for scale construction, assessment of internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and evaluation of content validity through correlations with established generic instruments. The validation cohort consisted of 46 patients with ADPKD aged 12-25 years (mean 19.3 ± 3.6 years). Subscores created according to factor analysis showed good internal consistency, especially for fatigue-, pain-, worry-, and disruption of everyday activities scores. Fatigue and total pain & fullness scores correlated well with the PedsQL physical functioning score (both r = -0.65, p < 0.0001). Disruption of everyday life converged with the PROMIS pain interference T-score (r = 0.76, p < 0.0001) and PedsQL scores, and total worry score with PedsQL emotional functioning score (r = -0.57, p = 0.0001). Repeatability was assessed with test-retest correlations after a median of 1.7 months (n = 35), and convergence of subjective and parental assessment with self-proxy correlations (n = 20). This initial validation of an age- and disease-specific PROM capturing pain, impact, symptoms, and worries in youth with ADPKD supports its suitability for further studies and clinical trials.

items.title: A qualitative exploration of self-control, emotions, and interoception in anorexia nervosa.
items.abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a prevalent condition associated with significant impairment across multiple domains of life and limited effective treatments. There is a need to refine theoretical frameworks of AN. There is also growing recognition of the value of incorporating first-person perspectives to inform researcher-derived models of mental disorders. Among individuals with lived experience of AN, this study aimed to explore the components of a previously proposed model that integrates self-control, emotions, and interoception. Using virtual semi-structured interviews, we asked ten adults (nine women, one non-binary individual) to describe their experiences of self-control, emotions, and interoception across different stages of their eating disorder. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using codebook thematic analysis. Five themes were identified: negative emotions, control to cope, salience of interoception, tension, and changes over time. Together, the findings highlight the dynamic and evolving nature of AN, as well as the coexistence of opposing experiences. Clinically, these results underscore the importance of attending to multiple interacting mechanisms rather than isolated symptoms, and of tailoring interventions to the stage and dominant processes of illness. Approaches that explicitly acknowledge ambivalence and shifting experiences of control may be particularly valuable.

items.title: The Trend of Out-of-Pocket Costs for Child Delivery Care in Bangladesh During 2014-2022: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: In Bangladesh, out-of-pocket payments are the primary means of covering childbirth-related expenses, often placing a substantial financial burden on households and disrupting family livelihoods. This study examines trends in out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditures and identifies the factors influencing childbirth costs between 2014 and 2022, highlighting differences across delivery types and socio-demographic groups. This study analyzed 12,752 ever-married women aged 15-49 who reported out-of-pocket costs for childbirth within 2 years before each survey, we pooled data from the 2014, 2017-2018, and 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys (BDHS). Out-of-pocket costs for home delivery, institutional normal delivery, and cesarean section (C-section) delivery expenses were the main outcome variables. Maternal age, employment status, antenatal care (ANC) visits, household wealth, body mass index (BMI), husband's education, birth order, geographic division, and place of residence were important independent variables. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, t-tests, and log-linear regression were used to investigate associations. The mean OOP of C-section delivery was the highest ($369.84), followed by institutional normal delivery ($102.78) and home delivery ($27.38). The mean cost of C-section delivery decreased from $501.46 in 2014 to $285.14 in 2022, while the cost of institutional normal delivery decreased from $116.23 to $93.03. The difference in costs between survey years was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Pooled regression analysis showed that higher household wealth was associated with higher costs in the selected delivery-type models. Other associated factors varied by delivery type and included maternal age, employment status, ANC visits, BMI, husband's age and education, birth order, geographic region, and place of residence. There were significant differences in the amount of OOP costs of childbirth by type of delivery and year of survey. Despite a decline in average costs between 2014 and 2022, costs for C-section deliveries remained consistently the highest. Socioeconomic and geographic disparities highlight the unequal financial burden of childbirth in Bangladesh and support the need for policies to improve financial protection and equitable access to maternal health care.

items.title: The Ghana Surgical Dialogue: A Whole-of-Society Innovation for Advancing Safe Surgery, Obstetric, Trauma, and Anesthesia Care in Ghana.
items.abstract: Ghana continues to face major gaps in access to safe surgery, obstetric, trauma, and anesthesia (SOTA) care, especially at district level, where workforce shortages, infrastructure deficits, weak referral systems, and limited data constrain service delivery. To support implementation of the Ghana National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plan (NSOAP) 2025-2029, the Ministry of Health convened the inaugural Ghana Surgical Dialogue in Koforidua in August 2025. The Dialogue brought together government, professional associations, clinicians, nurses, biomedical engineers, laboratory professionals, health managers, financiers, civil society, and international partners to identify practical solutions for strengthening SOTA care. Key innovations included alignment of SOTA priorities with national budgeting, exploration of public-private partnership models such as build-operate-transfer schemes, investment in district-level mentorship and telemedicine, improved surgical safety and audit culture, and development of biomedical equipment management systems. Participants also emphasized workforce retention, career progression for anesthetists and perioperative nurses, ring-fenced funding, interoperable data systems, and stronger referral networks. The Dialogue demonstrated that sustainable progress in surgical care requires a whole-of-society approach that combines policy, financing, workforce development, technology, and accountability. This report highlights implementation lessons from Ghana that may be useful to other countries seeking to translate surgical plans into action.

items.title: Association of breakfast skipping on quality of life among university students in Latin America: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundSkipping breakfast is a prevalent habit among university students and has been associated with poorer quality of life; however, evidence from Latin America remains limited, particularly from multicenter studies.AimTo analyze the association between breakfast skipping and quality of life across its physical, psychological, social, and environmental dimensions among Latin American university students.MethodsA cross-sectional multicenter study was conducted in ten Latin American countries using an online self-administered questionnaire. Breakfast frequency, sociodemographic variables, and quality of life were assessed using the WHOQOL-BREF instrument. Bivariate and multivariate linear regression analyses were performed, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, smoking status, physical activity, and socioeconomic status.SummaryA total of 4539 university students participated (67% women; mean age: 21.3 ± 2.5 years). Of these, 38.6% reported skipping breakfast three or more times per week. Breakfast skipping was significantly associated with lower scores in the physical (β = -2.8; 95% CI: -3.9 to -1.6), psychological (β = -2.3; 95% CI: -3.4 to -1.2), and environmental (β = -1.9; 95% CI: -2.9 to -0.9) domains. No significant association was observed with the social domain. In conclusion the frequent breakfast skipping is associated with poorer quality of life among Latin American university students. Promoting regular breakfast consumption may represent an effective strategy to improve overall well-being in this population.
