items.title: Advancing equitable pain care worldwide requires progress in low- and middle-income settings: priorities for practice, research, and policy.
items.abstract: Abstract Equitable, high-value pain care remains out of reach for many populations worldwide, particularly for people living in low- and middle-income countries and cultural minority groups in high-income settings. Despite carrying a disproportionate burden of chronic pain, these populations remain underrepresented in high-quality pain research, underserved by existing health systems, and constrained by social, political, environmental, and commercial determinants of health. The lack of locally generated evidence forces clinicians and policymakers to rely on externally produced research that may not translate to local cultural, linguistic, or health-system contexts. This invited viewpoint synthesizes key contributors to pain inequity-including limited prioritization of chronic pain in low- and middle-income countries, underdeveloped rehabilitation capacity, poor access to essential treatments, commercial exploitation, and misalignment between culturally shaped pain beliefs and Western-derived assessment and treatment models. I highlight opportunities to strengthen equity in clinical care through improved education of health professionals and the public, culturally and linguistically responsive assessment, and contextually adapted self-management and treatment strategies. Equitable research requires standardized collection of sociodemographic variables, deliberate inclusion of underrepresented groups, and global partnerships that avoid colonizing practices. I propose principles for fair and impactful North-South collaborations focused on co-creation of research agendas, shared leadership, sustainable capacity building, and transparent governance. Advancing equitable global pain care and research will require collective action from clinicians, researchers, institutions, policymakers, journals, funders, and communities. A coordinated shift toward culturally grounded, contextually adaptable, and ethically collaborative approaches is essential to meaningfully reduce global pain disparities and ensure all individuals benefit from scientific progress.

items.title: Advances in research on combination therapy for the management of pain.
items.abstract: Abstract Pharmacotherapy remains an important component of multidisciplinary, multimodal pain treatment. Based on a well-established understanding of multiple concurrent mechanisms of nociceptive transmission and modulation, the demonstrated potential for synergistic interactions of drug combinations seen in preclinical studies supports the hypothesis of superior analgesia, and possibly also, fewer side-effects as compared with monotherapy. Likely related to this hypothesis and rationale, real-world evidence shows that approximately half of all patients with chronic pain, and even more with acute pain, concurrently receive 2 or more drugs from different mechanistic classes. To date, many dozens of randomized controlled trials have evaluated various analgesic combinations for the treatment of postoperative, neuropathic, back, arthritis, fibromyalgia, pelvic, and cancer-related pain conditions. Despite this growing area of research, most analgesic drug combinations are currently administered without rigorous evidence, thus exposing patients to the added cost or risk of some combinations that are not necessarily superior to monotherapy. As such, we propose future efforts to more efficiently exploit the potential benefits of combination therapy including: (1) expansion and coordination of translational collaborations to prioritize the most beneficial and clinically relevant combinations; (2) ensuring that preclinical combination studies evaluate multiple drug dosages and multiple relevant adverse effects; (3) ensuring that clinical trials include comparisons with each and every monotherapy component of the combination; (4) conducting further real-world studies of clinically beneficial combinations to ensure safety and efficacy in broader clinical settings; and (5) the application of these principles also to the evaluation of nonpharmacological treatment combinations.

items.title: Brain sites involved in endogenous analgesia.
items.abstract: Abstract Pain modulation is a fundamental survival mechanism that prioritises, shapes, and suppresses nociceptive inputs to optimise behaviour. Although acute pain signals potential or actual tissue damage, sustained pain can impair essential behaviours, necessitating modulatory circuits that dynamically regulate nociception according to context and motivational state. These systems are deeply conserved, embedded within primitive spinal and brainstem structures, and capable of powerful modulation independent of cortical input, although higher regions such as the prefrontal cortex can influence their function. Decades of work have sought to identify these core modulatory circuits to advance basic understanding and develop strategies for clinically meaningful hypoalgesia. More recently, dysfunction within these circuits has been implicated in chronic pain, driving efforts to characterise how their organisation and function change during persistent pain states. Although most mechanistic insights come from animal studies, human neuroimaging, particularly since the advent of functional magnetic resonance imaging, has begun to map their location and engagement during pain modulation. Early work focused on forebrain regions due to the limited spatial resolution of standard MRI, but ultra-high-field functional magnetic resonance imaging now enables mm3-scale investigation of brainstem nuclei. This review synthesises evidence from animal and human studies to outline the best-characterised modulatory pathway, consisting of projections from the midbrain periaqueductal gray to the rostral ventromedial medulla and onward to the dorsal horn/spinal trigeminal nucleus, and highlights recent work detailing its organization.

items.title: Trustworthiness in pain research is essential. Developing and implementing the ENTRUST-PE framework.
items.abstract: Abstract Trustworthy pain research is essential for developing a deeper understanding of the phenomena, how it is experienced, its many impacts and how it might be reduced, prevented or managed to improve the lives of those who live with pain. Recognising multiple critical challenges that undermine trust in health research, an international, interdisciplinary network was convened to create an integrated framework for enhancing the trustworthiness of research in pain. The ENTRUST-PE framework was launched in 2024 with a call to action, proposing that trustworthiness in pain research is multidimensional and underpinned by 7 Core Values: Integrity and Governance; Equity, Diversity and Inclusivity; Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement; Methodological Rigour; Openness and Transparency; Balanced Communication and Data Authenticity. The framework includes specific recommendations for a range of interest holders and resources to support those recommendations. In this paper, we summarise the framework, reflect on the response to the framework from the pain research community, consider challenges and opportunities in the evolving research landscape and suggest how we might move towards deeper implementation to enhance the trustworthiness of pain research.

items.title: Chloride dysregulation: the next target for chronic pain therapeutics.
items.abstract: Abstract Chronic pain affects a substantial fraction of the population, yet pharmacological management remains deeply inadequate. This failure likely reflects the focus on developing analgesics suppressing normal nociceptive signalling rather than correcting the pathological substrates distinguishing chronic from acute pain. Here we review how the identification of injury-induced downregulation of the potassium-chloride cotransporter KCC2 in spinal dorsal horn neurons represents a landmark. It first provided a mechanistic, long-term substrate for spinal inhibitory failure. This form of disinhibition had the potential to explain several cardinal symptoms of neuropathic pain; not just hyperalgesia, through spinal hyperexcitability, and tactile allodynia, through cross-talk between sensory modalities, but also spontaneous pain, through enabling spontaneous bursts of activity in spinal nociceptive output to emerge. A second landmark is that chloride dysregulation as a substrate of disinhibition yields non-linear, non-intuitive predictions of neural circuit behaviours that shed light on several features of chronic pain and its therapeutic challenges. One is paradoxical pro-excitatory actions of tapping into normally endogenous inhibitory neurotransmission, potentially explaining failures of benzodiazepines analgesia and of conditional pain modulation. Others include degradation of sensory processing, possibly explaining diffuse pain, and leaky plasticity, predisposing to catastrophic sensitization. In turn, mechanisms regulating KCC2 itself emerge as substrates of chronification, as well as substrates of opioid-induced maladaptive paradoxical hyperalgesia. Finally, divergent yet convergent signaling cascades underlying KCC2-downregulation reveal a form of pathway degeneracy across sexes with lessons for therapeutics. All-in-all, these findings position KCC2 as a key novel target, not just for analgesia, but also for disease modification.

items.title: Behavioural and neurogenetic evidence for emotion primitives in the fruit fly Drosophila from an open field test.
items.abstract: Emotions are based on evolutionarily conserved building blocks ('emotion primitives') that are present across mammals. Whether these building blocks are found in insects is largely undefined. Here, we employ the open field test (OFT) in Drosophila and focus on wall-following and total walking activity as behavioural indicators of emotion-like states. Wildtype and transgenic flies were subjected to various conditions prior to behavioural testing. The results indicate that wall-following and total walking activity are independent measures that are modulated, with generally increased wall-following observed under aversive stimuli and decreased values under positive conditions, independent of the time of day. The effects of genetic manipulation of selected neuromodulatory systems support their role in modulating emotion-like states in Drosophila . Activation of reward-related neurons decreased wall-following while inhibition increased it. Moreover, treatment with ethanol or diazepam produced predictable changes in behaviour. Our findings suggest that Drosophila shares conserved core emotion-like building blocks with vertebrates, and show that wall-following and total walking activity in the OFT can serve as a reliable indicator of emotional valence and arousal in the fruit fly. This positions Drosophila as a powerful genetic model to dissect the neuronal and neurochemical substrates of emotion primitives.

items.title: Beyond the Stool: Circulating Short-Chain Fatty Acids Better Predict Human Gut-Related Diseases.
items.abstract: Background Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediate host-microbiota interactions and are typically measured in feces as markers of gut microbial activity. However, whether fecal SCFAs adequately reflect disease-associated host-microbiota dysfunction remains unclear. We hypothesized that circulating SCFAs, which integrate microbial production, intestinal absorption, barrier function, and host metabolism, provide a more informative representation of gut-related diseases. Methods Seven fecal and serum SCFAs were quantified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in 193 individuals, including patients with colorectal cancer (CRC, n = 30), celiac disease (CD, n = 35), obesity (OB, n = 33), and healthy controls (HCs, n = 95). We developed an interpretable machine-learning framework combining stacking ensembles, bootstrap validation, permutation testing, SHAP and LIME analyses. Cross-compartment predictive modeling was used to assess the reciprocal informativeness of fecal and circulating SCFAs. Results Circulating SCFAs exhibited markedly stronger disease-associated signatures than fecal SCFAs across all groups. Serum-based models achieved excellent classification performance (95% accuracy; multiclass ROC-AUC 1.00), whereas fecal SCFAs provided substantially lower predictive power (59% accuracy). Combining serum and fecal datasets yielded only marginal improvement (97.4% accuracy), indicating most diagnostic relevant information was already captured in circulation. Valeric, propionic, 2-methylbutyric, and isovaleric acids were consistently identified as the main contributors to disease discrimination. Cross-compartment modeling revealed weak predictive relationships between fecal and serum SCFAs, indicating these pools are largely non-redundant and reflect distinct biological processes. Conclusions Circulating SCFAs outperform fecal SCFAs as biomarkers of gut-related diseases, capturing the integrated effects of microbial activity and host physiology. These findings support blood-based SCFA profiling as a promising approach for precision diagnostics in microbiota-associated disorders.

items.title: Beyond motor rescue: defining adequate SMN restoration in spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is characterized by motor neuron degeneration due to deficiency in the survival of motor neuron (SMN) protein. Disease-modifying therapies have transformed outcomes in SMA, while also revealing an increasingly complex spectrum of residual disease biology. In this issue of the JCI, Tapken, Rahmel-Stein, and colleagues demonstrated cell-specific SMN expression and persistent alterations in peripheral immune cell populations in nusinersen- or risdiplam-treated adults with SMA. Their findings extend the question of selective vulnerability beyond motor neurons and raise an increasingly important therapeutic question: What constitutes adequate SMN restoration? This Commentary considers how cell type, developmental timing, SMN requirement, and downstream response may shape treatment-modified SMA, with implications for systemic and CNS-directed therapies.

items.title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
items.abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

items.title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism.
items.abstract: Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

items.title: Lessons from the UN Decade: from ecosystem restoration to regenerative transformation.
items.abstract: Although restoration science increasingly considers social-ecological complexity, many restoration projects still fall short of their ecological or social goals. We argue that such failures often stem from a lack of attention to long-term social-ecological dynamics within the target system. To overcome this problem, we propose 'regenerative transformation' as a new paradigm to guide ecosystem restoration. Regenerative transformation foregrounds the thriving of human and other forms of life and emphasizes healthy endogenous social-ecological dynamics rather than exogenous interventions. Facilitating regenerative transformation through restoration will require changes in how restoration is conceptualized, practiced, and governed-moving from a focus on abstract targets and simple outcome indicators toward developing supportive conditions for the long-term, equitable coevolution of healthy social-ecological dynamics.

items.title: Dietary Patterns, Ultra-Processed Food Consumption, and Food Environments Among Young Adult Students and Non-Students in Merida, Yucatan, Mexico.
items.abstract: Globalization has transformed Mexico's food system, increasing ultra-processed foods (UPFs) and sugar-sweetened beverages consumption while reducing traditional dietary practices. This study compared dietary patterns and food choice drivers among college students and age-matched non-students in Merida, Mexico. A cross-sectional study included 50 adults (26 students and 24 non-students; 25 males and 25 females) aged 21-23 years. Weekly dietary intake was assessed using a food frequency questionnaire; foods were classified according to the Mexican food group system and Nova. Students consumed fast food significantly less frequently than non-students (2.8 vs. 5.0 times/week; p = 0.001) and reported higher consumption of dairy products and nuts; non-students consumed refined cereals more frequently. No significant differences were observed in Nova food-group distributions, with UPFs accounting for approximately one-third of weekly intake in both groups. Taste and availability primarily influenced food choices. Improving food environments may promote healthier dietary behaviors in early adulthood.

items.title: Isoprenoid quinone profiling using a novel semi-quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method: application to wastewater sludges.
items.abstract: Isoprenoid quinones are ubiquitous redox lipids that mediate electron transfer in various cellular processes across all domains of life. These molecules also serve as taxonomic and metabolic markers, facilitating the characterisation of microbial communities. However, their structural diversity and extreme hydrophobicity are challenging for comprehensive detection and quantification in complex biological matrices. In this study, we present a semi-quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method that enables the sensitive analysis of the widest range of quinones reported to date. Using a 13-quinone standard mixture, we optimized separation within a 14-minute HPLC gradient and achieved a sensitivity ranging from 55.2 to 0.3 femtomoles in targeted analyses. When applied to sewage sludges sampled weekly over three weeks, our method detected 57 quinones, revealing distinct quinone profiles at various wastewater treatment stages. This rapid and sensitive workflow enables quinone profiling in complex samples, and holds significant promise for advancing microbial ecology, environmental monitoring, and biotechnological applications.

items.title: Species-specific bioaccessibility of microplastics by benthic macroinvertebrates.
items.abstract: Effect and bioaccumulation tests have mainly used monodisperse microplastics, whereas natural microplastics are diverse. Consequently, understanding of their actual biological accessibility remains limited, which constrains risk assessment. The goal of this study was to investigate species-specific uptake of an environmentally representative microplastic mixture (ERMP; 9-5386 μm; PE, PP, PET and PS) in 11 freshwater and marine benthic macroinvertebrate species. Species-specific uptake was assessed by describing ingested particles as a continuum through continuous size distributions and comparing these distributions among species and against controls. Samples underwent enzymatic/hydrogen peroxide digestion and FTIR microscopy, followed by polymer- and size-specific blank correction. Adverse effects previously observed in the freshwater worm Lumbriculus variegatus could be linked more directly to exposure because microplastics were detected in post-depuration organism samples. Only a select fraction of the ERMP mixture was ingested by Asellus aquaticus, Corbicula fluminalis, Corophium volutator, Hyalella azteca, L. variegatus, Limecola balthica, Mytilus edulis and Tubifex spp. Most particles detected in organisms ranged from 5.5 to 27.7 μm and differed in polymer composition among species; 5.5 μm was also the method's lower size-detection limit. Egested ERMP significantly exceeded particles remaining in post-depuration organism samples, indicating substantial egestion during the 24 h depuration period. The lowest ERMP numbers occurred in post-depuration organism samples of the midge larva Chironomus riparius and egestion samples of the mud snail Potamopyrgus antipodarum, respectively, averaging <1 particle/organism. The highest egested count occurred in the mussel M. edulis, at 49.9 particles/organism, primarily polystyrene. Similar size distributions were found for the amphipods A. aquaticus and H. azteca, both sediment grazers/scavengers, and for the clams C. fluminalis and L. balthica, both facultative deposit feeders. These particle size- and species-specific ingestion patterns provide a basis for understanding effect mechanisms such as particle volume-based food dilution.

items.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism.
items.abstract: Understanding how industrialization reshapes the human metaorganism requires integrating microbiome ecology with host physiology across globally diverse populations. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, immunoglobulin A (IgA) sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Finally, we show that microbiome-based disease predictors trained on industrialized populations are uninformative in less industrialized cohorts, highlighting limited cross-population transferability. Together, our results reveal coordinated restructuring of the microbial ecosystem and host physiology and emphasize the need for inclusive, globally representative data to improve translational microbiome applications across diverse human populations.

items.title: Evidence for diurnal habits in an exceptionally preserved Eocene owl.
items.abstract: It is poorly understood when owls (Strigiformes) became nocturnal, which impedes considerations of the evolutionary reasons behind this distinctive behavior. 1 , 2 Here, we report an extraordinary owl skeleton from the middle Eocene of Germany, which preserves remains of an iridescent cockroach as stomach contents-the first identifiable insect remains ever found as the last meal of a fossil bird. Because iridescence is correlated with diurnal habits in cockroaches, 3 the fossil provides the strongest evidence to date for diurnality in archaic Strigiformes. Further support for a diurnal ecology comes from the absence of barred flight feathers as well as the lack of frayed leading edges of the primaries; the presence of these features is associated with nocturnality in extant owls. 4 , 5 The humerus is much stouter than in extant owls, indicating that the wings were less adapted to silent flight. Conversely, a slenderer humerus suggests that late Eocene owls had shifted toward a nocturnal ecology. This timeframe rules out previously suggested factors for nocturnality in owls 2 and constrains the origin of an ecological hallmark of these birds.

items.title: pH-Regulated microelectrolysis-kaolinite coupling for Heterosigma akashiwo removal.
items.abstract: Mineral-assisted microelectrolysis couples in situ electrochemical oxidation with particle-mediated algal separation for harmful algal bloom control. Here, the process was advanced for Heterosigma akashiwo through comparative mineral evaluation, electrolysis-pH regulation, and interaction analysis. Kaolinite gave the highest removal among four minerals (95.7%) and the largest apparent active chlorine adsorption amount, while time-resolved aggregate and clarification measurements linked this advantage to efficient particle-mediated cell capture and separation. Increasing initial electrolysis pH from 2 to 10 raised removal at 400 μL from 51.8% to >95% together with a larger post-electrolysis active chlorine inventory;92-93% of measured chlorine remained dissolved, and equal-C₀ tests showed comparable apparent adsorption across pH, supporting chlorine availability as the main factor governing apparent adsorption in the contact experiments. Oxidative and photosystem II responses linked process optimization to algal injury, establishing a parameterized oxidation-separation strategy for bloom control.

items.title: Vegetation restoration and climate change shape the spatial distribution and biomass of terrestrial ants on the Loess Plateau.
items.abstract: As ecological engineers, terrestrial ants play a significant role in modifying soil structure, influencing the carbon cycle, affecting soil microorganisms and soil food webs. Accurately estimating ant biomass is crucial for assessing their ecological impacts. To investigate the spatial distribution and drivers of ant density, field sampling of ant communities, soil, and vegetation was conducted at 27 sites on the Loess Plateau from 2022 to 2024. The findings indicated that ants on the Loess Plateau exhibit pronounced zonal distribution characteristics. In addition to vegetation coverage, annual rainfall and air temperature emerged as the most significant factors influencing the ant density. Based on land-use types, climate, and soil parameters, two regression models were developed to estimate the ant density in farmland and forest-grassland ecosystems. The density of ants in forest-grassland areas was found to be 2.15 times greater than that in farmland. However, the differences among forest, shrub, and grassland habitats were not statistically significant (P > 0.05). The total ant population across the Loess Plateau was estimated to be 2.41 × 10 13 individuals, corresponding to a biomass of 1.49 × 10 4 tons of dry carbon. Rainfall was identified as the primary factor in calculating ant biomass. The majority of ant density are concentrated in regions with annual rainfall exceeding 400 mm, comprising 93.1% of the total ant biomass on the Loess Plateau. Our spatial estimates indicated that ant biomass on the Loess Plateau is 76.7% higher than the estimated pre-restoration baseline, a trend strongly associated with extensive vegetation restoration efforts since the initiation of the Grain for Green Project in 1999. This study underscores the significance of global revegetation and climate change in forecasting ant distribution and overall biomass. Our findings offer a vital reference for comprehensively understanding the abundance and ecological significance of ants.

items.title: Balancing ecological benefits and feasibility in large-scale restoration planning: A multi-objective optimization decision-support framework.
items.abstract: Large-scale ecosystem restoration requires spatial planning tools that identify where limited resources are most likely to deliver durable ecological benefits. Yet ecological feasibility is often treated as an exclusion filter or screening criterion; here, we optimize it alongside biodiversity and other ecological criteria. We developed a multi-objective optimization decision-support framework that integrates ecological feasibility with extinction risk reduction, carbon stock priority, and riparian restoration priority. The framework is grounded in systematic conservation planning and formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming model. Single-objective optimizations define benchmark performance for each criterion, and normalized goal programming identifies compromise portfolios under fixed restoration budget and land suitability constraints. Ecological feasibility is represented as a spatial indicator of relative favorability for restoration persistence under recurrent pressures, based on recurrent fire exposure, anthropogenic pressure, and invasive species richness. Applied to continental Chile at 1 km2 resolution (812,910 planning units), including ecological feasibility as an optimization objective resulted in a 16.52% spatial reallocation of the feasibility-excluded portfolio, with an equivalent proportion entering the feasibility-inclusive portfolio, under an illustrative 30% national restoration planning scenario. This reallocation increased feasibility performance by 11.07 percentage points and extinction risk reduction by 1.20 percentage points, with moderate reductions in carbon stock priority (-4.17) and riparian restoration priority (-2.47). Selection frequency diagnostics showed that compromise solutions were anchored in a shared backbone of multipurpose areas, complemented by specialized units that resolved local trade-offs. The framework provides a transparent and adaptable basis for balancing ecological value with favorability for restoration persistence in spatial prioritization.

items.title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption.
items.abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. We found that green and blue spaces in the city's built-up area had a pronounced influence on air temperature, ranging from a cooling effect of 1.27 °C to a warming effect of 0.29 °C, with the cooling effect being dominant over the course of a year. The cooling effect was greatest at moderate temperatures (~20 °C) and was lower on hotter days. We identified a temperature threshold of 16 to 18 °C above which urban nature produces measurable reductions in cooling energy demand. We found that residential electricity consumption was more temperature-sensitive than nonresidential electricity consumption. For the study year of 2021, the net electricity savings from urban nature was 1.5 billion kWh. This reduction in energy consumption translated to almost one million tons of avoided CO 2 emissions, which was 4.65-times the sequestration capacity of the city's terrestrial vegetation and equivalent to the annual emissions of over 223 thousand people using global average annual per capita carbon emissions.

items.title: Environmental forcing, individual repeatability, and mother-daughter resemblance shape the phenology of a long-lived seabird.
items.abstract: Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli's Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother-daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high ( R = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother-daughter cases, daughters' RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating into an annual fitness advantage. Differences in survival and BS across individuals were more evident during the first observed breeding attempts. Together, these results support a scenario in which plasticity shifts the population mean breeding date in response to climatic variation, while persistent traits generate differential fitness among individuals.

items.title: Rapid soil degradation of a cross-linked, semicrystalline polyethylene-like polyester produced by Colletes bees.
items.abstract: Polyethylene (PE)-like polyesters have long been investigated as biodegradable alternatives to conventional polyolefins but degrade poorly despite possessing hydrolyzable esters due to high crystallinity and hydrophobicity. Bees of the genus Colletes line their nests with a PE-like polyester that shows no environmental accumulation despite decades of nesting in dense aggregations, suggesting rapid biodegradability. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of Colletes inaequalis polyester and demonstrates its rapid degradation under ambient environmental conditions. Colletes polyester is completely insoluble in trichlorobenzene or toluene at elevated temperatures, indicating cross-linking despite originating from macrocyclic lactones that lack obvious cross-linkable functionality. Small molecules extracted from the network match the Dufour's gland secretion but lack macrolactone, indicating complete monomer conversion. Although its repeat unit resembles amorphous, network-like plant cutin, Colletes polyester is highly crystalline ( X c = 60%), with PE-like orthorhombic packing and T m = 75 °C, indicating a much lower cross-link density. Composition analysis of nest linings collected 0 to 11 mo after construction reveals significant degradation, with polyester content falling from 73 to 40 wt% within 4 mo in ambient soil. Esterase activity against the model substrate p-nitrophenylbutyrate is observed in both newly constructed and 4-mo aged linings, which may accelerate environmental degradation. Crystallites also lack higher-order spherulitic or lamellar structure, possibly due to cross-linking, which may promote degradation by leaving more esters exposed to cleavage. This PE-like polyester is shown to degrade rapidly in the environment, offering a template for next-generation biodegradable PE-like polymers.

items.title: Resistance mutation supply modulates the benefit of CRISPR immunity against virulent phages in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
items.abstract: Only a fraction of bacterial genomes encode CRISPR-Cas systems, but the selective causes of this variation are unexplained. How naturally virulent bacteriophages (phages) select for CRISPR immunity has rarely been tested experimentally. Here, we show against a panel of genetically and functionally diverse virulent phages that CRISPR immunity was not universally beneficial to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and its fitness effect varied strongly between phages in predictable ways. In addition to mechanisms known to alter the effectiveness of CRISPR immunity, such as encoding a matching spacer or a protective nuclear shell, we show that the fitness effect of CRISPR immunity negatively associated with the probability of evolving receptor-based resistance to the phage via spontaneous mutation. The supply of resistance mutations differed strongly between very closely related lipopolysaccharide-binding phages and was associated with variation at the C-terminus of the tail fibre protein altering residues involved in hydrogen bonding and the predicted binding site. Our results show that CRISPR immunity is more beneficial against virulent phages that are harder to evolve resistance to via receptor mutations, suggesting that virulent phage community composition and diversity will be important drivers of the prevalence of CRISPR immunity.

items.title: Exploration of lymphoproliferative disease virus strains in wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) in Iowa, USA.
items.abstract: Wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) were nearly extirpated in the early 1900's and extensive restoration efforts utilizing translocated wild turkeys were employed to restore populations. Although these efforts were successful, populations have again been in decline due to unknown causes. Lymphoproliferative disease virus (LPDV) was first detected in the United States in 2009. The coinciding appearance of LDPV and declining populations have led to studies in several states and provinces in North America to characterize its prevalence and distribution due to concerns about its potential role in population declines. The spread of disease agents is a common outcome during translocation programs and could be related to the spread of LPDV. Prior studies have performed phylogenetic analyses to examine genetic variation across and geographic clustering among strains. In this study we aimed to identify the diversity of LPDV strains present in wild turkeys in Iowa and if there was geographic clustering within the state or with other locations where LPDV has been detected. We sequenced a subset (n = 77) of hunter-harvested samples covering eight of the nine agricultural regions in Iowa that tested PCR positive with the viral gag gene. We performed phylogenetic analysis on 73 unique Iowan strains as well as previously catalogued strains from other regions retrieved from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank database. Overall, Iowa strains did not show geographic clustering within the state or with any other specific geographic regions. Our study demonstrated that there is a high level of genetic diversity among LPDV strains in Iowa and did not provide evidence of connection with a particular location external to Iowa as a source of introduction of LPDV to the state.

items.title: A novel methodology for assessing reinforcement choice in primates under human care
items.abstract: Positive Reinforcement Training is a technique commonly employed in zoological collections to elicit a desired behaviour from an animal under human care. Typically, a food item is offered as a reward for performing that behaviour. Three non-human primate species ( Mandrillus sphinx, Pan troglodytes , and Hylobates lar ) were offered four different foods (banana, grape, apple, and sweet potato) in a series of choice experiments. Latent variable models were employed to investigate which foods were the best selection to use as reinforcement items. Results show that food preference varies between the three primate species. Pan troglodytes and H. lar showed strong preferences for grape and banana, whereas M. sphinx showed a very strong preference for sweet potato. This study indicates that foraging ecology might play an important part in fruit selection and preference in primates. The findings highlight that understanding a species' natural behaviour and dietary preferences is key to informing reinforcement and training decisions.

items.title: Tropical Peatlands as Hotspots of Hidden Arcellinida Diversity: Insights from Maludam National Park, Borneo (Sarawak, Malaysia)
items.abstract: Recent investigations on tropical peatlands have shown their extremely high efficiency as carbon sinks, far beyond better studied boreal bogs. The microbial diversity found in those ecosystems, as well as their corresponding ecological and metabolic processes, are just starting to be revealed, and differ considerably from high latitudes systems. However, these efforts have been concentrated almost exclusively towards prokaryotes and fungi, leaving protist communities virtually unknown. Arcellinida (testate amoebae) are well acknowledged to play an important role in boreal and temperate peatland ecology by driving microbial community composition as top predators, but also as nutrient recyclers and carbon fixers. Yet, to our knowledge, no community–level study has addressed their diversity and its drivers in tropical peatlands. In this study, we surveyed Arcellinida communities' diversity across five functionally distinct vegetation–hydrological zones situated along a hydrological transect in a coastal tropical peatland in the Maludam National Park, Malaysia. Taxonomic composition of Arcellinida communities, characterized by a high diversity of Trigonopyxis-related taxa, indicated fundamental differences in diversity and community composition from extratropical ecosystems. Species richness was significantly higher in the zones with developed understory vegetation. Furthermore, the composition of diversity varied significantly among vegetation-hydrological zones. Altogether, this study shows unique Arcellinida communities in a Southeastern Asian peatland and suggests the importance of vegetation-hydrological characteristics for protist diversity.

items.title: Genomic and ecological specialization of Methanobrevibacter species shape human methane emission and overall gut ecosystem function
items.abstract: Abstract Methane is a unique archaeal metabolite that links gut microbial ecology to host physiology. Although intestinal methane production varies by several orders of magnitude between individuals and has been associated with gastrointestinal transit and disease states, the ecological and functional determinants underlying this variation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate breath methane phenotyping with shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, comparative genomics, cultivation and stable-isotope tracing in 80 deeply characterized individuals to determine the species-level and functional basis of human gut methanogenesis. Breath methane levels strongly reflected archaeal abundance but could not fully explain methane emission; species-resolved profiling revealed that methane emission represents distinct archaeome states rather than differences in methanogen quantity alone. High methane emitters were dominated by Methanobrevibacter smithii and M. intestini, whereas low emitters harbored a previously uncharacterized Methanobrevibacter lineage (M. sp900766745), for which we propose the name Candidatus Methanobrevibacter hominipaucus sp. nov. Comparative genomics revealed that M. sp900766745 represents a metabolically streamlined lineage lacking several methyl-compound utilization pathways and displaying reduced substrate acquisition capacity. Communities of low-emission individuals exhibited reduced microbial transcriptional activity and accumulated incompletely processed dietary metabolites, indicating lower fermentative turnover and altered hydrogen flux.

items.title: Between the “Left-Wing Tradition” and the “Middle Way”: The Evolution of the Republican People’s Party’s Political Identity (2002–2023)
items.abstract: Abstract The Republican People’s Party (CHP) is the oldest political party in Turkey. Over nearly a century of political change, its political positioning has undergone a profound transformation. The 2002 Turkish general election marked the beginning of the Justice and Development Party (AKP) era of single-party rule and plunged the CHP into a deep identity crisis: bearing the historical legacy of Kemalism while inheriting the “democratic left” tradition of the 1970s, the party was forced to seek a competitive position in a political landscape reshaped by Islamic conservatism and authoritarian populism. Over more than two decades from 2002 to 2023, the CHP’s identity displayed marked vacillation: it repeatedly swung between adhering to tradition and embracing the middle way, while remaining locked in a sustained tug-of-war between upholding Kemalist orthodoxy and renewing a social democratic agenda. This vacillation stemmed both from the constraints of Turkey’s particular political ecology and from the party’s strategic choice, as the main opposition party under authoritarian pressure, to ensure its survival. It was not until the defeat in the 2023 presidential election and the leadership turnover at the party congress that this two-decade-long identity entanglement reached a critical juncture. During the Baykal and Kılıçdaroğlu periods, the CHP’s composite left-wing index stagnated at around 2.2 points on a five-point scale, far below the benchmark levels of European social democratic parties. When Özgür Özel was elected party chairman in November 2023, he put forward a vision of returning to the democratic left.

items.title: Has climate change altered Jan Mayen Island Arctic Charr life-history traits and feeding ecology?
items.abstract: Abstract The population of Arctic charr in Lake Nordlaguna on the Arctic island of Jan Mayen became landlocked by a volcanic eruption in AD 1732 that caused a coastal uplift closing the lake off from the sea. Although considered as a relatively productive lake in terms of planktonic primary production, the lake is relatively species poor in comparison to lakes in other parts of the Arctic. Jan Mayen has already undergone significant shifts in temperature, with mean open-water season temperatures having risen from 3.8 o C in the early 1960s (1960-65) to 5.6 o C in the 2015–2020 period. To assess how rising temperatures may have influenced Arctic charr life-history traits and feeding ecology, we conducted a test fishery in Lake Nordlaguna to evaluate whether current life-history strategies and trophic niche use of the resident population has shifted from the early 1960s as the climate has warmed. The results showed that smaller Arctic charr were larger and age-at maturity younger than in 1963–1965, however trophic niches appear to have remained stable. It is, therefore, suggested that the increased temperature over the last six decades at Jan Mayen has changed the Arctic charr life-history strategy to mature at younger ages due to a limited food supply. Additional genetic analyses did not show differentiation of trophic morph types, however, the Jan Mayen population as a whole is shown to be highly genetically distinct from Arctic charr in other North Atlantic locations.

items.title: Repoliticising the CE: Sen’s Theory of Justice and the Ideologies Shaping Circular Transitions
items.abstract: Abstract The circular economy has emerged as a dominant sustainability framework, yet its rapid institutionalisation obscures critical questions about power, equity, and justice in industrial transitions. This article challenges the technocratic framing prevalent in circular economy discourse by developing an integrative framework that centres distributional, procedural, and recognitional justice alongside environmental performance. We synthesise critical scholarship on circular economy depoliticisation with Sen's theory of justice to reveal how ostensibly neutral technical choices embody political commitments with differential impacts across social groups and geographies. Our framework illuminates how different ideological orientations, from green anarchism to environmental authoritarianism, shape circular transitions and generate distinct justice outcomes. We argue that industrial ecology must expand beyond material flow analysis to incorporate justice assessment, moving from win-win assumptions toward honest engagement with the conflicts and trade-offs inherent in economic transformation. This shift is essential for the circular economy to deliver genuine sustainability rather than optimising existing inequalities within circular loops.

items.title: Helleborus caucasifcus and Helleborus abchasicus : An Integrative Review of Taxonomy, Ecology, Phytochemical Diversity, and Conservation
items.abstract: Helleborus caucasicus and Helleborus abchasicus are two Caucasian taxa of the family Ranunculaceae with considerable botanical, pharmacognostic, and phytochemical interest. However, knowledge of these plants remains fragmented across historical and contemporary publications, including a substantial body of literature published in Russian and Georgian, which limits its accessibility to the international scientific community. This narrative review synthesizes available evidence on their taxonomy, morphology, anatomical characteristics, distribution, ecology, phytochemical composition, biological activities, traditional uses, toxicity, and conservation. Attention is given to taxonomic uncertainties, intraspecific anatomical variability, and differences in research coverage between the two taxa. H. caucasicus has been more extensively investigated for steroidal constituents, including furostanol and spirostanol glycosides, caucasicosides A–M, ecdysteroids, and bufadienolides, whereas the phytochemistry of H. abchasicus remains comparatively underexplored. Studies of both species have also revealed complex lipid profiles influenced by plant organ, lipid class, and cultivation conditions. Available experimental evidence indicates cytotoxic and apoptosis-related effects of certain constituents of H. caucasicus, together with anti-inflammatory and wound-healing activities of lipid preparations from both species. Nevertheless, these findings remain predominantly preclinical, and species-specific toxicological evidence is insufficient. Conservation studies further reveal declining natural populations and variable outcomes of ex situ cultivation and reintroduction.

items.title: Synthetic microbial communities enable sustainable restoration of coal gangue-impacted soils by reprogramming nutrient cycling.
items.abstract: Coal gangue disrupts microbial diversity and impairs nutrient cycling, constraining sustainable regional development. Traditional bioremediation relies on functional microbial traits, yet they often fail to colonize and perform in carbon-limited environments despite exogenous carbon inputs. We designed activity-oriented synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) to leverage exogenous carbon amendments and subsequently evaluated carbon use efficiency (CUE) as a community-level functional trait. High-activity SynComs were assembled from native and non-native strains based on their activity and metabolite interactions. The native-derived SynCom (SC3) enhances carbon and nitrogen cycling, whereas the non-native-derived SynCom (SC5) boosts diversity and phosphorus cycling (P < 0.05). These contrasts were associated with differences in strain functional contributions, community interactions, and carbon-source utilization. Metabolomics revealed greater functional microbial activation in SC5-conditioned biochar-derived metabolites than in glucose-derived metabolites. Multi-omics, single-cell Raman spectroscopy, and field studies confirmed the positive roles of SynComs in rhizosphere metabolism and nutrient cycling. Activity-driven SynComs approach was more efficient than single amendments, offering a potentially scalable strategy to restore carbon-limited tailing ecosystems and promote sustainability.

items.title: Quantifying microbial fitness in high-throughput experiments.
items.abstract: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. What are the consequences of these different fitness statistics, and is there a best way to quantify fitness in a given context? Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli , affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.

items.title: CircoTax: a novel circular representation of differentially abundant microbial ranks.
items.abstract: One of the most relevant applications of NGS-based microbial abundance analysis is the discovery of taxa that appear as differentially represented between ecological niches. In the last years several methods have been proposed to accomplish this task, invariantly reporting the differentially represented taxa at the appropriate taxonomic rank as well as an adjusted p-value and a log2 fold change, representing the confidence on differential call and the amount of variation recorded. This work describes CircoTax, a specialized R ggplot2 plot representing a rank-aware collection of differentially abundant taxa in an intuitive, compact radial form. Specifically, the CircoTax is a circular plot with sectors encoding the taxonomy depth (from phylum to genus) and, departing from the center, a number of radial bars that reach rank-based sectors whose color and transparency are proportional to the log fold change intensity direction and p-value. The visualization of results is graphically appealing and allows to accommodate tens of differentially abundant ranks each with an associated amount of up or down variation so that results are easily intelligible for each differentially represented taxa at a glance. The software is freely available and can be run natively in R or through a dedicated ShinyApp for an interactive usage.

items.title: Why be deciduous in a tropical savanna climate? Insights from leaf deployment, stem growth and sap flow dynamics.
items.abstract: Savannas are ecosystems with hot and wet summers and warm and dry winters. How and why savanna trees partition their physiological activity through this seasonal cycle is unknown; yet it is important to understand this temporal partitioning in order to anticipate how anthropogenic climatic change will impact the functioning of savannas. In a South African savanna ecosystem, we examined the temporal pattern of leaf deployment, sap flow and stem increment phenology over three growing seasons for six species. We found that although the phenologies varied between years, there was a high degree of temporal overlap in leaf, sap flow and stem increment phenology between the six study species. Further, we found that a surprisingly large proportion of days on which the measured soil water potential was sufficient for physiological activity remained unused. Although our data are consistent with convergent selection for deciduousness, the unused soil water niche we detected suggests that climate should select for evergreen strategies. Possible explanations for the dominance of deciduousness in these savannas relate to the costs of leaf construction coupled with the risk of leaf destruction due to fire and/or foliovory.

items.title: Allometric scaling of adaxial-abaxial stomatal allocation in amphistomatous plants worldwide.
items.abstract: Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual-surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. We quantified their allometric relationship using phylogenetic reduced major axis regression and calculated amphistomatal scaling residuals (ASR) as signed perpendicular deviations from the fitted scaling relationship. We then examined variation in ASR among plant functional groups and across climatic and edaphic gradients. Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities showed a significant allometric relationship after accounting for phylogenetic nonindependence, with a slope significantly > 1. ASR showed a significant phylogenetic signal but did not differ significantly between woody and herbaceous species, evergreen and deciduous woody species, or annual and perennial herbs. Individual environmental associations with ASR were generally modest, whereas the selected phylogenetic model retained multiple interaction terms, indicating that associations between ASR and environmental conditions were strongly context-dependent. By quantifying departures from adaxial-abaxial scaling, our study identifies a distinct dimension of stomatal allocation that is structured by evolutionary history and associated with multidimensional climatic and edaphic context. This framework provides a basis for testing the physiological and evolutionary mechanisms underlying variation in amphistomatous stomatal allocation.

items.title: The role of animals in the epidemiology and pathogenesis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS): a scoping review.
items.abstract: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis with a high case-fatality rate and expanding geographic range. Its persistence depends on complex cycles involving ticks and vertebrate animal hosts. A comprehensive understanding of animal roles is critical for predicting spillover risk and developing effective interventions under a One Health framework. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize existing evidence on the roles of domestic animals, wildlife, and companion animals in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and transmission of SFTSV. Methods A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Multiple databases (MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang) and grey literature sources were searched from January 1, 2011 to October 21, 2025. Eligible studies involved non-human animals or ticks and confirmed SFTSV infection or exposure. Evidence was narratively synthesized across prespecified themes: animal host roles, clinical manifestations, transmission dynamics, and prevention strategies. We mapped the distribution of evidence across animal species, study designs, geographic regions, diagnostic approaches, and thematic domains. Results The review identified a broad animal host range comprising at least 15 vertebrate species across domestic, wildlife, and companion categories. Domestic ruminants show high seroprevalence and act as primary amplification hosts. Wildlife (e.g., rodents, shrews) contribute to enzootic maintenance. Cats are highly susceptible, develop severe disease with high viral loads, and are a major source of direct non-vector transmission to humans. Dogs often have mild illness but can shed virus persistently. Transmission primarily occurs via the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis, but direct transmission via contact with blood/secretions of sick animals (especially cats and farmed mink) is significant. Prevention requires integrated tick management, biosecurity in veterinary/farm settings, and public education. Conclusions Animals are central to the ecology of SFTSV. Current evidence underscores the necessity of integrated, multisectoral One Health strategies for surveillance, risk communication, and control. Future research priorities include standardizing host-competence studies, harmonizing diagnostics, elucidating comparative immunopathology, and evaluating the feasibility and impact of intervention bundles, including potential veterinary vaccines.

items.title: In vitro colonic fermentation of ferulic acid and trans-resveratrol: kinetic profiling and metabolic convergence.
items.abstract: In vitro batch fecal fermentation offers a controlled approach to study colonic catabolism of dietary (poly)phenols and their microbial metabolites. Here, the bioconversion of two (poly)phenols, ferulic acid (FA) and trans -resveratrol ( t -R), was followed over 48 h to assess metabolic convergence in their catabolic pathways. Using a human fecal inoculum, samples collected at 2, 6, 24 and 48 h were analyzed by UPLC-ESI-QqQ-MS/MS. FA and t -R displayed distinct degradation kinetics, consistent with their different molecular structures and steric constraints. FA was rapidly depleted within 2 h, whereas t -R persisted throughout incubation, with less than half converted by 6 h and ≈37% remaining at 48 h. Accordingly, FA catabolites peaked at 85% molar mass recovery at 2 h, while t -R-derived catabolites accumulated gradually, reaching ≈44% at 48 h. Despite these differences, both substrates were mainly processed through reduction followed by dehydroxylation, converging toward a shared pool of low-molecular-weight phenolic acids. FA degradation was characterized by phenylpropanoic acid formation after hydrogenation of the unsaturated side chain, whereas t -R catabolism yielded dibenzyl derivatives, mainly dihydroresveratrol and lunularin. Notably, 3-(4'-hydroxyphenyl)propanoic acid emerged as a major FA catabolite, and several phenolic acids were quantified as t -R-derived products, suggesting minor routes involving the cleavage of the stilbene central linkage and subsequent methyl oxidation. Overall, we propose a sequence of microbial enzymatic reactions underlying FA and t -R colonic catabolism. Future studies should validate these findings across donors and integrate microbiome functional readouts to explain inter-individual variability in bioconversion.

items.title: A comprehensive mapping review of participatory autism research over a 22-year period.
items.abstract: Background Participatory research, which involves community members as partners rather than merely research subjects, has gained prominence in autism research. However, the extent and nature of participatory approaches across the field remain unclear. Methods We conducted a mapping review of autism research reporting community involvement, searching six databases. We coded who was involved, at what level, and in which research activities, and examined factors associated with participation. Results We identified 382 studies published between 2001 and 2023, with 95% published in the past decade. Two-thirds (67%) involved Autistic people, though one-third claiming to be "participatory" excluded them entirely. The most common participation level was consulting (31%), with community-led (5%) and community-controlled (1%) research remaining rare. Community involvement concentrated in study design (73%) rather than analysis (33%) or dissemination (29%). Participatory research was heavily concentrated in Western countries (USA, UK, Australia, Canada: 86%), applied research areas, and qualitative studies. Deeper participation was associated with identity-first language use and publication in journals with clear community-centered agendas. Conclusions While participatory language is increasingly becoming the norm in autism research, genuine power-sharing between researchers and community members is still a rare occurrence. Most participatory research operates at consultative levels, with academic researchers retaining primary decision-making authority. Moving toward authentic participation requires systemic changes to funding structures, institutional policies, and epistemic hierarchies that determine whose knowledge counts.

items.title: Investigating associations between personality and problematic social media use by considering trait and state FoMO as mediators.
items.abstract: High Neuroticism and low Conscientiousness robustly correlate with both Problematic Social Media Use (PSMU) and Fear of Missing Out (FoMO). However studies investigating these concepts simultaneously are relatively rare, and few have examined the associations between the personality traits and PSMU by investigating both trait and state FoMO as potential mediators. In a sample of 576 German-speaking participants (of whom n = 94 were aged 13-17), we observed that higher Neuroticism and lower Conscientiousness were associated with higher PSMU. Mediation results indicated that Neuroticism was indirectly associated with PSMU via both state FoMO (β = 0.10, b = 0.63, Proportion Mediated [PM] = 27.3%, 95% CI [0.36, 0.91]) and trait FoMO (β = 0.05, b = 0.33, PM = 14.3%, 95% CI [0.13, 0.53], p < .001). Conversely, for Conscientiousness, only state FoMO emerged as a significant mediator (β = -0.06, b = -0.48, PM = 33.8%, 95% CI [-0.81, -0.16], p = .002); the indirect pathway via trait FoMO was non-significant (β = -0.02, b = -0.12, 95% CI [-0.28, 0.02], p = .09). These findings suggest that state FoMO, which reflects online-specific anxiety, is a more consistent factor linking personality traits to PSMU than general trait FoMO. This distinction suggests that state FoMO could be considered a potential target for practical interventions, as it is more situational and might be easier to change than personality traits.

items.title: Harnessing the placebo effect: A practical review of mechanisms and clinical applications.
items.abstract: The placebo effect is a powerful psychobiological phenomenon that significantly influences clinical outcomes in a wide range of medical conditions. Conversely, the nocebo effect, whereby negative expectations worsen symptoms or generate adverse effects, can undermine treatment efficacy, increase symptom burden, and reduce medication adherence. This review examines the historical evolution, neurobiological underpinnings, and key determinants of the placebo and nocebo responses. Practical strategies are outlined to ethically harness placebo effects and minimize nocebo responses in clinical practice.

items.title: The neuropsychological profile of an individual with early-onset CSF1R- related disorder with biallelic mutation.
items.abstract: CSF1R-related disorder (CSF1R-RD) is a rare, rapidly progressive microgliopathy due to Colony Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor (CSF1R) gene mutation, resulting in movement disorder and dementia in young people. Clinical phenotypes are bimodal, including middle-age onset with a monoallelic mutation and early childhood onset with a biallelic mutation. The latter, more proliferative phenotype, has historically been known as Brain Abnormalities, Neurodegeneration, and Dysosteosclerosis (BANDDOS). There are no research studies characterizing cognition in biallelic CSF1R-RD. We present the neuropsychological profile of a 21-year-old woman with biallelic disease. This patient completed the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Dementia Rating Scale-2 (DRS-2), Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale-IV selected subtests, Trail Making Test, Boston Naming Test-15, and mood measures. Performance was normal on the MoCA (28/30) but below average on the DRS-2 (123/144). The full neuropsychological profile revealed impaired general and verbal processing speed but preserved naming and memory retention. Findings represent the first formal cognitive characterization of biallelic CSF1R-RD, confirming a profile consistent with monoallelic CSF1R-RD. In CSF1R-RD, comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation is needed, as brief cognitive screening alone may fail to fully characterize the cognitive impact of the disease.

items.title: Menarche and ADHD: associations between puberty, ADHD traits and mental health in female adolescents.
items.abstract: Background Adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) may be more vulnerable to cooccurring mental health challenges during puberty, and some evidence suggests that puberty impacts ADHD traits. However, pubertal influences on psychological outcomes in female adolescents with ADHD are poorly understood. We investigated how menarche relates to ADHD traits and its potential moderation of associations between ADHD status or traits and mental health. Methods Analyses used Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development SM Study data from baseline to wave 3 (N = 5,318; 100% female; baseline age M = 9.9, SD = 0.6; 52.3% non-Hispanic White). ADHD traits, internalising difficulties and externalising difficulties were measured using the Child Behavior Checklist. Bayesian generalised linear mixed models examined cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between menarche status and ADHD traits. Interactions between menarche status and ADHD status or traits as predictors of mental health outcomes were also investigated. In comparative analyses, breast development replaced menarche status. Results ADHD traits did not differ between pre- and post-menarche adolescents in cross-sectional analyses, but post-menarche adolescents had higher ADHD traits the following year. Complete breast development (vs. not started) also predicted higher ADHD traits the next year. Interactions between menarche and ADHD status were not associated with mental health outcomes cross-sectionally or longitudinally. Positive associations between ADHD traits and mental health difficulties were marginally stronger in post-menarche adolescents. The association between higher wave 2 ADHD traits and greater wave 3 externalising difficulties was substantially stronger with more advanced breast development at wave 2. Conclusions Longitudinal findings provide preliminary evidence that more advanced gonadarche in early adolescence is prospectively associated with elevated ADHD trait expression in females when controlling for individual differences in ADHD trait levels. More advanced breast development may reflect physiological and psychosocial changes that could contribute to a stronger relationship between higher ADHD traits and greater subsequent externalising difficulties.

items.title: Cost-Utility of Improving Access to Psychological Therapies compared with usual care in Norway: A Registry-Linked Randomised Trial.
items.abstract: Objectives Prompt Mental Health Care (PMHC), Norway's adaptation of England's Improving Access to Psychological Therapies, provides cognitive behavioural therapy for adults with anxiety or mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms. We assessed cost-utility using registry-linked data. Methods This evaluation included 738 participants from a randomised trial (70:30 allocation) of PMHC versus treatment-as-usual (TAU). Registry data provided healthcare costs, prescriptions, sick leave and work assessment allowances. EQ-5D-5L was assessed through 36 months in PMHC and 12 months in TAU; TAU utilities at 24 and 36 months were model-projected. Presenteeism was assessed with the Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Cost-utility was estimated over 1-, 2-, and 3-year horizons from healthcare and public-sector perspectives. Results Over 1 year, incremental QALYs were 0.07 (95% CI 0.05-0.10), with incremental healthcare costs of €1,710 (95% CI €1,557-€1,865), yielding an ICER of €23,809/QALY (95% CI €16,272-€38,321). Over 3 years, model-based estimates were 0.24 incremental QALYs (95% CI 0.14-0.35) and €1,551 in incremental healthcare costs (95% CI €1,266-€1,837), yielding an ICER of €6,376/QALY (95% CI €4,055-€11,533). At €30,000/QALY, cost-effectiveness probability was 84% over 1 year and ≥99% over 2 and 3 years. Incremental public-sector costs over 3 years were -€296 (95% CI -€3,588 to €2,848) when sick-leave benefits and work assessment allowances were included alongside healthcare costs. Presenteeism gains equalled 0.25 full-productivity years. Conclusions PMHC delivered sustained health gains at modest additional healthcare cost and was likely cost-effective, with ICERs below Norwegian and UK NICE thresholds. Incremental public-sector costs were close to zero over 3 years, although uncertain.

items.title: Long-term effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy on cognition: A narrative review.
items.abstract: Short-to-medium-term studies provide robust evidence of improved psychosocial functioning but are equivocal on gender affirming hormone therapy's (GAHT) influence on cognition and cognitive aging in transgender adults. As such, the longer-term influence of exogenous steroids on cognitive functions, and age-related decline, remains relatively unexplored. We carried out a narrative review of the literature and found 18 studies that assessed the effect of GAHT on cognition in transgender adults; only two assessed its effects on cognitive aging. There was significant variability in the studies along the lines of design, cohort, age of participants, and GAHT regimens all of which likely contributed to equivocal findings of the effect of GAHT on most cognitive tasks assessed. The paucity of studies of cognition and aging, the methodological variations across studies, and potential biases in recruitment leave an important gap in our understanding of the long-term effects of GAHT on cognitive health in transgender individuals.

items.title: Regional Radiomics Similarity Networks Reveal Specific Brain Morphological Connectivity Patterns in Migraine and Tension-Type Headaches.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated structural brain alterations in migraine and tension-type headache using regional radiomics similarity network to characterize disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns. Background Migraine and tension-type headache are the most prevalent primary headache disorders involving central nervous system dysfunction. While functional magnetic resonance imaging has revealed abnormalities, structural changes remain incompletely understood. Regional radiomics similarity network, a novel approach for modeling individualized morphological brain networks, has not been applied in primary headaches. Methods We enrolled 65 migraine patients, 49 tension-type headache patients, and 53 healthy controls. Regional radiomics similarity network was constructed using 88 radiomics features. Regional mean connectivity strength and voxel-based morphometry were compared across groups. Spearman correlation was performed between network measures and visual analogue scale scores. Generative adversarial networks were used for classification. Results Voxel-based morphometry revealed gray matter volume alterations in cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions across the three groups. Regional radiomics similarity network analysis identified distinct morphological connectivity patterns: patients with migraine showed altered connectivity involving frontal, limbic, and subcortical regions, whereas patients with tension-type headache exhibited prominent alterations involving the cerebellum and thalamic-temporal connections. Exploratory partial correlation analyses suggested associations between several altered connections and pain severity. The model achieved 84.31% classification accuracy. Conclusions Regional radiomics similarity network captures disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns beyond conventional structural measurements, providing insights into structural network substrates of primary headaches. This study establishes regional radiomics similarity network as a promising neuroimaging framework for investigating brain structural alterations in migraine and tension-type headache.

items.title: Design of a pragmatic cluster randomized controlled trial: Reducing high risk polypharmacy using behavioral economics through electronic health records.
items.abstract: Background Inappropriate polypharmacy can lead to harms among older adults. Behavioral nudges delivered using decision support in electronic health records (EHR) may be a scalable way to reduce polypharmacy. The goal of the High-Risk PolyPharmacy (HRPP) trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of a 'commitment nudge' and a 'justification nudge' alone and in combination on reducing HRPP via a pragmatic, clinic-randomized trial among patients aged 65 years and older. Methods/design This 2 × 2 clinic-randomized factorial trial in primary care clinics in two health systems has four parallel arms: EHR commitment nudge, EHR justification nudge, both, or neither, all coupled with optional clinician education activities. Eligible patients are aged ≥65 years actively using ≥5 systemic, oral medications. The primary outcome is a composite of seven indicators of HRPP. Secondary outcomes include the individual components of HRPP and measures of health system burden: all-cause and adverse drug event-specific emergency department (ED) visits and ED visits followed by hospitalization. Results We used constrained randomization to produce balance between study arms for 124 primary care clinics comprising 804 clinicians. At randomization, the median (range) practice had 573 (326-947) eligible patients; the average clinic-level prevalence of HRPP among these patients was 30.0%. The 18-month intervention began in 2023-October and 2024-November at NM and UPMC, respectively. Data collection will end in 2026-April at NM and 2026-December at UPMC. Conclusions This trial is evaluating the effectiveness and safety of EHR-embedded interventions to reduce HRPP. If successful, this intervention could offer a low-cost, scalable solution. Clinical trials registration number NCT05656560.
