items.title: From Daily Attitudes to Alcohol-Related Harm: A Within-Person Serial Mediation Test Informed by the Theory of Planned Behavior.
items.abstract: Background The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) posits that attitudes influence behavior through intentions, yet this pathway has not been thoroughly examined at the within-person level in the alcohol literature. This study tested whether daily fluctuations in attitudes toward heavy drinking predicted same-day alcohol-related consequences and alcohol-induced blackouts through a serial mediation involving daily drinking intentions and alcohol consumption. Methods Participants were 87 heavy-drinking young adults (53.4% female; Mage = 22.22 years) enrolled in the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial who completed up to 30 consecutive days of morning diary assessments. Multilevel models separated within-and between-person variance by person-mean centering daily predictors. Serial mediation pathways were estimated using multilevel regression models, and specific indirect effects were tested using Monte Carlo confidence intervals. Results On days when participants reported more favorable attitudes toward heavy drinking than their own average, they also reported stronger intentions to drink, which predicted greater same-day alcohol consumption. Greater drinking, in turn, predicted increased odds of both alcohol-related consequences and blackout. Significant serial indirect effects supported the hypothesized pathway from attitudes to consequences and blackout through intentions and drinking. Drinking intentions also directly predicted alcohol-related consequences independent of drinking quantity but did not directly predict blackout after accounting for drinking, suggesting differences in the mechanisms underlying these outcomes. Conclusion Findings provide day-level support for a TPB-informed pathway linking within-person fluctuations in drinking attitudes to alcohol-related harm through drinking intentions and alcohol consumption. Results extend prior between-person TPB research by demonstrating that attitudes and intentions function as dynamic, day-to-day processes that help explain when individuals are at elevated risk for harmful drinking outcomes. Daily attitudes and intentions may represent promising targets for ecological momentary interventions designed to reduce alcohol-related harm.

items.title: Functional Health Illiteracy in Cancer Patients and Caregivers in the Era of Precision Medicine and Immunotherapy: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Functional health illiteracy is a significant barrier to equitable cancer care for patients and caregivers, a challenge that is exacerbated by precision medicine and immunotherapy. This review article aimed at synthesizing current evidence on functional health illiteracy among cancer patients and caregivers and examines its interaction with the demands of precision medicine and immunotherapy. The article also outlines practical strategies to mitigate the impact of health illiteracy on therapy adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes. Articles published between 2010 and 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Policy reports from the National Cancer Institute, the Institute of Medicine, and the American Society of Clinical Oncology were also included to provide contextual background. Consistency in article selection was assessed using the K coefficient. Approximately 36-50% of cancer patients were found to be unable to effectively use health information. Older adults, racial and ethnic minorities, and individuals with lower incomes are disproportionately affected. The complex terminology of precision oncology further complicates matters for patients and caregivers, who must manage intricate drug regimens and monitor for immune-related side effects at home. Low health literacy is associated with reduced clinical trial enrollment, decreased therapy adherence, increased emergency department visits, and poorer survival. Interventions, including plain-language use, culturally tailored instructions, digital health skill development, and organizational modifications, have demonstrated efficacy in enhancing health literacy among cancer patients and caregivers. These approaches improve access to medical information, reduce misunderstandings, and support self-management. As precision medicine evolves, aligning clinical complexity with targeted health literacy strategies is essential to optimize adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes.

items.title: Difficult Clinical Encounters in Chronic Wound Care: An Interview Study of Nurses' Experiences and Approaches.
items.abstract: Although difficult social interaction patterns are scientifically addressed in other medical fields, it is an under-researched topic in wound care. A knowledge gap exists pertaining to what kind of interpersonal problems occur between patients with chronic wounds, their relatives and nurses. In an exploratory interview study, we analyzed 37 interviews with nurses from different settings to explore how they perceive and approach difficult encounters with patients with chronic wounds. A content analysis conducted with MAXQDA revealed three broad themes of difficult nurse-patient interactions. First, conflicts included aggression, violence, insults, arguments, unrealistic demands, discrimination, lying, complaints, and general unfriendly behaviour. Often, nurses function as a kind of outlet for patients' annoyance. Second, non-adherence was associated with perceiving treatment as difficult. Third, difficult but non-conflictual situations were also common, that is, various and multilayered issues which complicate treatment. In addition, an overview of what respondents considered an ideal wound care practitioner is provided. Interventions could target self-care, nonviolent communication, and health literacy.

We examined: (i) use of illicitly traded tobacco (ITT) and reasons for use among two populations of people who use drugs in Australia; and (ii) factors associated with ITT use, versus exclusive licit tobacco use, in 2024 and 2025. items.title: Environmental scan of hearing health services and databases in Australia: barriers and enablers for a national child deafness Learning Health System.
items.abstract: Objective To conduct a national environmental scan of child hearing health-related services and databases as part of the Australian National Child Hearing Health Outcomes Registry program, and to identify system-level barriers and enablers to developing a coordinated Learning Health System for deaf and hard-of-hearing children. Methods A cross-sectional national survey of organisations providing hearing health-related services or managing data for Australian deaf and hard-of-hearing children. The survey examined the scope and practices related to data collection, standardisation, interoperability, stewardship, and governance. Results Ninety-nine respondents from 92 organisations delivering 290 services participated. The scan identified a disjointed data landscape. Standardised data were limited, with inconsistent capture of key variables across organisations and 49.4% rating their data quality as acceptable or good. Interoperability was constrained by heterogenous data practices, including use of multiple databases (34.3%), limited external reporting (24.2%) and lack of accessible data dictionaries (71.9%). Stewardship and data governance arrangements were variable, with fewer than half of organisations reporting formal consent (47.6%), privacy statements (51.2%) or ethics oversight (38.1%). Despite these challenges, 56.5 and 54.8% of organisations expressed interest in data linkage and research participation, indicating readiness for coordinated system development. Conclusion Despite Australia's substantial investment in newborn hearing screening and hearing health-related services, fragmented data systems limit Australia's ability to monitor outcomes, equity and system performance in child hearing health. However, strong stakeholder interest in data linkage provides important momentum. These findings inform policy and service planning, and support staged development of a national child deafness Learning Health System through the Australian National Child Hearing Health Outcomes Registry.

items.title: Neurophysiological and Behavioural Effects of Combined Cannabis Concentrates and Alcohol Among People Who Regularly Use Alcohol and Cannabis.
items.abstract: Increasingly potent concentrated cannabis products containing high levels of Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) are being consumed with alcohol. This combination is known to acutely impair cognitive and psychomotor abilities, although few studies have evaluated alcohol and cannabis co-use using neural measures. This naturalistic feasibility study explored the acute effects of co-intoxication on behavioural performance and brain activity, measured via electroencephalography (EEG), during a performance monitoring task administered three times over a 4.5-h period. Participants (N = 17, 65% male) were heavy drinking community members (age M = 31.7 years; SD = 10.27) who regularly use cannabis. EEG was recorded while participants completed a speeded visual-flanker task at baseline (sober) before consuming a standardized dose of alcohol and a cannabis concentrate product, followed by EEG recordings 1-h (intoxicated) and 4-h post co-consumption (recovery). Recordings were processed to obtain six event-related potential components: the stimulus-locked N1, P2, N2 and P3 and response-locked error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed that behavioural measures at the intoxicated timepoint showed an increase in errors (p 2 p = 0.35) and significant decrease in response time (RT) (p 2 p = 0.50) compared to sober and recovery periods. Measures of brain activity also demonstrated significant change across time with largest amplitudes when sober, smaller amplitudes when intoxicated, then an increase in amplitude to near sober levels at recovery for stimulus-locked (P2, N2 and P3) and response-locked components (ERN and Pe). Thus, compared to sober and recovery periods, the behaviour at the intoxicated timepoint revealed significantly greater impulsivity (RT) leading to significantly higher error rates, while measures of cognitive processing (i.e., decision-making, error detection, performance monitoring/adaptation) showed significantly diminished levels of brain activity. Performance and neurophysiology measures remained diminished at recovery compared to baseline. Understanding neurocognitive functioning during co-intoxication may provide insights into specific cognitive processes that may impact function in everyday activities such as driving. items.title: Pavlovian cues and self-control choice: The role of unpaired training.
items.abstract: Interventions seeking to reduce impulsive choice in nonhuman animals (i.e., preference for smaller sooner over larger later rewards [SSR vs. LLR]) often require long training durations. However, prior studies illustrate how a brief course of Pavlovian training can reduce rodents' impulsive choice by attracting them to the LLR and by providing an appetitive Pavlovian conditioned stimulus (CS) contingent on LLR choices. In these studies, the comparison group completed unpaired (UN) training where the CS and US never co-occurred. The present study added a truly random control (TRC) group to evaluate whether UN training made the CS aversive, exaggerating the effect of Pavlovian training on self-control. Following Pavlovian (PAV), UN, or TRC training, a lever CS was inserted into the chamber during half the delay to the LLR. PAV rats were significantly more attracted to the lever during training and chose the LLR significantly more often than TRC or UN rats. Significant sex differences were detected, with self-control influencing the effects of Pavlovian training predominantly observed in male rats. Because sex differences in self-control outcomes were not observed in the only other study to examine the effects of presenting an appetitive CS after LLR choices, possible reasons for this interexperiment difference are discussed.

items.title: Human Development and the Architecture of Everyday Worry: Latent Worry Profiles in the World Risk Poll.
items.abstract: Whether public concern about risk rises or falls with national development has been debated for three decades, but the debate has compared countries hazard by hazard, asking how much people worry rather than how worry is organized. We provide a person-centered analysis of everyday worry at global scale, applying latent class analysis to the six-hazard worry battery of the Lloyd's Register Foundation World Risk Poll and linking profiles to the Human Development Index (HDI) in 140 countries ( n=139,111 ; 2023 wave), with the 2021 wave ( n=118,703 ; 119 countries) as an independent replication. Four worry profiles replicate almost exactly across waves, including a configurationally distinct secure-basics profile (15% of respondents) combining low worry about food and water with high worry about crime, severe weather, and traffic. Profile prevalence is consistent with the ordered sequence predicted by a need-priority account of worry allocation: pervasive worry falls from 33% to 13% between low- and very-high-HDI countries, low worry nearly doubles, and the secure-basics profile holds steady across low- and medium-HDI countries before declining at higher development. Traffic accidents are the most intense worry in every tier below very high HDI. These gradients persist after adjustment for self-reported recent harm and demographic composition and are only partly accounted for by the objective hazard environment, though the cross-sectional design cannot separate development from macroregional clustering. Development is associated with the composition of worry, not only its overall level; risk communication may be better matched to a country's worry architecture than to a single global template.

items.title: The Role of Stress and Resilience Profiles in Emotional Health.
items.abstract: Distal and proximal life stressors, including past trauma, subjective social status, and perceived stress can accumulate over time, placing strain on the body and contributing to increased allostatic load. Consequently, those with heightened stress experiences are at elevated risk of both mental and physical health concerns. However, research suggests that resilience may be a seminal protective factor, often safeguarding against negative health outcomes in the context of stress. Despite the extensive research base in stress and resilience, limited investigations have focused on how they co-occur and shape emotion processes. The current study strives to address these gaps by (1) exploring patterns of distal and proximal stress and resilience and (2) mapping these patterns onto two emotion processes found to have significant influence on health outcomes: emotion regulation and emotionality stigma. A sample of 329 adults (M age = 37.83, SD age = 11.86) were recruited using an online recruitment system and reported on their experiences of distal and proximal stress, resilience, emotion regulation, and emotionality stigma. Participants primarily identified as non-Hispanic (90.2%) and White (77.8%), with a household income of less than $55,000 (52.8%). Using latent profile analysis (LPA), three unique subgroups emerged based on the co-occurrence of distal and proximal stressors with resilience: (1) low stress, high resilience, (2) high proximal stress, low resilience, and (3) high distal stress, moderate resilience. These profiles were significantly associated with emotion processes such that those in the high proximal stress, low resilience profile reported significantly lower emotion regulation than those in the other two profiles. Participants in both higher-stress profiles reported significantly greater emotionality stigma than those in the low stress, high resilience profile. Finding implications for future research and practice are discussed.

items.title: Callous-Unemotional Traits and Aggression: Maternal Parenting as a Developmental Moderator.
items.abstract: Conduct Disorder (CD) is associated with persistent and severe forms of aggression, particularly among youth with callous-unemotional (CU) traits. Although CU traits are linked to proactive aggression, less is known about how environmental factors, such as parenting, shape these associations over time. The present study examined whether maternal and paternal warmth and hostility moderated the longitudinal associations between CU traits and proactive and reactive aggression in adolescents with CD. Participants included 148 youth with CD aged 12-17 years (M age = 15.57, 69% male, 51% African American) assessed at baseline and 6 months. Hierarchical regression models tested moderation effects of maternal and paternal warmth and hostility between CU traits and aggression subtypes while controlling for baseline aggression. Maternal warmth and hostility significantly moderated the association between CU traits and proactive aggression, such that CU traits predicted increases in proactive aggression under conditions of low maternal warmth and high maternal hostility. No significant moderating effects were observed for reactive aggression or paternal parenting. Findings suggest that the influence of CU traits on aggression is context-dependent and varies across aggression subtypes, with maternal parenting playing a key role in shaping the development of proactive aggression. By highlighting the interaction between dispositional traits and caregiving environments, these results refine theoretical models of aggression and identify potential targets for intervention, suggesting that efforts to increase maternal warmth and reduce hostility may help mitigate risk for severe, goal-directed aggression in this high-risk population.

items.title: A systematic review of observational and report-based measures of caregiver sensitivity: A Latin American perspective.
items.abstract: Sensitivity is a cornerstone of early childhood mental health; however, its measurement relies heavily on tools developed in English-speaking, high-resource contexts. This systematic review identified observational and report-based instruments used to assess sensitivity in caregivers of children aged 0-6 years. It evaluated the methodological robustness and usability of these instruments within Latin American contexts. Following a systematic search in Web of Science, Scopus, PsycInfo, and Redalyc, 732 eligible studies were identified. Based on a frequency-of-use threshold, 16 instruments (14 observational and 2 report-based) represented across 616 papers were selected for in-depth evaluation. Measures were coded for theoretical alignment with Ainsworth's sensitivity definition, psychometric evidence, and usability-specifically training accessibility, administration complexity, and evidence of use with diverse Latin American populations (e.g., caregivers in rural settings or with lower educational levels). Results revealed that only a minority of measures adhered explicitly to Ainsworth's original definition. Most instruments prioritized warmth and positive affect, potentially leading to cross-cultural underdetection in contexts where responsiveness is expressed through proximity and routine-based care. While observational tools predominated, report-based measures showed limited validation and minimal regional use. These findings highlight the urgent need for culturally grounded validation and the development of accessible training programs for the region.

items.title: Limitations in the Assessment of Pain Reporting Reliability-Validation of the Focused Analgesia Selection Test.
items.abstract: Background Unreliable pain reporting predicts placebo responses in clinical trials and has been documented in chronic pain populations. The thermal Focused Analgesia Selection Test (FAST) quantifies Pain Reporting Reliability (PRR) by assessing consistency when rating repeated thermal stimuli of varying intensities presented in pseudo-randomized order. However, FAST's validity as a pure measure of reporting reliability remains unclear. Methods We investigated whether PRR derived from the thermal FAST is confounded by individual differences in pain sensitivity (pain and tolerance thresholds), stimuli extending beyond individual pain ranges, and temporal trends. Fifty-five healthy participants (32 women) completed the thermal FAST protocol comprising 49 stimuli across seven temperatures (43°C-50°C). Results Higher pain thresholds predicted lower PRR (b = -4.66, 95% HDI [-9.18, -0.07]). Exploratory analysis suggests that rating variability was reduced when stimulation fell outside individual pain ranges (below-range: b = -8.04, 95% HDI [-11.44, -4.72]; above-range: b = -4.45, 95% HDI [-7.98, -0.90]). Greater coverage of FAST temperatures by individual pain ranges correlated with higher PRR (ρ = 0.33). Thermode repositioning to prevent habituation at the stimulation site may have induced acute sensitization at the repositioned site as pain ratings increased by +33 and +19 VAS points at the first two stimuli following repositioning. Excluding these trials improved median PRR by 16% (from R 2 = 0.65 to 0.81). Conclusions PRR derived from the current thermal FAST implementation likely conflates reporting consistency with pain sensitivity, psychophysical range effects, and procedural artifacts and may therefore risk misclassifying pain phenotypes as reporting inconsistencies. We propose methodological refinements, particularly individualized stimulus calibration and optimized repositioning protocols, which should be evaluated in confirmatory studies and chronic pain populations.

items.title: Validation of the Romanian Version of the Young Positive Schema Questionnaire in the General Population.
items.abstract: Early adaptive schemas (EASs) are a recent extension of schema theory, conceptualized as positive cognitive-emotional patterns that arise when core psychological needs are consistently met during early development. Although early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) have been extensively linked to psychopathology, empirical research on EASs remains comparatively limited. Our study aimed to validate the Young Positive Schema Questionnaire (YPSQ) in a nonclinical Romanian sample (N = 1309). The original 14-factor structure showed excellent fit, the YPSQ subscales demonstrated adequate to good internal consistency, and construct validity was supported by theoretically consistent associations with EMSs, personality traits, psychological well-being, and psychological distress. As hypothesized, EASs were negatively associated with irrational beliefs and positively associated with rational beliefs, extending evidence on the construct validity of EASs to cognitive constructs derived from rational emotive behavior therapy. Exploratory hierarchical regression analyses further indicated that EASs explained additional, although modest, variance in depression, stress, and anxiety beyond EMSs, providing evidence of incremental validity. Overall, the findings support the Romanian YPSQ as a psychometrically sound measure of EASs and reinforce the value of assessing adaptive schemas alongside maladaptive schemas. Further longitudinal and moderation-based research is needed to clarify whether EASs contribute prospectively to resilience or buffer the effects of risk factors on psychological distress.

items.title: Male mice are more susceptible than females to obesity-induced muscle atrophy when fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet.
items.abstract: Obesity-related skeletal muscle atrophy poses a significant health burden, with marked sex differences in this condition. However, the mechanisms underlying these sex differences remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether and to what extent skeletal muscle quality was impaired in C57BL/6 mice fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet, focusing on sexual dimorphism. Male and female mice were assigned to control or HFHC groups for 40 weeks. The results showed that both sexes fed the HFHC diet developed obesity and dyslipidemia, with males exhibiting a more severe phenotype. Notably, males experienced more pronounced obesity-induced muscle atrophy than females. This study further revealed that HFHC feeding disrupted physiological homeostasis in both sexes, leading to sexual dimorphism in gut microbial composition and short-chain fatty acid levels, with males displaying a diminished capacity to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, males exhibited more severe mitochondrial dysfunction and higher oxidative stress levels compared to females, manifesting as reduced muscle strength and upregulated atrophy-related gene expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that long-term HFHC feeding disrupts gut microbiota and glucolipid metabolic homeostasis, further impairing mitochondrial function and exacerbating muscle atrophy preferentially in males, whereas females are relatively protected through superior maintenance of physiological homeostasis, resulting in milder muscle atrophy.

items.title: Is SARS-CoV-2 Infection (COVID-19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Wales.
items.abstract: Objectives Explore the relationship between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales. Study design Mixed observational epidemiological cross-sectional and cohort. Methods Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory-confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with the population trend. Results Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020-22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009-19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020-2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre-pandemic population-level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level. Conclusions There was no clear evidence at population-level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe-wide trend that pre-dated COVID-19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

items.title: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling.
items.abstract: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

items.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
items.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides, terpenoids, phenylpropanoid-derived compounds, and hybrid metabolites with antibacterial activities mediated through inhibition of ribosomes, cell wall and membrane biosynthesis, and bacterial resistance mechanisms. Their genomes encode diverse PKS, NRPS, TPS, and hybrid biosynthetic systems, many of which remain cryptic. Advances in chemical elicitation, co-cultivation, epigenetic modulation, CRISPR-based engineering, genome mining, and machine learning are accelerating the activation of silent clusters and the assignment of BGCs to their metabolites. Several fungal metabolites exhibit potent activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MRSA, and some enhance the efficacy of existing antibiotics. This review highlights current progress, identifies remaining challenges in metabolite production and BGC annotation, and outlines future directions for translating endophytic fungi into a sustainable platform for next-generation antibacterial drug discovery.

items.title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
items.abstract: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HIT block ) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V˙O2max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min -1 kg -1 ) were assigned to either HIT block or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HIT block completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity 15-min ), velocity at 4 mmol·L -1 blood lactate (velocity 4mmol ), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V˙O2max testing ( velocityV˙O2max ). HIT block demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocityV˙O2max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity 4mmol (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity 15-min did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HIT block compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

items.title: γ-T3 Increases the Sensitization of Gastric Cancer Cells to OXA by a Regulation of ARHGAP29.
items.abstract: γ-Tocotrienol (γ-T3) exhibits potent anti-cancer effects in vitro and in vivo. Our previous study demonstrated that γ-T3 modulates autophagy activity in gastric cancer (GC) cells via the GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway. In this study, we further explored whether γ-T3 also enhances the chemosensitivity of GC cells to oxaliplatin (OXA) by regulating ARHGAP29, and verified the direct binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29 as well as the physical interaction of ARHGAP29 with GSK-3β. We employed cell viability assays, flow cytometry, tumor cell spheroid formation assays, RT-qPCR, Western blot analysis, and stable overexpression transfection. Additionally, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and chloroquine (CQ) rescue CCK-8 assays were performed for molecular interaction and autophagy function verification; we established a xenografted tumor model using MKN45 cells in BALB/c nude mice (nu/nu). γ-T3 and OXA inhibited GC cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo, with a synergistic effect when combined (CI = 0.55 in MKN45 cells). In a mouse model, intraperitoneal injection of γ-T3 (20 mg/kg b.w.) and OXA (2.0 mg/kg b.w.) suppressed MKN45 cell xenograft growth. This was related to cell cycle arrest and inhibition of cancer stem cells (CSCs). γ-T3 alone or combined with OXA altered autophagy-related protein levels after 48 h treatment, with elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratio and Beclin1 expression, and reduced p62 abundance, functional rescue with autophagy inhibitor CQ confirmed that the changed autophagy contributes to drug-induced cell death, and this phenotypic change was accompanied by suppressed GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway activity. ARHGAP29 was inversely correlated with GC prognosis; CETSA results validated the direct intracellular binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29, and Co-IP assays confirmed physical interaction between ARHGAP29 and GSK-3β. γ-T3 inhibited the expression of ARHGAP29 at protein and mRNA levels in a time- and dose-dependent manner, whether alone or with OXA. Overexpression of ARHGAP29 reversed the synergistic effects of γ-T3 and OXA in GC cells, further supporting the regulatory linkage between ARHGAP29 and the GSK-3β/β-Catenin axis. The combination of γ-T3 and OXA represents a promising therapeutic strategy to elevate oxaliplatin sensitivity and alter autophagy-related marker expression in GC, at least partially via the ARHGAP29-associated modulation of GSK-3β/β-Catenin signaling.

items.title: Genetic Risk, Lifestyle, and Colorectal Cancer Across Age at Onset: A Prospective UK Biobank Study.
items.abstract: Background Polygenic risk scores (PRS) and lifestyle factors are associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether their associations and joint effects vary according to age at CRC onset remains unclear. We evaluated age-related heterogeneity in the associations of genetic risk and lifestyle with CRC and examined their additive interaction in early- and late-onset CRC. Methods We analyzed data from 405,453 cancer-free participants aged 38-73 years at baseline in the UK Biobank. PRS and a healthy lifestyle score (based on eight modifiable factors) were assessed. Age-scale Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CRC risk by age at onset. Heterogeneity across age intervals was assessed using likelihood ratio tests. Additive interaction was assessed using the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI), and differences in standardized incidence rates were evaluated. Results During a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 6620 CRC cases were identified. Compared with low genetic risk, high genetic risk was associated with HRs of 3.72, 3.32, 2.80, and 2.01 for CRC occurring at ages Conclusions The associations of genetic susceptibility and baseline lifestyle with CRC varied according to age at onset. Positive additive interaction between genetic risk and an unfavorable lifestyle was observed for late-onset but not early-onset CRC. These findings provide further evidence that the relative and joint associations of genetic and lifestyle factors with CRC vary across the life course.

items.title: Huaier Attenuates Renal Injury in Type 2 Diabetic Nephropathy by Ameliorating Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inhibiting Tubular Epithelial Cell Apoptosis.
items.abstract: Background Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major microvascular complication of Type 2 diabetes, with renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) apoptosis playing a pivotal role in its progression. The aqueous extract of Trametes robiniophila Murr. (Huaier) has shown renoprotective effects, but its specific molecular mechanisms in DN remain to be fully elucidated. Objective This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of Huaier aqueous extract on DN and verify whether its anti-apoptotic mechanism is mediated through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway using the pathway activator SKL2001. Methods In vivo, KKAy Type 2 diabetic mice were treated with Huaier (5 g/kg/day) for 12 weeks to evaluate renal function and histopathology. In vitro, HK-2 cells were treated with high glucose and palmitate (HG + PA) to induce injury. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway activator SKL2001 was employed to determine if activating this pathway could abolish the protective effects of Huaier. Results Bioinformatics analysis indicates that the regulation of apoptosis is the primary mechanism by which Huaier improves DN. In vivo, Huaier reduced UACR and improved renal histopathology in KKAy mice. Consistently, TUNEL staining and molecular analysis confirmed that Huaier significantly suppressed RTECs apoptosis within the renal tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that Huaier significantly inhibited HG + PA-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RTECs apoptosis. Notably, the administration of SKL2001 effectively reversed these protective effects, leading to increased β-catenin expression and elevated apoptosis levels despite Huaier treatment. Conclusion Huaier aqueous extract mitigates RTECs apoptosis and renal injury in Type 2 diabetic nephropathy by suppressing the Wnt5a/β-catenin signaling pathway.

items.title: Safety of Multiple Sclerosis Treatments During Pregnancy: An Overview of the EU Regulatory Approach to Risk Management Planning.
items.abstract: Purpose Multiple Sclerosis (MS) may affect women of childbearing age. Information on safety of disease modifying treatment (DMT) in pregnancy is often limited at time of marketing authorisation. We summarised the EU regulatory experience with the implementation and performance of additional pharmacovigilance activities concerning safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding for medicines to treat MS. Methods We reviewed EU risk management plans (RMPs) for centrally authorised MS DMTs to identify additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding. Information was analysed descriptively for type of measure, data collection method and data source. For non-interventional cohort studies and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases, information on current status, planned and actual size and duration was retrieved. Results We identified 17 DMTs that included 21 additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding across 15 RMPs. These comprised nine non-interventional cohort studies and four structured follow-up activities of pregnancy cases that had been started. Of those, three were terminated due to low recruitment with an inclusion rate slower than planned, while inclusion was faster than planned in three finalised activities. Inclusion rate was slowest in primary data collection and faster in secondary analyses and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases. Conclusion Despite efforts to evaluate safety of MS medicines during pregnancy, recruitment and data collection remain challenging. Planning for use of multiple real-world data sources-including primary data collection, secondary use of electronic health records, and analyses of case reports-may help overcome these challenges and strengthen MS drug safety evaluations in pregnancy.

items.title: Fungal ADP-ribosylation: an emerging signalling pathway in adaptation and virulence.
items.abstract: ADP-ribosylation is a posttranslational modification conserved across all domains of life and some viruses. While it is well established as a critical signalling mechanism in humans and is widely exploited as a therapeutic target in cancer, its roles in other kingdoms, particularly Fungi, remain poorly understood. Despite this, recent advances highlight the importance of fungal ADP-ribosylation in the regulation of key cellular maintenance processes such as DNA damage and oxidative stress responses, morphogenesis, growth, and proliferation. Here, we summarise our current understanding of fungal ADP-ribosylation and how it supports stress adaptation and virulence. While many aspects of fungal ADP-ribosylation remain unexplored, emerging discoveries underscore its importance in fungal biology and hint at a great potential for future antifungal therapies.

items.title: Association of runoff risk with private well contamination in a fractured dolostone aquifer.
items.abstract: In the United States, private well owners are responsible for monitoring and maintaining their drinking water but have little control over neighboring contamination sources and limited information about daily water quality. Potential for rapid contamination in karst settings exacerbates the challenge. The Runoff Risk Advisory Forecast (RRAF) is a real-time online tool available in five US states that helps nutrient applicators avoid times and locations of high runoff risk. We wanted to determine if RRAF could be repurposed in areas susceptible to groundwater contamination to inform well owners of conditions when contamination is likely. Private wells were repeatedly sampled on seven dates (32-36 wells per date) and analyzed for nitrate-nitrogen, total coliforms, and bovine manure markers. Three-day windows of RRAF risk prior to sampling were selected post hoc, ranging from 1 to 3 days prior for manure markers to 10-12 days prior for nitrate. Contaminants were associated with RRAF values of ≥75% within these windows based on observed weather. A hydrologic association between RRAF risk and groundwater depth was also apparent. Overall, results suggest the RRAF model anticipates conditions of elevated contamination risk for susceptible wells. For nitrate, between-well variation and delayed peak concentration suggested that well location and construction factors may be more informative than runoff events. Microbial contamination was rapid and distributed among wells, with one or more detections of coliforms in 31% of wells and bovine markers in 61% of wells. Thus, a warning system based on the RRAF model could help identify conditions of acute pathogen exposure.

items.title: High Level of Component C1q Binding Protein (C1QBP) is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Dysfunction of Mast Cells in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Background Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown. Methods C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo. Results The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice. Conclusion C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

items.title: Hollow Convective Carrier Design Enhances Biofilm Retention and Mass Transfer for Improved Nitrification Performance.
items.abstract: This study developed a novel carrier configuration (i.e., hollow convective carrier [HCC]) to enhance biofilm retention and mass transfer in biofilm-based wastewater treatment. The HCC was fabricated by stitching two layers of permeable nylon mesh to form internal hollow compartments, enabling biofilms to grow within protected spaces while maintaining diffusive and convective transport. Long-term reactor operation showed that HCC-based pure biofilm systems achieved faster start-up and better performance than single-layer convective carriers (CCs) and commercial polyethylene carriers (PEK5). The superior performance was mainly attributed to the improved biomass accumulation and mass transfer. HCC-based reactor exhibited higher biofilm densities (2.4-4.1 g/m 2 ) than CC (1.6 g/m 2 ) and PEK5 (0.6 g/m 2 ) carriers. Biofilms on the surface and inside the hollow compartments of HCC carriers had high nitrification activity and also accumulated more slowly-growing bacteria of Nitrospira than CC and PEK5 carriers. Nitrate tracer experiments confirmed that substrates could penetrate the thick convective biofilms on HCC carriers, with a mass transfer flux of 61.3 mg-N/(m 2 h) and overall mass transfer coefficient of 1.58 × 10 -6 m/s. Both mass transfer flux and overall coefficient in convective biofilms increased linearly with mixing intensity, supporting the role of convective transport in alleviating diffusion limitations. Overall, the hollow convective design integrates enhanced biofilm retention with improved substrate accessibility, providing a promising carrier strategy for stable and efficient treatment in biofilm reactors.

items.title: LncRNA A1BGAS1 Serves as a Tumor Suppressor in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Modulating the Expression of miR-3942-5P.
items.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading contributor to global cancer mortality, is associated with a notably unfavorable prognosis. This study aims to explore the regulatory interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p and its molecular mechanisms. The level of A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p in both tumor tissues and cell lines (BEAS-2B, A549, H226) were measured using qPCR. Functional effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression in NSCLC cells were evaluated through CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. The interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p was validated through dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue studies. A1BG-AS1 expression was markedly reduced in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. A1BG-AS1 expression was significantly associated with various clinical parameters. Overexpression of A1BG-AS1 suppressed NSCLC cell function. Mechanistically, A1BG-AS1 interacted with and negatively regulated miR-3942-5p, and the antitumor effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression were reversed by miR-3942-5p mimics.A1BG-AS1 inhibits NSCLC tumor progression by targeting miR-3942-5p.

items.title: Pan-Cancer Landscape of TMEM9 With Experimental Validation in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Background Transmembrane protein 9 (TMEM9) has been implicated in tumor progression, but its pan-cancer diagnostic, prognostic, and immunological relevance remains incompletely characterized. Methods TMEM9 expression, diagnostic and prognostic value, genetic alterations, functional states, and immune associations were systematically evaluated using TCGA, GTEx, and complementary public cancer databases. Experimental validation was primarily performed in HNSC models using Western blotting, colony-formation, wound-healing, Transwell, and xenograft assays, with additional exploratory validation in RCC models. Results TMEM9 showed good-to-high diagnostic performance in 15 evaluable cancer cohorts, with particularly high AUCs in CHOL (1.000), KICH (0.970), LIHC (0.949), and THYM (0.925), whereas BRCA also showed strong discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.890). Higher TMEM9 expression was associated with unfavorable survival in several cancers, although its prognostic relevance varied by tumor type. TMEM9 expression was also associated with cancer-related pathways, functional states, immune cell infiltration, and immunoregulatory gene expression in a context-dependent manner. Experimentally, TMEM9 knockdown suppressed colony formation, wound closure, migration, and invasion in HNSC cells and inhibited FaDu xenograft growth. Similar inhibitory effects were additionally observed in exploratory RCC models. Conclusion TMEM9 exhibits cancer-type-dependent diagnostic, prognostic, and immunological associations, whereas functional experiments support a tumor-promoting role for TMEM9 in HNSC. Exploratory RCC experiments suggest that this effect may also occur in selected renal cancer cellular contexts.

items.title: METTL7B-Mediated m6A Modification of PLEKHA4 Suppresses Ferroptosis via Reducing AURKA Ubiquitination to Promote Papillary Thyroid Cancer Progression.
items.abstract: The malignant progression of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is closely associated with the acquisition of ferroptosis resistance by tumor cells; however, the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to elucidate the function and molecular mechanisms of the methyltransferase-like 7B (METTL7B)/pleckstrin homology domain-containing family A member 4 (PLEKHA4)/aurora kinase A (AURKA) signaling axis in ferroptosis resistance in PTC. Our results showed that PLEKHA4 was highly expressed in PTC. By binding to kelch-like protein 12 (KLHL12), PLEKHA4 inhibited KLHL12-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of AURKA, thereby stabilizing the AURKA protein and enhancing ferroptosis resistance in PTC cells. Upstream, METTL7B stabilized PLEKHA4 mRNA and upregulated its expression through N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that knockdown of METTL7B increased ferroptosis sensitivity and suppressed PTC progression. This study reveals a novel paradigm in which PLEKHA4, as an effector of m6A modification, regulates ferroptosis by interfering with ubiquitin-mediated degradation, providing a theoretical basis for targeting this pathway in the treatment of PTC.

items.title: Development of Highly Efficient Lysosome-Targeting Peptide Ligands for the Internalization of Extracellular Proteins.
items.abstract: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) induce the internalization of extracellular and membrane-associated proteins by routing them to lysosomes via endogenous receptors, such as the insulin-like growth factor-2 receptor (IGF2R), also known as cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor. While current IGF2R ligands are effective, expanding the LYTAC toolkit with structurally simple and synthetically accessible ligands remains a practical necessity. Here, we first validated that previously reported dimeric and monomeric peptides induce robust internalization, establishing them as effective IGF2R-targeting LYTAC ligands. To further optimize the peptide architecture, we performed systematic mutational scanning on its monomeric sequence to simplify the peptide architecture. We identified the L4 variant, which features a single leucine substitution at the fourth position. This optimized monomer induces greater internalization efficiency than the previously reported wild-type monomeric peptide ligand. To demonstrate its utility, we conjugated the L4 recruiter to a specific PCSK9 binder. The resulting bifunctional molecule successfully induced the dose- and time-dependent internalization of PCSK9. Collectively, these findings establish several peptide variants as practical and highly effective building blocks for the development of extracellular protein internalization platforms.

items.title: "Life and Lower Limb Threatening Condition" Clinical Features, Management and Outcomes of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Complicated by Gas Gangrene: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common complication of diabetes in low- and middle-income countries and may be complicated by gas gangrene (GG), a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection. This prospective study assessed whether GG can be diagnosed clinically in low-resource primary care and explored factors associated with wound-healing outcomes in DFU complicated by GG. From December 2021 to June 2025, consecutive patients with diabetic foot infection and clinically active GG were enrolled. Data included demographics, ulcer history and examination, SINBAD classification, GG signs, sepsis status, comorbidities, management, and outcomes. All participants had classical clinical features of GG and were admitted for urgent surgical treatment. Ninety-nine patients (58 male) with classical GG were admitted for urgent surgery. Initial amputation was required in 18% (major 12%, minor 6%). Ten patients were lost to follow-up; that included six who died from foot-ulcer-related causes. Of 89 followed, 30 (33.7%) healed in 225.5 ± 126.9 days, while 59 remained unhealed after 146.1 ± 175.4 days; major amputations during treatment were more frequent in the healed group. Having a previous history of ulcer showed to increase the time to heal by 136 days. A one-day increase in treatment duration was associated with a 1% decrease in both the chance of healing or risk of amputation. Early diagnosis, aggressive medical and surgical intervention are the keys to decreasing morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients with gas gangrene; and remain the mainstay treatment of this dangerous condition globally. Patient's with previous ulcer history were found to need longer time to heal. Increasing treatment duration seems to be a double-edged sword, as while it is associated with reduced risk of amputation, it also decreases the chance of ulcer healing.

items.title: Two-Stage Estimation for Causal Inference Involving Semi-Continuous Exposures.
items.abstract: Methods for causal inference are well developed for binary and continuous exposures, but in many settings, the exposure has a substantial mass at zero-such exposures are called semi-continuous. We propose a general causal framework for such semi-continuous exposures, together with a two-stage estimation strategy. A two-part propensity structure is introduced for the semi-continuous exposure, with one component for exposure status (exposed vs unexposed) and another for the exposure level among those exposed, and incorporates both into a marginal structural model that disentangles the effects of exposure status and dose. The two-stage procedure sequentially targets the causal dose-response among exposed individuals and the causal effect of exposure status at a reference dose, allowing flexibility in the choice of propensity score methods in the second stage. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the resulting estimators, and characterize their limiting values under misspecification of the propensity score models. Simulation studies evaluate finite sample performance and robustness, and an application to a study of prenatal alcohol exposure and child cognition demonstrates how the proposed methods can be used to address a range of scientific questions about both exposure status and exposure intensity.

items.title: Quercetin activates lysosomal function to ameliorate neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
items.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) is a major contributor to vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), often resulting in progressive learning and memory deficits. Quercetin (Qu), a natural flavonoid with potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, demonstrates neuroprotective potential against ischemic injury, yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. In this study, a rat model of CCH was established by bilateral common carotid artery occlusion, followed by Qu administration at doses of 20, 40, and 80 mg·kg -1 . In parallel, HT22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) were treated with Qu at 5, 10, or 20 μmol·L -1 . Behavioral tests, histological staining, ELISA, and Western blot were used to assess cognitive performance, neuronal injury, lysosomal activity, NF-κB pathway activation, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Hippocampal RNA sequencing was also performed. Our results demonstrate that Qu greatly improved cognitive performance and attenuated neuronal damage in both the cerebral cortex and hippocampus. Mechanistically, Qu improved lysosomal function and suppressed NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammatory response, leading to less production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Notably, co-administration of a lysosomal inhibitor attenuated the neuroprotective effects of Qu, underscoring the functional importance of lysosomal activation. In conclusion, Qu alleviates CCH-induced cognitive decline and neurodegeneration by restoring lysosomal function and inhibiting NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation. These findings support the therapeutic potential of Qu for VCI and provide a rationale for its further development as a neuroprotective agent.

items.title: Artemisinin derived from Artemisia annua L. promotes thrombopoiesis via targeting FLT3: a novel strategy for thrombocytopenia management.
items.abstract: Artemisia annua L. (A. annua) has long been documented in traditional Chinese medicine for managing hemorrhagic conditions, attributed to its cooling and hemostatic properties. These historical applications suggest a potential role of A. annua in platelet-related disorders, although its hematopoietic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the thrombopoietic activity of A. annua, identify its bioactive constituent, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on thrombopoiesis. Chemical profiling identified major compounds in A. annua. MK differentiation was assessed in K562, Meg-01 cells, and primary murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). A murine radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) model was used to evaluate in vivo efficacy. Molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and signaling assays were conducted to explore molecular mechanisms. A. annua promoted MK differentiation, upregulating CD41/CD42b and enhancing polyploidization. Artemisinin was identified as the principal active compound. It promoted MK maturation in vitro and restored platelet counts, MK numbers, and HSPC populations in RIT mice without inducing systemic toxicity. Artemisinin also reduced bone marrow (BM) apoptosis and DNA damage while restoring platelet function. Mechanistically, artemisinin directly bound to FLT3 and activated the FLT3/MAPK pathway, leading to increased phosphorylation of MEK/ERK and upregulation of NF-E2 and TAL1. FLT3 and ERK inhibition abrogated these effects. Artemisinin is a potent thrombopoietic agent that acts via direct activation of FLT3 and its downstream MAPK signaling cascade. The findings identify FLT3 as a novel therapeutic target for thrombocytopenia and support the potential clinical application of artemisinin in radiation-related hematological disorders.

items.title: A Comparative Analysis of Deaths Due to Drug-Related Causes Between Rural and Urban Areas in the United Kingdom, 1997-2026.
items.abstract: Introduction Multiple jurisdictions report disproportionately elevated rates of drug-related harm in urban settings, alongside unique treatment needs in rural populations. We examined differences in case characteristics, circumstances of death and implicated drugs among individuals dying from drug-related causes, stratified by rural or urban setting, and determined changes in the proportion of deaths between settings over time. Methods Retrospective registry-based analysis of coronial records of individuals who died from drug-related causes, submitted to the National Programme on Substance Use Mortality in the UK, 1997-2026. UK Government Rural-Urban Classification methodology dichotomised cases using postcode at date of death. Results Overall, 39,975 decedents died, 36,350 (90.9%) in urban settings. The urban percentage decreased significantly over the study period from 96.6% in 1999 to 92.3% in 2025 (AAPC -0.34%, 95% CI -0.47% to -0.15%, p = 0.002). Accidental poisoning was the most common direct cause of death in both rural (45.5%) and urban (54.8%) settings, while intentional self-poisoning was more common rurally (17.3% vs. 9.5%). Opioids were the most frequently implicated drug group in both rural (61.1%) and urban (65.4%) settings. The median number of drugs implicated did not differ significantly between settings (both 2, IQR 1-3), but rural decedents had a significantly higher median number of prescribed implicated drugs (1, IQR 0-2 vs. 0, IQR 0-2). Discussion and conclusions Over three decades, approximately one in 11 UK drug-related deaths occurred rurally. Intentional self-poisoning was substantially more common in rural fatalities, and opioids were the leading implicated drug group across both settings.

items.title: Creator Type, Content Format, and Engagement Among Highly Liked Cancer-Related TikTok Search Results: A Cross-Sectional Content Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Engagement differences by creator type among highly liked cancer-related TikTok videos remain unclear. Methods We analyzed 250 videos from five cancer searches, selecting the first 50 results per search filtered to the preceding six months and sorted by likes. Health professionals or trainees were classified as medical. The primary analysis modeled log-transformed views by creator type, adjusting for followers, video age, content type, and cancer search. Results Adjusted views showed no significant difference (ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.44-1.85; p = 0.773). Medical creators had a higher adjusted share rate (ratio, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.24-3.24; Holm-adjusted p = 0.026). Median views per follower were lower for medical creators (2.55 vs. 16.40; ratio, 0.16; 95% CI, 0.06-0.45; Holm-adjusted p = 0.003). Conclusions Despite no clear difference in absolute views, lower views per follower raise the possibility that medical creators have more limited reach beyond established audiences than nonmedical creators, while greater sharing may broaden distribution.

items.title: DBT Modulates Copper-Dependent Cuproptosis-Related Injury in Experimental Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a severe cardiovascular complication of chronic alcohol consumption, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Cuproptosis is a recently identified copper-dependent form of regulated cell death; however, its role in ACM remains unclear. In this study, male C57BL/6 mice were fed an ethanol-containing Lieber-DeCarli liquid diet to establish an ACM model, and RNA sequencing combined with bioinformatics analysis was performed to identify cuproptosis-related genes. Among the candidate genes, dihydrolipoamide branched-chain transacylase E2 (DBT) showed a consistent trend of downregulation across both independent RNA-seq cohorts, and was further validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. ACM mice exhibited increased serum and cardiomyocyte copper content, altered cuproptosis-related markers and impaired cardiac function. In AC16 cells, DBT knockdown induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, which were markedly alleviated by the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate. Conversely, DBT overexpression attenuated EtOH-induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, with effects similar to those of tetrathiomolybdate. These findings suggest that DBT regulates ACM-related cardiomyocyte injury through cuproptosis-associated processes at the cellular level and may represent a potential therapeutic target for alcohol-induced myocardial injury.

items.title: Person-Centred Climate Despite Unmet Fundamental Care Needs: Findings From inCHARGE Using a Convergent Parallel Mixed Methods Design.
items.abstract: Aim To explore person-centred care in surgical inpatient settings by examining the person-centred climate alongside patients' experiences of the fulfilment of fundamental care needs. Design A convergent parallel mixed methods design. Methods Surgical inpatients (n = 26) completed the Person-centred Climate Questionnaire-Patient version and participated in structured interviews, comprising binary questions with open-ended elaborations. Quantitative and qualitative data were analysed separately and thereafter brought together through an integrated interpretation of the findings. Results Questionnaire scores indicated a person-centred climate. Interview findings showed that patients described staff as kind, present, and compassionate, while also reporting several unmet fundamental care needs related to information, participation, hygiene, toileting, and symptom management. The integrated findings showed that patients reported a person-centred climate while simultaneously describing shortcomings in the delivery of fundamental care. Conclusion These findings highlight that global assessments of person-centred climate may overlook deficiencies in fundamental care and underscore the importance of considering multiple dimensions when evaluating person-centred care in clinical practice. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Assessing person-centred care requires attention to both the care climate and the extent to which patients' fundamental care needs are met. Combining structured measures with opportunities for patients to describe their care experiences may improve the identification of unmet needs and inform efforts to strengthen person-centred care in practice. Impact The study illustrates that being treated with kindness and goodwill does not necessarily ensure high-quality person-centred care. The findings are relevant for clinicians, nurse leaders, and researchers and support the use of multi-method approaches when evaluating person-centred care. Reporting method The quantitative and qualitative content in this study is reported in accordance with the relevant STROBE guidelines. Patient or public contribution The project is part of a research program developed in collaboration with the nurses and nursing leaders at the care units. WHAT DOES THIS PAPER CONTRIBUTE TO THE WIDER GLOBAL CLINICAL COMMUNITY?: The findings highlight the importance of combining different approaches when evaluating person-centred care. Asking about concrete care situations and experiences may help reveal unmet fundamental care needs that might otherwise remain hidden in survey responses.

items.title: Quality of Life, Self-Image, and Body Acceptance Among Mastectomized Women: A Questionnaire-Based Study in Maranhão, Brazil.
items.abstract: Aim To evaluate quality of life, body image, body acceptance, and sexuality among women after unilateral mastectomy, comparing those with and without breast reconstruction. Design Analytical observational cross-sectional study. Methods The study included 100 women aged 18 years or older who underwent unilateral mastectomy for primary breast cancer and were recruited consecutively between January 2019 and February 2022 at two tertiary oncology referral hospitals. All participants were interviewed 3-6 months after their respective surgical procedure. Quality of life was assessed using the validated Portuguese version of the World Health Organization Quality of Life Instrument-Short Form (WHOQOL-BREF). Body image, body acceptance, and sexuality were assessed using five study-specific, nonvalidated questions. Adjusted analyses were performed for the psychological WHOQOL-BREF domain and, post hoc, for reported change in sexual desire. Results Of the 100 participants, 38 underwent breast reconstruction and 62 did not. Women with breast reconstruction had higher scores in the psychological, social relationships, and environment domains of the WHOQOL-BREF, whereas no differences were observed in the physical health domain or the two general items. After adjustment for age and adjuvant treatment, breast reconstruction remained associated with a higher psychological domain score. Body image and appearance differed significantly between groups, whereas self-satisfaction, acceptance of physical appearance, acceptance of bodily changes, and current sexual activity did not. A higher proportion of women with reconstruction reported a change in sexual desire after surgery; however, the direction of change was not assessed. Correlations between body image-related variables and quality-of-life domains were generally negligible or weak and were considered exploratory. Conclusion Breast reconstruction was associated with differences in selected psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of quality of life and in the WHOQOL-BREF item on body image and appearance, but not with physical health, the two general WHOQOL-BREF items, self-satisfaction, acceptance of physical appearance, acceptance of bodily changes, or current sexual activity. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of psychosocial adaptation after mastectomy and the importance of comprehensive survivorship care. Implications for the profession and/or patient care These findings support individualized nursing assessment of psychosocial adaptation after mastectomy, including body image, sexuality, and quality of life, and may inform patient education, supportive referrals, and shared decision-making when discussing reconstructive options. Impact This study highlights psychosocial dimensions of survivorship that may be relevant to women after mastectomy and to nurses involved in psychosocial assessment, patient education, supportive care, and coordination of multidisciplinary services. Reporting method The study was reported according to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Data S1. STROBE checklist for cross-sectional studies (STROBE_checklist_cross_sectional.pdf). Patient or public contribution Patients were not involved in the design, analysis, or interpretation of the study. They participated as study participants and provided data through the study-specific interviews and questionnaires.

items.title: Polarizing Views About Feminists and Gender Egalitarianism in Canada.
items.abstract: International evidence reveals growing ideological divisions between women and men. On average, in industrialized countries, women are leaning more liberal, men more conservative. Among young men especially, anti-feminist sentiment is growing, while simultaneously more women are embracing feminist causes. Little recent national research in Canada has explored these trends. Analyzing pooled national surveys conducted between 1993 and 2025 (N > 130,000), I examine longitudinal trends in how women and men place themselves on the political right or left, feel about feminists, and support gender egalitarianism. Four key findings emerge: (i) evidence of an expanding gender gap across several core measures; (ii) a subtle yet notable increase in opinion diversity among men; (iii) a recent surge among women in support for feminist causes; and (iv) recent period effects that appear to be driving the growing gender gap. Together these results offer a nuanced portrait of gendered realignments in contemporary Canada.

items.title: Ixodes ricinus-Contact Phase Inhibitor Promotes Functional Recovery and Attenuates Neutrophil Associated Neuroinflammation After Experimental Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
items.abstract: Aims Neutrophil-associated inflammation contributes to secondary brain injury after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). We evaluated whether Ixodes ricinus-Contact Phase Inhibitor (Ir-CPI), a selective factor XIa/XIIa inhibitor with reported thromboinflammatory modulatory properties, improves outcome after experimental ICH without worsening bleeding. Methods In a collagenase-induced mouse ICH model, Ir-CPI was administered as an intravenous bolus followed by a 3-day infusion. Vehicle animals served as controls and enoxaparin as an anticoagulant comparator. Cohorts evaluated hemorrhage and lesion volumes, endothelial activation, neutrophil-associated inflammation, and longitudinal functional recovery. Ir-CPI association with human neutrophils was evaluated in vitro. Results Ir-CPI did not increase hemorrhage or lesion volumes versus PBS through Day 14, whereas enoxaparin showed a higher Day 1 hemorrhage volume than Ir-CPI. Flow cytometry showed Ir-CPI association with human neutrophils. In the mouse model, Ir-CPI produced region-specific reductions in neutrophil infiltration and NET formation and reduced neuronal degeneration at the injection site and caudal level, without affecting VCAM-1-associated endothelial activation. Ir-CPI accelerated functional recovery, improving neurological scores and sensorimotor asymmetry by Day 5, with restoration of baseline corner test performance by Day 14. Conclusion Ir-CPI improves recovery after experimental ICH without exacerbating bleeding and is associated with reduced neutrophil-associated secondary brain injury. These findings support its translational potential as a therapeutic strategy for ICH.

items.title: Maximum Gape in Developing Macaca mulatta.
items.abstract: Objectives Maximum gape and bite force are two key metrics of primate craniodental performance, but without mitigating adaptations, large gapes are associated with reduced bite force. Primate craniodental morphology undergoes functional transitions across development, but how these performance variables vary with life-history transitions is unknown. Material and methods Maximum gapes of 211 rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) spanning infancy to post-prime developmental stages from Cayo Santiago (Puerto Rico) were collected in vivo, and jaw leverage, a contributor to bite force, was calculated from skeletal measurements of the same individuals post-mortem. Allometric relationships were tested using a combination of OLS regressions and mixed-effects models with developmental stage and sex as interaction terms. Results In vivo gape did not differ from isometry relative to body mass and jaw length across developmental stages by sex, but jaw leverage was significantly lower in larger compared to smaller macaques. The largest developmental differences occurred between pre-prime and prime individuals. Canine length scaled with positive allometry against body mass and jaw length in males but not females, while maximum gape scaled with negative allometry relative to canine length in both sexes. Discussion These results indicate that macaques undergo a functional tradeoff between jaw leverage and gape around the onset of sexual dimorphism. Pre-prime macaques exhibit relatively greater jaw leverage, whereas adults maintain proportionate gape relative to body and jaw size at reduced mechanical advantage. The eruption of large canines in males does not influence linear gape outside of size differences captured by body mass and jaw length.

items.title: Asymmetric Migration Shapes Genetic Structure of the Invasive Avian Vampire Fly (Philornis downsi) Across the Galápagos Islands.
items.abstract: Biological invasions on islands provide a natural framework to study how dispersal and connectivity influence evolutionary and ecological processes. The avian nest parasitic fly, Philornis downsi-first recorded in Darwin's finch nests in 1997-causes high mortality in endemic land birds, yet its inter-island and sex-specific patterns of dispersal and genetic structure remain poorly understood. We use low-coverage whole genome sequencing to investigate genome-wide patterns of genetic diversity, directional migration and effective population size in P. downsi across five major Galápagos Islands and its native range in mainland Ecuador. We find evidence for a genetic bottleneck in the Galápagos, isolation by distance, and evidence that the island closest to the Ecuadorian mainland, San Cristóbal, is genetically divergent from the other four islands sampled, despite retaining the highest genetic diversity. No evidence was found for sex-biased dispersal; however, sex-biased genetic structure was detected using only markers from inferred autosomal scaffolds. We found asymmetric gene flow with higher migration rates from San Cristóbal westward to the other islands, matching the direction of both southeast trade winds and major cargo shipping routes. Our results suggest both natural and human-mediated colonisation of P. downsi from the mainland through San Cristóbal to the other islands, followed by high inter-island dispersal among closely situated sink islands. Our findings are critical for prioritising islands for control strategies that will reduce P. downsi impacts on vulnerable endemic birds and underscore the value of understanding directional migration patterns for managing invasive species in metapopulations.
