items.title: Brain Transcriptomic Changes Associated With the Socially Regulated Behavioural Specialisation of Ant Queens.
items.abstract: Insect societies are characterised by a reproductive division of labour between queens that monopolise egg production and workers that perform all non-reproductive tasks. The queen specialisation in egg laying is typically considered to be constitutive and independent of environmental conditions, but this common assumption was recently challenged by the finding that the presence of workers both induces and maintains the queen specialisation in several species of ants. However, the molecular changes that translate worker presence into queen behavioural specialisation remain unknown. To investigate the transcriptomic basis of the socially regulated specialisation of ant queens, we produced 93 individual brain transcriptomes from queens of the black garden ant Lasius niger that were experimentally maintained in different social environments. Our transcriptomic analyses revealed that 123 genes were differentially expressed between the brains of queens maintained with and without workers. These genes were enriched for processes related to brain energy metabolism and neuronal plasticity and signalling. By investigating the response of selected genes of interest to further manipulations of the social environment, we identified four candidate genes that fully mirrored the queen behavioural changes. Specifically, their expression changes in response to worker presence were reversible and they did not respond to mere cues of the worker presence. These candidate genes included the transcription factor Krüppel-homologue 1 and other genes in the juvenile hormone and insulin signalling pathways, both known to regulate multiple aspects of division of labour in social insects. By producing a robust, well-replicated and well-controlled investigation of the transcriptomic basis of the behavioural specialisation of ant queens, this study provides a better understanding of the emergence and maintenance of reproductive division of labour in insect societies.

items.title: Whale swimming evolution recorded in vertebral microanatomy from the Eocene to present.
items.abstract: Among modern aquatic amniote clades that evolved pelagic locomotion, whales are a prime example, but timing and mode of evolutionary changes in their swimming are poorly understood. Here, we use 3D vertebral microanatomy derived from CT scanning to investigate swimming patterns in extinct whales. All vertebral centra from a single specimen of the extant common dolphin Delphinus delphis were used to provide a baseline for the correlation of microanatomical parameters and spinal movements in our dataset of fossil whales. We find that bone anisotropy, and to some extent bone compactness, mirrors the amount of compression and movement in vertebral regions. We use these parameters to infer regional movements and thus swimming mode for several lineages of stem cetaceans (Natchitochia jonesi, Pachycetus wardi, Zygorhiza kochii) and crown cetaceans (Maiabalaena nesbittae, an undescribed Oligocene odontocete and a modern minke whale). Natchitochia jonesi could walk on land, whereas Pachycetus wardi and Zygorhiza kochii were obligately aquatic, but show more spinal flexibility than modern taxa. The early Oligocene mysticete and odontocete differ in microstructural properties and might have experienced a different trajectory towards their extant bauplans. Overall, microanatomical data confirm increasing pelagic specializations in cetacean evolution that include a stiffer torso, but our data also highlight modular patterns of compactness within vertebral regions. Our approach is promising for future use of three-dimensional vertebral microanatomical data to understand locomotory patterns.

items.title: The Impact of Nutrition Social Marketing on Awareness, Behaviour Change, and Food Expenditures: A Cluster Matched Study from Coastal Kenya.
items.abstract: Malnutrition continues to be a persistent global challenge, frequently affecting small-scale producers. Nutrition-focused social marketing has been shown to increase nutrition awareness and improve diets and nutrition outcomes, but less is known about the pathways to these positive outcomes as well as impacts on other nutrition-related behaviors like household food expenditure. We present findings from Samaki Salama , a community-based nutrition and fisheries sustainability trial conducted in coastal Kenya. Samaki Salama delivered an integrated nutrition social marketing campaign and modified fishing traps to matched communities in three study arms: (1) control ( n = 200); (2) social marketing ( n = 100); and (3) social marketing plus modified fishing traps and training ( n = 100). Messaging platforms included personalized caregiver home visits, cooking demonstrations, fisher/father workshops, and the distribution of diverse branded materials. The main findings showed the intervention significantly improved diets and child growth. Here, we show Samaki Salama increased participants' nutrition awareness, observations of encouraged behaviors, and household food expenditures. However, the expenditure increase was small, suggesting that improved child growth resulted from fishers bringing catch home for household consumption. Social marketing approaches with small-scale producers should encourage retention of household harvest/catch together with purchasing quality foods.

items.title: Aridity reshapes leaf and root trait dispersion through distinct microbial pathways.
items.abstract: Aridity is a primary driver of plant community assembly, yet most trait-based studies focus on mean traits rather than trait dispersion. Soil microbes may mediate plant responses to aridity, but whether leaf and root trait dispersion responds to aridity through shared or distinct microbial pathways remains unclear. Using 535 species-by-plot records (247 species) along an aridity gradient in north-west China, we quantified four leaf and four root traits, soil properties, microbial diversity and composition, and microbial carbon use efficiency. We tested whether aridity differentially regulates leaf vs root functional dispersion (FD is ), and whether these responses are associated with different microbial predictors. Leaf traits shifted more consistently with aridity and were more tightly linked to environmental variation than root traits. Leaf FD is negatively correlated with CUE, whereas root FD is negatively correlated with fungal diversity and bacterial community composition. These associations weakened toward less arid sites. Structural equation modeling further showed that leaf FD is linked primarily to microbial functioning, whereas root FD is linked more strongly to microbial diversity and composition. Our results reveal that aridity reshapes trait dispersion through organ-specific plant-microbe pathways, highlighting that predicting dryland community responses to increasing drought must treat above- and belowground traits separately.

items.title: Exogenous Kaempferol Application Enhances Salt Tolerance Over Quercetin in Apocynum pictum Seedlings: An Integrated Multi-Level Analysis.
items.abstract: Salinity stress limits plant growth by disrupting water uptake and inducing ion toxicity. Natural bioactive molecules, including flavonols, have gained attention for their potential to enhance abiotic stress tolerance. This study aimed to compare the effects of exogenous kaempferol (200 μmol L -1 ) and quercetin (25 μmol L -1 ) on growth and stress mitigation in Apocynum pictum seedlings under salt stress. Although both flavonoids alleviate salt stress in various species, their regulatory roles in A. pictum remain unclear. Both compounds significantly alleviated salt-induced growth inhibition, with kaempferol showing stronger effects on plant height, leaf number, leaf length, and root length. Ultrastructural analysis revealed distinct protective strategies: kaempferol enhanced cellular structural stability by preserving root cell integrity and promoting cell wall thickening, whereas quercetin maintained mitochondrial integrity and abundance. Kaempferol treatment also resulted in higher superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, soluble protein accumulation, and photosynthetic pigment levels compared to quercetin. Transcriptomic profiling uncovered distinct regulatory mechanisms: quercetin primarily activated the ABC transporter pathway for ion homeostasis, whereas kaempferol markedly stimulated the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway by upregulating key structural genes (CHS, CHI, F3H, F3'H, LAR), suggesting enhanced flavonoid accumulation. Collectively, kaempferol and quercetin employ different yet effective strategies to confer salt tolerance in A. pictum. This study highlights the potential of exogenous kaempferol as a biosafe strategy to enhance plant stress tolerance in agricultural systems.

items.title: Fruit color and size provide reliable signals of macronutritional rewards for seed dispersers.
items.abstract: Fruit color and size provide vital cues for determining seed dispersers' preferences; however, any consistent underlying link between these traits and fruit macronutritional rewards remains to be established by large-scale analyses. We collated a global database comprising 2626 observations of 1626 fruiting plant species from 460 global sites to test whether fruit color and size traits do indeed consistently signal macronutritional rewards to frugivores. We found that consistent fruit color and size signaled macronutrient reward specifically relating to bird-, mammal-, and mixed-dispersed dispersal syndromes. Lipids were the predominant macronutrient in black, blue, red, orange, and yellow fruits with birds (27.24%), whereas sugar predominated in mammal-dispersed fruits (72.55%). Fruits dispersed by mammals (25.55 mm) were consistently larger than those dispersed by birds (10.17 mm) regardless of fruit color, and total macronutrient mass per fruit increased with fruit size. These signal-mutualist relationships are shaped by associated disperser traits, demonstrating co-evolutionary mechanisms driving adaptive differentiation of fruit morphological and macronutrient traits. By integrating the disperser syndrome hypothesis and signal theory with nutritional geometry theory and trait-matching theory, our study expounds the role of seed disperser selective preferences in the evolution of fruit traits, thus advancing the seed disperser mutualism paradigm.

items.title: The microbiome and brain metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer: A graded appraisal and a framework for prevention-oriented research.
items.abstract: Background Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality and treatment failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, current models of cerebral dissemination rarely integrate microbiome-dependent systemic and intratumoral biology.This Review examines the potential microbiome-brain metastasis axis linking gut, lung, and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination and therapeutic response. Methods A reproducible literature search was conducted to evaluate proposed mechanisms underlying microbiome-associated brain metastasis. Evidence for each mechanistic claim was graded using a four-level evidence scheme (E1-E4), while microbial detection confidence was assessed using a four-tier hierarchy (D1-D4). Results No component of the proposed axis reached E1 evidence, and all published microbial observations in NSCLC brain metastasis rests on nucleic-acid detection alone. Five mechanisms are examined: circulating microbial metabolites acting on endothelial permeability and glial reactivity; microbiome-imprinted immune-cell trafficking;intracellular bacteria within primary lung tumours; cross-kingdom MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling; and candidate host genetic determinants. The available human data are small, single-centre and cross-sectional, reporting association with brain-metastasis status rather than prediction or causation; that bacteria accompany disseminating tumour cells into the brain remains a hypothesis awaiting paired sampling, spatial localization and experimental perturbation.We therefore reserve the term prevention for proposed trials, integrate microbial features with established molecular risk models, and specify the genetic-perturbation program and research-only decision pathway that would convert these claims into E1 evidence. Conclusions The microbiome-brain metastasis axis provides a hypothesis-generating framework for investigating microbial contributions to cerebral dissemination. Multi-centre validation, paired primary-brain metastasis profiling and gnotobiotic models are required before microbiome-directed strategies can be said to improve intracranial outcomes;until then this framework is hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing. Key points The proposed microbiome-brain metastasis axis links gut, lung and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination in NSCLC. Current evidence remains insufficient to establish causality, with no proposed mechanism reaching the highest evidence level (E1). Five candidate mechanisms involve microbial metabolites, immune-cell trafficking, intratumoral bacteria, MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling, and host genetic determinants. Multicentre validation, paired primary and brain metastasis profiling, spatial microbial localisation and experimental perturbation are needed to establish causality and assess clinical relevance. Microbiome-directed prevention and therapeutic strategies remain investigational and should not yet inform routine clinical practice.

items.title: From energy and cooling systems to multifunctional environmental infrastructure: A decision-support review of photovoltaic-green roofs.
items.abstract: Photovoltaic-green roofs (PV-GRs) are increasingly recognized as an integrated solution for climate-resilient cities because they combine renewable energy generation, evaporative cooling, stormwater retention, biodiversity enhancement, and more efficient use of limited rooftop space. However, existing research often evaluates their energy, hydrological, ecological, material, and operational functions separately. This study provides a structured narrative and critical synthesis of 67 publications, distinguishing direct PV-GR evidence from supporting evidence from related systems. Attention is given to energy performance and thermal processes, including evapotranspirative cooling, radiation balance, PV module temperature reduction, and mitigation of the photovoltaic heat island effect. The review further examines vegetation, substrate properties, stormwater management, biodiversity, design parameters, maintenance, recycled materials, economic considerations, and life cycle performance. Available evidence indicates that PV-GRs can improve PV performance, reduce roof and module temperatures, support vegetation under partially shaded conditions, and provide hydrological, ecological, and microclimatic benefits. However, the magnitude of these benefits depends strongly on climate, system configuration, water availability, vegetation characteristics, substrate properties, and long-term maintenance. From an environmental management perspective, PV-GRs should therefore be regarded not merely as technologies for energy generation and cooling, but as multifunctional infrastructure whose performance should be evaluated through integrated, site-specific decision-support frameworks and against a reference system appropriate to the specific decision question.

items.title: Targeted Microbial Co-Inoculation Enhances Flavor and Community Structure in Nongxiangxing Baijiu Fermentation.
items.abstract: Distilled Nongxiangxing Baijiu (NXB), produced from lower-layer fermented grains (FG), consistently exhibits superior quality, whereas upper-layer FG often yield variable and inferior sensory attributes. Biofortification of fermentation by inoculation with complementary microorganisms is a promising approach for stabilizing and enhancing NXB quality. This study compared single-strain inoculations with Bacillus subtilis (B group), Pichia kudriavzevii (P group), and mix-strain inoculations with Bacillus subtilis and Pichia kudriavzevii (BP group) in terms of physicochemical properties, volatile flavor metabolites, and microbial community structure of the upper-layer FG during NXB fermentation. Mantel and correlation analyses were used to assess the correlations among these parameters. Results showed that both inoculants significantly improved ethanol yield, with the greatest enhancement observed in the BP60 treatment (inoculated with Bacillus subtilis and Pichia kudriavzevii). The semi-quantified relative concentrations of key volatile organic compounds, including ethyl butyrate and ethyl hexanoate, were significantly elevated in the BP60 FG. Mantel and correlation analyses identified moisture content and reducing sugar concentration as the dominant physicochemical drivers shaping microbial community composition and collaborative interactions, which were mainly related to acid-, alcohol-, and ester-associated metabolism, whereas fungi were more closely linked to ester, aromatic, and phenolic compound formation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that co-inoculation with Bacillus subtilis and Pichia kudriavzevii promotes the accumulation of signature flavor metabolites during NXB fermentation. This mechanistic insight provides a foundation for rational process optimization and targeted quality control for strategies in industrial-scale NXB production. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: The co-inoculation with Bacillus subtilis and Pichia kudriavzevii promotes the accumulation of signature flavor metabolites during NXB fermentation.

items.title: Do agents need to sleep?
items.abstract: LLM-based agents, which increasingly operate persistently across sessions and accumulate memory through interaction, already exhibit the familiar symptoms of unchecked plasticity: semantic drift, degraded retrieval precision, propagation of stored errors, and saturation of memory capacity. Drawing on the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep, we propose that each of its three phases maps onto an operation feasible in digital memory architectures. Engineers building stateful agents, meanwhile, are independently rediscovering the problems sleep evolved to solve: what to forget, and when to do the forgetting. From this we derive the falsifiable prediction that selectionist consolidation will outperform instructionist alternatives as memory stores grow large. The core claim concerns the nature of continuous learning itself: plasticity has a price, and for any system that learns continuously under finite capacity while coupled to its environment, that price is sleep.

items.title: Prevalence of and risk factors associated with growth and developmental delays among children in urban and suburban primary care settings in Indonesia: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of growth and developmental delays and identify associated risk factors among children living in urban and suburban areas. Methods This analytical cross-sectional study included 247 children aged 3-24 months from 2 health center catchment areas, 1 urban and 1 suburban. Anthropometric measurements and growth-monitoring records from January-December 2024 were collected. Development was screened using the Denver Developmental Screening Test II during field visits from January-March 2025. Interviews assessed demographics, parental education and occupation, breastfeeding, prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal histories, and digital media exposure. Bivariate analyses (chi-square or Fisher's exact test) and multivariable logistic regression were performed using IBM SPSS ver. 29.0. Results Short stature prevalence was 18.6% in the urban area and 26.6% in the suburban area. Suspected developmental delays were identified in 11.4% and 24.3% of children, respectively. Development status was associated with maternal education (p=.006), screen time exposure (p=.047), vaginal delivery (p=.039), and postnatal history (p=.034). multivariable analysis showed that higher maternal education (adjusted odds ratio, 0.22; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.56) and delivery method (0.46; 0.23-0.89) were associated with lower odds of suspected developmental delays. Longer screen time (1.92; 1.09-3.37) and postnatal complications (2.37; 1.09-5.15) were associated with higher odds. Conclusion Frequent growth monitoring was associated with better nutritional status and weight gain in both areas and increased body length in the suburban area. Lower odds of developmental delays were associated with maternal education and delivery method, whereas higher odds were associated with screen time duration and postnatal complications.

items.title: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning Modulates Brain Expression of PIWI Proteins After Experimental Cerebral Ischemia.
items.abstract: This study explores the involvement of PIWI family proteins in cerebral ischemia and their potential contribution to the neuroprotective effects of remote ischemic post-conditioning (RIC), a promising intervention for ischemic stroke whose underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. Using a mouse model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAo), we evaluated the effects of RIC induced by femoral artery occlusion (FAo) on brain injury, inflammation, and PIWI proteins expression in the brain. RIC significantly reduced infarct volume, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits, while attenuating the ischemia-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1β and TNF-α, in the brain cortex. The ischemic insult induced a robust upregulation of PIWIL2 and PIWIL4 in the ipsilateral cortex, primarily in neurons, with PIWIL4 also detected in astrocytes, few microglia and numerous infiltrating myeloid cells. Notably, RIC suppressed this cortical upregulation, suggesting a potential link between PIWI proteins and ischemic damage. By contrast, in neurogenic regions of the hippocampus, RIC selectively enhanced PIWIL4 expression, particularly in neurons of the CA3 region and dentate gyrus. This increase was associated with elevated expression of the neurogenic and repair-related factors TGF-β1 and TREM2. Accordingly, in the subventricular zone of post-conditioned mice, PIWIL4 was localized in SOX2-positive neural progenitor cells that also express the proliferation marker Ki67. These findings reveal a region- and cell-specific modulation of PIWILs expression in cerebral ischemia and RIC, strongly supporting the concept that PIWI pathways may represent promising targets for neuroprotection and recovery following stroke.

items.title: Body Mass Index-Specific Central Adiposity and Risk of Incident Type 2 Diabetes Among Aging Women.
items.abstract: Body mass index (BMI) does not capture central adiposity, which may provide additional information for type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk stratification. To evaluate BMI-specific waist circumference (WC) categories in relation to incident T2D and assess their performance across independent cohorts. Prospective analyses included 133,620 Women's Health Initiative (WHI) participants free of T2D at baseline, randomly assigned to training (70%; n=93,463) and test (30%; n=40,157) samples. External validation included the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n=2,885) and Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS; n=1,037). Cox models estimated T2D risk across BMI and BMI-specific WC categories. Discrimination was assessed using Harrell's C-statistic. In WHI, T2D risk increased progressively across BMI categories (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.51-3.30) and joint BMI-WC categories (HRs, 1.40-4.43). Within BMI strata, higher WC generally identified greater T2D risk. Associations were directionally consistent in HRS and HANDLS. Age modified associations, with stronger gradients at younger ages, whereas race and ethnicity interactions were not statistically significant. Model discrimination was modest (C-statistics approximately 0.60-0.75). BMI-specific WC categories refine adiposity-related T2D risk stratification beyond BMI alone but provide modest individual-level discrimination. WC may complement BMI in identifying women warranting more comprehensive metabolic risk assessment rather than serving as a stand-alone T2D prediction tool.

items.title: Socioeconomic, behavioral, and psychological correlates of body weight and weight gain: evidence from a 12-year German panel study.
items.abstract: Overweight and obesity are major public health challenges in Germany. Body weight is shaped by a wide range of socioeconomic, behavioral, and psychological factors, but less is known about how these factors jointly relate to weight gain among adults in Germany. Data were drawn from the adult cohort of the National Educational Panel Study (NEPS-SC6). The analytical sample included 8,209 individuals aged 28-55 years at baseline (2011/12), followed over approximately 12 years. In this exploratory study, cross-sectional associations with BMI and overweight/obesity status were estimated using regression models, while longitudinal associations with BMI changes were analyzed using fixed-effects panel models, capturing within-individual changes. Missing values were handled by multiple imputation (50 imputed datasets). Higher household income (-0.16), tertiary education (-0.41), higher social origin (-0.26), greater conscientiousness (-0.64), higher neuroticism (-0.27), and more frequent sports participation (-0.38) were associated with lower BMI at baseline, whereas higher extraversion was associated with higher BMI (+ 0.23). Women had significantly lower BMI than men (-1.42). Longitudinal analyses showed that BMI increased over time (0.08 points per year), with the steepest increase in the first three years. Within individuals, increases in household income (+ 0.10) and transitions into cohabitation with a partner (+ 0.29) were associated with higher BMI, whereas smoking (-0.52) and greater sports participation (-0.13) were associated with lower BMI; the smoking association likely reflects, at least partly, weight gain after cessation (smoking prevalence fell from 30% to 20%). Women experienced a stronger BMI increase than men only at the last measurement point (2023/24), and those with tertiary education (-0.02) showed slower BMI increases. Body weight and weight gain are associated with socioeconomic, behavioral, and psychological factors. Among the Big Five personality traits, conscientiousness showed the strongest association with lower BMI, whereas neuroticism was unexpectedly associated with lower rather than higher BMI and warrants replication with more comprehensive personality measures. Higher educational attainment and more frequent physical activity were associated with lower BMI and, within individuals, with more favorable weight trajectories; given the exploratory design, these associations should not be interpreted causally. The findings highlight the relevance of psychological characteristics for obesity research and prevention.

items.title: Asymmetric Y-chromosomal and mitochondrial haplogroup structure in two pastoralist Tibetan communities of the Sanjiangyuan region.
items.abstract: Uniparental diversity in the Sanjiangyuan region, the pastoralist interior of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, is uncharacterised. We analysed Y-chromosomal haplogroups in 547 males and mitochondrial haplogroups in 623 samples from a cohort of 1 226 Tibetans in Qumalai and Tanggula, with household pedigrees for 470 Tanggula participants. Both fall within Tibetan variation yet are separable on both marker systems. Qumalai carries haplogroup D at 74.3% (effective haplogroup number 1.74), matched among the Tibetan reference samples only by Nagqu; Tanggula lies within the published range at 2.48. Two features mark the Tanggula maternal pool. The West Eurasian lineage U7, on 26 carriers, stands at 5.6% of assigned samples (26/467; 95% CI 3.5-7.7%), 10.3% of the quality-filtered set (26/252), at or above the highest value recorded on the plateau (5.3%) under every treatment, although the most conservative interval includes it; the carriers fall in 12 matrilines occupying half the households expected by chance (P < 0.0001). Haplogroup Z, present in Qumalai in every Tibetan reference sample, was not observed in Tanggula (P = 7 × 10⁻⁴ among informative assignments). Paternal haplogroup diversity differs significantly between the communities, while maternal diversity does not, at both levels and on an unbounded scale. Raw FST is not comparable across these marker systems: its attainable maximum ranges from 0.343 to 0.024 across four levels; standardised measures reverse the ordering. Sanjiangyuan Tibetans are not a genetically homogeneous unit; the large valley Amdo samples on which the published picture chiefly rests do not span plateau paternal diversity.

items.title: Database on distribution and ecology of silica-scaled chrysophytes from Siberia
items.abstract: Silica-scaled chrysophytes include algae within the class Chrysophyceae that are characterized by species-specific silica elements covering the cell. For this group, a well-established species concept based on the ultrastructure of these elements, studied through electron microscopy, has been developed. These organisms are widely distributed in freshwater ecosystems, where they form an important component of phytoplankton. Because individual scales can be used for species identification and remain preserved in sediments, silica-scaled chrysophytes are increasingly recognized as valuable indicators for monitoring freshwater ecosystems and as promising subjects for paleolimnological and biogeographic research. They also provide important material for investigating biodiversity and the processes underlying its formation. To support this work, an online database has been established documenting 194 species and intraspecific taxa of silica-scaled chrysophytes recorded from Siberian water bodies. Each species record includes original electron micrographs, sampling-site information with geographical coordinates linked to an online map, the sampling date, and key water-quality parameters, including temperature, pH, and electrical conductivity. The database is freely accessible to all interested researchers.

items.title: Identifying shared and parasite-specific determinants of Plasmodium falciparum and Schistosoma mansoni co-infection in a large-scale community-based study in rural Uganda
items.abstract: Malaria and schistosomiasis are co-endemic across much of sub-Saharan Africa, yet it remains unclear whether co-infections reflect shared risk factors, unexplained biological determinants, or chance co-occurrence. We analysed data collected at recruitment from 4290 individuals aged 5-90 years across 52 villages in rural Uganda within the SchistoTrack cohort. A bivariate copula model was developed to separate shared and disease-specific associations from residual dependence. Prevalence was 41.47% for Schistosoma mansoni , 41.19% for Plasmodium falciparum , and 18.51% for co-infection. Prevalence overlapped in school-aged children with co-infection prevalence peaking at 13 years. Greater distance to a government health centre was the strongest shared determinant, apart from age, male gender and living in western districts, increasing the risk of both. Local water ecology influenced each pathogen in opposing directions. Fishing was associated with higher S. mansoni and co-infection risks, but not P. falciparum risk. A modelled scenario combining household drinking-water treatment, handwashing facilities and protected water sources with cessation of freshwater contact reduced co-infection prevalence by 32%. Our findings support integrated control around shared demographics and limited healthcare access and household water infrastructure, while highlighting the need for non-integrated approaches for ecological interventions aiming to reduce parasite-specific transmission determinants.

items.title: Sonic Stage: Automatically Generating Interactive Spatial Soundscapes to Facilitate Dialogue Video Comprehension for Blind Viewers
items.abstract: Audio description (AD) makes film and television accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) audiences by narrating characters’ actions. However, in scenes with lots of dialogue, AD often omits important actions because it is constrained not to overlap with speech. It is not yet known how to convey characters’ actions during dialogue. We present Sonic Stage, a system that transforms dialogue videos into interactive spatial soundscapes, enabling BLV audiences to intuitively understand characters’ actions and movements through immersive auditory cues. Sonic Stage conveys essential visual information during dialogue through three auditory techniques: (1) spatialized dialogue to represent spatial layout, (2) diegetic sound to convey character actions, and (3) interactive descriptions to provide context-specific visual details. Evaluation with 12 BLV viewers showed that Sonic Stage significantly improved video comprehension, spatial presence, and narrative engagement. We highlight opportunities for enhancing video accessibility across diverse genres through immersive, interactive audio representations.

items.title: Reimagining Sustainable Natural Resource Governance through the Paradigm of Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘ah and Ecological Justice
items.abstract: The exploitation of natural resources and environmental degradation call for sustainable governance grounded in ethical and normative values. This study aims to identify Islamic principles in responding to contemporary environmental governance challenges and their relevance to sustainable natural resource management. This study employs a qualitative-descriptive approach through an integrative literature review of 25 scientific publications, primarily from 2021–2026, using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The results indicate that there are eight sustainable governance strategies closely linked to Islamic values within the framework of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, including public interest-based planning, regulation, participation, accountability, and law enforcement which reflect the principles of justice (‘adl) and stewardship (amānah),pollution monitoring, ecosystem restoration, and sustainability evaluation grounded in the principles of balance (mīzān) and ecological stewardship (khilāfah). The contribution of this research is that it offers an integrative framework for environmental governance that is equitable, sustainable, and oriented toward the well-being of future generations.

items.title: Future directions on integrated wildlife monitoring based on non-invasive approaches in Europe
items.abstract: Abstract The growing trend of emerging diseases at the wildlife-livestock-human interface underscores the need to establish integrated surveillance strategies within a One Health framework. In Europe, Integrated Wildlife Monitoring (IWM) tends to focus on specific pathogens, often with limited spatial and temporal scope. In this perspectives article, we address some of the most recent technological advances that could strengthen future IWM programs, with special emphasis on non-invasive approaches for monitoring wildlife populations and pathogen communities. We analyse the potential complementarity of different monitoring tools, such as camera traps, unmanned aerial vehicles, acoustic recording, and especially the detection of environmental nucleic acids (ENAD) using next-generation sequencing techniques, for the simultaneous characterization of pathogen and host communities. Despite the potential of molecular tools for large-scale monitoring, the lack of methodological standardization, the limited capacity to obtain quantitative information (e.g. population abundance or pathogen prevalence), and the difficulty of inferring the epidemiological significance of findings (e.g. whether molecular detection indicates viable pathogen) remain key challenges that limit their application. Finally, we argue that integrating these technologies with artificial intelligence (AI) represents a promising approach for managing large, heterogeneous datasets and developing proactive early warning systems. Moving toward the implementation of standardized and harmonized strategies that integrate ecological and epidemiological information should be a priority in European health surveillance frameworks. Strengthening coordination among surveillance systems by incorporating multi-source, AI-supported approaches will be key to improving early detection capacity and supporting evidence-based decision-making in addressing the global emergence of diseases.

items.title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
items.abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. Phylogenetic reconstructions reveal early aureochrome diversification in the stramenopile lineage, originating in a heterotrophic ancestor before photosynthesis was acquired. This challenges the assumption that aureochromes are restricted to phototrophs, suggesting an ancestral role in spectral light signaling. We find that, despite changes in light quality and photoperiod by latitude, diatom aureochrome domain architecture remains conserved. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

items.title: DNA-based monitoring of bushmeat trade dynamics and hotspots across western and central Africa
items.abstract: The bushmeat trade in Africa is a largely unregulated activity that drives the unsustainable exploitation of wild terrestrial vertebrates—an issue often coined the “bushmeat crisis”. We build on a four-gene mitochondrial DNA-typing approach to develop an unprecedented reference database framework for effectively tracing the bushmeat trade in tropical Africa. Our dataset comprises c. 2500 samples collected over a 13-yr period across 10 African countries and two European airports. Relying on an expert analytical pipeline and ~8700 nucleotide sequences, we identified 96% of bushmeat samples to the species-level. In contrast, we estimated that conventional two-gene approaches would have yielded 18–26% erroneous or inconclusive taxonomic assignments. DNA-typing refined >50% of field identifications, with refinement reaching 92–95% for highly processed carcasses seized in Europe. Leveraging expanded taxonomic representation, we empirically refined the genetic species thresholds applied to bushmeat surveys and provide a reproducible pipeline for using our expert reference database. Overall, we identified 133 species—mostly mammals—with one-third listed as of conservation concern, and uncovered evidence of cryptic diversity within several taxa. Our results also demonstrated the value of community ecology indexes for large-scale monitoring of the bushmeat trade. While national markets generally mirrored regional biodiversity patterns across tropical Africa, Benin emerged as a notable outlier and a key wildlife trade hotspot. We advocate for the integration of community ecology frameworks into surveillance efforts to guide more effective, regionally tailored mitigation strategies. Continued, standardized sampling effort is essential to broaden taxonomic coverage and enhance detection of cryptic biodiversity in genetic bushmeat monitoring.

items.title: Protecting birds in protected areas: a multi-scale analysis of forest structure and species occurrence
items.abstract: Protected areas are cornerstones of avian conservation, yet forest-associated bird communities continue to decline even within protected lands. The capacity of a protected area to sustain bird populations depends on both internal habitat quality and the surrounding landscape context, yet the relative importance of these scales remains poorly understood. We evaluate how forest structure at three nested spatial scales (local, park, and county) influences the occurrence of forest-associated birds within protected areas. We analyzed 17 years (2006–2023) of point count data for 16 forest-bird species across eight National Parks in the Northeastern United States to determine the relationships between species occurrences and five forest-structure variables, including the dominant spatial scale for each. Forest-structure variables were derived at local, park, and county spatial scales using long-term park monitoring and national forest inventory data. County-scale forest variables were selected most frequently as the dominant scale of effect on bird occurrence probabilities (19 species-covariate combinations), followed by local (16) and park (5) scales, with at least one county-scale forest variable influencing 75% of species. All but two species showed significant associations with forest structure variables. Park size had weak and inconsistent effects on occurrence, likely because the parks included in our study are all small. While these parks contain quality avian habitat, county-scale forest availability and connectivity may constrain which species persist within them. Protected areas cannot conserve forest-associated birds in isolation; regional landscape context at the county-scale is an equally important determinant of species occurrences, especially for small, protected areas. Management of the matrix habitat surrounding protected areas, such as restoring forest availability and improving connectivity, may yield greater conservation returns than management of protected areas in isolation. This can be a tractable strategy for practitioners in regions where expanding formal protection is constrained by competing land uses.

items.title: Contrasting viability clusters in the fen orchid Liparis loeselii across NE German fens: reproductive output varies with productivity, light and iron concentration
items.abstract: Abstract The decline of many temperate orchid species has intensified efforts to understand the ecological conditions required for conservation. Long-term monitoring of life stages and traits is commonly used to assess population viability. However, comprehensive monitoring is challenging for inconspicuous orchids in spatially discrete subpopulations. Comparing subpopulations within sites from a single census using key viability proxies may therefore provide insight into site-level population viability and identify habitat conditions associated with contrasting subpopulation viability. Across 17 fen sites in NE Germany, 225 individuals from 65 subpopulations of the fen orchid Liparis loeselii were analysed. Analyses tested whether (i) subpopulations formed distinct clusters based on viability proxies, (ii) clusters differed in environmental factors and (iii) clusters were associated with differing plant species composition. Vegetation relevés were conducted, nine environmental factors recorded and viability proxies assessed for each subpopulation. Three clusters with contrasting subpopulation viability were identified. Cluster 1 had a low reproductive output and tall vegetation, Cluster 2 showed high herbivory and low vegetation height, and Cluster 3 high reproductive output and high peat iron concentration. Plant species composition also differed among clusters. At the site level, Cluster 1 dominance was associated with smaller estimated population sizes, whereas sites dominated by Clusters 2 and 3 had larger estimated population sizes. The identified clusters may support initial assessments of site-level population status, although recruitment data are needed to evaluate long-term population viability. Management should promote open, low-stature vegetation mosaics encompassing contrasting hydrochemical conditions, including calcium-rich and iron-rich habitats.

items.title: Diversity of Hemiptera (Insecta) in Different Coffee Plantation Districts of Karnataka, India
items.abstract: The present study provides a faunistic account of the order Hemiptera (Insecta) associated with coffee plantations in different districts of Karnataka, India. Field surveys were conducted in selected coffee-growing regions representing different geographical and ecological conditions of the state. Hemipteran specimens were collected using standard entomological methods, including sweep netting, hand collection, and light trapping, and were subsequently preserved, examined, and identified using relevant taxonomic literature and comparative material. The study documents the diversity and distribution of hemipteran insects occurring in coffee plantation ecosystems, with representatives of several families and genera. The recorded taxa comprise phytophagous as well as predatory forms, reflecting the ecological complexity of the coffee agroecosystem. Particular attention was given to species identification, diagnostic characters, locality records, and their known distribution in India and elsewhere. The study contributes to the existing knowledge of the hemipteran fauna of Karnataka and provides baseline information on the insect diversity associated with coffee plantations. Such faunistic inventories are important for understanding insect diversity, species distribution, and ecological interactions within coffee agroecosystems and may also provide useful information for future studies on economically important and beneficial hemipteran species. During the present study, 41 species belonging to 37 genera and 15 families of Hemiptera were documented from coffee plantation areas in Kodagu, Shivamogga and Chikkamagaluru districts of Karnataka, India.

items.title: Edukasi Fermentasi Limbah Daun Gugur Menjadi Pupuk Organik Cair di SMA Negeri 1 Kota Serang
items.abstract: Lingkungan sekolah menghasilkan limbah organik berupa daun gugur yang belum dimanfaatkan secara optimal. Kondisi ini menjadi peluang untuk mengenalkan pengelolaan limbah organik yang bermanfaat melalui kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan siswa dalam mengolah limbah daun gugur menjadi pupuk organik cair (POC) melalui fermentasi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di SMA Negeri 1 Kota Serang dengan melibatkan 35 siswa dan 1 guru. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan edukatif-partisipatif melalui sosialisasi, demonstrasi, diskusi, dan praktik pembuatan POC menggunakan daun gugur kering, gula, bioaktivator EM4, dan air. Hasil pengamatan selama kegiatan menunjukkan adanya perubahan respons siswa dalam menjawab pertanyaan. Sebelum sosialisasi, hanya sedikit siswa yang mampu menjawab pertanyaan secara langsung, sedangkan setelah sosialisasi dan praktik, lebih dari separuh siswa dapat menjawab pertanyaan dengan cepat. Kegiatan ini juga memberikan pengalaman langsung kepada siswa dalam memanfaatkan limbah daun gugur menjadi produk yang berpotensi digunakan sebagai sumber unsur hara bagi tanaman. Dengan demikian, kegiatan ini diharapkan dapat mendorong pemanfaatan limbah organik dan menumbuhkan kepedulian lingkungan di sekolah.

items.title: When troglobites set the rules: How cave‐restricted species shape community responses in the richest tropical subterranean hotspot
items.abstract: Abstract Neotropical subterranean ecosystems remain poorly understood, particularly regarding the environmental factors structuring their communities and how these processes vary across spatial scales. Moreover, no previous study has examined how cave‐restricted species influence community responses to habitat attributes. We investigated the drivers shaping invertebrate assemblages in the Água Clara Cave System (ACCS), Bahia, Brazil (the richest subterranean biodiversity hotspot in the tropics), using a multiscale analytical framework and assessing the role of troglobitic taxa. Invertebrates were sampled in 59 sectors (10 × 3 m) and 177 quadrats (1 × 1 m) distributed along ~9 km of four interconnected caves. We recorded 6835 individuals representing 27 orders, at least 87 families and 129 species, including 30 troglobitic taxa. Species richness responded to different predictors across scales: at the microscale, richness increased with trophic resource diversity and declined with distance from the entrance; at the mesoscale, it was negatively associated with shelter availability and distance from the entrance. Beta diversity was high at both spatial scales and was consistently dominated by species turnover, with patterns associated with distance from the cave entrance, humidity, temperature, resource availability, shelter availability and substrate diversity. After excluding troglobitic taxa, ecological patterns weakened substantially: richness responded only to distance from the entrance at the microscale and β‐diversity lost most environmental associations. These findings show that microclimatic and trophic factors structure ACCS communities and that troglobitic taxa strongly mediate these responses. Preserving the environmental integrity and microclimatic stability of the system is essential for safeguarding this subterranean biodiversity hotspot.

items.title: Consciousness as Present Lived Awareness
items.abstract: This reflection develops an interdisciplinary account of human consciousness as present lived awareness. The argument is not that neuroscience, ecology, Ubuntu, and spirituality all say the same thing. Rather, it distinguishes levels of explanation. Neuroscience investigates the brain-body mechanisms that enable conscious experience. Phenomenology describes experience as lived from the first-person present. Ecology shows that conscious organisms are sustained by air, water, food, microbes, soil, biodiversity, climate, and the wider web of life. Social theory and Ubuntu show that human persons are formed through care, language, recognition, cooperation, institutions, and mutual responsibility. Spiritual metaphysics interprets consciousness in relation to soul, God, nature, love, being, knowledge, mortality, and ultimate meaning. The central claim is that human consciousness is a first-person field of experience enabled by brain and body, structured by time, bounded by mortality, sustained by the biosphere, formed through social relation, and capable of situated agency. The analysis further distinguishes awareness itself from the changing contents of awareness, arguing that thoughts, emotions, memories, perceptions, spiritual experiences, and social meanings appear within awareness but do not exhaust awareness itself. The past is not directly re-entered; it appears now as memory, habit, record, wound, learning, or wisdom. The future is not yet possessed; it appears now as anticipation, plan, hope, fear, or possibility. Agency is therefore exercised only in the present, and it is never unconditioned: it is shaped by biology, development, culture, institutions, unconscious processes, ecological conditions, and social supports. Yet conditioned consciousness can still sometimes pause, attend, deliberate, inhibit, repair, learn, and act. It also adopts methodological caution: following Connolly’s distinction between awareness itself and the contents of awareness, the analysis treats neuroscience, phenomenology, ecology, Ubuntu, and metaphysics as complementary but non-identical ways of approaching a phenomenon whose ultimate ontology remains open (Connolly, 2026a, 2026b, 2026c, 2026d). Alan Watts offers a complementary interpretive voice for the same themes: present-moment awareness, the insecurity of clinging to a fixed future, the critique of the isolated ego, the unity of human beings and nature, and the non-dual insight that the self is not a separate controller standing outside life (Watts, 1951, 1957, 1958, 1966). Watts is used here as a philosophical and spiritual interlocutor, not as a scientific authority. The exploration argues for a layered view rather than a reductionist one. Ordinary human consciousness is brain-enabled but not adequately understood as neural mechanism alone. It is embodied but not merely physiological. It is socially constituted but not dissolved into the collective. It is ecologically embedded but not identical with all life. It is spiritually interpretable, but spiritual interpretation should not be mistaken for empirical proof. The resulting account is dual-aspect, ecological, relational, and panentheistic in orientation: the same conscious life can be described outwardly in terms of embodied processes and inwardly in terms of lived meaning, value, relation, and participation in being. Human consciousness is present lived awareness: a first-person field of experience enabled by brain and body, structured by time, bounded by mortality, sustained by the biosphere, formed through social relation, and capable of situated agency. Scientific explanation investigates its enabling mechanisms; phenomenology describes how it is lived; ecology and Ubuntu reveal its dependence on life and relation; and spiritual metaphysics interprets its ultimate meaning in relation to soul, God, love, being, knowledge, and responsibility. The appendices extend the main argument by applying the definition of consciousness to practical, cultural, metaphysical, technological, and theological questions. Appendix A explains the George Harrison and Brainwashed source quotation concerning the soul as love, existence, and knowledge, treating it not as proof but as a cultural and spiritual starting point for reflection on soul, Vedantic thought, and inward spiritual depth. Appendix B translates the thesis of present lived awareness into daily practice, arguing that consciousness should be lived through presence, responsibility, humility, compassion, memory transformed into learning, future-oriented preparation, bodily care, ecological participation, Ubuntu, and the capacity to pause before action. Appendix C situates Alan Watts as a philosophical and spiritual interlocutor. Watts’s writings on Zen, insecurity, nature, non-duality, ego, and theology support the paper’s critique of the isolated self and its emphasis on present awareness, while the paper retains a more cautious method by distinguishing spiritual insight from scientific explanation and metaphysical proof. Appendix D develops the phrase “one coherent moment of experience and responsible action” as a phenomenological singularity. This does not mean a physical singularity like the Big Bang or a black hole, but a lived point of convergence where body, brain, memory, anticipation, mortality, society, ecology, meaning, and agency become one present field capable of responsible action. Appendix E applies the definition of consciousness to artificial intelligence. It distinguishes intelligence from lived awareness and argues that current AI should not be treated as conscious merely because it produces fluent language, plans, summaries, or simulations of selfhood. AI may extend human memory, planning, reflection, creativity, and social coordination, but responsibility remains human. A future AI would become a serious candidate for consciousness only if it possessed, or functionally approximated, a unified field of awareness, embodied or self-maintaining vulnerability, temporal continuity, affective concern, social formation, and some capacity for responsible agency. The ethical implication is that AI should be used to enlarge human awareness, truthfulness, relationality, ecological responsibility, and wise present action, not to replace consciousness or evade accountability. Appendix F asks “Who Created Whom?”: did God create human consciousness, or did human consciousness create God? The answer is developed through the paper’s layered method. Theologically and metaphysically, God may be understood as the source and ground of human consciousness, being, love, truth, and responsibility. Psychologically, historically, and socially, human consciousness clearly creates God-concepts, God-images, doctrines, rituals, symbols, and God-language. The appendix therefore rejects a simplistic either/or. Its strongest conclusion is that God may be understood as creating the conscious being, while human consciousness creates the finite forms through which God is imagined, named, misunderstood, worshipped, doubted, sought, purified, and responsibly lived. Free will is central to this process: inherited God-images may be received from family, culture, trauma, or community, but present lived awareness can examine, reject, deepen, purify, or responsibly embody them. Appendix G, “The Meaning of Life,” applies the paper’s definition of consciousness to the personal question of meaning and purpose. It argues that the meaning of life is not a detached abstraction or distant achievement, but the way existence becomes personally significant in present lived awareness. Meaning arises as the person receives life, carries the past as learning, prepares the future through hope and plan, faces mortality, becomes aware of conditioning, honours the body, participates in the biosphere, recognises others through Ubuntu, and remains open to God, soul, mystery, and ultimate meaning. The appendix concludes that the purpose of life is to become more fully awake, loving, truthful, responsible, and life-giving in the present. In its simplest formulation, life has meaning when consciousness becomes love in action. Appendix H, “Free Because I Am Discerning Awareness,” connects the reflection’s account of free will with Ignatian spirituality and the Jesuit goal of interior freedom. It argues that freedom is not freedom from all conditioning, but the capacity of present lived awareness to notice interior movements, discern where they lead, loosen disordered attachments, and choose what serves love, truth, God, neighbour, life, and shared flourishing. The Ignatian Examen is interpreted as a practice of discerning awareness in which memory becomes learning, future possibility becomes intention, and conditioned impulses become available for reflection and responsible action. items.title: A coastal beach seed bank shows high diversity, but low similarity to the adjacent forest vegetation in an Amazonia Marine Extractive Reserve
items.abstract: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. A floristic inventory was conducted on the main beaches of the reserve, while seeds were manually collected from the sand during low tide. The vegetation comprised of 20 species distributed across 16 families, with dominance of Rhizophora sp. and a predominance of arboreal habit (50 – 56% of individuals). A total of 786 seeds were recorded, representing 21 plant families, 64 identified species, and 46 morphospecies, exhibiting substantially higher diversity than the vegetation (Shannon 3.90 – 4.13 for seed taxonomy versus 0.79 – 2.29 for vegetation) and high evenness (Pielou ≥ 0.95). Mean seed density did not differ statistically among beaches. The divergence between seeds and vegetation indicated a strong influence of external dispersal, likely shaped by hydrochory. The results demonstrate the genetic potential of the seed bank, characterized as an important propagule reservoir for the ecological restoration of coastal ecosystems. Therefore, it was observed that seed composition does not fully reflect the adjacent vegetation but reinforces the role of Amazoniana coastal ecosystems as biodiversity source areas, highlighting the need for conservation strategies that consider ecological connectivity, monitoring of natural regeneration, and sustainable management of tourism use.

items.title: Specimen occurrences of six Neotropical tree species used to estimate realized climatic niches (Área de Conservación Guanacaste climate-tolerance study)
items.abstract: Description: Georeferenced preserved-specimen records of Eugenia monticola, E. siggersii, E. truncata, E. valerii (including records under E. costaricensis), Pouteria reticulata and Vitex cooperi, retrieved from GBIF with rgbif (occ_search; basisOfRecord = PRESERVED_SPECIMEN, with coordinates, no geospatial issues, occurrenceStatus = PRESENT) on 30 October 2026. BIEN withholds coordinates for these species, so GBIF was used instead. Records were cleaned with CoordinateCleaner: invalid, zero and equal coordinates were removed, as were records at sea, at country capitals or centroids, at biodiversity institutions, duplicates, records outside the tropical and subtropical Americas, and records with coordinate uncertainty above 5 km. The remaining records were thinned to one per species per 2.5′ cell. The 1,221 retained records, from 110 source datasets, were combined with CHELSA V2.1 climate to estimate each species’ realized climatic niche, which was compared with leaf heat tolerance and turgor loss point measured in the Área de Conservación Guanacaste, Costa Rica (Hulshof et al., in prep., Functional Ecology).

items.title: Functional genomic analysis of Vreelandella zhaodongensis BS253: a new isolate from hypersaline lakes from Brazilian Pantanal
items.abstract: Abstract Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. In this study, we report the complete genome sequencing and functional characterization of isolate BS253, isolated in a hypersaline alkaline lake from Brazil’s Pantanal region. Using a hybrid sequencing strategy combining Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads, we assembled a circular chromosome of 3.76 Mb and two plasmids. Phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses identified the isolate as Vreelandella zhaodongensis . Digital DNA-DNA hybridization (76.4%) and ANI (96.83%) values supported the designation of BS253 as a strain of V. zhaodongensis . Genome mining revealed genes potentially associated with salt and alkali tolerance, hydrocarbon and plastic degradation, and the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites. Phenotypically, BS253 is a moderately halophilic, facultatively anaerobic, Gram-negative rod that also exhibits emulsifying activity (55.1%) under defined culture conditions. These findings highlight strain BS253 as a metabolically versatile extremophile and a promising candidate for future studies in environmental and industrial biotechnology.

items.title: Technological approach to invasive species: the role of remote sensing and predictive modelling
items.abstract: Remote sensing, predictive modelling and machine learning are increasingly central to detecting and monitoring invasive plant species across broad and heterogeneous landscapes. This review synthesises 25 years of remote sensing–based invasive plant species research (2000–2025) to determine how sensor selection, analytical methods and reporting practices have evolved. Records from Web of Science and Scopus were screened using defined eligibility criteria and coded by platform, sensor, species, region, method, impact category, accuracy reporting and linkage with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Bibliometric keyword analysis was used to examine thematic structure and emerging research directions. The evidence shows rapid publication growth after 2015, continued dominance of satellite data, increasing use of uncrewed aerial systems, light detection and ranging, synthetic aperture radar and machine learning classifiers and persistent geographic imbalance. Of 166 retained studies, 149 provided extractable impact information and 76 reported overall accuracy values. The literature indicates a shift from descriptive mapping toward integrated monitoring, risk assessment and decision support frameworks for biodiversity conservation, restoration planning and invasive plant management. items.title: Y-linked Genome Editor (YLE) a Self-Limiting Genetic Control Tool: An Updated Review
items.abstract: Invasive species are increasingly impacting forests, food, fisheries, and agriculture, with global economic repercussions. The majority of vertebrate pest management methods lack effective strategic control tools and are unsustainable and unsuitable for effective landscape-scale management. The application of genetic techniques is intended to prevent invasive populations. Employment of a mix of strategies has enabled sustained control, depending on the species, region, and degree of dissemination. Advantages of the genetic methods include species specificity, long-term and self-sustainability, 100% trait transferability, minimum infrastructure requirement, and non-requirement of physical modification of the landscape. This renders these methods feasible and applicable globally to control a large number of invasive pests. The possibility of using gene drive technology in conjunction with conventional control techniques opens new horizons in the management of vertebrate invasive populations. Since these techniques are environmentally suitable and non-polluting, they are suited for a green economy. The success of these methods is currently illustrated in the control of invasive species across vast geographic regions, such as Asian carp in the Mississippi River, lionfish in the Caribbean, and zebra mussels in the Great Lakes. Thus, judiciously designed experimental and field study methods suited for a particular pest will enable long-term goals of control and sustenance of invasive pest control.

items.title: Lake Sediments Exposed Under Warmer Temperatures Hatched a Lower Diversity of Microfauna From the Egg Bank
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dormant structures produced by aquatic microorganisms are ecologically important for restoring ecosystems after extreme climatic events. Among these events, heat waves cause the desiccation of environments and expose sediments to high temperatures, which reduce the viability of dormant propagules. Here, we measured the richness and species composition of the dormant aquatic microfauna (ciliates, rotifers, cladocerans, copepods and ostracods) hatched from sediments heated under a gradient of increasing temperatures. Sediment samples were collected from a temporary lake in the Upper Paraná River floodplain, Brazil. The material was exposed at temperatures of 25°C, 30°C, 40°C, 50°C, and 60°C. They were subsequently inundated and kept in mesocosms at 25°C with a 12‐h light/dark photoperiod for 8 weeks. Hatched organisms were harvested weekly. Increasing drying temperature significantly reduced the richness of hatching aquatic microfauna and led to significant differences in species composition between temperature treatments, although these trends were less linear for microcrustacean. Temperatures above 50°C (not uncommon for dried sediments exposed to direct sun in humid tropical areas) negatively affected community richness and promoted biotic homogenization of the communities hatched from the egg bank. Therefore, increased sediment temperatures in dry wetlands are a potential threat to dormant microfauna through biotic homogenization and species loss. Mitigation measures may be needed to conserve wetland egg banks.

items.title: Keanekaragaman Avifauna dan Analisis Potensi Gangguannya di Area Gardu Induk PLN Medari, Sleman, Yogyakarta
items.abstract: Gardu induk berperan dalam distribusi listrik untuk memenuhi kebutuhan listrik masyarakat dan terkadang mengalami gangguan internal maupun eksternal. Salah satu gangguan yang muncul berasal dari avifauna. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mempelajari keanekaragaman spesies avifauna yang ada di area Gardu Induk PLN Medari, menganalisis potensi gangguan yang ditimbulkan avifauna di area Gardu Induk, serta memahami potensi bentang alam sebagai habitat avifauna yang berada di area Gardu Induk tersebut. Metode yang digunakan adalah point count pada tujuh titik sampling yang telah ditentukan, yaitu titik di area Gardu Induk PLN Medari dan bentang alam di sekitar lokasi utama (area persawahan dan zona riparian). Pengambilan data dilakukan pada musim kemarau dan musim penghujan, dengan tiga kali pengulangan pada tiap sampling. Data avifauna kemudian diidentifikasi, ditabulasi, serta dianalisis dengan Indeks Dominansi Simpson dan Matriks Penilaian Risiko. Hasil menunjukkan terdapat 12 spesies avifauna yang dijumpai di Gardu Induk PLN Medari, dengan 9 spesies diantaranya ditemui pula pada inventarisasi tahun 2024. Keduabelas spesies tersebut juga dijumpai di titik bentang alam sekitar Gardu Induk. Bentang alam tersebut berperan sebagai habitat dan tempat mencari pakan spesies avifauna. Gangguan dari 12 spesies avifauna pada Gardu Induk dikategorikan mulai dari ekstrem (sangat mengganggu) hingga rendah (tidak mengganggu).

items.title: CULTURAL LANDSCAPE PERCEPTION AND INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE INHERITANCE IN DALI VILLAGE, GUIZHOU
items.abstract: Intangible cultural heritage represents the collective memory, cultural identity, and traditional knowledge of local communities, while its sustainable inheritance increasingly faces challenges arising from modernization, migration, and lifestyle transformation. Cultural landscapes provide important spatial and cultural contexts for maintaining and transmitting intangible cultural heritage; however, the relationship between residents’ perceptions of cultural landscapes and intangible cultural heritage inheritance (ICHI) remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the relationship between cultural landscape perception (CLP) and intangible cultural heritage inheritance (ICHI) in Dali Village, Guizhou Province, using questionnaire survey data collected from local residents. Through descriptive analysis, reliability testing, and correlation analysis, the study examines residents’ perceptions of cultural landscapes and their willingness to participate in intangible cultural heritage inheritance. The findings reveal that residents generally demonstrate high levels of CLP and ICHI, and CLP is significantly positively associated with ICHI. The results indicate that stronger recognition of cultural values, historical meanings, and emotional connections with local landscapes can enhance residents’ willingness to preserve and transmit traditional cultural practices. This study highlights the importance of integrating cultural landscape conservation with community-based intangible cultural heritage inheritance. The findings provide practical implications for promoting sustainable heritage conservation and cultural continuity in traditional villages.

items.title: Engineering Eucalyptol-in-Water Nanoemulsions with Pluronic F-127: From Formulation to Stability and Function
items.abstract: Abstract Eucalyptol (1,8-cineole) is a valuable bioactive monoterpene, but its volatility, water immiscibility, and chemical lability limit practical use. Here, we developed eucalyptol-in-water nanoemulsions stabilized by Pluronic F-127 and mapped their composition-dependent phase behavior, structure, and interfacial properties. A pseudoternary formulation map revealed a narrow window of transparent single-phase oil-in-water nanoemulsions, obtained at eucalyptol fractions of 0.01–0.04 (w/w) and Pluronic F-127 fractions up to 0.13 (w/w), whereas higher oil loadings promoted phase separation and excess polymer led to highly viscous or gel-like states. Dynamic light scattering showed nanodroplets with apparent hydrodynamic diameters of about 20–40 nm under optimal conditions, with droplet size increasing as eucalyptol content rose and a second smaller population appearing at higher polymer content, consistent with micellization and structural crowding. Conductivity increased with Pluronic F-127 content, while pH remained near 6.5–6.9 and zeta potential was essentially unchanged, confirming stabilization by a nonionic interfacial layer. Fluorescence spectroscopy indicated two eucalyptol environments, with emission bands centered near 310 and 325 nm, and increasing polymer content reduced fluorescence intensity through self-quenching. Contact angles on polystyrene averaged about 35°, independent of composition, whereas droplets spread almost immediately on glass. In a DPPH assay, nanoemulsions increased radical scavenging relative to free eucalyptol, although excessive Pluronic F-127 reduced this effect by densifying the interfacial shell. Overall, these results define the narrow but well-defined compositional window for carrier-oil-free, kinetically stable O/W eucalyptol nanoemulsions and reveal how oil–polymer interactions govern their formation, stability, and function.

items.title: AKARI near-infrared spectroscopy of circumstellar hydrocarbon dust associated with young stellar objects
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate the processing of the circumstellar polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) associated with young stellar objects (YSOs) through their stellar activities. We analyze the AKARI near-infrared (2.6–4.4$\, \mu {\rm m}$ ) long-slit spectral data of 10 YSOs, focusing on the aromatic feature at a wavelength of 3.3$\, \mu {\rm m}$ and the aliphatic features at 3.4–3.6$\, \mu {\rm m}$. The spectral fitting results show large variations from target to target in the flux ratio of the aliphatic to aromatic features, the shape of the aliphatic feature profile, and the central wavelength of the aromatic feature. In particular, ${\rm HD}\,\,97048$ and Elias 1 show strong aliphatic features at wavelengths longer than 3.5$\, \mu {\rm m}$, which is consistent with the hydrogenated nanodiamond features reported in previous studies. We find that the properties of the hydrocarbon dust vary under the influence of the YSO activity, where the degree of dust processing is likely to be related to the age of the YSO and the amount of the circumstellar dust. In addition, correlation is observed between the variations of the H$_2$O and CO$_2$ ice features and the aliphatic feature profiles, suggesting connection between the formation of CO$_2$ ice and the processing of aliphatic hydrocarbons. Finally, we find a significant correlation between the variations in the central wavelength of the aromatic feature and the shape of the aliphatic feature profile. These findings may be consistent with a tentative scenario in which circumstellar PAHs are converted to nanodiamonds through irradiation by high-energy particles produced by YSO activity.

items.title: Influence of Competitor Niche on the Ability of Enterobacter cloacae to Suppress the Germination Globisporangium ultimum Sporangia.
items.abstract: Enterobacter cloacae is a bacterium that can prevent seedling damping-off by Globisporangium ultimum (formerly Pythium ultimum). This bacterium suppresses damping-off by metabolizing the fatty acid cue released by germinating seeds that initiates G. ultimum sporangia germination and infection. However, this suppression mechanism has been unreliable because it only occurs only when carbohydrates are scarce. We hypothesized that niche preemption by competitor bacteria in carbohydrate rich environments could enhance the pathogen suppression success by E. cloacae by narrowing its realized niche to consist mainly of fatty acids. We tested this hypothesis through pair-wise competition experiments between E. cloacae and bacteria with varying niche overlap profiles and measured the germination of G. ultimum sporangia. After these trials, we postulated that other chemical substrates may influence the behavior of G. ultimum and E. cloacae based on patterns witnessed; namely amygdalin, hydroxybenzoic acid, palatinose, D-gluconic acid, and L-glutamic acid. We then exposed G. ultimum and E. cloacae to these compounds to determine how they influenced the suppression behavior of E. cloacae and the germination of G. ultimum sporangia. We found that although niche preemption does not predict pathogen suppression patterns between E. cloacae and competitor bacteria, niche overlap was inversely correlated with sporangia germination for gram-negative bacteria; the opposite pattern predicted by niche overlap. We also found several taxa that significantly enhanced the pathogen suppression by E. cloacae. Finally, we found that amygdalin and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid inhibited the suppression performance E. cloacae and found that 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, palatinose, and L-glutamic acid inhibited sporangia germination.

items.title: Distributions, transport and environmental effects of BTEX along the Pearl River-estuary-ocean continuum.
items.abstract: Benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene isomers (BTEX) are important anthropogenic pollutants with implications for coastal ecosystems and atmospheric chemistry. However, their land-ocean spatial gradients and transport remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated aquatic and atmospheric BTEX across the Pearl River Basin-Pearl River Estuary (PRE)-northeastern South China Sea (SCS) continuum. Surface BTEX concentrations in the PRE (198 ± 137 ng L-1) were significantly higher than those in rivers (29.4 ± 15.2 ng L-1) and the northeastern SCS (39.8 ± 25.3 ng L-1), possibly due to intensive industrial emissions and shipping activities. Using a LOICZ box-model framework, the apparent seaward export flux was estimated to be 0.547 ± 0.204 t d-1. Although the ecological risks were low at the observed concentrations, potential effects associated with continuous BTEX inputs warrant attention. The entire continuum acted as a net source of atmospheric BTEX, with mean water-to-air fluxes of 6.56 ± 8.14, 233 ± 153, and 73.8 ± 46.5 g km-2 d-1 for rivers, the PRE, and the northeastern SCS, respectively. BTEX-derived ozone formation potential and secondary organic aerosol formation potential averaged 5.54 ± 4.24 and 0.084 ± 0.064 μg m-3, respectively, highlighting the potential influence of BTEX on coastal atmospheric chemistry.
